Those who try to destroy them should not enter Allah’s places of worship, except fearfully and with trembling hearts, after their disbelief and having stopped people worshipping in them. (and strive for their ruin) means those who prevent whoever maintain the Masjids with Allah's remembrance and who visit Allah's House to perform Hajj and 'Umrah. (As for such) for the Romans, (it was never meant that they should enter them) Bayt al-Maqdis (except in fear) hiding from the believers for fear of being killed, for they would be killed if found. If a worshipper has the correct attitude, he will never deny the right to worship to those who come to do so; he will never persecute those who come to serve the Lord. When one is truly conscious of God’s greatness and one’s own helplessness before Him, one’s humility will show in one’s dealings with others: one will not seek to harm one’s fellow men in any way, let alone deny them their fundamental right to worship God.

**No right to enter except with fear.**

Only those do populate the mosques of Allah who believe in Allah and in the Day of Judgment, who are steadfast in Salah and pay the Zakah, and do not fear anyone but Allah" (9:18). What he means by "populating" the mosques is that one should enter them in a spirit of humility and with the fear of Allah in one's heart, and then engage oneself in prayers or in reciting the Holy Qur'an or in making "dhikr. ' In opposition to this, the laying waste of mosques would mean that few, or only a few people should offer their prayers in them, or that a set of circumstances is allowed to develop which makes it difficult for those who are present to acquire the proper attitude of humility. (It is not for the Mushrikin (polytheists), to maintain the Masjids of Allah while they witness against their own selves of disbelief. The works of such are in vain and in Fire shall they abide. The Masjids of Allah shall be maintained only by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day; perform the Salah, and give the Zakah and fear none but Allah. It is they who are on true guidance.)(9:17-18) (They are the ones who disbelieved and hindered you from Al-Masjid-Al-Haram (at Makkah) and detained the sacrificial animals, from reaching their place of sacrifice. Had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you may kill them and on whose account a sin would have been committed by you without (your) knowledge, that Allah might bring into His mercy whom He wills if they (the believers and the disbelievers) had been apart, We verily, would have punished those of them who disbelieved with painful torment)(48:25). So, the Holy Prophet g has foretold that when the Day of Judgment comes close, the mosques of the Muslims would be beautifully designed and decorated and be apparently full of people, but they would in reality be deserted, for a few people would go there for the purpose of offering their prayers. If Verse 114 was revealed on the occasion of the Peace of Hudaybiyyah when the mushrikin (associators) of Makkah had prevented the Muslims from entering Al-Masjid al-Haram, then it is quite obvious that laying waste a mosque does not merely mean demolishing it, but also that it is not being allowed to be used for the purpose for which it was built -- that is, for Salah and for the Dhikr (remembrance) of Allah. As for Verse 115, we have already pointed out that Allah not being limited to any particular direction or place, the Muslims do not, in turning towards the Ka'bah at all mean to worship it, but that this particular orientation has been fixed on account of certain other considerations.

**Disgrace here, and punishment there.**

They will have shame and humiliation in their life on earth at the hands of the believers, and in the Afterlife is a great torment for having stopped people from Allah’s Houses of worship. (Theirs in the world is ignominy) a chastisement in that their cities, Constantinople, Amorium ('Ammuriyyah) and Rome (Rumiyyah) would be ruined (and theirs in the Hereafter is an awful doom) more severe than the punishment they were subjected to in this world. (And why should not Allah punish them while they hinder from Al-Masjid Al-Haram, and they are not its guardians? None can be its guardians except Al-Muttaqun (the pious), but most of them know not.)(8:34)

115.text:
To Allah belong the east and the west names the two directions that between them take in every point on the earth, so the sentence is a way of saying that no quarter is outside His ownership, and the two points are named rather than the whole because they are the edges by which a person sets himself. So wherever you turn you are facing towards Allah draws the conclusion for the one who prays: since the directions belong to Him, the turning is not wasted wherever it lands, and the face of the servant is described as coming to God rather than to a wall or a city. Surely Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing closes with two names, and the two answer the two halves of the verse, since the encompassing is what keeps every place and the knowing is what keeps every intention, so the wideness of the mercy and the exactness of the knowledge are put together. The verse therefore answers a difficulty about direction with a statement about ownership, and it does so without setting the command to face a particular way aside, since the value of the direction is kept in the following verses. Nothing here takes the direction away from the Muslims, and that is worth keeping in view: what the verse answers is a case in which the place is not known or not open, and it answers from the ownership of the east and the west rather than from the merit of the one who turns. The two names at the end are the seal on that comfort, since what is wide enough to include every place is also knowing enough to include every intention, so a turning made in the dark and a turning made in the open are both received by the same Lord, and the servant is told where his turning arrives rather than what his turning deserves.

**What the verse was revealed about.**

The following was revealed either when the Jews criticised the change of the direction of prayer qibla or concerning the supererogatory prayers on animal-back during journeys which one may pray in any direction To God belong the East and the West that is the entire earth because these two directions represent both sides of it the earth; whithersoever you turn your faces in prayer by His command there is the Face of God the direction of prayer with which He is pleased. For some sixteen or seventeen months after that, the Muslims had to, under the commandment of Allah, turn towards the Baytul-Maqdis (at Bayt al-Maqdis) while offering Salah. But the Holy Prophet felt a deep longing for turning towards the Ka'bah, and from time to time he would look upwards, waiting for the Archangel Jibra'il to come with a new commandment in this respect. When Allah changed the Qiblah that is to say, commanded the Muslims to turn towards the Ka'bah in their Salah, and not towards the Baytul-Maqdis --, the Jews raised all kinds of objections to it, and tried to produce in the minds of the Muslims doubts and misgiving which, had they taken root, would have led to the denial of the Holy Prophet g and to the giving up of prescribed Salah, thus laying waste the mosque of the Holy Prophet . This verse was revealed about a group of Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who prayed whilst travelling in the wrong direction after doing their best to determine the correct direction. It is also said that saying (Unto Allah belong the East and the West) means: the people of the East and the people of the West have one direction of prayer which is the Sacred Precinct, and therefore (there is Allah's Countenance) means: that is the direction of prayer to Allah, (Lo! Allah is All-Embracing) regarding the direction of prayer, (All- Knowing) of their intentions. Allah, exalted is He, then revealed this verse (Unto Allah belong the East and the West)' . The verses (Unto Allah belong the East and the West) was revealed so that one prays toward whatever direction one's mount directs one upon offering supererogatory prayer . Allah has authority over the entire world, and He instructs His servants as He wills.

**The east and the west belong to Him.**

And to Allah belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn (yourselves or your faces) there is the Face of Allah (and He is High above, over His Throne). (And to Allah belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn (yourselves or your faces) there is the Face of Allah (and He is High above, over His Throne). (What is between the east and the west is the Qiblah for the people of Al-Madīnah, Ash-Sham and 'Iraq.) Whether He instructs you to face Bayt al-Maqdis or the Kaaba, or you make a mistake in the direction of prayer or are not sure of it, then it is not an issue, because to Allah belongs every direction. The verse points out that had Allah been limited to any one direction, a fixed and permanent orientation would have been necessary for worshipping Him, but that, being infinite and beyond all possible limitations and qualifications, He is the Lord of the East and the West and of all conceivable directions -- He is everywhere, and surrounds everything.

**Wherever you turn.**

Wheresoever a man turns, he shall find Allah "facing" him -- that is to say, ready to accept his prayers and to shower His bounties on him. Whichever way one turns, one would, no doubt, find Allah "facing" him; but if one has to choose a direction every time one starts to pray, it would only mean a dispersion of one's attention. Verse 115 says that whichever way one turns, one would find "the face of Allah", and that Allah being "All-Embracing" surrounds everything. (So wherever you turn (yourselves or your faces) there is the Face of Allah (and He is High above, over His Throne)." (So wherever you turn (yourselves or your faces) there is the Face of Allah (and He is High above, over His Throne) means, "Allah's direction is wherever you face, east or west. Ibn Jarir said, "Others said that this Ayah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah permitting the one praying voluntary prayers to face wherever they wish in the east or west, while traveling, when in fear and when facing the enemy. All that matters is to obey the commandment of Allah, which alone can make one worthy of receiving His grace.

**Worshipped in every place, and nothing is hidden from Him.**

Allah is vast in His blessings; He covers His creation with His mercy and ease. Surely, Allah is Sufficient (for His creatures' needs), Knowing. (Surely, Allah is Sufficient (for His creatures' needs), Knowing) is that Allah encompasses all His Creation by providing them with sufficient needs and by His generosity and favor. Therefore, turn your face towards the Holy Mosque at Makkah, and all of you too, wheresoever you may be, turn towards it. The verse points out that had Allah been limited to any one direction, a fixed and permanent orientation would have been necessary for worshipping Him, but that, being infinite and beyond all possible limitations and qualifications, He is the Lord of the East and the West and of all conceivable directions -- He is everywhere, and surrounds everything. The Qiblah for the People of Al-Madīnah is what is between the East and the West. True, He has prescribed a direction for us to face when we worship, but this is a purely organizational requirement for prayer; it does not mean that God is to be found in only one direction and not in any other. The Holy Qur'an, however, speaks in general terms of the mosques of Allah" so as to lay down a regular and permanent law, for all the peoples, covering all the possible cases of desecrating mosques and of hindering the "remembrance" of Allah in any way and thus laying them waste -- it denounces those who are capable of such a misdeed as being "unjust" or "cruel", and threatens them with humiliation in this world and dire punishment in the other, for the dignity of a mosque requires that one should enter it in a spirit of lowliness and respect, and with the fear of Allah in one's heart. Moreover, an impartial investigation into the respective attitudes and frames of minds would easily show how genuine the Muslims are in their claim to be worshipping no one but Allah, and how dubious the position of the others is in this respect.

116.text:
They say, "Allah has offspring." Glory be to Him! In fact, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, all are subject to His Will. The claim is set down first and left with those who make it, and the word for offspring is the one used for a child of any kind, so the sentence covers the Jews and the Christians and the pagans in one accusation. Glory be to Him! is the immediate answer, and the form of it is a declaration of purity rather than an argument, so the reader is turned from the claim to the one it is made about. In fact, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth gives the ground of the answer: the one who owns everything that exists cannot be one of two partners in a line, and the phrase covers the whole of creation so that no partner is left outside it. All are subject to His Will closes the sentence on the relation that undoes the claim, since a child is of the same kind as its parent and what is subject is of another, and the verse leaves the reader with the difference between the creator and everything he owns. The verse does not move from the claim back to the people who make it, it goes behind the claim to the relation between the creator and everything else, and in that relation the word offspring has no place at all, since the one who has a child is a man among men. The last clause then keeps every creature in one hand, the Jew and the Christian and the pagan and the one who keeps silent, so the reader is not asked to weigh one community against another but to look at the ground he stands on along with everything else.

**The claim, and who made it.**

And they the Jews and the Christians and those that claim that the angels are God’s daughters say read wa-qālū or simply qālū ‘God has taken to Himself a son’; God says Glory be to Him! as a way of exalting Himself above this; Nay to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants and this sovereignty contradicts having a child and is expressed by the particle mā ‘all that’ in order to include all creation that is not rational; all obey His will submitting to that which is required from each one of them here the emphasis is on rational beings. Allah has begotten a son (children or offspring). Then Allah mentions the claims of the Jews and Christians that Ezra and Jesus are the sons of Allah, saying: (And they) the Jews and Christians (say: Allah hath taken unto Himself a Son) Ezra and the Messiah (Jesus). The Jews, the Christians and the idolaters, who worship others alongside Allah, said that Allah had taken a son. Having refuted the false claims of the Jews, the Christians and the mushrikin, the two verses proceed to demonstrate how and why the Attributes of Perfection are peculiar to Allah Himself and Him alone. Were it at all possible, the situation would necessarily involve either of the two alternative characteristics -- the offspring would belong either to the same genus as the father does, or to a different genus.

**He is far above what they attribute to Him.**

Glory is to Him (Exalted is He above all that they associate with Him). (Be He glorified!) He is far exalted to have a son or partner it is not as they say, (but whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth) of creation (is His) are His servants. He is far above and beyond such a thing, because He has no need of His creation, and no one has a son unless he is needy; and to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He is one in Essence, one in attributes, rid of causes, incomparable with obsequiousness, praised by all expressions, fitting for all allusions, the creator of time and the hours, the determiner of instants and moments. He is a lord without associate or partner, a king without equal or need. Were it at all possible, the situation would necessarily involve either of the two alternative characteristics -- the offspring would belong either to the same genus as the father does, or to a different genus. If it belongs to a different genus, that obviously is a defect, while God should in order to be God, be free of all defects -- as reason itself requires, and as Verse 116 affirms. If the offspring belongs to the same genus, that too is a contradiction in terms, for God has no equal and no existent can belong to the same genus as He does.

**Whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him.**

(Nay, to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth,) meaning, the truth is not as the disbelievers claimed, rather, Allah's is the kingdom of the heavens and earth and whatever and whoever is in, on and between them. Allah is the Supreme Authority in the heavens and earth, and He is the Creator, Provider and Sustainer Who decides all the affairs of the creation as He wills. Firstly, all that exists in heaven or earth belongs to Allah. Rather, to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoted to Him. All created beings are His servants, in submission to Him, glory be to Him! They are His servants and He deals with them as He wills.

**All are subject to His Will.**

This and the following Ayat refute the Christians, may Allah curse them, and their like among the Jews and the Arab idolators, who claimed that the angels are Allah's daughters. (And they say: "The Most Gracious (Allah) has begotten a son (offspring or children)." Indeed you have brought forth (said) a terrible evil thing. Whereby the heavens are almost torn, and the earth is split asunder, and the mountains fall in ruins. That they ascribe a son (or offspring or children) to the Most Gracious (Allah). But it is not suitable for (the majesty of) the Most Gracious (Allah) that He should beget a son (or offspring or children). There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes unto the Most Gracious (Allah) as a servant. Verily, He knows each one of them, and has counted them a full counting. And everyone of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection (without any helper, or protector or defender)(19:88-95), and,. Ibn Jarir said, "Thus the meaning of the Ayat (2:116-117) becomes, 'Allah is far more glorious than to have had a son, for He is the Owner of everything that is in the heavens and earth. Allah stated that He created the heavens and earth out of nothing and without precedent. The commentator al-Baydawi has remarked that, Allah being the First Cause of the things, the earlier Shari'ahs had allowed the use of the title "Father" for Him, but that the ignorant misunderstood and distorted the sense of "Fatherhood" so badly that to entertain such a belief or to apply this title to Allah has now been declared to be an act of infidelity (Kufr). That is to say, the phrase does not signify that Allah actually addressed an existent and commanded it "to be", but it is an allegorical illustration of His omnipotence, suggesting that there is no interval between an act of will on His part and its realization. For, Allah is omniscient, and Divine Knowledge comprehends everything that has been, or is, or will be, so that what does not yet exist according to our reckoning does already exist in Divine Knowledge. (The Badī' (Originator) of the heavens and the earth.) which means, He created them when nothing resembling them existed. (He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have children when He has no wife? He created all things and He is the Knower of everything)(6:101).

117.text:
He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth gives the answer to the claim of the verse before it in the form of a name, and the name chosen is the one for bringing a thing into being without a model or a partner, so the originator stands alone in the sentence exactly as the subject of the earlier claim did not. When He decrees a matter turns from the making of the world to the making of anything at all, and the decrees covers the decision before any word comes out, so the will is placed before the command and not after it. He simply tells it, Be marks how little stands between the decision and the thing, and the word for telling is used of a command rather than of speech in time, so nothing is let in that could be understood as labour or delay. And it is closes the verse with two words that leave no gap, and the brevity is the point, since what is being answered is a claim about descent and offspring and the answer is the ease with which God brings anything he wills into being. The verse therefore answers a false claim with a statement about creation, and the verses around it keep the same contrast between the owner of everything and the things he owns.

**Originator of the heavens and the earth, and what the name carries.**

Creator of the heavens and the earth making them exist without any exemplary precedent; and when He decrees wills a thing to exist He but says to it ‘Be’ and it is that is to say it becomes fa-yakūnu a variant reading has fa-yakūna on account of it being the response in the subjunctive mood to the jussive statement. The Originator al-badīʿ according to the scholars is the One who brings the entity ʿayn into existence without any model lā ʿalā mithāl. (The Badī' (Originator) of the heavens and the earth.) which means, He created them when nothing resembling them existed. (He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have children when He has no wife? He created all things and He is the Knower of everything)(6:101). (The Originator of the heavens and the earth!) He originated them when they were nothing before. Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them; and there is nothing in creation that is like Him.

**What is peculiar to Him alone.**

Having refuted the false claims of the Jews, the Christians and the mushrikin, the two verses proceed to demonstrate how and why the Attributes of Perfection are peculiar to Allah Himself and Him alone. God alone is the Necessary Being (Al-Dhat al-Wajib), and hence necessarily carries within Himself the Attributes of Perfection which are peculiar to Him alone and which cannot exist in any one other than God. Hence, it would be a plain and simple contradiction in terms of claim that anyone other than God can belong to the same genus. Firstly, all that exists in heaven or earth belongs to Allah. Thirdly, He is the Creator and the Inventor of the skies and of the earth. Fourthly, His power of creation is so mighty that when He wishes to do something (for example, wishes to create something), He does not need any instruments or helpers -- all that He does is to say, "Be", and the thing becomes what He wishes it to be.

**When He decrees a matter.**

(When He decrees a matter, He only says to it : "Be! and it is.) thus, demonstrating His perfectly complete ability and tremendous authority; if He decides a matter, He merely orders it to, 'Be' and it comes into existence. (When He decreeth a thing) when He wants to create a child without a father, like Jesus, (He saith unto it only: Be!) be a child without a father, just like Adam was without a father or mother, (And it is). If He decrees and wills something, He only says to it ‘Be’ and it is as He willed it. When He decides on an affair nothing preordained maqdūr can oppose it and nothing created mafṬūr can separate itself from His decree. The commentator al-Baydawi has remarked that, Allah being the First Cause of the things, the earlier Shari'ahs had allowed the use of the title "Father" for Him, but that the ignorant misunderstood and distorted the sense of "Fatherhood" so badly that to entertain such a belief or to apply this title to Allah has now been declared to be an act of infidelity (Kufr).

**Be, and it is.**

Let us begin by saying that it is a mystery -- and we are using the word "mystery", not in the debased and the modern sense, but in the original meaning of the term which implies that certain realities are altogether beyond the reach of human understanding, and that certain other realities cannot and must not, even when partially or wholly understood, be given out to those who have no aptitude for receiving them, and that with regard to them it is advisable "to keep one's lips closed. For, Allah is omniscient, and Divine Knowledge comprehends everything that has been, or is, or will be, so that what does not yet exist according to our reckoning does already exist in Divine Knowledge. (Nay, to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth,) meaning, the truth is not as the disbelievers claimed, rather, Allah's is the kingdom of the heavens and earth and whatever and whoever is in, on and between them. Allah is the Supreme Authority in the heavens and earth, and He is the Creator, Provider and Sustainer Who decides all the affairs of the creation as He wills. Allah stated that He created the heavens and earth out of nothing and without precedent. True, He has prescribed a direction for us to face when we worship, but this is a purely organizational requirement for prayer; it does not mean that God is to be found in only one direction and not in any other.

118.text:
Those who have no knowledge say names the speakers by what they lack rather than by who they are, so the verse puts the demand down before the reader hears it, and the lack is a lack of knowledge and not of information. If only Allah would speak to us or a sign would come to us is the demand, and it is put as a wish, so what is asked for is a private word from God or a wonder of their own choosing, and either way the demand sets the terms on which they will believe. The same was said by those who came before takes the demand out of its moment and shows it to be the oldest objection there is, so the people addressed are not being answered as a new case but are being shown their own likeness in an old mirror. Their hearts are all alike, Indeed gives the reason for the likeness: the hearts are one in kind, so the same demand grows out of the same ground in every generation, and the words are joined by Indeed to the verse's own confirmation. We have made the signs clear for people of sure faith answers the demand by pointing to what is already there, and the signs are described as made clear for a particular kind of people, so what is lacking is not the signs but the faith that reads them. The verse does not answer the demand with a wonder of its own, it points back to signs already given, and the phrase people of sure faith is what marks the difference, since the signs are made clear for those who come to them with a heart that is ready to receive, so the fault is placed in the reader and not in the message. The likeness between the first demand and the last one is also the lesson of the passage, since a demand that has been made in every age cannot be the mark of a new proof but only of the same want read in new words.

**The demand, and those who make it.**

And they that is the disbelievers of Makkah who do not know say to the Prophet s ‘Why does God not speak to us? to say that you are His Messenger; Why does a sign not come to us?’ of the sort we have requested in order to show your sincerity. To begin with, they insisted that Allah Himself should speak to them, either directly as He speaks to the angels, or through the angels as He speaks to the prophets, and that He should Himself proclaim his injunctions to them so as to make the intervention of a new prophet unnecessary, or should at least announce that He had sent Sayyidna Muhammad as a prophet, thus making it easy for them to have faith in him and to follow his guidance. The first of these demands was, on the face of it, silly enough, for, with all the grossness of their minds and hearts, they had the audacity to place themselves on the level of angels and prophets. Those without knowledge from among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters asked, in their stubbornness against the truth, why Allah did not speak to them directly, or why a miracle was not sent for them to see. (And those who have no knowledge) who do not know the Oneness of Allah, i.e. the Jews (say: Why doth not Allah speak unto us) directly, (or some sign come unto us) a sign confirming the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ; for then, we would surely believe? And they who do not know say Why does God not speak to usḍ; Why does a sign not come to usḍ So spoke those before them the like of what they say; their hearts are much alike.

**The same was said by those who came before.**

So in the same way that these disbelievers have spoken spoke those before them from among past communities to their prophets the like of what they say in their obstinacy and demand for signs; their hearts are much alike in terms of unbelief and stubbornness this is meant as consolation for the Prophet s. The Jews and the Christians were the People of the Book", and some of them were men of learning, and yet Allah calls them ignorant. " So said the people before them words of similar import. (So said the people before them words of similar import.) He said, "These are the Jews and the Christians." (And when there comes to them a sign (from Allah) they say: "We shall not believe until we receive the like of that which the Messengers of Allah had received." Allah knows best with whom to place His Message. Humiliation and disgrace from Allah and a severe torment will overtake the criminals (polytheists and sinners) for that which they used to plot.)(6:124) and. (And those who expect not a meeting with Us (i. e. those who deny the Day of Resurrection and the life of the Hereafter) said: "Why are not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?")(25:21) and,. Disbelieving communities said similar things to their prophets in the past: their hearts are all similar, because all disbelievers are the same, even if they are from different times and places. (Even thus, as they now speak, spoke) similar words (those before them) their forefathers. A human being, for instance, cannot be in two places at the same time, and, in consequence, people think that God is also to be found only in some particular place.

**Their hearts are all alike.**

Then, the verse traces the origin of this demand to a distortion of the heart, in respect of which all the ignorant people, past or present, are alike, hence the parrot-like repetition of the same demand throughout the ages. (Their hearts are alike.) means, the hearts of the Arab idolators are just like the hearts of those before them, containing disbelief, stubbornness and injustice. As for those whose hearts and hearing Allah has stamped and whose eyes have been sealed, Allah described them: As for those who are not in search of the truth, but enjoy being stuck in their malice and obstinacy, there is no help for them. The reason is that although Allah had sent such a large number of clear signs and definite proofs to establish the prophethood of Sayyidna Muhammad .i" , yet they persisted in their denial. But only those who have needs beget sons, and God is above all such imperfections and limitations.

**The signs made clear for people of sure faith.**

Yet We have made clear the signs to a people who are certain a people who know that these are God’s signs and so they believe in them for to request other signs would be obduracy. (We have indeed made plain the signs for people who believe with certainty.) meaning, We made the arguments clear, prooving the truth of the Messengers, with no need of more questions or proofs for those who believe, follow the Messengers and comprehend what Allah sent them with. But in answer to the other demand, Allah reminds them that He has sent, not one, but a number of clear signs and proofs to confirm and establish the prophethood of Sayyidna Muhammad . But these signs and proofs can be of help only to those who sincerely wish to know the truth and to attain certitude. Allah makes His signs clear to those who are certain of the truth when it appears to them, not doubting or resisting it. (We have made clear the revelations) the signs: the commands, prohibitions and your traits in the Torah (for people who are sure) who believe. Included in the signs which He made manifest were that which removes the defect of anything other [than Him] al-ʿilla min al-aghyār and quenches the thirst from things that are better al-ghulla min al-akhyār.

119.text:
The verse answers the sadness that the passage before it had left open, and it does so by turning the attention of the one who carries the message away from the response of those who hear him and back to the task he was given. We have surely sent you with the truth, O Prophet, as a deliverer of good news and a warner. The sending is named first, and with it the truth he was sent with, so that the message is described as something entrusted and carried rather than something a man produced, and the emphatic opening states the sending as a settled fact that no refusal on the part of the hearers can undo. The address O Prophet stands in the middle of the sentence and marks it as a word spoken to him personally, at a point where he had reason to be grieved by what the passage before had said of the people he was sent to. The two descriptions that follow are given as a pair. He is a deliverer of good news, and the good news comes first, and he is a warner, and the warning comes second, so the verse opens its account of his work on the gentler of the two and does not begin with threat. Read together, the two names describe a function and not a result. They say what he does, which is to carry the message and to set out plainly both the promise and the warning, and they do not promise that everyone he speaks to will accept. That distinction is the hinge of the verse. Then And you will not be accountable for the residents of the Hellfire removes from him a weight that the earlier passage could easily have laid on him. He is not being asked to answer for the inner state of people who have decided against the message, and he is not being asked to explain why they refused or to answer for them on any day. The last word of the verse is the name of the fire that is kept for those who persist, and it closes the sentence on the fate he is not responsible for rather than on his own sorrow. The reader is left with a Prophet told to keep going and told that the accounting belongs elsewhere, which is the same consolation the earlier verses had prepared by describing people who broke their pledges and turned away.

**What the sending with the truth means.**

The truth named here is given a content by the sources rather than left as a general quality. One reading takes it as the guidance itself, so that the truth sent with him is the direction a life is meant to take and not merely a claim to be believed. Another takes it as the Qur'an together with the declaration that Allah is one, so that what he carries is the same claim about God that the earlier scriptures announced, stated plainly. A third calls it the religion of truth and attaches to it that there is no doubt in it, which puts the doubt on the side of the hearers and not on the side of the message. The run of verses before this one had been listing errors, and this verse sets the truth he carries against them, the likening of God to man, the notion that He is present in one place rather than another, and the attribution of a son to Him. On that reading the direction prescribed for worship is an organizational requirement for prayer and not a statement that God is confined to one quarter, and the beliefs the passage rejects are called man's own invention, since God is complete in Himself and above the needs and limitations that would make such things thinkable. The sending with the truth is therefore the correction of all of it at once, and the verse follows immediately on the report that those who persisted in denial did so out of sheer malice and ignorance, so that the truth is stated at the head of the verse and the consolation at its end, and the two belong together.

**Who the good news and the warning are for.**

The pair names two works and the sources specify both. The good news is explained as Paradise for those who believe in what he brought and respond to the guidance, and the warning as the fire for those who disbelieve in what he brought and do not respond to it. The order in the verse puts the good news first, and the descriptions are given in that order each time they are set out. The same source adds that the Prophet is described in the Tawrah with the same characteristics with which he is described in the Qur'an, as a witness, a bringer of good news, a warner, and a safe refuge for the unlettered people, named there as the servant and messenger who depends and relies on Allah, who is not harsh, not hard, and not obnoxious in the bazaars, and who does not reward an evil deed with an evil deed but forgives and pardons. The account of that description reaches us through ʿAṭāʾ bin Yasār, who asked ʿAbdullāh bin ʿAmr bin al-ʿĀṣ to tell him about it, and what he was told is what Imām Aḥmad recorded, and al-Bukhārī recorded it alone. The same description carries that Allah would not bring his life to an end until the religion of the wicked was set straight by his hands, so that people would proclaim that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and that by his hands blind eyes, deaf ears and sealed hearts would be opened. The verse's own two names for him are thus the two names the earlier book had already used.

**The two responses the verse divides people into.**

A spiritual reading of the verse takes the sending as a distinction given to this Prophet, singled out with qualities that were not made to appear in anyone else, so that all people stand under his banner. In that reading the acceptance and the refusal become the two halves of a single division, and the division is stated from his side. Those who are accepted are the ones in conformity with him, and those who are rejected are the ones who oppose him. The same reading draws its comfort out of the last clause, that he will not be questioned about the states of others and that he will not be turned away because of anyone. The verse therefore separates what belongs to the messenger from what belongs to those who hear him, and it leaves the separation where the sources leave it, with the response belonging to the one who responds.

**Why he will not be accountable for the residents of the Hellfire.**

The clause is explained as a removal of responsibility for the disbelief of those who rejected him, and the same idea is supported from elsewhere in the Qur'an. In one cross-reference his duty is only to convey the message and the reckoning is with Allah. In another he is told to remind, and told that he is only one who reminds and not a dictator over them. In a third, Allah knows best what they say, he is not the one to force them to belief, and the instruction is to warn by the Qur'an the one who fears the threat. The point in all three is that the messenger delivers and does not compel, and that the outcome is not his to produce. The reason the assurance is given at this point is that the thought of a people being incorrigible was likely to make him sad on their account, and the verse states that he will not be held responsible or taken to account for those who willingly pursue the way to Hell. All that he is required to do is to keep performing his own function and not to worry about who accepts the truth and who does not. One concise reading puts the same thing in a sentence, that the Prophet only had to deliver the message clearly, and that Allah will not ask him about those people in the fire who did not believe in him.

**The reading that makes the sentence an instruction not to ask.**

The last clause is read by the sources in a second way, and the difference turns on how the verb is pronounced. In the reading followed in the standard text it is a statement, that he will not be asked. In the other reading the verb is an imperative and the clause becomes an instruction, do not ask, which one source spells out as a prohibition with the final vowel dropped because the form is a command. Both readings are carried and neither is treated as cancelling the other. Under the second, the meaning given is that it is not fitting for him to ask about the dwellers of hell, and it is also given as meaning that he should not ask for their forgiveness. That second reading is the one the reports of the occasion attach to, and the sources are careful to say so, which is why a report about a question the Prophet once asked belongs with the imperative reading and not with the statement.

**What the reports of the occasion carry.**

Two reports are carried on the occasion of this verse, and both are tied by the source that carries them to the imperative reading. From Ibn ʿAbbās comes a report that the Prophet once said he wished he knew what had become of his parents, and that the verse was sent down as an answer to that. From Muqātil comes a report that he said the Jews would have believed if Allah had sent His harm upon them, and that the verse was sent down in response to that. Both reports explain why the clause is read as an instruction, since on that reading the verse answers a question directly, and both are given in that setting. They are occasions and not rulings. What the verse itself settles is what the messenger is and is not answerable for. It does not settle the state of anyone who died before the message reached him, and the sources here do not put that question to this verse in this place, which is why the commentary leaves it where they leave it and does not answer more than the wording asks.

120.text:
Never will the Jews or Christians be pleased with you is put as a statement about them rather than about the Prophet, so the reader hears what the two communities will accept before he hears what is asked of him. The next phrase, until you follow their faith, Say, Allah's guidance is the only true guidance, keeps the two parts together, and the answer to the condition is placed in the mouth of the Prophet, so the refusal is met with a plain word rather than with a step back. The word guidance is repeated inside that word, and the repetition is what gives it force, since the only guidance is named as God's and everything else is left outside it. And if you were to follow their desires after all the knowledge that has come to you then turns the sentence to the Prophet himself, and the turn is a warning that does not wait for the deed: the knowledge is named as already come, so the danger is not ignorance but the size of what has been received. The word desires is chosen in that clause rather than faith, and the choice is deliberate, so the two communities are described by what they want rather than by what they hold, and the ground of the warning is that a want can be followed while the knowledge is kept. Then comes the closing, there would be none to protect or help you against Allah, and both words are negated, so no protector and no helper is left in any quarter, and the reader is put alone with God exactly where he may wish to keep a friend among the others. The verse therefore names the price of pleasing people, and it names the price to the Prophet himself, so the warning reaches everyone who reads after him.

**The two communities, and what would please them.**

(And Jews) The Jews of Medina (will not be pleased with thee, nor will Christians) the Christians of Najran, (till thou follow their creed) their religion and direction of prayer. Never will the Jews be pleased with you neither the Christians not until you follow their creed their religion Say ‘God’s guidance that is Islam is the true guidance’ besides which there is only error. Allah addresses and warns His Prophet, telling him that the Jews and the Christians will never be happy with him unless he leaves Islam and follows what they do; and that if he, or one of his followers, were to do such a thing, after the clear truth has come to them, they would not find protection or help from Allah. This is because the Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najran were in the hope that the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, will remain praying to their qiblah.

**The guidance that is God's alone.**

(Say: "Verily, the guidance of Allah (i.e. Islamic Monotheism) that is the (only) guidance") means, 'Say, O Muhammad , the guidance of Allah that He sent me with is the true guidance, meaning the straight, perfect and comprehensive religion.'" Qatadah said that Allah's statement,. (Lo! The guidance of Allah is Guidance) the Religion of Allah is Islam and Allah's direction of prayer is the Ka'bah. (Say: "Verily, the guidance of Allah (i.e. Islamic Monotheism) that is the (only) guidance) is, "A true argument that Allah taught Muhammad and his Companions and which they used against the people of misguidance. True religion can be accepted only by those who are alive to their own true, human natures unlike those who, having suppressed their own true natures, have forsaken natural religion for artificial dogmas. Other verses of the Holy Qur'an, of course, definitely establish the fact that Allah is pleased and will always remain pleased with the Holy Prophet and thus he can never be the object of divine wrath. ’ Such people themselves can think only in worldly terms, so they expect God’s messenger to come up to their materialistic standards. When Allah directed him to pray toward the Ka'bah, they were disappointed and despaired of him ever following their religion.

**After the knowledge has come.**

And if you (O Muhammad) were to follow their (Jews and Christians) desires after what you have received of Knowledge (i.e. the Qur'an), then you would have against Allah neither any Wali (protector or guardian) nor any helper Those to whom we gave the Book recite it as it should be recited (Yatlunahu Haqqa Tilawatihi) they are the ones who believe therein. (And if you (O Muhammad) were to follow their (Jews and Christians) desires after what you have received of Knowledge (i.e. the Qur'an), then you would have against Allah neither any Wali (protector or guardian) nor any helper.) It is on account of the present distorted state of the earlier religions, and specially because of their having been abrogated by Divine Commandment that Verse 120 equates them with Ahwa' (the plural of Hawa) -- that is to say, personal desires, or individual opinions and baseless conjectures. (And if thou shouldst follow their desires) their religion and direction of prayer (after the knowledge which hath come unto thee) that the Religion of Allah is Islam and His direction of prayer is the Ka'bah, (then wouldst thou have from Allah) from His chastisement (no protecting friend) no one to benefit you (nor helper) to save you from this chastisement. Call your community to free them selves from them and their path and be for Us through Us free of anyone other than Us trusting in Our help for you are through Us and from Us.

**The warning against following their way.**

This Ayah carries a stern warning for the Muslim Ummah against imitating the ways and methods of the Jews and Christians, after they have acquired knowledge of the Qur'an and Sunnah, may Allah grant us refuge from this behavior. Now, supposing just for the sake of supposing that he should accept their fancies in spite of having received the Truth from Allah through revelation, the verse informs him that in such a case he would find no helper to save him from divine wrath. Should they affect a more friendly stance towards the Holy Prophet g , Allah asks him to say to them in plain and simple words that the only guidance worth the name is that which comes from Allah -- and He has already made it clear enough that Islam is now the only form of "guidance" acceptable to Him. And if you were wa-la-in the lām is for oaths to follow their whims hypothetically speaking whims to which they are calling you after the knowledge the Divine revelation that has come to you you shall have against God neither friend to protect you nor helper to defend you against Him. Since the deniers are not willing to extricate themselves from their desires and fancies, it is not possible to please them without accepting their opinions -- a thing which a Messenger of Allah can never do.

**Following their whims, and what it costs.**

In this verse, Allah informs him that their denial is not due to lack of convincing arguments and proofs, but is motivated by pride and self-satisfaction, for each of the two groups -- namely, the Jews and the Christians -- believes its own religion to be the only genuine religion, and there is no likelihood of pleasing either of them until and unless the Holy Prophet accepts their religion. Since divine wrath necessarily follows upon the acceptance of baseless fancies, it is logically impossible for him to follow the opinions of the Jews and the Christians, as divine pleasure and divine wrath cannot be combined with each other. This makes clear the seriousness of leaving the truth and of following people of falsehood. They used to ask the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, for truce, giving him the impression that if he were to accord them truce and respite they will follow him and believe in him. Know that their reliance on what they find pleasing is the cause of endless wretchedness.

121.text:
Those We have given the Book follow it as it should be followed opens on the people who were given the Scripture before, and the giving is named first, so the following is heard as an answer to a gift. The clause follow it as it should be followed puts the standard inside the book itself: the recitation is measured by what the book asks of the one who reads it, and the sources take that to mean keeping it, understanding it and holding to what it commands rather than running over its words. It is they who truly believe in it then joins the two acts, since the belief is named as the fruit of the following, and the pronoun ties the belief to the same book, so the verse describes a faith that is proved by what it does. As for those who reject it turns the sentence to the other side, and the rejection is set against the following, so the two groups are drawn by what they do with one book and not by who they are. Then comes the closing, it is they who are the losers, and the word used is the one for loss in a bargain, so the verse ends by naming what the rejection costs rather than what it deserves, and the reader is left to weigh the two ends himself. The verse also keeps the two sides in one sentence, so the following and the rejecting are read as answers to one gift, and no reader can hear it as a claim about descent.

**Following the Book as it should be followed.**

Those to whom We have given the Scripture this is the subject of the sentence and who recite it with true recitation that is who recite it as it was revealed haqqa tilāwatihi ‘its true recitation’ is a circumstantial qualifier; haqqa is in the accusative because it is the object of the verbal noun they believe in it this is the predicate this was revealed concerning a group of Ethiopians that presented themselves to the Prophet and accepted Islam; and whoever disbelieves in it that is in the revealed Book by distorting it they shall be the losers because they will be destined for the Fire made everlasting for them. (Those to whom We gave the Scripture (i. e. the Tawrah and the Injil) before it, they believe in it (the Qur'an). And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believe in it. Verily, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed even before it we have been from those who submit themselves to Allah in Islam as Muslims. These will be given their reward twice over, because they are patient, and repel evil with good, and spend (in charity) out of what We have provided them.)(28:52-54) and,. That is to say, they have distorted neither the words nor the meanings, nor have they tried to misinterpret or conceal the prophecies about the coming of the Holy Prophet . In other words, they have used their intellect in trying to understand the meanings, and their will in accepting the truth and in following it.

**The rightful due of recitation.**

The rightful due of recitation is that you recite the Qur'an with burning, need, limpidness of heart, and pure belief, with a remembering tongue, a believing heart, and a limpid spirit-the tongue in remembrance, the heart in grief, the spirit with love; the tongue with loyalty, the heart with limpid ness, the spirit with shame; the tongue in the work, the heart in the mystery, and the spirit in joy. As for reading the Book "observing the rights of its recitation", it means enunciating each word correctly and clearly, and keeping the fear and love of Allah present in one's heart while reading, and also the resolve to follow divine guid-nce and to obey divine commandments. (Those unto whom We have given the Scripture) given knowledge of the Scripture, i.e. the Torah, (who read it with the right reading) describe it as it is and do not alter it: expositing what is lawful and unlawful, its commands and prohibitions to whomever asks them, and they further act according to what is clear and unambiguous and believe in that which is ambiguous therein, (those believe in it) in Muhammad and the Qur'an. The Pir of the Tariqah said, "In the remembrance the servant reaches a place where the tongue reaches the heart, the heart reaches the spirit, the spirit reaches the secret core, and the secret core reaches the Light.

**Who believes, and who loses.**

(And who disbelieveth in it) in Muhammad and the Qur'an, (those are they who are losers) who are duped in that they lose both this world and the world to come. As for those who persist in their denial, they are bound to suffer the greatest loss, for they have refused to believe in the Last Revelation, and have, in fact, not shown much of a belief in their own Books, and not followed the guidance provided by them in this matter. 33. Another group sticks to its disbelief, and for them is loss. These Ayat mean, "Those among the People of the Book who perfectly adhered to the Books that were revealed to the previous Prophets, will believe in what I have sent you with, O Muhammad! In doing so, they are actually affirming their own Books too and acting upon them insofar as their Books explicitly foretell the coming of the Last Prophet and of the last Book of Allah. (And say to those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and to those who are illiterates (Arab pagans): "Do you (also) submit yourselves (to Allah in Islam)?" If they do, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the Message; and Allah is the Seer of servants)(3:20).

**Those who were given the Book before.**

Allah then mentioned the believers from among the people of the Book: 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his companions, Bahirah the Monk and the Negus and his followers, saying: The Qur’ān mentions a group from the People of the Scripture who know the revealed texts they have been given and follow them properly. (Say (O Muhammad to them): "Believe in it (the Qur'an) or do not believe (in it). Verily, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their faces in humble prostration. And they say: "Glory be to our Lord! Truly, the promise of our Lord must be fulfilled.")(17:107-108). But other commentators believe that "those to whom We have given the Book" are the blessed Companions, and "the Book" is the Holy Qur'an. The heart says to the tongue, 'Silence!' The spirit says to the heart, 'Silence!' The secret core says to the spirit, 'Silence!' God says to the traveler, 'My servant, you have been speaking for a while.

**The prophets, and the truth they carried.**

When they went into decline, however, their religion was reduced to a set of ethnic customs: piety lay in belonging to their community and impiety in being apart from it. Their minds were moulded in such a manner that they acknowledged only tangible, visible signs of greatness; the invisible, but intensely meaningful signs that God gave His prophets meant nothing to them. The signs of God were reflected in the lives and teachings of His prophets; indeed, the prophets’ words and deeds, based as they were on truth, were manifestations of God’s signs. All those whom God has sent to preach truth on earth have been confronted with the same kind of reaction. How, people think, could a great God, whose kingdom encompasses everything, starting with the earth and going to the furthest expanse of the heavens, have chosen such an ordinary person as His messenger?

122.text:
O Children of Israel is the address that opens this verse and the passage it belongs to, and it names the people by their ancestor, so what follows is spoken to a family and not to a party. The word used is the one for the descendants of Jacob, and the sources keep that sense, so the address reaches every generation of them and not only the ones who stood at the mountain. Remember My favours upon you and how I honoured you above the others is the charge the verse is built on, and the verb there is the one for calling something back to mind, so the favours are treated as things already given that need only to be recalled. The favours are ascribed to God alone, and that is the point of the sentence: the reader is asked to see his own history as a gift and not as an achievement. And how I honoured you above the others closes the verse by naming the honour that was given to them over the peoples of their time, and the sources are careful to say what that honour was, which is the guidance sent among them rather than any privilege of blood. The verse therefore repeats an address that came earlier in the chapter, and the repetition is a reminder of how much has been given, which is also the ground of the warning that follows it.

**The favours they were told to remember.**

O Children of Israel remember My favour wherewith I favoured you and that I have preferred you over all the worlds a similar verse has already been mentioned. (O Children of Israel!) O Children of Jacob (Remember) recollect (My favour wherewith I favoured you) favoured your forefathers by delivering them from Pharaoh and his people as well as by the blessings and bounties that I favoured them with (and how I preferred you) with Islam (to the worlds) the people of your time. Remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the nations) And fear the Day (of Judgement) when no person shall avail another, nor shall compensation be accepted from him, nor shall intercession be of use to him, nor shall they be helped. O Israelites, remember the blessings, sacred and worldly, which I gave to you, and remember that I favoured you over those of your time with prophethood and authority.

**The children of Israel addressed by name.**

The Children of Israel were selected by God to perform a very special task: they were to call other nations to turn to God, impressing on them the fact that they were answerable to their Lord for their actions. Envy should not incite them to oppose or deny the Prophet or refrain from following him, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him until the Day of Judgment. His way sunna in His address to the people of Moses is to call them by their proper name saying O children of Israel remember... that is O children of Jacob. Allah then mentions His favour upon the Children of Israel, saying:

**A reminder repeated so that the point sinks in.**

Allah warned them against concealing this information, which is among the favors that Allah granted them. On the one hand, it encourages the Israelites to come back to the Straight Path by reminding them of the blessings which Allah has bestowed on them; on the other hand, it warns them of the consequences of their lapses by depicting the Day of Judgment. In the art of writing and speaking, it is considered to be one of the most effective means of carrying conviction that, before starting on a long analytical discussion of a subject, one should define the basic ideas very briefly and clearly which are always helpful in comprehending the details and the particularities, and that, in concluding the argument, one should repeat these ideas by way of a summary. The purpose of repeating the statement at the end of the discussion is to make the two ideas sink deep into their minds.

**The people and the prophet sent to them.**

The rule that applied to Abraham applies to every generation: only those who prove themselves worthy will be granted a share in God’s covenant; those who do not will meet the same fate as any other offenders in God’s sight, regardless of the nation to which they belong. The coming of the Arab prophet signified the replacement of the Children of Israel by the Children of Ishmael as God’s chosen people: it was they who were chosen to carry on the task of communicating God’s word to other nations of the world. We mentioned a similar Ayah at the beginning of this Surah, and it is mentioned here to emphisize the importance of following the Ummi Prophet and Messenger, who is described for the People of the Scriptures in their Books by his characteristics, name, the good news about him and the description of his Ummah. A large section of this Sarah, ending with the previous verse, has been dealing with different aspects of the conduct of the Israelites (that is, the Jews) in the course of their history.

123.text:
And guard yourselves against the Day when no soul will be of any help to another puts the warning in the plural and names the day before it names what happens in it, so the reader is told to protect himself first and hears afterwards what he is protecting himself from. The words for help and soul are set against each other in that clause, so the closest relation a person has is the one that gives way there, and a soul is named rather than a body because what is at stake is what the soul carries. No ransom will be taken names the price that a person would wish to pay, and the sentence denies it before anyone has asked, so the door of bargaining is shut in advance. Then no intercession accepted closes the second door, since even a plea from someone else is refused, and the sources keep the point that the intercession which will be granted on that day is granted by God's leave, so what is refused here is refused to those who come with nothing of their own. And no help will be given ends the sentence with the plainest of the three, since help is what remains when a ransom cannot be paid and no one may plead, and the verse takes that away too. The three denials are put in one order that leaves nothing in the hand of the reader, and the address is to the believers, so the warning is given to those who already believe.

**The day when no soul will help another.**

(And guard against a day) fear the torment of a day, i.e. the Day of Judgement (when no soul will in anything avail another) no unbelieving soul will be able to drive away anything from another unbelieving soul; it is also said that this means: no righteous soul will be able to drive away anything from another righteous soul; and it is said that this means: no father will be able to drive away anything from his son and no son will be able to drive away Allah's punishment from his father, (nor will compensation be accepted from it) no ransom will be accepted, (nor will intercession be of use to it) no intercessor will intercede for it: not a close angel, a sent messenger or a righteous servant; (nor will they be helped) will be prevented from what they will face. Protect yourself from the torment of the Day of Return by following the instructions of Allah and keeping away from what He has prohibited, because on that day no soul will be able to help another soul in any way; no ransom will be accepted for it, no matter how great; and no one pleading on its behalf will benefit it, no matter how high their position. And beware of fear a day when no soul shall for another on this Day be requited that is when no soul for another shall be of any avail and no compensation no ransom shall be accepted from it nor any intercession shall benefit it neither shall they be helped against God’s chastisement.

**The day when no payment will be accepted.**

And beware of a day when no soul will be requited for another and no compensation will be accepted from it nor will any intercession benefit it neither will they be helped. As for the enemies nothing [that is no payment or compensation] will be accepted from them. Everyone on that day will be saying My soul my soul but our Prophet will say My community my community. On that day, a soul will have no helper other than Allah. There, God’s justice will apply to one and all equally, for no ethnic group holds a monopoly over the next world. The intercession of intercessors will not benefit the disbeliever for this is a determination made for each community with their prophet. As for the believers they will benefit in particular from the Prophet's intercession. As for the friends [the Prophet] said Protect yourself from the fire even if it be by half a date [given in charity].

**The statement repeated at the end of the passage.**

This account had begun with the statement which has been repeated at the end in these two verses. The statement is of a general and principal kind, and the verses which come in between the beginning and the end are, so to say, a detailed demonstration of the statement. The repetition of the introductory statement here is of this very nature. God sent innumerable prophets from amongst them to help and guide them in the performance of this task—Abraham, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, David, Solomon, Zachariah, John the Baptist and Jesus, to name just a few. The Children of Israel were selected by God to perform a very special task: they were to call other nations to turn to God, impressing on them the fact that they were answerable to their Lord for their actions.

**The duty laid on them, and the warning given.**

One who is willing to make soul-searing sacrifices for God’s cause shows his utmost dedication to it: it is only just and natural, then, that he should become the leader of his people. In this world one person is able to bear the burden of another; sometimes intercession is accepted; sometimes one can free oneself by giving compensation; sometimes a helper is at hand to see one through a difficult situation. For, what is aimed at in a discussion is the affirmation of certain basic and general principles -- being succinct, they are easily kept alive in the mind, and, being comprehensive and readily applicable to particular situations, they make it easy for one to remember the details too. On the one hand, it encourages the Israelites to come back to the Straight Path by reminding them of the blessings which Allah has bestowed on them; on the other hand, it warns them of the consequences of their lapses by depicting the Day of Judgment. In the next world, however, none of these mitigating factors will be allowed to come into play. Allah warned them against concealing this information, which is among the favors that Allah granted them. Envy should not incite them to oppose or deny the Prophet or refrain from following him, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him until the Day of Judgment. We mentioned a similar Ayah at the beginning of this Surah, and it is mentioned here to emphisize the importance of following the Ummi Prophet and Messenger, who is described for the People of the Scriptures in their Books by his characteristics, name, the good news about him and the description of his Ummah. Remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the nations) And fear the Day (of Judgement) when no person shall avail another, nor shall compensation be accepted from him, nor shall intercession be of use to him, nor shall they be helped. Allah also commanded them to remember their daily life and their religious affairs and how He blessed them. They should not envy their cousins, the Arabs, for what Allah has given them, the Final Messenger of Allah being an Arab.

124.text:
Remember when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commandments opens the account with a command to recall, so what follows is put in the memory of the reader rather than in a story told for its own sake, and the testing is ascribed to the Lord who chose him, so the trial is read as a mark of nearness and not of rejection. The word for the testing is the one used for a thorough trial, and the sources take the commandments to be the duties and laws that were laid on him, which is why the verse names them as things given rather than as things asked. The next phrase, which he fulfilled, Allah said, is the turn of the sentence, since the fulfilment is named first and only then does the answer come, so the promise that follows is shown to rest on what had been done. I will certainly make you into a role model for the people, Abraham asked names the rank that was given, and the word is the one for a leader who is followed, while the promise is put in the future with an oath, so the rank is pledged before it is given and Abraham hears of it while he is still being tried. What about my offspring, Allah replied is the question that follows, and the sources note that Abraham asked it after the promise out of care for his family and not out of doubt about the promise, and the asking is kept in the verse because it is the ground of the answer that closes it. My covenant is not extended to the wrongdoers ends the account by naming the limit of the pledge: the covenant is honoured and it is not inherited, and the answer puts the wrongdoers outside it, so the reader is told that a line of descent counts for nothing where the conduct is wrong. The verse therefore turns a gift into an obligation, and it does so in the order of the account itself rather than in a sentence of its own. The passage also keeps the promise and the limit in one answer, so the reader is taught that what God pledges he keeps, and that the pledge is not a licence for the line it runs through.

**The words of the test, and what they were.**

(with Kalimāt (words) which means, "Laws, commandments and prohibitions." 'Words' as mentioned here, sometimes refers to what Allah has willed, such as Allah's statement about Maryam,. Muhammad bin Ishaq reportd that Ibn 'Abbas said, "The words that Allah tested Ibrahim with, and that he implemented were: abandoning his (disbelieving) people when Allah commanded him to do so, disputing with Nimrod (king of Babylon) about Allah, being patient when he was thrown in the fire (although this was extremely traumatic) migrating from his homeland when Allah commanded him to do so, patience with the monetary and material demands of hosting guests by Allah's command, and Allah's order for him to slaughter his son. In addition to those rigorous trials, a number of other restrictions were imposed on him in the shape of certain injunctions, which too, he fulfilled as devotionally. Ten of these commandments are known as the characteristics of the Fitrah and are concerned with the cleanliness and purification of the body.

**What the Friend of Allah was asked to give up.**

Unflinchingly he obeyed the divine command, and, with the courage and determination of the prophet that he was, he set out to wage a war against idol-worship and to call them to the unalloyed worship of the One God. This obviously drew upon him the ire of his people and of their king Namrud (Nimrod), who finally decided to burn him alive in a blazing fire. The second trial was that Sayyidna Ibrahim was asked to leave his homeland and to migrate to Syria along with his family. "The Friend of Allah" had so annihilated his own will and desire, and was so anxious to obey his Lord that he did not allow even a moment to lapse between the command and its execution, and started on his journey without informing his wife. Now, the father received the command to slaughter his son with his own hand. In recompense for this total submission to divine will, Allah sent down a ram from heaven to be sacrificed in place of Sayyidna Isma'il . He tried him with the sacrifice of the son, and he was patient in that and did not fall short.

**The leader the people were to follow.**

He (Allah) said (to him), "Verily, I am going to make you an Imam (a leader) for mankind (to follow you). ("Verily, I am going to make you an Imam (a leader) for mankind (to follow you).") as a reward for Ibrahim's good deeds, adhering to the commandments and avoiding the prohibitions. This is why Allah made Ibrahim a role model for the people, and an Imam whose conduct and path are imitated and followed. " The Arabic word imam which we have not translated here, lexically signifies "leader or chief or guide. " Since the present verse is related to Sayyidna Ibrahim the word 'Imam in this context means, above all, "a prophet", though it includes the general sense of "leadership", too, as also of the title "Patriarch" which the Jews and Christians have given to him. This verse gives a resume of the thirty qualities in the two words, Sabr (patience) and Yagin (sure faith, or certitude) - the second refers to the perfection of knowledge, and the first to the perfection of actual practice. Allah told His prophet Abraham that He would make his manners and behaviour an example for people to follow. And mention when his Lord tested tried Abraham Ibrāhīm also read Ibrāhām with certain words with certain commands and prohibitions with which He charged him it is said that these included the rituals of the Pilgrimage the rinsing of the mouth snuffing up water into the nostrils to clean them cleaning of the teeth trimming facial hair combing of the hair trimming the fingernails shaving armpit and pubic hair circumcision and washing one’s private parts after elimination; and he fulfilled them he performed them thoroughly; He God exalted said to him ‘I make you a leader an exemplar in religion for the people.

**The offspring, and the covenant that does not reach the wrongdoers.**

" (Allah) said, "My covenant (prophethood) includes not Zalimin (polytheists and wrongdoers). When Allah made Ibrahim an Imam (Leader for the faithful), he asked Allah that Imams thereafter be chosen from his offspring. Allah accepted his supplication, but told him that there will be unjust people among his offspring and they will not benefit from Allah's promise. Allah mentioned that there are unjust people among the offspring of Ibrahim, and they will not benefit from Allah's promise, nor would they be entrusted with anything, even though they are among the children of Allah's Khalil (intimate friend, Prophet Abraham). There will also be those who do good among the children of Ibrahim, and these it is who will benefit from Ibrahim's supplication. Also, Ibn Khuwayz Mindad Al-Maliki said, "The unjust person does not qualify to be a Khalifah, a ruler, one who gives religious verdicts, a witness, or even a narrator (of Hadiths)." The last question pertains to the law which lays down that the station of a guide and leader would not be granted to the unjust and the disobedient. Allah (said: My covenant) with you and My promise to you and the honour and mercy I bestowed upon you (includeth not wrong-doers) from among your offspring; it is also said that this means: My covenant will not include the wrong-doers in the Hereafter but it will include them in this life. Allah replied by saying that His promise to him of sacred leadership would not extend to the wrongdoers among his descendants. ’ Said he ‘And of my seed?’ my progeny make leaders from among them; He said ‘My covenant of leadership shall not reach the evildoers’ the disbelievers from among them this indicates that the covenant will reach only those who are not evildoers.

**The religion that Abraham followed, and the claim made about him.**

Remind the idolators and the People of the Scriptures, who pretend to be followers of the religion of Ibrahim, while in reality they do not follow it, while you, O Muhammad, and your followers are the true followers of his religion; remind them of the commands and prohibitions that Allah tested Ibrahim with. (Verily, Ibrahim was an Ummah (or a nation), obedient to Allah, Hanif (i.e. to worship none but Allah), and he was not one of those who were Al-Mushrikin (polytheists), (He was) thankful for His (Allah's) favors. He (Allah) chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and in the Hereafter he shall be of the righteous. Then, We have sent the revelation to you (O Muhammad saying): "Follow the religion of Ibrahim Hanif (Islamic Monotheism to worship none but Allah) and he was not of the Mushrikin.)(16:120-123) (Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true Muslim Hanifan (Islamic Monotheism to worship none but Allah alone) and he was not of Al-Mushrikin. Verily, among mankind who have the best claim to Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet (Muhammad) and those who have believed (Muslims). And Allah is the Wali (Protector and Helper) of the believers)(3:67-68). The coming of the Arab prophet signified the replacement of the Children of Israel by the Children of Ishmael as God’s chosen people: it was they who were chosen to carry on the task of communicating God’s word to other nations of the world. In short, all we wish to point out is that the nature of prophethood is a degree of reality which we can understand only partially and that too only with the help of Divine Books, and hence it is not a sphere in which human fantasy may be allowed to roam at its sweet will. Now, Sayyidna Ibrahim rX...JI _L was, even according to the admission of Jews and Christians, a prophet, and not " 1'homme moyen sensuel" which is the subject matter of the novel, of psychology, and, not the least, of the theology of the Dane. (And when his Lord tried Abraham with some words) He commanded him to fulfil ten traits: five in relation to his head and five to his body, (and he fulfilled them) he complied. It is also said that (And when his Lord tried Abraham with some words) means: with every single word he prayed to Allah, (He said) to him:

125.text:
And remember when We made the Sacred House a centre and a sanctuary for the people, saying, opens with the making of the House, and the two names carry the two things the place is for, since a centre is where people keep returning and a sanctuary is where they are safe while they are there. The grant that follows, You may take the standing-place of Abraham as a site of prayer, is put in the form of a gift as much as of a duty, so the spot where Abraham stood is named as a place where prayer is offered and heard, and the sources take the standing-place to be the stone he used while the house was being raised. And We entrusted Abraham and Ishmael to purify My House for those who circle it names the charge that belonged to the two who built it, and the cleansing is of the house itself, so the worship it is meant for can be offered there with no rival set beside God in it.
