The mark of God sibghata’Llāhi a verbal noun reaffirming the earlier āmannā and it is in the accusative because of the verbal construction implied that is to say sabaghanā’Llāhu ‘God has marked us’ this denotes His religion the one towards which He made human beings naturally inclined as it leaves its mark on a person in the same way that a dye leaves its mark on a garment; and who has that is none has a better mark sibghatan ‘marking’ is for specification than God? Verse 138 delineates Islam as the "colouring of Allah", and explains this "colouring" as the unalloyed worship of Allah and total submission to Him. " If we put Verse 135 and 138 together, it becomes clear that essentially Islam - or any authentic religion, for that matter – is the religion of Allah, and that the association of a religion with the name of a prophet can only be symbolised. ((We take our) colour from Allah) i.e. follow the Religion of Allah, (and who is better than Allah at colouring) better than the Religion of Allah. Hold tightly to the religion of Allah which is the natural way of life for you, on the inside and outside. There is no better way of life than the path of Allah, which agrees with our nature, benefiting us in every way and protecting us from evil and corruption. But the immediate allusion is to a certain ceremony of the Christians. If faith is to be of the kind which pleases God, it must be identical with that of the Companions of the Prophet. What was so special about that faith was that it amounted to acceptance of the truth on an abstract level; it was belief in truth for the sake of truth.

**Who is better than Allah in ordaining a way.**

(Allah's Fitrah (i.e. Allah's Islamic Monotheism)(30:30) directs Muslims to, "Hold to it." In this sense, the verse is a commandment, asking Muslims "to dye" themselves in the "colouring of Allah", outwardly and inwardly by offering unalloyed worship to Him alone, by submitting themselves totally to His commandments, and by gladly accepting His will. The verse suggests that this colour is wasted away with the water, without leaving a trace outside or inside, nor does this kind of baptism serve the purpose of circumcision and cleanse a man of physical impurity. And the verse declares that the only colouring worth the name is the colouring of a genuine and unabrogated religion - that is, Islam the only colouring which can guarantee physical and spiritual purification, and the only one which shall remain. On the seventh day of its birth, they used to bathe an infant in coloured (probably yellow) water, which was supposed to be a substitute for circumcision, and a sufficient guarantee for the external and internal purification of the infant - the fast and indelible "colouring" of Christian faith, so to say. God's color-and who is more beautiful in color than God? There is no better way of life than the path of Allah, which agrees with our nature, benefiting us in every way and protecting us from evil and corruption. This had become a rarity in a society which, revering the words of the ancient prophets, regarded as truth whatever had been sanctified by centuries-old tradition. Continued belief in such ‘truth’, embellished as it was by myth and legend, became a matter of national pride; to regard it in any other light would have been to deny a great legacy from the past.

**And we worship none but Him.**

(And We are His worshippers) say: we are monotheists and acknowledge that we worship Him and declare that there is only one true God. Say that you worship Allah alone and do not worship anything apart from Him. And Him we worship the Jews said to the Muslims ‘We are the people of the first Book and our direction of prayer qibla is more ancient and prophets were never sent from among the Arabs; if Muhammad were a prophet he would have been one of us’. One is that I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that MuḤammad is God's messenger,' and he took off the sash. 'The other is that I say, "O God, if there is any danger here, then I will begin with this."' So he began. "Then We will bring a people who have come out in the color of tawḤīd and who are adorned with the attribute of love and clothed in God's color, which is colorlessness. " He who has painted a thousand worlds with color why would He buy my color and yours, O bankrupt man! And He is the Hearer, the Knower [Our Sibghah (religion) is] the Sibghah of Allah (Islam) and which Sibghah can be better than Allah's? Ad-Dahhak said that Ibn 'Abbas commented, "The religion of Allah. (then they are only in opposition. So Allah will suffice you against them) meaning, Allah will aid the believers against them,. When truth stands on its own, unsupported by history or tradition, as it was in the time of the Prophet, those who accept it do so for the pure and simple reason that it is the truth. This is the kind of belief that God recognizes and accepts. This is true faith; only faith of such strength and purity is acceptable to God.

139.text:
Say, Would you dispute with us about Allah is put as a question to the People of the Book, and the sources take the point that the dispute was about the family of the prophets and about who had the better claim to them, so the question is aimed at the ground of the argument rather than at its details. While He is our Lord and your Lord is the answer to the dispute, since the Lord of both sides is one, and the sources notice that the verse gives the other side their share in the same Lord before it names anything else, so no one is pushed away from him. We are accountable for our deeds and you for yours puts the deeds of each community in its own hand, and the words are put as a statement of fact rather than as a threat, so the reader hears again the principle the passage set out a few verses before, that no one carries the account of another. And we are devoted to Him alone closes the verse with the sincerity of the worship, and the word used is the one for clearing one's religion of every partner, so the reader is left with the difference between people who argue about God and people who worship him. The verse therefore ends the section where the passage has been heading, with the claim of each community handed to its own account. The reader is left with a question that has already been answered by the two Lordship, and with a difference that is a difference of deeds and not of blood, so the section closes on the note the whole passage has been sounding, that a person is what he does and not what his fathers did.

**The dispute that was put to them.**

, O Muhammad, ((unto the People of the Scripture) dispute ye with us) do you argue with us (concerning Allah) concerning the Religion of Allah (when He is our Lord and your Lord?) when Allah is our Lord and yours? (Say (O Muhammad to the Jews and Christians), "Dispute you with us about Allah) meaning, "Do you dispute with us regarding the Oneness of Allah, obedience and submission to Him and in avoiding His prohibitions,. If the People of the Scripture argue with you, saying they have more right to Allah and His religion than you do because their way of life is older and their scriptures came before yours, then it will not benefit them. Should the Jews and the Christians still continue, in their stubbornness, to deny, Allah asks the Holy Prophet and the Muslims to declare in plain and simple words that Allah, being the Lord of All, cannot show any special favour to any particular group of His creatures, and that on the Day of Judgment He will assess the Jews and the Christians as well as the Muslims according to what each has believed in and how each has been behaving - a principle which was accepted by the People of the Book too. If the People of the Book should, on account of their affiliation with the earlier prophets, still keep insisting on their own rectitude, the Muslims may ask them a basic question - who knows the truth better, Allah or the People of the Book?

**One Lord for both sides.**

(while He is our Lord and your Lord?) meaning, He has full control over us and you, and deserves the worship alone without partners. How can dispute with strangers be appropriate when they are covered by absence and shaded by concealment while the friends are lit by unveiling and the bright noon of witnessingḍ When is the state of one who is bankrupt by his absence equal to one whose selection and sincere devotion [and] immersion in acts of drawing near to Him has [already been] decreedḍ It is preposterous-there is no equality! Verse 139 brings out the essential and peculiar characteristic of the Islamic Ummah it has purified itself of all possible admixture of Shirk (association), and devoted itself, externally and internally, to Allah. (Ours are our works) we have our religion (and yours your work) your religion. Say to them ‘Would you then dispute with us concerning God that He chose a prophet from among the Arabs and He is our Lord and your Lord? and so it is for Him to choose whom He will Our deeds belong to us for which we will be requited and to you belong your deeds for which you will be requited so that it is not improbable that among our deeds there will be those for which we will deserve to be honoured; and to Him we are sincerely devoted in religion and in deed unlike you hence we are more worthy to be chosen the hamza of a-tuhājjūnanā ‘would you then dispute’ is for rejection and the three clauses that follow it are all circumstantial qualifiers.

**Our deeds and your deeds.**

(They shall receive the reward of what they earned, and you of what you earn.) meaning, they bear their deeds while you bear yours,. Tell them, O Prophet, that you have your actions which they will not be asked about; and they have their actions which you will not be asked about. Allah knows what they have been doing, and will judge them according to their own deeds, and not according to the deeds of their ancestors. The Muslims have also been asked to announce that they on their part recognize no other god but Allah, and have purified their religion of all traces of association (Shirk) - as against the Jews and the Christians who consider Sayyidna Uzayr (Ezra) and Sayyidna Isa (Jesus) respectively to be "the Son of God", and whose religions have, moreover, been abrogated. Everyone will be rewarded according to what they have done. What was so special about that faith was that it amounted to acceptance of the truth on an abstract level; it was belief in truth for the sake of truth. Continued belief in such ‘truth’, embellished as it was by myth and legend, became a matter of national pride; to regard it in any other light would have been to deny a great legacy from the past.

**The sincerity of the worship that was asked.**

Tell them that you are sincere to Allah in your worship and in doing as He instructs you, and that you do not worship anything apart from Him. (And we are sincere (in our faith) in Him) we acknowledge that we worship Him and declare that there is only one true God. " According to Said ibn Jubayr, Ikhlas consists in worshipping no one but Allah, associating no one with Allah, and doing good deeds only for the sake of obeying Allah, and not for the purpose of winning the admiration of the people. For, one cannot attain even the lowest degree of Ikhlas without forming a clear intention to obey the injunctions of the Shaah as against letting oneself be guided by one's instinctual urges or emotional inclinations while the concept of "sincerity" in vogue requires one to ignore the Shari'ah or even mundane considerations and to do the bidding of one's impulse of the moment, thus reducing man to an automaton at the mercy of his reflexes. (So if they dispute with you (Muhammad) say: "I have submitted myself to Allah (in Islam), and (so have) those who follow me")(3:20). Indeed, whoever disbelieves in even one Prophet, will have disbelieved in all the Messengers, especially if one disbelieves in the master and Final Messenger from Allah, the Lord of the worlds, to all mankind and the Jinns.

140.text:
Do you claim that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants were all Jews or Christians, Say, Who is more knowledgeable: you or Allah. The verse opens with a question put to the People of the Book, and the fathers are named one after another in a single line, so the reader measures how far back the family reaches before any word is heard about what the family was, and the question is left standing as the shape of the whole address. The claim itself is the thing under discussion, since the verse does not argue about this or that father but about a whole line of them, and the line is made to stand on one side of the two names that came long after them. The question turns the claim into a matter of knowing, and it is put in a form that leaves only one answer, since a claim about the fathers of the prophets cannot be weighed against what the one who sent them knows. You or Allah keeps the two sides of the question in view for a moment, the claim of the people and the knowledge of the One who gave them the Book that carries the claim. Who does more wrong than those who hide the testimony they received from Allah then names the deed that the question has exposed, and the wrong is placed on the concealment rather than on the mistake, so the reader is told that the testimony was in their own hands and was covered over. And Allah is never unaware of what you do closes the verse with the knowledge that cannot be misled and with a sentence that leaves the hidden thing in front of the One who sees it, so the last word is not comfort for the people addressed but a fact about what they have done. The verse is thus closed on knowledge rather than on argument, and the reader is left to see that the hidden testimony was never hidden from the One who received it first.

**The claim that the fathers belonged to one of the two houses.**

Or say you that Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and Al-Asbat, were Jews or Christians? Allah then criticized them in the claim that Ibrahim, the Prophets who came after him and the Asbat were following their religion, whether Judaism or Christianity. These three verses bring to an end the section of the Surah in which certain claims of the Jews and the Christians have been refuted -- for example, their assertion that Sayyidna Ibrahim (Abraham), Sayyidna Ismail (Ishmael), Sayyidna Ishaq (Isaac), Sayyidna Ya qub (Jacob) and the prophets in his lineage were either Jews or Christians, and the claim that they were the chosen people and would have the exclusive privilege of being sent straight to Paradise which would be denied to Muslims. The earlier verses have established that the religion of all these prophets was Islam, in the general sense of the term, but that the earlier Shari ahs have now been abrogated, and the title of "Islam" been specially given to the religion of Sayyidna Muhammad .

**Who is more knowledgeable, you or Allah.**

(Say, "Do you know better or does Allah?") meaning, Allah has the best knowledge and He stated that they were neither Jews, nor Christians. Ask, O Prophet, in reply to them, whether they are more knowledgeable or is Allah. (Do ye know best, or doth Allah?) do you know best about their religion or does Allah? ’ Say to them ‘Have you then greater knowledge or has God? that is God has greater knowledge; He dissociated Abraham from both groups when He said Abraham was not a Jew nor a Christian Q. 367; and those mentioned with him Abraham are his followers in not belonging to either group. Have you then greater knowl edge or has Godḍ And who does greater injustice than he who conceals a testimony received from Godḍ And God is not heedless of what you do. (Say (O Muhammad to the Jews and Christians), "Dispute you with us about Allah) meaning, "Do you dispute with us regarding the Oneness of Allah, obedience and submission to Him and in avoiding His prohibitions,. If the People of the Book should, on account of their affiliation with the earlier prophets, still keep insisting on their own rectitude, the Muslims may ask them a basic question - who knows the truth better, Allah or the People of the Book?

**Hiding the testimony they were given.**

No one does greater wrong than someone who hides firm evidence that they have from Allah, as some of the People of the Scripture did. (And who is more unjust) in his disbelief and more insolent and daring vis-�-vis Allah (than he who hideth a testimony which he hath received from Allah) in the Torah concerning the prophethood of this Prophet ﷺ? And who does greater injustice than he who conceals hides from people a testimony he has received from God? that is there is none more unjust than him these are the Jews for they concealed God’s testimony about Abraham’s pure faith in the Torah; And God is not heedless of what you do’ this is a threat for them. If they claim that they were Jews or Christians, then what they say is false, because they were sent and died before the Torah and the Gospel were revealed. This shows that what they say is a lie against Allah and His Prophet, and that they hid the truth of what was revealed to them. (2:140) Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, They used to recite the Book of Allah He sent to them that stated that the true religion is Islam and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Allah has already informed us that Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian.

**Allah is not unaware of what you do.**

(And Allah is not unaware of what you do), is a threat and a warning that His knowledge encompasses every one's deeds, and He shall award each accordingly. Allah is not unaware of what you do, and you will be rewarded accordingly. (Allah is not unaware) heedless (of what ye do) about concealing your testimony. Further, do not be deceived by the fact that you are their descendants, unless you imitate them in obeying Allah's orders and following His Messengers who were sent as warners and bearers of good news. Are those who have been drawn away from their own testimony like those who are veiled by itḍ Is the one who is snatched away from all of it equal to the one who is thrown back to what is like himḍ That is the conjecture of those who disbelieve-what misery is theirs! Allah knows what they have been doing, and will judge them according to their own deeds, and not according to the deeds of their ancestors.

**The truth their own Book carries.**

The Muslims have also been asked to announce that they on their part recognize no other god but Allah, and have purified their religion of all traces of association (Shirk) - as against the Jews and the Christians who consider Sayyidna Uzayr (Ezra) and Sayyidna Isa (Jesus) respectively to be "the Son of God", and whose religions have, moreover, been abrogated. Allah has definitely and finally announced the truth in the Last Revelation, and the People of the Book themselves know that the religion of the earlier prophets was Islam. Their Book also stated that Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the tribes were neither Jews, nor Christians. Should the Jews and the Christians still continue, in their stubbornness, to deny, Allah asks the Holy Prophet and the Muslims to declare in plain and simple words that Allah, being the Lord of All, cannot show any special favour to any particular group of His creatures, and that on the Day of Judgment He will assess the Jews and the Christians as well as the Muslims according to what each has believed in and how each has been behaving - a principle which was accepted by the People of the Book too. Whoever looks from himself to creation forms an image of each thing based on his own character and considers everything to be something like him. When they by virtue of being outsiders [to the Real] judged the prophets [ ] according to their own state the Real threw their conjecture back upon them and left them with their own opinion. If faith is to be of the kind which pleases God, it must be identical with that of the Companions of the Prophet. What was so special about that faith was that it amounted to acceptance of the truth on an abstract level; it was belief in truth for the sake of truth. Continued belief in such ‘truth’, embellished as it was by myth and legend, became a matter of national pride; to regard it in any other light would have been to deny a great legacy from the past. When truth stands on its own, unsupported by history or tradition, as it was in the time of the Prophet, those who accept it do so for the pure and simple reason that it is the truth.

141.text:
That was a community that had already gone before opens with the word for a people who have passed out of the scene, and the past tense carries the whole point of the sentence, since the people being addressed are disputing about a family that is no longer there to answer for itself. For them is what they earned and for you is what you have earned then puts the two accounts side by side, and the word for earning is used twice so that neither side is handed the other's work, with the fathers carrying what they did and the children carrying what they do. And you will not be accountable for what they have done closes the verse with the sentence the passage has been reaching, and the word for being accountable is the word for being asked, so the reader is told that the question put to him will be about his own deeds and not about the deeds of his fathers before him. The verse therefore answers the claim of the earlier verse with a plain principle, and the principle is that a person is not raised by the house he was born into but by what he himself has earned. The order of the sentences matters as well, since the community is dismissed first and the two accounts are set out afterwards, so the reader is not left with a memory to defend but with a ledger of his own.

**A community that has passed away.**

That is a community that has passed away; theirs is what they have earned and yours is what you have earned; you shall not be asked about what they did a similar verse has already been mentioned above. The barriers of fate came between you and them for they built their struc tures on separation and heedlessness while you have pitched your tents on closeness and connection. (Those are a people) a group of people (who have passed away) perished; (theirs is that which they earned) of goodness (and yours is that which ye earn) of goodness.

**What they earned, and what the reward is.**

(They shall receive the reward of what they earned, and you of what you earn.) meaning, they bear their deeds while you bear yours,. They shall receive the reward of what they earned, and you of what you earn. They have earned for themselves from their own actions; and you have earned from your own actions. Each person will receive his reward, according to what they themselves do. (And if they belie you, say: "For me are my deeds and for you are your deeds! You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do!")(10:41), and,.

**You will not be asked about what they used to do.**

(And you will not be asked of what they used to do) meaning, the fact that you are their relatives will not suffice, unless you imitate their good deeds. No one is held accountable for the disobedience of someone else, and no one benefits from what someone else does. (And ye will not be asked) on the Day of Judgement (of what they used to do) in this world. The Muslims have also been asked to announce that they on their part recognize no other god but Allah, and have purified their religion of all traces of association (Shirk) - as against the Jews and the Christians who consider Sayyidna Uzayr (Ezra) and Sayyidna Isa (Jesus) respectively to be "the Son of God", and whose religions have, moreover, been abrogated.

**Allah knows what they have been doing.**

Allah knows what they have been doing, and will judge them according to their own deeds, and not according to the deeds of their ancestors. Further, do not be deceived by the fact that you are their descendants, unless you imitate them in obeying Allah's orders and following His Messengers who were sent as warners and bearers of good news. Indeed, whoever disbelieves in even one Prophet, will have disbelieved in all the Messengers, especially if one disbelieves in the master and Final Messenger from Allah, the Lord of the worlds, to all mankind and the Jinns. Certain spiritual masters have said that Ikhlas is a deed which can be identified neither by men, nor by angels nor by Satan and that it is a "secret" between Allah and His servant.38. If faith is to be of the kind which pleases God, it must be identical with that of the Companions of the Prophet. The freedman of Our favor ʿatīq faḌlinā is not like the fugitive of Our force Ṭarīd qahrinā.

**The faith that is accepted.**

What was so special about that faith was that it amounted to acceptance of the truth on an abstract level; it was belief in truth for the sake of truth. When truth stands on its own, unsupported by history or tradition, as it was in the time of the Prophet, those who accept it do so for the pure and simple reason that it is the truth.

142.text:
The foolish among the people will ask puts the question in the mouths of people the verse itself has already named, and the name is not a compliment, so the reader is told how much weight the objection deserves before the objection is heard. Why did they turn away from the direction of prayer they used to face, Say, O Prophet is the objection itself, quoted word for word and then handed back to the Prophet, and the answer that follows is not an argument about places at all but a statement about who owns them. The east and west belong only to Allah turns the whole horizon into a single estate, and once the two quarters of the sky are his, the turning of a face from one part of the horizon to another cannot be a change of master, since nothing has been taken from him and nothing added. He guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path then gives the purpose of the whole arrangement, because the aim of the command was never the point on the compass but the road that the point marks out, and the guidance is put where the verse wants the reader to look. The sources read this passage as the answer to an objection that was raised when the direction of prayer was changed from the sanctuary at Bayt al-Maqdis to the House at Makkah, and they note that the change was made in the second year after the Prophet came to Madīnah, so the verse is speaking to people who had turned with him and to people who were watching the community from outside and measuring it by the places it faced. The objection is answered in the verse by an appeal to ownership rather than to precedent, because the lord of the two quarters of the sky is free to appoint any point within them as the place towards which his servants turn. The answer is therefore built on two things, a lord whose rule covers every direction and a people whom he guides along one road.

**The fools who put the question.**

The fools among the people, meaning the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians), said, "What made them change the former Qiblah that they used to face? The foolish and weak-minded among the Jews, and those like them from among the hypocrites, will ask what turned the Muslims away from the prayer direction of Bayt al-Maqdis, which was their direction of prayer before. (The foolish of the people) the ignorant among the Jews and Arab idolaters (will say: What hath turned them) made them change (from the Qiblah which they formerly observed) except that they want to revert to the religion of their ancestors; it is also said that this means: there was no reason to turn from the direction in which they prayed, i.e. The fools the ignorant among the people that is the Jews and the idolaters will say ‘What matter has turned them the Prophet s and the believers from the direction they were facing in their prayers formerly?’ this being the Holy House bayt al-maqdis sc. The foolish among people, who are none other than the Jews, said: The Holy Qur'an reports this objection, adding that such an objection can come only from stupid people - just as earlier in this Surah those who turn away from the religion of Sayyidna Ibrahim have been described as people who have besotted themselves. They looked with an eye to finding ugliness and let loose their tongues to oppose everything that was and would be from [the believers].

**Why did they turn away from the direction they used to face.**

(What has turned them (Muslims) from their Qiblah to which they used to face in prayer.) (What hath turned them from the qiblah which they formerly observed?) Allah, exalted is He, said: They said that if their qibla was correct what would turn them from itḍ So [God] said: The opponents of Islam used the change of the qiblah as an excuse to spread all sorts of rumours about the Prophet. How, they thought, could another place be the qiblah when Bayt al-Maqdis had held this position for time immemorial? It indicates that for those who live far away from Makkah it is not necessary, while offering Salah, to have the Ka'bah itself exactly in front of them, but turning one's face in the direction of the "House of Allah" is quite sufficient. "What has turned them (Muslims) from their Qiblah [prayer direction (towards Bayt al-Maqdis)] to which they used to face in prayer.

**The east and the west belong only to Allah.**

(unto Allah belong the East) praying to the Ka'bah (and the West) the prayer that you prayed in the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis-both are with Allah's command. Tell them, O Prophet, in reply, that to Allah belongs the east and the west and every direction, and He directs whomever He wills of His servants to whatever direction He wills. "Righteousness is not that you turn your faces to the East or the West; but righteousness is that one believes in Allah" (2:177).

**He guides whoever He wills.**

He guides whom He wills of His servants to the right path which is free of distortions and misguidance. He guides whomever He will His guidance being to a straight path’ that is the religion of Islam and you are among these guided ones. Thus He commands that they face whichever direction He wills and there can be no objection. The direction that He lays down is the one that we should face in our prayer, irrespective of what direction it may be.

**The qiblah that was appointed for the Prophet.**

In the second year after the Prophet’s emigration to Madīnah, he was commanded to alter the direction of prayer, and face Makkah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis. The commandment regarding the change of qiblah was revealed seventeen months after the Prophet’s emigration to Madīnah. As soon as God’s commandment was revealed, all of them turned, still praying, from Bayt al-Maqdis to Makkah—a 160 degree turn from north-west to south. Allah, exalted is He, revealed (We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven) up to the end of the verse [2:144] . And We made the Qiblah which you used to face, only to test those who followed the Messenger (Muhammad) from those who would turn on their heels (i.e., disobey the Messenger). It was rebuilt, under divine command by Sayyidna Ibrahim and Sayyidna Ismail (Abraham and Ishmael (and became their Qiblah . After that, the Baytul-Maqdis at Bayt al-Maqdis was established as the Qiblah for the Hebrew prophets and their people. Even so, these prophets, according to Abu al- Aliyah, used to offer their prayers in the Baytul-Maqdis in such a way that they should be facing not only the Rock (Sakhrah) but the Ka'bah also. (Qurtubi) (And We made the Qiblah (prayer direction towards Bayt al-Maqdis) which you used to face, only to test those who followed the Messenger (Muhammad) from those who would turn on their heels (i.e., disobey the Messenger). Indeed it was great (heavy, difficult) except for those whom Allah guided.) The raison d'etre of changing the Qiblah for the Holy Prophet might well be to show to the people in a visible form that a Qiblah is not an idol to be worshipped but only a concrete expression of divine commandment, and may hence be changed as and when Allah wills. Verse 142, thus, fully refutes the antagonists of Islam, and points out that Allah guides whosoever He wills on the Straight Path - the Straight Path, of course, being the readiness to obey divine commandment without demur. Moreover, the only merit in adopting a particular Qiblah lies in one's obedience to the divine commandment and in one's total submission to the will of Allah, which is the basic principle of the religion of the founder of the Ka'bah Sayyidna Ibrahim . Similarly the companions of absence and those who are veiled from witnessing [the way in which] the Real grants free agency to His friends seek only certain aspects of the affair and bring their own states to bear upon them.

**The House towards which the faces are turned.**

" (2:115) These verses clearly define the meaning and significance of adopting an orientation - that is, the place which has been chosen to serve as the Qiblah does not possess any merit in its own right, but the special merit arises from its having been chosen by Allah, and similarly turning towards it constitutes a meritorious act only insofar as it shows a readiness to obey divine commandment. When the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, went to Medina, he prayed toward the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months. The servants worship toward any region and direction they will. Bayt al-Maqdis; the sīn of sa-yaqūlu ‘they will say’ denotes the future tense and informs of the Unseen. In replying to this objection, the second part of the verse shows that their stupidity lies in not realizing that the East and the West both belong to Allah Himself, and that He guides whomsoever He likes on the straight path. If they had seen the whole picture with singular vision they would have been saved from the pain of divisive thinking the distraction of accursed thoughts and the claims of fractured conjecture but God guides whom He wills to His light. They did not see anything new without bringing forth a new objection to it.

143.text:
And so We have made you believers an upright community so that you may be witnesses over humanity and that the Messenger may be a witness over you opens with a making that is put in the past, so the standing of this community is described as something already given and not as something it has still to earn. The word rendered upright is the word for the middle, and the sources take the middle here as the position between two extremes, so the community is described as the people who hold the centre in what they believe and in how they live. The witness over humanity is read by the sources as the testimony this community will give about the prophets in the presence of the nations, and the Messenger is named as the witness over the community in the same sentence, so the two testimonies stand facing each other, one from the Prophet to his people and one from his people to the rest of mankind. We assigned your former direction of prayer only to distinguish those who would remain faithful to the Messenger from those who would lose faith turns to the change itself, and the purpose given to it has nothing to do with a point on the earth: the earlier direction was appointed so that the people who follow the Prophet would be separated from the people who turn back on their heels. It was certainly a difficult test except for those rightly guided by Allah names the weight of that separation and puts the exception where this passage puts every exception, in the guidance of God, so the difficulty is admitted before the way through it is named. And Allah would never discount your previous acts of faith is the sentence that answers the fear of the people who had prayed toward the earlier direction and were afraid that their worship had gone to waste, and the verse tells them that nothing of it was lost. Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity closes on the two names that answer that fear, so the reader is left with the mercy that chose the community and the mercy that kept the record of its worship. The verse thus joins the two things the whole passage has been carrying, a community that was given a direction and a community that was given a task, and it binds them by naming the testimony first and the direction afterwards, so the reader is told that the place he faces matters less than the witness he is to bear. The mercy named at the end is also the answer to the fear of the earlier sentence, since the two names do not stand loose at the close but gather the whole verse into the care of the One who chose this community and who keeps the account of what it has done.

**A community made upright.**

(Thus We have made you [true Muslims], a Wasat (just)(and the best) nation, that you be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger (Muhammad) be a witness over you.) According to the present verse, Allah has made the Islamic Ummah an equitable and just, and hence a trustworthy community, "so that" it may be qualified to bear witness. Those among the earlier Ummahs who had been denying their prophets would, on that day, pretend that they had never received a book from Allah nor had any prophet given them any kind of guidance. (Thus) i.e. just as we have honoured you with the Religion of Abraham (Islam) and his direction of prayer (We have appointed you a middle nation) a middlemost community, (that you be witnesses) for the prophets (over mankind, and that the Messenger) Muhammad ﷺ (may be a witness over you) that you are upright and follow the straight path. Just as I made a direction of prayer for you, I have chosen you to be a good, just and balanced nation from among all the communities: in your beliefs and your ways of worship and in your transactions, so that you will be witnesses for the prophets of Allah on the Day of Judgement, confirming that they delivered the messages Allah instructed them to deliver to their people; and so that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ will also witness that he delivered his message to you. This is a responsibility which is eternally incumbent upon the Muslim community.

**Witnesses over humanity.**

Thus We have made you [true Muslims real believers of Islamic Monotheism, true followers of Prophet Muhammad and his Sunnah (legal ways)], a Wasat (just and the best) nation, that you be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger (Muhammad) be a witness over you. The Islamic Ummah would, then, be called upon to bear witness, and it would, testify that prophets had been coming from Allah in every age, and providing guidance to each and every people. In reply to this, the Islamic Ummah would maintain that even if it was not an eyewitness to the events of the past, yet it had received an authentic report from the most reliable source of information that can possibly be - that is, from the Last Prophet and from the Last Book of Allah. On the contrary, we have the Islamic Ummah which has such a deep love for the Holy Prophet g that Muslims have, in every period of their history, taken it to be the greatest blessing to be able to sacrifice their own lives and even the lives of their wives and children at his call, and yet it has never exceeded the limit, and has placed the Holy Prophet only in the station of a prophet and not in the station of Allah. Now, with the end of the prophethood, the entire Muslim community stands between God and the people, a position formerly occupied by the prophets. This is not a reward for superiority but a massive responsibility, so that all of the Muslims’ social and community-based planning must of necessity be dawah-oriented. Allah changed the direction of prayer that you used to face (Bayt al-Maqdis) to demonstrate who was content with Allah’s decree, willingly doing as He instructed and following the Messenger; and to also demonstrate who turned away from his religion, following his own desires and not obeying Allah’s sacred law.

**The Messenger as a witness over you.**

According to this interpretation, Allah assures the Muslims that the commandment changing the Qiblah would in no way affect the validity of the prayers they have been offering so far in the direction of the Baytul-Maqdis - Allah would not allow these prayers to go waste, for they are valid, and have already been accepted. " What is understood from this report is that MuṣṬafā is the best of the Adamites, the chosen from among the world's folk, the leader of the creatures, the adornment of the world, the weighty one of the time, the lamp of the earth, the full moon of heaven, the shelter of the disobedient, the interceder for the sinners, the master of all the messengers and their seal. He addressed them saying, 'By Allah, I bear witness that I have offered prayer with the Prophet facing Makkah (Ka'bah).' Hearing that, those people immediately changed their direction towards the House (Ka'bah) while still as they were (i.e., in the same bowing position). (Verily, We have seen the turning of your (Muhammad's) face towards the heaven. Surely, We shall turn you to a Qiblah (prayer direction) that shall please you, so turn your face in the direction of Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah).)(2:144) Acting as intermediaries, the prophets used to receive guidance from God and convey it to the people. This is why MuṣṬafā said, "I was brought forth from the best generation of the children of Adam, generation after generation, until I came to be in the generation in which I am.

**The qiblah appointed as a test.**

(And We made the Qiblah (prayer direction towards Bayt al-Maqdis) which you used to face, only to test those who followed the Messenger (Muhammad) from those who would turn on their heels (i.e., disobey the Messenger). Indeed it was great (heavy, difficult) except for those whom Allah guided.) And We made the Qiblah which you used to face, only to test those who followed the Messenger (Muhammad) from those who would turn on their heels (i.e., disobey the Messenger). Anyhow, the real import of the verse remains the same in either case - the commandment with regard to the change in orientation is a test of the faith of those who claim to be the followers of the Holy Prophet which would openly demonstrate the distinction between those who are genuinely obedient to Allah and His Messenger and those who follow their individual opinion. (And We appointed) changed (the Qiblah which ye formerly observed) prayed towards for a period of 19 months (only that We might know) see and distinguish (him who followeth the Messenger) concerning the Qiblah, (from him who turneth) reverts (on his heels) to his former religion and direction of prayer. (In truth it) the changing of the Qiblah (was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided) whose hearts Allah had protected. The first change of prayer direction was difficult, except for those who Allah granted faith to and who were certain that whatever He decrees for His servants has far reaching wisdom and underlying reasons behind it. Thus in the same way that We guided you to it We appointed you O community of Muhammad a midmost community excellent and upright that you might be witnesses to the people on the Day of Resurrection that their messengers delivered the Message to them; and that the Messenger might be a witness to you that he delivered the Message to you and We did not appoint make the direction for you now the direction you were facing that is the Ka‘ba the Prophet s used to face it in prayer but when he emigrated he was commanded to face the Holy House of Bayt al-Maqdis in order to win the hearts of the Jews. The change of qiblah was a sign that God had removed the Children of Israel from their position of spiritual leadership and appointed in their place the followers of Muhammad. Now the Ka’bah shall remain, until the end of time, the rallying point for the call of divine religion, a centre for all true believers in God, with Muslims acting as a ‘middle nation’ (ummat wasat), or intermediaries, between God and man.

**The faith that was not lost.**

Allah did not thwart your prayers towards Bayt al-Maqdis but He has abrogated the ruling which required you to pray towards Bayt al-Maqdis, (for Allah is full of pity, Merciful) in that He does not thwart your faith as it was before the abrogation of legal rulings (towards mankind) towards the believers. (But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain) that He thwarts your faith as it was prior to the abrogation of legal rulings; and it is also said that this means: it is not Allah's purpose to thwart your faith but rather His purpose is to abrogate the legal rulings which conduct your faith; and it is also said that this means: Allah will not make you lose your faith in Him, or your good actions, including the prayers you prayed before the change of prayer direction. Allah is kind and compassionate with people, not overburdening them, and they will not lose the reward for their actions. Surely God is clement, ever-merciful toward the people. This verse also goes to show that the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah too, in a certain respect, cannot be delinked from the Holy Qur'an, and that the Holy Qur'an recognizes the legitimacy of those injunctions which find no mention in the Holy Qur'an but have been instituted by the Hadith alone.

**The community that was chosen.**

(He has chosen you (to convey His Message of Islamic Monotheism to mankind), and has not laid upon you in religion any hardship: it is the religion of your father Ibrahim. It is He (Allah) Who has named you Muslims both before and in this (the Qur'an), that the Messenger (Muhammad) may be a witness over you and you be witnesses over mankind!)(22:78) It is the best Ummah, for it has been granted a unique Prophet who taught us to respect all other prophets and a Book which is the most comprehensive and the most perfect of all the Divine Books, and has in itself been endowed with the quality of temperateness, moderation and equilibrium to a degree as no other Ummah does enjoy; it has been destined to be the recipient of the most subtle modes of knowledge, to outshine others in all the forms of faith and practice, and, above all, in the fear of Allah - its field of action not limited to any one country or race but extending all over the world, and infusing all the spheres of human existence. From among the animals He chose the Adamites, from the Adamites He chose the faithful, from the faithful He chose the prophets, and from the prophets He chose MuḤammad. He chose his community above the previous communities. He chose my community over the other com munities, so He sent me forth in the best generation. He chose four of my companions and made them the best of my companions-and in all of my companions there is good-Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī. Muslims should be most eager to carry out this mission, should make it their principal goal and be ready to sacrifice their all for it. It is for them to communicate the word of God to their fellow human beings, just as the Prophet had done in his time.

144.text:
Indeed, We see you O Prophet turning your face towards heaven opens on the watching of the Prophet and not on his words, since the verse describes a look that is raised to the sky and does not report a request that was put into speech. The sources dwell on that silence, and they take the raising of the face as a sign of longing that the Prophet kept to himself, so the reader is shown a servant who waits rather than one who demands. Now We will make you turn towards a direction of prayer that will please you answers the look, and the promise is put in the plural of majesty with a direction left unnamed for the moment, so the attention is kept on the pleasure of the one who will be answered rather than on the place itself. *So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque in Mecca* then names what was promised, and the command is given in the singular, so the Prophet is asked to turn first, and the turning is toward the house that the passage has already tied to Abraham and to the first house of worship. Wherever you are keeps the command from being a rule for one place or one person, and turn your faces towards it puts the same command on the whole community in the plural, so the direction becomes a bond that keeps the believers together wherever they may be, in the market or on a journey or at home. Those who were given the Scripture certainly know this to be the truth from their Lord brings the People of the Book back into the passage, and the verse treats their knowledge as something they already have, so their refusal is a matter of the will and not of the understanding. And Allah is never unaware of what they do closes the verse with the knowledge that reaches what they hide, and the closing sentence leaves both the objection and the concealment in front of the One from whom nothing is covered.

**The look that was raised to heaven.**

God saw you, O Prophet, turning your face and gazing towards the heavens, anticipating revelation about changing the direction of prayer to the place you loved. We have seen thy face turning about in heaven. This principle leads us to believe that the Holy Prophet had already been allowed to pray for his wish to be fulfilled, and that he hoped his prayer would be granted. Now, prophets are as close to Allah as man can ever be, and this exalted station teaches them to observe a very strict spiritual etiquette - they never submit a request before Allah until and unless they have received the permission to do so. (We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven (for guidance, O Muhammad) turning your sight to heaven in anticipation of Gabriel coming down to announce the change of the Qiblah. He had let him know that he was in the sight of the Real so that he would model his courtesy on the Real's courtesy. When he put courtesy into practice, he did not ask the Real for what his heart wanted and did no more than gaze upon heaven. " Hence when his heart was intent on the kiblah, he did not make this manifest, in keeping with courtesy. " When those caresses came forth from the Presence of Unity and those generosities reached him, the tongue of his state said in his yearning, "When your heart reaches out once in love for me, suffering separation from You becomes easy, sweetheart.

**The direction that would please him.**

God will turn you to a prayer direction which you will be pleased with, to the Sacred House of God, instead of the prayer direction you now face, so turn your face to the Sacred House of God in Makkah, and wherever you are, O believers, turn towards it to perform your prayers. (And now surely We shall make thee turn (in prayer) toward a Qiblah that is dear to thee) that you like, namely, the Qiblah of Abraham. Now We shall turn thee toward a kiblah that thou shalt approve. We have come to know that wish in your heart and We have admired your beautiful courtesy in not asking. We will bestow upon you that of which you approve in the work of the kiblah. Then He gave him better than what He gives to those who ask. (And We made the Qiblah (prayer direction towards Bayt al-Maqdis) which you used to face, only to test those who followed the Messenger (Muhammad) from those who would turn on their heels (i.e., disobey the Messenger).)(2:143)

**Turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque.**

(So turn thy face) when in prayer (towards the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be) whether on land or in the sea, (turn your faces (when ye pray) in prayer (towards it. (Lo! Those who have received the Scripture know that) the Sacred Precinct (is the Truth from their Lord) is the Qiblah of Abraham but they conceal this fact. (And Allah is not unaware) heedless (of what they do) of what they conceal. Immediately after the promise, there follows the commandment: ‌ ‌ : .Now turn your face in the direction of the Sacred Mosque. Although, the Qiblah to be precise, is the Baytullah which is known as the Ka'bah yet it is obvious that one can turn exactly towards the Baytullah only so long as one can see it with one's own eyes, and that for those who live at some distance and cannot see it directly, it would be too rigorous an obligation to fulfill, if they were required to turn exactly towards the Baytullah - in the case of distant towns, an exact orientation would be difficult and uncertain even with the help of the instruments and calculations. The only condition necessary to be fulfilled in turning to-wards the Qiblah is that the man offering his prayers should be duly convinced that his face is turned in the direction of the Ka'bah . Faithful to this principle, he initially made Bayt al-Maqdis his prayer direction, or the qiblah, for prophets since the time of Solomon had prayed in that direction. The Jews, who did not like that you change your Qiblah from Bayt Al-Maqdis, already knew that Allah will command you (O Muhammad) to face the Ka'bah. ("What has turned them (Muslims) from their Qiblah (prayer direction) to which they used to face in prayer." Say (O Muhammad), "To Allah belong both, east and the west.")(2:142)

**Wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.**

Also, included are those who are not sure of the direction and offer prayer in the wrong direction, thinking that it is the direction of the Qiblah, because Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear. So, the word itself points to the rule that in the case of places which are far from Makkah it is not even necessary for the prayers to be valid that one should turn exactly towards Al-Masjid al-Harm for, it is quite sufficient to turn only "in the direction" of the Sacred Mosque, as the Holy Qur'an itself.has indicated. Since the point at which the sun sets in the summer is different from that where it sets in the winter, the Fuqaha' (the Muslim jurists) have decided that for the purposes of Salah in such countries, the West (the direction of the Qiblah in this case) lies in between these two points. If there was a mosque built by the blessed Companions present in a town, the neighbouring mosques were given the same orientation, and these in their turn used to serve as the models for the mosques in the villages or towns in the region concerned, thus setting up a chain which went on prolonging itself. This is the general principle; one should, however, make an effort to ensure, in laying down the foundation of a mosque, that the orientation towards the Baytullah is as exact as possible.

**Those who were given the Scripture know it.**

Those who have been given the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians, know well that the change of prayer direction is the truth revealed from their Creator Who arranges and manages their lives, as it is clear in their Scripture. Those who have been given the Scripture know that it the change towards the Ka‘ba is the fixed truth from their Lord on account of the description in their Scripture of how the Prophet s would re-orient himself to it; God is not heedless of what you do O believers when you obey His command alternatively ta‘malūna ‘you do’ can be read ya‘malūna ‘they do’ in other words it would be referring to the Jews’ denial of the matter concerning the direction of prayer. Yet only a few of them, such as ‘Abdullah ibn Salam and Mukhairiq, confirmed the authenticity of this commandment and acknowledged that God had revealed the truth through the Prophet Muhammad. The reason for the majority’s refusal to follow the Prophet was the fact that they were used to behave as they wished. They had certain romantic notions about the special position occupied by their own people, and they had made these the bedrock of their life and creed. The coming of Islam signalled the removal of the Jews from their position as torch-bearers of the true faith. The true faith had also to be separated and made distinct from Jewish tradition, so that it could appear in a new and unmistakably pure form. The prophets who hailed from among the Jewish people had been informed that one day God would alter the qiblah, and they had passed the knowledge on to the Jews. He, glory be to Him, is aware of everything, and will reward them according to their actions. Those who give free rein to their own desires will never follow the path of reason. In their perversity, they want the kind of satisfaction from the denial of God’s signs, which God would have wished them to derive from their acceptance.

145.text:
Even if you were to bring every proof to the People of the Book, they would not accept your direction of prayer puts the whole matter beyond argument at the very start, because the proofs are granted in the opening words and the refusal is placed after them, so the reader sees that the evidence was never the thing standing in the way. They would not accept your direction of prayer is joined by nor would you accept theirs, so the refusal is placed on both sides and the reader sees a parting of ways rather than a failure of evidence. Nor would any of them accept the direction of prayer of another widens the sentence one more time, since the People of the Book are not one party either, and the sources take the words as a statement about the stubbornness each group keeps towards the others as much as towards the Muslims. And if you were to follow their desires after all the knowledge that has come to you then turns from the people who refuse to the Prophet himself, and the warning is put as a condition that cannot be imagined, so the reader is made to hear how far the command reaches and how little room it leaves. Then you would certainly be one of the wrongdoers closes the verse with a name that the Prophet cannot bear, and the sources read the sentence as a mark of how completely he was kept from the thing that is described in it, since the warning is given to him so that the community behind him will weigh it for itself. The passage thus answers the argument about the direction of prayer with a statement about the people who are making it, and the reader is left with the knowledge that has come to him and with the choice of what to do with it. The verse is also a lesson about where disputation should stop, since the Prophet is told in advance that the argument will not be won by proofs, and the reader learns that a refusal rooted in the will is not answered by piling up evidence in front of it.

**The proofs that would not change them.**

And even if you were to bring to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) all the Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), they would not follow your Qiblah (prayer direction), nor are you going to follow their Qiblah. (And even if you were to bring to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) all the Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), they would not follow your Qiblah (prayer direction). (And even if thou broughtest unto those who have received the Scripture all kinds of portents) all the signs they asked of you, (they would not follow your Qiblah) they would not pray towards your Qiblah nor embrace your Religion, (nor canst thou be a follower of their Qiblah) nor can you pray towards the Qiblah of the Jews or Christians; (nor are some of them followers of others) nor are some of them going to pray towards the Qiblah of the Jews and Christians. If you provided the Jews and Christians who have been given the Scripture with every sign and proof that the change of prayer direction was the truth, they would not face your prayer direction, stubborn against what you say and too proud to follow the truth. It is not that they demand solid and convincing arguments in order to be able to accept the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah : it is sheer stubbornness which does not allow them to give their assent, and no proof in the world, declares the Holy Qur'an, is ever going to satisfy them. Yet if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you should bring to those who have been given the Scripture every sign about your truthfulness in the matter of the direction of prayer they will not follow your direction out of obduracy and you are not a follower of their direction this is a categorical negation of his the Prophet’s desire that they become Muslims and of their desire that he return to their direction of prayer; neither are they the Jews and the Christians followers of one another’s direction. In continuing the discussion on the subject of the Qiblah or the divinely-ordained orientation, the present verse provides yet another instance of the maliciousness of the People of the Book .

**Not your direction, nor theirs.**

You will not face their prayer direction after God has directed you away from it, and they will not face the prayer directions of one another, because each group calls the other disbelievers, and because they follow their desires in the matter of the prayer direction and in other sacred laws and rulings, even after the true knowledge which was revealed to you and about which there is no doubt. They will not follow your qibla even if you were to show them evidence that was clearer than suns and moons. (...nor are you going to follow their Qiblah), indicates the vigor with which Allah's Messenger implements what Allah commanded him. "You are not to follow their Qiblah ", it is meant to declare that the Baytullah shall now stay as the Qiblah upto the end of the world. So, there is no likelihood of an agreement between the People of the Book and the Muslims in this matter. The true faith had also to be separated and made distinct from Jewish tradition, so that it could appear in a new and unmistakably pure form.

**The refusal that runs through the People of the Book.**

Allah's statement also indicates that as much as the Jews adhere to their opinions and desires, the Prophet adheres by Allah's commands, obeying Him and following what pleases Him, and that he would never adhere to their desires in any case. In fact, their two groups display an equal malice even towards each other - the Jews have adopted the Baytul-Maqdis as their Qiblah while the Christians have chosen the East, and each group rejects the Qiblah of the other. From this principle it logically follows that it is impossible for him to favour the desires of the People of the Book, and to accept their Qiblah as his own. Thus, the declaration refutes the scoffing allegation of the People of the Book that there was no stability in the Islamic injunctions, and that the Muslims might again adopt the Baytul-Maqdis as their Qiblah . The reason for the majority’s refusal to follow the Prophet was the fact that they were used to behave as they wished. They had certain romantic notions about the special position occupied by their own people, and they had made these the bedrock of their life and creed. In their perversity, they want the kind of satisfaction from the denial of God’s signs, which God would have wished them to derive from their acceptance.

**The warning against following their desires.**

(And if thou shouldst follow their desires) after being warned and pray towards their Qiblah (after the knowledge which hath come unto you) that the Sacred Precinct is the Qiblah of Abraham, (then surely) if you do that then surely (wert thou of the evil-doers) who harm themselves. If you were to follow their whims the ones to which they summon you after the knowledge the revelation that has come to you then you if hypothetically you were to follow them will surely be among the evildoers. Verily, if you follow their desires after that which you have received of knowledge (from Allah), then indeed you will be one of the wrongdoers. (Verily, if you follow their desires after that which you have received of knowledge (from Allah), then indeed you will be one of the wrongdoers.) Allah then warns those who knowingly defy the truth, because the proof against those who know is stronger than against other people. Here God addresses the Prophet directly to show how wrong it would be to follow them.

**The warning that stands after the knowledge.**

But, supposing for the sake of supposition, were he to do so even after having received a definite injunction through the Wahy (Revelation), he would be counted among the unjust - that is, among those who disobey divine commandments. Of course, God has protected the prophet himself from ever doing so, and this as a warning for his followers after him. Devotion to the path of the Real was already yours from the eternal decree [just as it was decreed] that your enemies would fall to the side. Between the two of you there is a barrier barzakh. Those who give free rein to their own desires will never follow the path of reason.

**Those who will not be guided.**

(Truly, those, against whom the Word (wrath) of your Lord has been justified, will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful torment.)(10:96-97) Allah describes the Jews' disbelief, stubbornness and defiance of what they know of the truth of Allah's Messenger , that if the Prophet brought forward every proof to the truth of what he was sent with, they will never obey him or abandon following their desires. The coming of Islam signalled the removal of the Jews from their position as torch-bearers of the true faith. Yet only a few of them, such as ‘Abdullah ibn Salam and Mukhairiq, confirmed the authenticity of this commandment and acknowledged that God had revealed the truth through the Prophet Muhammad. Naturally, it is impossible for the Holy Prophet g to follow the desires of the People of the Book. In that there is a decree from God from pre-eternity.

146.text:
Those We have given the Scripture recognize this Prophet as they recognize their own children is one of the sharpest sentences in the passage, because it does not charge the People of the Book with ignorance but with recognition, and the comparison it chooses is the closest knowledge one person has of another. The sources read the simile as a deliberate argument, since a man knows his own son without needing a proof and without a doubt being left in him, and the verse puts the Prophet in exactly that place in the eyes of the scholars of the Book. The people addressed are named as the ones who were given the Scripture, so the recognition is tied to the gift they carry, because the book in their hands had already described the coming Prophet and had set out his marks. Yet a group of them hides the truth knowingly then turns from the recognition to the deed, and the group is kept as a part of the whole, so the reader may not say that every one of them did the same. The word for hiding is the word for covering over something a person has, and the word knowingly takes away the excuse of the ignorant, so the sentence ends with the two things it has charged them with, that they knew and that they covered what they knew. The verses around this one carry the same charge, and the passage tells the Prophet afterwards not to be among those who doubt, so the recognition and the concealment are held next to each other until the reader feels the weight of the contrast.

**Recognized as a man recognizes his own son.**

Those to whom We gave the Scripture (Jews and Christians) recognise him (Muhammad or the Ka'bah at Makkah) as they recognize their sons. The scholars of the Jews and the Christians to whom Allah gave the scripture recognise Muhammad ﷺ as completely as they recognise their own children and distinguish them from others. (Those unto whom We gave the Scripture) gave the knowledge of the Torah, 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his followers (recognise) know Muhammad ﷺ with his description and traits (as they recognise their children) in the midst of other children. Those to whom We have given the Scripture they recognize him as they recognize their sons; even though there is a party of them that conceal the truth while they know. On the basis of the irrefutable evidence provided by their own Sacred Books, the Jews and the Christians knew him to be the promised Last Prophet but many of them refused to acknowledge him as such out of sheer obstinacy. The Torah and the Evangel had already foretold the coming of the Holy Prophet and set down the signs and indications which should help the people to recognize him. Allah states that the scholars of the People of the Scripture know the truth of what Allah's Messenger was sent with, just as one of them knows his own child, which is a parable that the Arabs use to describe what is very apparent.

**The simile of the son and what it means.**

As everyone knows, in bringing two terms into comparison with each other, a simile does not involve in this analogy all the aspects of these two terms, but only those which should be relevant to the occasion. For, the present simile intends to make a very simple and obvious point - since the son grows from infancy to manhood normally under the eyes of his parents, his face or general appearance is quite sufficient for his father to recognize him without any doubt or hesitation. The Jews and the Christians enjoyed the same kind of facility - or even certainty - in being able to recognize the Last Prophet . They knew Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, by his description, traits and mission from their Scripture as did any one of them know his son upon seeing him with other boys. The Jews know that the Prophet is True, but they hide the Truth. Now, the two present verses show that their conduct towards the Holy Prophet was equally dishonest and malicious.

**A party of them conceals the truth while they know.**

But verily, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it [i.e., the qualities of Muhammad which are written in the Tawrah and the Injil This is) the truth from your Lord. Nevertheless, a group of them hide the truth that has come to them, out of envy, fully aware that it is the truth. (But lo! A party of them) of the people of the Book (knowingly) knowing it to exist in their Book (conceal the Truth) conceal the description and traits of Muhammad ﷺ. The Ayah indicates that they hide the truth from the people, about the Prophet , that they find in their Books,. (while they know it.) Allah then strengthens the resolve of His Prophet and the believers and affirms that what the Prophet came with is the truth without doubt, saying: Allah states next that although they had knowledge and certainty in the Prophet , they still: Their hidden envy causes haughtiness in them concerning what they necessarily know.

**Concealing the truth from their own people.**

Some of them, while denying the truth themselves, even tried to keep it concealed from others, although they knew fully well that this particular truth (that is to say, the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah) had been established by Revelation from Allah Himself. Because I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah truly and out of certainty, but I cannot bear witness truly and out of certainty that my son is mine, for I have no knowledge of what women do [behind their husbands' backs] . 'Umar then said: I knew Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, better than I knew my son . 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asked him: One who has understood this fact can never allow himself to be in doubt with regard to this particular truth or to any other which has been revealed to a prophet by Allah. Verses 144 and 145 have told us how the People of the Book knew in their hearts that a divine commandment itself had instituted the Baytullah as the Qiblah of the Muslims, and yet denied this fact in public. This was revealed about the believers of the people of the Book: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.

**Those who would not take the truth as their own.**

Similarly whoever has been defeated in the darknesses of his lower self throws off the cloak of bashfulness. There is no use censuring him; words will not rein in his abandon. Those who do not make the truth their own, show that they had never realised God, for, if they had, they would have recognized His word when they heard it. Those who find words to reject the truth think that they have discovered strong arguments to justify their stand. But very soon they realize that those words were nothing but imaginary props, which they themselves had devised to give false satisfaction to their egos.

**The truth that was handed to them.**

((This is) the truth from your Lord. So be you not one of those who doubt.) Then Allah mentions the believers of the people of the Book, saying: According to Al-Qurtubi, it was narrated that 'Umar said to 'Abdullah bin Salam (an Israelite scholar who became a Muslim), "Do you recognize Muhammad as you recognize your own son? Those to whom We have given the Scripture they recognise him Muhammad as they recognise their sons because of the descriptions of him in their Scripture ‘Abd Allāh Ibn Salām said ‘I recognised him the moment I saw him as I would my own son; but my recognition of Muhammad was more intense’; even though there is a party of them that conceal the truth that is his description while they know this truth which you Muhammad follow.

147.text:
This is the truth from your Lord is put as a statement of fact before it is put as a warning, so the sentence names the source of the message rather than arguing about its content. The sources take the words to mean that the message the Prophet carries is not his own invention and does not come from his own mind, but comes from the Lord who sent him, and the possessive is what settles the matter, since the one who sent him is the one who knows what he sent. So do not ever be one of those who doubt then turns the statement into an address, and the warning is given to the Prophet himself, which the sources explain as a way of strengthening the community behind him, because what he is told not to do is what the people around him are being taught to avoid. The word for doubt is the word for wavering between two sides, so the verse is not forbidding a question but forbidding a standing in the middle, and the reader is left with the truth on one side and the wavering on the other. The verse therefore follows the account of the people who recognized the Prophet and hid what they knew, and it answers the whole of that account with a single sentence of certainty.

**The truth from your Lord.**

The truth comes from your Lord; then be not among the doubters who doubt it that is to say ‘be not of such a disposition’ which is more eloquent than merely saying ‘do not waver’. The truth comes from your Lord; then be not among the doubters. i.e. 'after the suns of certainty have appeared to you do not yield to the results of mere guessing'. (It is the Truth from thy Lord (O Muhammad) that you are a Prophet sent by Allah. The phrase, "The Truth is from your Lord", can also be interpreted in a general sense as providing a definition of the nature of truth - namely, that alone is truth which comes from Allah.

**Do not be among those who doubt the truth.**

(So be not thou of those who waver) who doubt whether they know or not. One who has understood this fact can never allow himself to be in doubt with regard to this particular truth or to any other which has been revealed to a prophet by Allah. The address is to [the Prophet] but what is intended by it is the community. But verily, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it [i.e., the qualities of Muhammad which are written in the Tawrah and the Injil This is) the truth from your Lord.

**Those who insist on rejecting the truth.**

Whenever God reveals some truth to the world, it is supported by clear arguments. Those who do not make the truth their own, show that they had never realised God, for, if they had, they would have recognized His word when they heard it. Those who find words to reject the truth think that they have discovered strong arguments to justify their stand. But very soon they realize that those words were nothing but imaginary props, which they themselves had devised to give false satisfaction to their egos. And it was just this kind of gross dishonesty that the People of the Book were indulging in. Some of them, while denying the truth themselves, even tried to keep it concealed from others, although they knew fully well that this particular truth (that is to say, the new injunction with regard to the Qiblah) had been established by Revelation from Allah Himself.

148.text:
Everyone turns to their own direction of prayer opens the verse with a sentence about the whole of mankind, and the sources take it as the plain fact that each community has been given a way to face, so the difference between the directions is set out before the competition in good deeds is named. So compete with one another in doing good then turns the difference into a summons, and the race that is ordered here is not a race for places but a race in deeds, so the reader is moved from where the face is turned to what the hands are doing. The sources draw out the point that the merit of a direction lies in the obedience it carries and not in the quarter of the sky, and that a community which is sure of its way should spend its strength on good rather than on dispute about the way. Wherever you are keeps the reader from tying the matter to one place or one journey, since the sentence reaches the man at home and the man on the road with the same word, and it prepares the gathering that the next words name. Allah will bring you all together for judgment is the answer to the scattering of the directions, and the sources read the gathering as the hour when the disputes will be settled by the One who knows what each community did with what it was given. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything closes the verse with the reason why the gathering is certain, since the One who gave each people its way is able to bring them all back to one place and to ask them about the way they took. The verse therefore answers the argument about the direction of prayer by handing the whole question to the day when nothing will be left unasked. The order of the verse is worth following, since the direction comes first and the deeds come after it, and the reader is told in that order that the way he face is a gift to be used and not a prize to be won, while the contest that is set before him is the contest of the good he does.

**Every community and its direction.**

For every nation there is a direction to which they face (in their prayers). (For every nation there is a direction to which they face (in their prayers) Abul-'Aliyah said, "The Jew has a direction to which he faces (in the prayer). The Christian has a direction to which he faces. Allah has guided you, O (Muslim) Ummah, to a Qiblah which is the true Qiblah. Hence, every nation and tribe has its own Qiblah that they choose, while Allah's appointed Qiblah is what the believers face." Every nation has a direction they turn to, whether physically or spiritually. For this reason, there is a difference between them in their directions of prayer and in their sacred laws. Every person of every community has his direction wijha his qibla to which he turns muwallīhā ‘he turns to it’ is also read as muwallāhā ‘he is made to turn to it’ in his prayers so vie with one another in good works strive with acts of obedience and acceptance of these.
