(And each one hath a goal) to each adherent of a religion a Qiblah (towards which he turneth) he faces according to his own whim; it is also said that this means: to each prophet a Qiblah, which is the Ka'bah, towards which he is ordered to face; (so vie with one another in good works) so hasten, O community of Muhammad, to perform acts of obedience more than any other nation.

**Compete with one another in good deeds.**

They should, indeed, give up fruitless controversies and strive to excel in good deeds, for they have to appear before Allah on the Day of Judgment when they will be rewarded or punished according to their deeds. Anyhow, once the divine commandment has been promulgated, the Muslims need not worry about the objections or the ridicule of others, but should, above all, concern themselves with the performance of good deeds (as defined by Allah and His Prophet). This steadfastness, too, is a blessing from Allah, and the blessing will appear in its perfect glory in the other world when the Muslims shall, as a reward for their faithfulness, be admitted to Paradise. For, the ability to do a good deed is a favour from Allah, and negligence in performing it amounts to ungratefulness and disrespect towards Allah. =Hence, it is to be feared that procrastination in this matter may be punished with a withdrawal of the divine favour, and that the culprit may altogether lose the ability to perform good deeds. When someone puts himself right in following MuṣṬafā, the candle of friendship with the Real will be lit in his road and he will never fall away from friendship's avenue. The change of qiblah, rather than denoting a change from one direction of worship to another, more sacred one, showed the completion of God’s guidance to mankind.

**Wherever you are, Allah will gather you.**

(Wheresoever you may be, Allah will bring you together (on the Day of Resurrection). Truly, Allah is able to do all things.) meaning: Allah will bring you together from wherever you may be on the Day of Judgement, to reward you according to what you have done. It is not difficult for Him to bring you all together and reward you. (Wheresoever you may be) on land or at sea, (Allah will bring you all together) gather you together and reward you for the good works you performed. Wherever you may be God will bring you all together gathering you on the Day of Resurrection and requiting you for your deeds; surely God has power over all things.

**Allah is Most Capable of everything.**

(Lo! Allah is Able to do all things) like gathering you together as well as other things. There is nothing wrong with them facing different directions if it is by Allah’s command and law, so try to outdo each other, O believers, in doing the good actions that you have been instructed to do. So, the verse ends with the rejoinder that on the Day of Judgment Allah shall bring all men together, and suggests that the desire to be safe from the criticism of others and the anxiety to win over them in disputes only betrays one's attachment to the temporal world, and that wisdom lies in caring more for what is everlasting. Since the Muslims can be sure of their right to a Qiblah peculiar to them, and the People of the Book are not expected to listen to reason, Allah asks the Muslims in this verse not to engage themselves in fruitless discussions and futile disputes, but to "strive, then, to excel in good deeds. Verse 145 has already indicated to the Muslims that although Allah has now appointed a new and permanent Qiblah for the whole of mankind, yet the Jews and the Christians are not going to give up their respective orientations, nor shall the Muslims ever forsake their own.

**The House of God that was appointed as the direction.**

When the Ka‘bah in Makkah was appointed as the prayer direction, or qiblah, the People of the Book started discussing whether the East was God’s direction or the West. They saw the matter as one of direction alone, but this was nothing other than sheer ignorance on their part. The selection of the House of God as the qiblah was not merely the specification of a certain direction for prayer; it was a sign that the time had come for God to reveal His greatest favour to man. The change of qiblah, rather than denoting a change from one direction of worship to another, more sacred one, showed the completion of God’s guidance to mankind. It had been decided a long time ago, that, in answer to the prayer of Abraham and Ishmael (see 2:129), God would send a final Prophet to the world. The bringing of religion to its final stage of perfection in Islam does not mean that previous religions were incomplete. What these men of good will tend to ignore is the elementary fact that the Word of Allah cannot be subservient to the rules of philosophical or literary composition, and that the reiteration of words and phrases, even of a sequence of sentences, is a regular mode of expression common to all the Sacred Books of the world. Before we leave the subject, let us remark that nowadays quite a good number of people, especially those with a Western formation, approach the Holy Qur'an as they do a book composed by a human author who pays due regard to what commonly passes as logic and sequential argument, and often do feel embarrassed or confused when they come across the close repetition of words and phrases in the Book of Allah, finding it impossible to explain or justify what is seemingly redundant.

Wherever you are O Prophet, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque repeats the command that was given earlier in the passage, and the sources take the repetition as a strengthening rather than as a new rule, since a matter that the Prophet is told three times over is a matter the community behind him is meant to keep. " The answer to this question is that Allah has chosen His Prophet to face Bayt Al-Maqdis first for certain wisdom, and he obeyed Allah regarding this command. Allah instructed you to face the Kaaba to perfect His blessings upon you, distinguishing you from all other communities and guiding you to the noblest direction of prayer. I will perfect My bounty on you by legislating for you to face the Ka'bah, so that the (Islamic) Shari'ah is complete in every respect. When the Ka‘bah in Makkah was appointed as the prayer direction, or qiblah, the People of the Book started discussing whether the East was God’s direction or the West. 151.text:
Since We have sent you a messenger from among yourselves. The verse names the sending as a favour, and it puts the messenger inside the community rather than above it, so that the one who speaks to them shares their language and their life. reciting to you Our revelations, purifying you. What he brings is first recited and then it cleans, and the order is kept, since the recitation is the means and the purifying is the effect it has on the one who listens. teaching you the Book and wisdom. The teaching is named twice in the verse, and here it is the Book together with the wisdom, which the sources take as the understanding of it and the right use of it, so that the reader is given both the text and the judgement that goes with it. and teaching you what you never knew. The last phrase states the ground of the whole favour, since what is taught is not an improvement on knowledge the community already had but knowledge that they had no way of reaching. The verse is the second half of what the passage has been building on, because the house that was made a centre and the direction that was appointed have already been spoken of, and the sending of a messenger from among them is named here as the other half of the same gift. The four phrases also follow the course of the message in a life, since it is heard, then it cleans what is inside the hearer, then it is taught, then it opens a door to what was closed. The verse closes the discussion of the direction on the same note, and it prepares for the command to remember and to give thanks that comes straight after it, since a people who have been given all this are the ones asked to answer it.

**What the sending of a messenger from among them carries.**

Allah blessed you in another way: sending a messenger to you from among you, who recites His verses, purifying you by directing you to virtue and goodness and forbidding you from evil and wrong, teaching you the Qur’ān and the Sunnah, and teaching you worldly and sacred knowledge which you did not know. Similarly (to complete My blessings on you), We have sent among you a Messenger (Muhammad) of your own, reciting to you Our verses (the Qur'an) and purifying you, and teaching you the Book (the Qur'an) and the Hikmah (i. e., Sunnah, Islamic laws and Fiqh jurisprudence), and teaching you that which you did not know Therefore remember Me (by praying, glorifying).

(Even as We have sent unto you a Messenger) remember Me as I have sent a Messenger (from among you) from your own lineage, (who reciteth unto you Our revelations) i.e. the Qur'an: its commands and prohibitions (and causeth you to grow) cleanses you of sin through divine Oneness, the poor-due, and alms, (and teacheth you the Scripture) the Qur'an (and wisdom) the lawful and the prohibited, (and teacheth you) of legal rulings, legal punishments and stories of bygone nations (that which ye knew not) before the revelation of the Qur'an and the advent of Muhammad ﷺ. Allah blessed you in another way: sending a messenger to you from among you, who recites His verses, purifying you by directing you to virtue and goodness and forbidding you from evil and wrong, teaching you the Qur’ān and the Sunnah, and teaching you worldly and sacred knowledge which you did not know. He recites to them the verses of the Qur'an; He teaches them the Book and the wisdom; He purifies them; He teaches them things which his listeners did not know of, nor could they be found in the earlier Divine Books or through individual reason.

He recites to them the verses of the Qur'an; He teaches them the Book and the wisdom; He purifies them; He teaches them things which his listeners did not know of, nor could they be found in the earlier Divine Books or through individual reason. (Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger (Muhammad) from among themselves, reciting unto them His verses (the Qur'an), and purifying them (from sins).)(3:164) (Similarly (to complete My favor on you), We have sent among you a Messenger (Muhammad) of your own,)

**What the prayer of Ibrahim asked for, and how it was granted.**

So, Verse 151 repeats the second part of the prayer of Sayyidna Ibrahim with which the discussion had begun (Verses 127 - 129). Now, Verse 151 declares that similarly the second request has also been granted, suggesting that since the Holy Prophet has been sent in answer to the prayer of the founder of the Ka'bah it is no wonder that it should be appointed as his Qiblah . It was at the time of the construction of the Ka‘bah that Abraham and Ishmael prayed for a prophet to be born among the people of Makkah. The prayer was answered, and the coming of the final prophet, whose focus would be Makkah, was decreed. Verse 151 has specifically mentioned that the new Prophet (Muhammad) is sent with the same attributes as specified by Sayyidna Ibrahim in his prayer, namely:

**What the blessing and the remembrance carry for the community.**

Since Allah has, in granting the two prayers, sent such great blessings to mankind, Verse 152 asks men to "remember" Him as the Supreme Benefactor, and to render Him thanks by being obedient. As long as they do so, Allah will "remember" them in showering on them His material and spiritual blessings. In this Ayah, Allah commands that He be thanked and appreciated, and promises even more rewards for thanking Him. (Those whom Allah has favored with a bounty, then Allah likes to see the effect of His bounty on His creation), or he said, "on His servant" - according to Ruh (one of the narrators of the Hadith). (Even as We have sent unto you a Messenger) remember Me as I have sent a Messenger (from among you) from your own lineage, (who reciteth unto you Our revelations) i.e. the Qur'an: its commands and prohibitions (and causeth you to grow) cleanses you of sin through divine Oneness, the poor-due, and alms, (and teacheth you the Scripture) the Qur'an (and wisdom) the lawful and the prohibited, (and teacheth you) of legal rulings, legal punishments and stories of bygone nations (that which ye knew not) before the revelation of the Qur'an and the advent of Muhammad ﷺ.

152.text:
remember Me; I will remember you. The command is put in the plainest words, and the promise is attached to it in the same sentence, so that the servant is told at once what is asked of him and what he is given for it. The remembering that is asked is not a matter of the tongue alone, since the sources take it as obedience to what has been commanded, and the remembering that is promised is the acceptance and the favour that answer it. And thank Me. The second command follows the first, because the favour that is being remembered is a blessing that has been received, and gratitude is the recognition of it. and never be ungrateful. The verse ends on the prohibition rather than on a further request, and the sources read that closing as a warning against denying what has been given, whether by word or by the life that is lived in the face of it. The two commands and the warning are short because the verse is the answer to what came before it, where the sending of a messenger from among the community was named as the gift. The verse therefore turns the account of the blessing into a duty, and it gives the duty a promise, which is the reason the sources dwell on it as a saying to keep close. What is asked is not a formal repetition of a name, since the sources explain the remembrance as obedience and the gratitude as the acknowledgement of the giver, and they warn that a tongue busy with a name while the life goes another way is not the remembrance meant here. The verse is thus one of the places where the passage turns from what Allah has done for the community to what the community owes back, and it does so in three clauses that a reader can carry with him.

**What remembering Allah means here.**

Dhikr : or "Remembrance" essentially pertains to the heart, but in so far as the tongue is the interpreter of the heart the oral recitation of a Divine Name or a verse of the Holy Qur'an is also described as Dhikr . In other words, oral Dhikr can be worth the name only when it is accompanied by the "remembrance" of the heart. (Therefore remember Me) through the performance of acts of obedience, (I will remember you) by granting you Paradise; and it is also said that this means: remember Me in time of ease, I will remember you in times of hardship. So, remember Allah with your hearts and your whole beings, and He will remember you with approval and protection, for you are rewarded according to what you do. This is to remember the lovingly kind Friend, the heart's ease and the spirit's food.

**What the promise that He will remember them carries.**

(Therefore remember Me. I will remember you), "Remember Me regarding what I have commanded you and I will remember you regarding what I have compelled Myself to do for your benefit (i.e., His rewards and forgiveness)." (Allah the Exalted said, 'O son of Adam! If you mention Me to yourself, I will mention you to Myself. If you mention Me in a gathering, I will mention you in a gathering of the angels (or said in a better gathering). If you draw closer to Me by a hand span, I will draw closer to you by forearm's length. If you draw closer to Me by a forearm's length, I will draw closer to you by an arm's length. And if you come to Me walking, I will come to you running). He replied that, according to the promise made in the Holy Qur'an, when a Muslim remembers Allah, He too remembers him, and thus everyone can know for himself that as soon as he turns to Allah and remembers Him, Allah too remembers him. (Allah the Exalted said, 'Whoever mentions Me to himself, then I will mention him to Myself; and whoever mentions Me in a gathering, I will mention him in a better gathering.)'.

**What it is to thank and to be grateful, and what the warning is against.**

(Give thanks to Me) for the blessings I bestowed upon you, (and reject not Me) do not stop giving thanks for these blessings. Also, be grateful to Allah for the blessings He has given you, and do not be ungrateful by denying them or using them in prohibited ways. (...and be grateful to Me (for My countless favors on you) and never be ungrateful to Me.) In this Ayah, Allah commands that He be thanked and appreciated, and promises even more rewards for thanking Him.

**Why the remembrance is a matter of the heart before the tongue.**

As the great Sufi poet Rumi points out, the recitation of a Divine Name can have no efficacy if one keeps thinking of cows and donkeys while repeating it mechanically with the tongue. "He who has not obeyed Him has not remembered Him, even though he has kept himself externally busy in offering (nafl : supererogatory) prayers and reciting His praises." Let us add that Verse 152 means to say that if men "remember" Allah by obeying His commandments, He will "remember" them by granting His pardon and His rewards. The commentator Said ibn Jubayr has, in fact, interpreted the Dhikr or "Remembrance" of Allah as obedience and submission to Him. This explanation is fully supported by a hadith cited by Al-Qurtubi on the authority of "Ahkam al-Qur'an " by Ibn Khuwayz Mandadh. The Holy Prophet has said that one who has been obeying Allah – that is, following the injunctions with regard to the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) - has truly been remembering Allah, in spite of being deficient in (nafl : supererogatory) prayers and fasting, while one who has been disobeying divine commandments has, in fact, forgotten Allah, in spite of devoting long hours to nafl prayers, fasting and recitation of His praises.

**What the great ones of this community carried about remembrance.**

The great Sufi Master Dhu al-Nun al-Misri has said that the man who remembers Allah in the full sense of the term forgets everything else, and that, in reward of such a total absorption, Allah Himself takes care of all his concerns, and grants him something far more valuable for everything he loses. And in a hadith reported by the blessed Companion Abu Hurayrah Allah Himself says that so long as the servant keeps remembering Him and his lips keep moving in Dhikr Allah is with him (for a more elaborate discussion of the subject, see Dhikrulldh by the author). This remembrance is the watering place for the tree of tawḤīd, the fruit and produce of which is friendship with the Real. This is why the Lord of the Worlds said, "My servant does not cease remembering Me, and I remembering him, until he is passionate for Me and I passionate for him. If one day you pass by the street of the Haqiqah and remember Him in your secret core, you will see "What no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what has never passed into the heart of any mortal.

**What the Prophet's own words carry about remembering.**

The Holy Prophet has said that one who has been obeying Allah – that is, following the injunctions with regard to the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) - has truly been remembering Allah, in spite of being deficient in (nafl : supererogatory) prayers and fasting, while one who has been disobeying divine commandments has, in fact, forgotten Allah, in spite of devoting long hours to nafl prayers, fasting and recitation of His praises. (Allah the Exalted said, 'O son of Adam! If you mention Me to yourself, I will mention you to Myself. If you mention Me in a gathering, I will mention you in a gathering of the angels (or said in a better gathering). If you draw closer to Me by a hand span, I will draw closer to you by forearm's length. If you draw closer to Me by a forearm's length, I will draw closer to you by an arm's length. And if you come to Me walking, I will come to you running). (And (remember) when your Lord proclaimed: "If you give thanks (by accepting faith and worshipping none but Allah), I will give you more (of My blessings); but if you are thankless (i.e., disbelievers), verily, My punishment is indeed severe.)(14:7)

153.text:
O believers, Seek comfort in patience and prayer. The address comes to the community as believers, and the verse does not ask them first for argument or for defence, since the passage they have just heard has been answering objections and they are the ones who have to live with the answers. The help they are told to seek is named as comfort, so what is offered is a support to lean on rather than a weapon to use. Two things are named together, patience and prayer, and the sources take them as a remedy prescribed for a situation and not as a general counsel, since the community had been under pressure from people who would not stop arguing and the verse answers the weariness that follows. Patience is the larger of the two words here, and the sources explain that it covers more than the endurance of hardship. It is the keeping of oneself under control in three directions: holding back from what has been forbidden, staying steady in the duties of worship, and bearing the troubles that come without turning from the path. Prayer is named separately although patience already covers the acts of worship, and the sources give the reason, that prayer is the clearest form of the restraint being asked for, since a person who stands in it binds himself to obedience at a fixed time and turns away from what he would otherwise be doing. Allah is truly with those who are patient. The verse closes on that promise, and it is a promise of company and help rather than of ease, since the sources read the company of Allah as His aid and protection for the one who keeps faith. The two halves of the verse therefore answer each other, the command with its method and the promise with its guarantee, and the reader is left with a remedy he can use in the situation the passage has described.

**What the word patience carries in this verse.**

The Arabic term Sabr is much more comprehensive than its usual English equivalent, "patience". Lexically, the word "Sabr" signifies "restraining oneself, or keeping oneself under control. There are several types of Sabr patience: one for avoiding the prohibitions and sins, one for acts of worship and obedience. Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam said, "Sabr has two parts: patience for the sake of Allah concerning what He is pleased with (i.e., acts of worship and obedience), even if it is hard on the heart and the body, and patience when avoiding what He dislikes, even if it is desired. O you who believe seek help regarding the Hereafter through patience in obedience and afflictions and prayer He singles it out for mention on account of its frequency and its greatness; surely God is with the patient helping them. (O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness) to fulfil the obligations of Allah and to abstain from contraventions and shameful works (and prayer) and with abundant supererogatory prayers at night and during the day in order to come clean from sin.

**What the Sabr of the Qur'an is, and its modes.**

" In the terminology of the Holy Qur'an and the Hadith, Sabr has three modes: Lexically, the word "Sabr" signifies "restraining oneself, or keeping oneself under control. People generally identify Sabr with the third mode alone, and ignore the first two which are, indeed, more basic and essential. There are several types of Sabr patience: one for avoiding the prohibitions and sins, one for acts of worship and obedience. Restraining oneself from what the Shari'ah has declared to be illegal or impermissible (Haram). Forcing oneself to be regular in the observance of the different forms of worship and to be steadfast in obeying the commandments of Allah and the Holy Prophet . To endure all kinds of trouble and pain - in other words, to understand clearly and to believe that it is the will of Allah to make one suffer, and to hope that one shall receive a reward for this suffering.

**What the Salah named here is.**

As for the second ingredient of the prescription, it is Salah (Prayer). Salah however, has been mentioned separately, because that is the most perfect model of Sabr . For, in the state of Salah ; one binds oneself to obedience and worship, and restrains oneself not only from all that is sinful or reprehensible but even from what is otherwise permissible - e.g., from eating or drinking or talking. Hence, Salah is a visible demonstration of Sabr which signifies keeping oneself under control in shunning everything sinful and in submitting oneself totally to obedience. Allah has stated that the best tools to help ease the effects of the afflictions are patience and prayer.

**What is promised to those who are patient.**

And the method consists in turning to patience and prayers; for Allah assures us here that He is with those who are patient. It is said that the patient are entitled to the ultimate treasures and the highest ranks inasmuch as they have attained the company maʿiyya of God most high who said Surely God is with maʿa the patient. Those who acquire these qualities will be among the patient persons whom Allah shall greet (when they meet Him in the Hereafter; refer to Surat Al-Ahzab 33:44), Allah willing." " That is to say, as a reward for Sabr man receives the honour of the "company" of Allah. (Lo! Allah is with the steadfast) He helps, and protects the steadfast from shameful works.

**What is promised to the Sabirun.**

According to the Hadith, people will hear a call on the Day of Judgment, "Where are the Sabirun ?"; at this, those who had been constant in observing the three forms of Sabr will stand up, and they will be allowed to enter Paradise without having to present the account of their deeds. In the terminology of Holy Qur'an and the Hadith, Al-Sabirun is the title of those who are steadfast in observing all the three forms with equal rigour. "The Sabirun shall certainly receive their full reward without reckoning. In citing this hadith, Ibn Kathir points out that it is corroborated by the Holy Qur'an itself: ‌ ‌ ‌ :

**What the enemies of Islam and the Muslims faced.**

As we have already seen, the enemies of Islam have been objecting to the change in the ‘orientation of Qiblah wishing to produce in the minds of the people doubts about the validity of Islam as a religion. But some of the enemies simply ignored the answers, and still persisted in their hostility. This situation was likely to dishearten the Muslims. So, the present verse nullifies such a re-action on the part of the Muslims by prescribing the method of overcoming one's grief or anxiety. In explaining the context, we have mentioned a specific situation, but the verse, in fact, identifies the elixir for all the ills which are a necessary part of human existence, whether they be wants and needs, or anxiety and suffering.

154.text:
Never say that those martyred in the cause of Allah are dead, in fact, they are alive. The verse addresses the believers and it rules out a way of speaking rather than a belief, which tells the reader that the words a community uses about its dead are part of what it is being taught. The people in view are those killed in the path of Allah, so the sentence is about a death that carries no shame and no loss of standing. The verse corrects the statement at once and without a pause, and the sources take the life named here as a real one that continues after the body has gone, not as a figure of speech for the good name a person leaves behind. they are alive. The words are repeated in the sources as the heart of the verse, and the commentaries gather under it what they carry of the state of the martyrs, who are described as provided for and to move about as they wish. But you do not perceive it. The last clause explains why the correction was needed, since the life being described is not one the eye can reach, and it puts the limit on the perception of the living rather than on the life of the dead. The verse therefore carries two things at once: a plain prohibition that keeps the community from speaking of its martyrs as it speaks of its ordinary dead, and a statement of a life that continues, which the sources divide into the general life given to everyone after death and the greater share given to those who die in the path of Allah. It comes straight after the command to seek help in patience, and it belongs with it, since a community that is told to endure hardship is here told what becomes of those who do not return from it.

**What the verse tells the believers about calling them dead.**

Allah thereafter mentions the saying of the hypocrites apropos the martyrs of Badr, Uhud and all the other battles: " So-and-so has died and lost all comfort and happiness " , this in order to aggravate sincere believers, and so Allah says: And say not of those slain in God’s way that ‘They are dead’; rather they are living their spirits are according to a hadīth contained in green birds that take wing freely wherever they wish in Paradise; but you are not aware but you do not know their condition. (And say not of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Nay, they are living,) indicates that the martyrs are alive and receiving their sustenance. Do not say, O believers, about those who are killed whilst striving in Allah’s path that they are dead just as others are; rather, they are alive with their Lord, but you do not realise that they are living, because the way in which they are alive can only be understood through revelation from Allah.

**What the life of the martyrs is.**

(Nay they are living) they are rather living like those living in Paradise, being provided with comfort and bounties, (only ye perceive not) you are not aware of the honour bestowed upon them or of their real state. One who dies in the cause of Allah is a Shahid (Martyr) and, although, it is correct and even allowed to call him "dead", yet we are forbidden to regard their death like ordinary deaths. The distinction a Shahid has over others in Barzakh is that in effect, for the fullness and sensitivity of life, his perception is, keener and deeper. The life of this world has left them behind, but they have reached endless life.12 What have they lost by being released from this world's abasement? (And say not of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Nay, they are living,) indicates that the martyrs are alive and receiving their sustenance.

**What the general life after death is, and how the martyrs stand in it.**

According to Islamic traditions the dead person is given some kind of a "new life" in Barzakh44 which develops in him a sensitivity to punishment and reward. Regardless of whether one is a believer or disbeliever, virtuous or vicious, this taste of life-in-Barzakh is given to everybody. An intermediary stage which begins with death and stretches till the Doomsday. For, though, life in Barzakh is given to' everybody which gives him perception of reward and punishment but Shahid in the Barzakh life is qualitatively different from the one given to other persons. Consequently, a Shahid's body does not waste away, decay or mingle with dust. They are, therefore, reported as living and we are forbidden to call them dead.

**What was promised to the martyrs, and how they are provided for.**

(The souls of the martyrs are inside green birds and move about in Paradise wherever they wish. Then, they take refuge in lamps that are hanging under the Throne (of Allah). Your Lord looked at them and asked them, 'What do you wish for?' They said, 'What more could we wish for while You have favored us with what You have not favored any other of your creation?' He repeated the question again. When they realize that they will be asked (until they answer), they said, 'We wish that You send us back to the earthly life, so that we fight in Your cause until we are killed in Your cause again,' (because of what they enjoy of the rewards of martyrdom). The Lord then said, 'I have written that they will not be returned to it (earthly life) again.) Thus, the fact that the Qur'an mentions the martyrs in particular in the above Ayah serves to honor, glorify and favor them (although the other believers share the rewards they enjoy). As, for instance, the life sensation is there in finger tips, as also, it is there in heels, but the sensitivity of finger tips is sharper than that of heels. The effect of the finer life-quality of a Shahid in Barzakh reaches his physical body as well; whereas ordinarily bodies remain unaffected. On the contrary it retains it freshness and a semblance of being alive too. This is duly endorsed by Ahadith and observations.

155.text:
We will certainly test you with a touch of fear and famine and loss of property, life, and crops. The sentence is put as a promise and not as a threat, and the testing is described as something that will certainly come, so the believer is prepared for it instead of being surprised by it. The word for a touch keeps the trials within measure, and the sources take it as a little of each kind, since what is named is not the whole of a person's fear or the whole of his hunger but a portion of it. The troubles are listed as a series. Fear comes first, and it is the fear of an enemy, which reaches a person before anything has been taken from him. Famine follows, and the sources read it as drought and hunger. Then loss of property, which the sources explain as wealth that is destroyed in part. Then life, and the losses named there are the deaths of friends, relatives and those who are loved. Then crops, which the sources explain as gardens and farms that do not produce what they used to produce. The list therefore moves from what a person feels, to what he owns, to the living things he loves most, and it ends with what feeds him, so that no area of a life is left outside the promise. Give good news to those who patiently endure. The command stands at the head of a verse full of trouble and it asks for good news to be given, not received, which tells the reader that the patience being asked for is already the beginning of something good. The verse is placed here after the command to seek comfort in patience and prayer and after the account of those who are alive although they have been killed, so it belongs to a passage teaching a community how to stand under pressure. The news that is to be given is left to the verses that follow, which name the blessings and the mercy and the guidance, and the effect of the order is that the promise of trouble is read together with the promise that follows it.

**What the test is, and why it is promised here.**

Allah informs us that He tests and tries His servants, just as He said in another Ayah: (And surely, We shall try you till We test those who strive hard (for the cause of Allah) and As-Sabirin (the patient), and We shall test your facts (i.e., the one who is a liar, and the one who is truthful).)(47:31) Hence, He tests them with the bounty sometimes and sometimes with the afflictions of fear and hunger. This world has not been created for reward: it has been created for the trial of man. This world being a testing ground, God’s servants face obstacles in their path so that the earnest among them may be distinguished from those who are not serious and sincere. Earlier, alluding to an unpleasant incident, patience and steadfastness were inculcated and the excellence of Sabirun (the patient people) was mentioned. (And surely We shall try you) test you (with something of fear) fear of the enemy (and hunger) in the years of drought, (and loss of wealth and lives) through killing, death and illnesses (and crops) and the loss of crops;. Allah will test people with different types of hardships: some with fear of those who are against them; hunger because of lack of food; lack of money because of losing it or difficulty gaining it; loss of lives due to death from diseases and tragedies that kill people, or being martyred for the sake of Allah; and a lack of resources from the earth.

**What the fear, the hunger and the losses mean.**

(with something of fear, hunger,) meaning, a little of each. (loss of wealth,) meaning, some of the wealth will be destroyed,. (lives) meaning, losing friends, relatives and loved ones to death,. (and fruits,) meaning, the gardens and the farms will not produce the usual or expected amounts. Surely We will try you with something of fear of an enemy and hunger by way of drought and diminution of goods as a result of destruction and lives as a result of slaughter death and disease and fruits by way of crop damage that is to say We will try you to see if you practise patience or not; yet give good tidings of Paradise to the patient during calamities;. And certainly, We shall test you with something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits, but give glad tidings to As-Sabirin (the patient)Who, when afflicted with calamity, say:

**What is given to the patient when the affliction strikes.**

(but give glad tidings to As-Sabirin (the patient).) He then explained whom He meant by 'the patient' whom He praised: (Who, when afflicted with calamity, say: "Truly, to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return.") meaning, those who recite this statement to comfort themselves in the face of their loss, know that they belong to Allah and that He does what He wills with His servants. (They are those on whom are the Salawat (i. e., who are blessed and will be forgiven) from their Lord, and (they are those who) receive His mercy,) meaning, Allah's praise and mercy will be with them. (They are those on whom are the Salawat from their Lord, and (they are those who) receive His mercy) are the two righteous things. The heights means more rewards, and these people will be awarded their rewards and more. Those who do not waver from the path despite all the difficulties it presents—who stay with God even when no worldly benefit seems to accrue therefrom—are the ones who will finally emerge successful from the trials of life.

**What is carried in the words of belonging and return.**

"Truly, to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return. They also know that nothing and no deed, even if it was the weight of an atom, will be lost with Allah on the Day of Resurrection. These facts thus compel them to admit that they are Allah's servants and that their return will be to Him in the Hereafter. (and it is they who are the guided ones.) 'Umar bin Al-Khattab commented: There are several Ahadith that mention the rewards of admitting that the return is to Allah by saying: ("Truly, to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return.") when afflictions strike. I heard Allah's Messenger recite a statement that made me delighted.

**What Allah compensated Umm Salamah with.**

For instance, Imam Ahmad reported that Umm Salamah narrated: Once, Abu Salamah came back after he was with Allah's Messenger and said: (No Muslim is struck with an affliction and then says Istirja' when the affliction strikes, and then says: 'O Allah! Reward me for my loss and give me what is better than it,' but Allah will do just that.) When Abu Salamah died I said Istirja' and said: (As for the jealousy that you mentioned, Allah the Exalted will remove it from you. As for your being old as you mentioned, I have suffered what you have suffered. And for your having children, they are my children too.) She said, "I have surrendered to Allah's Messenger.

**What this world is, and what it has not been made for.**

But peace and happiness will materialize in their complete form only in the next eternal world. This world being a testing ground, God’s servants face obstacles in their path so that the earnest among them may be distinguished from those who are not serious and sincere. This world has not been created for reward: it has been created for the trial of man. There is only one way to succeed in the trials of life, and that is through patience and prayer. This entails attaching oneself to God and conscientiously adhering to the path of truth, enduring all the setbacks that afflict one on the way. God has reserved the eternal blessings of the next life for those who show themselves willing to sacrifice this life for the next. Those verses give preference to the theme of war with infidels over other themes for two reasons: first, the sacrifice of life is a grand sacrifice; whoever steadfastly endures this loss will, undoubtedly, learn to be patient on losses of lesser magnitude; second, it is relevant to the situation too, as the objectionist on the orientation of Ka'bah had been facing it. Give good news, O Prophet, to those who are patient in the face of these hardships, of what will make them happy in this world and in the Afterlife.

who, when faced with a disaster, say. The verse describes the people who were given the good news, and it describes them by what they say rather than by what they feel, which keeps the emphasis on the words a person puts into his mouth at the hardest moment. The disaster is named in the singular and it covers whatever comes, great or small, since the sources take the verse as the definition of the saying in every calamity. Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we will all return. The sentence is the whole of the verse, and the sources explain why it works. The first half states that a person and everything he cares for are the property of Allah, so what has been taken was never his to keep in the first place. The second half states that the return is to Allah, so what has been lost has not gone away into nothing but has gone ahead of him. The two halves together are therefore a confession of ownership and a statement of destination, and they are spoken in the plural, in the first person, so that a person speaks them of himself and of everything that belongs to him. This is the saying the sources call the istirjāʿ, and they treat it as the mark of the patient, since it is the point at which the heart agrees with the tongue that nothing has been lost that was not lent. The verse stands between the promise of testing and the account of the blessings that the patient are to be given, so it supplies the words that carry a person from the hardship to the reward. It also reaches back to the verse before it, where the good news was commanded, and forward to what follows, where the mercy and the guidance are named, so that the small sentence is the hinge of the passage.

**Whoever gives wealth, self or spirit for His sake.**

The verse names the people it has just described, and it hands them three things, the blessings, the mercy and the guidance, so that the reader sees what the patient are given rather than only what they were asked to bear. **Where the patience of these people came from.**

They attained their patience and their ability to withstand the demands of the divine decree from His prior blessings to them. It was not because of their patience or their endurance that they arrived at His blessings for if not for His pre-eternal mercy their obedience would not have arisen through the condition of servitude for His prior solicitude is what brought pure guidance to them. Because He blessed them in the beginning lammā raḥimahum fī l-bidāya they were guided in the end ihtadaw fī l-nihāya. The suggestion is that this is what the patient people should say as it brings excellent reward, relieves from the burden of sorrow and suffering and consoles effectively the grieved heart.

**What Allah gave Umm Salamah in place of what she lost.**

Once, Abu Salamah came back after he was with Allah's Messenger and said: Compensate me for my loss and give me what is better than it. " Allah's Messenger married her and Umm Salamah said later, "Allah compensated me with who is better than Abu Salamah: (As for the jealousy that you mentioned, Allah the Exalted will remove it from you. As for your being old as you mentioned, I have suffered what you have suffered. And for your having children, they are my children too.) She said, "I have surrendered to Allah's Messenger.

158.text:
Indeed, the hills of Ṣafa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. The two hills are named as belonging to the marks of the religion, so what follows is not a new practice being introduced but the placing of an established place under the name of Allah. So whoever performs the pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage. The two visits are named together, the greater and the lesser, and the verse therefore covers both of the journeys in which the walking is done. let them walk between the two hills. The command is given in the form of a permission and it carries an obligation, and the sources spend their attention on that form, because the people being addressed had held back from the walk and the verse had to remove what held them back. And whoever does good willingly. The verse then widens from the one act to any good a person does beyond what is required, and the sources read the word as covering the voluntary beyond the prescribed. Allah is truly Appreciative, All-Knowing. The two names at the end answer the two halves of the verse, since the Appreciative acknowledges the smallest act and the All-Knowing knows what was done and by whom, so a person need not fear that a hidden deed will go unnoticed. The verse sits inside the passage that has dealt with the direction of prayer and with the House, and it turns from the building to the walking done at its side, so that the whole account of the pilgrimage is held together. The sources also tie the command to the story of the woman who ran between these same hills looking for water, and the walk is kept as a remembrance of that search, which is why the rulings attached to it are discussed at such length.

**What the hills and the rites mean here.**

Allah has stated that Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah is among the symbols of Allah, meaning, among the acts that Allah legislated during the Hajj for Prophet Ibrahim. (Lo! Al-Safa and al-Marwah) going around al-Safa and al-Marwah (are among the rites of Allah) among the rites of pilgrimage that Allah, Exalted is He, has commanded. The two mountains known as Ṣafā and Marwah, near to the Kaaba, are landmarks of the clear sacred law. So, the "Sha a'ir of Allah" signify what He has determined to be the marks of Islamic faith. The present verse opens with the solemn declaration that the two hills, Safa and Marwah adjoining the Ka'bah in Makkah, are tangible signs from Allah. When Muslims perform the pilgrimage to Makkah, they repeat Hajar’s historic quest between these hills, thus commemorating the profound relevance of the event to everyone who struggles in the path of God.

**Why the Muslims had hesitated over the walk.**

Those who assumed Ihlal for Manat, used to hesitate to perform Tawaf (going) between Mounts As-Safa and Al-Marwah. So they (during the Islamic era) asked Allah's Messenger about it, saying, 'O Messenger of Allah! During the time of Jahiliyyah, we used to hesitate to perform Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.' Allah then revealed: Ash-Sha'bi said, "Isaf (an idol) was on As-Safa while Na'ilah (an idol) was on Al-Marwah, and they used to touch (or kiss) them. After Islam came, they were hesitant about performing Tawaf between them. By clarifying that there was no fault in this action, Allah was comforting those Muslims who avoided walking between the mountains because they feared it was an unacceptable action from the time of ignorance before Islam; but Allah made it clear that the walking between the mountains was an acceptable act of Hajj. Allah then mentions the believers' dislike of going between al-Safa and al-Marwah in front of the idols which were placed there, saying:

**What the earlier practice of the walk was.**

Pilgrims walk briskly between them after they have made the tawaf of the Holy Ka'bah . This act of walking briskly or "making rounds" between them, as the Qur'an elects to call it, is known as Sayee a practice which was there even in the Jahiliyyah and which made Muslims doubt its propriety. Earlier we mentioned the Hadith by Ibn 'Abbas that the origin of Tawaf comes from the Tawaf of Hajar (Prophet Ibrahim's wife), between As-Safa and Al-Marwah seeking water for her son (Isma'il) Ibrahim had left them in Makkah, where there was no habitation for her. When Hajar feared that her son would die, she stood up and begged Allah for His help and kept going back and forth in that blessed area between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. Distressed, she ran back and forth between the hills of Safa and Marwah. There she found a spring, now known as the spring of Zamzam, flowing from the ground. When Muslims perform the pilgrimage to Makkah, they repeat Hajar’s historic quest between these hills, thus commemorating the profound relevance of the event to everyone who struggles in the path of God.

**Who performs the walk, and in which visit.**

The present verse opens with the solemn declaration that the two hills, Safa and Marwah adjoining the Ka'bah in Makkah, are tangible signs from Allah. The question related to all those idols sitting on top of the Safa and Marwah hills and it was to show their devotion to them that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do say between Safa and Marwah and in which case, this practice should be haram (forbidden). So it is not a sin on him who performs Hajj or 'Umrah (pilgrimage) of the House to perform Tawaf between them. (Verily, As-Safa and Al-Marwah (two mountains in Makkah) are of the symbols of Allah. So it is not a sin on him who performs Hajj or 'Umrah (pilgrimage) of the House (the Ka'bah at Makkah) to perform the going (Tawaf) between them (As-Safa and Al-Marwah).) Lexically, Hajj means to aim, to intend; while, in the terminology of the Qur'an and Hadith, the act of deciding to go solely on a pilgrimage of the House of Allah and performing required rites while there, is called the Hajj. Lexically, Umrah means ziyarah or pilgrimage; while, in the terminology of the Shari'ah, the visit to al-Masjid al-Haram and the doing of tawaf and Sayee there is called Umrah.

**What the accounts carry about the pacing between the two.**

(Perform Sa'i, for Allah has prescribed Sa'i on you.)'" This Hadith was used as a proof for the fact that Sa'i is a Rukn of Hajj. It was also said that Sa'i is Wajib, and not a Rukn of Hajj and that if one does not perform it by mistake or by intention, he could expiate the shortcoming with Damm. It is reported from Ibn ‘Abbās that this pacing between the two is not obligatory based on the fact that when no sin can be incurred the context implies free choice. The Prophet made clear its obligatory aspect when he said that ‘God has prescribed for you the pacing sa‘y’ as reported by al-Bayhaqī and others; and he the Prophet also said ‘Begin with what God has begun’ meaning al-Safā as reported by Muslim; and whoever volunteers tatawwa‘a a variant reading is yattawa‘ the ta’ here being assimilated good that is any good deed such as circumambulation or other that is not obligatory on him; God is Grateful for such a deed and rewards that person for it Knowing it. It may be noted that Sayee is a mustahabb (desirable or commendable) practice of the Holy Prophet according to Imam Ahmad ; a fard (absolute obligation) according to Imams Malik and Shafi i ; and a wajib (necessity) according to Imam Abu Hanifah which means, one who abandons it would have to slaughter a goat in compensation.

**What Allah rewards and acknowledges.**

(...then verily, Allah is All-Recognizer, All-Knower.) meaning, Allah's reward is immense for the little deed, and He knows about the sufficiency of the reward. Hence, He will not award insufficient rewards to anyone. (Surely, Allah wrongs not even of the weight of an atom, but if there is any good (done), He doubles it, and gives from Him a great reward.)(4:40) Allah accepts the smallest of your works and His reward is abundant. Whoever sincerely does what is recommended of voluntary sacred acts, Allah acknowledges them and rewards them. And whoever does good voluntarily, then verily, Allah is All-Recognizer, All-Knower.

159.text:
Those who hide the clear proofs and guidance that We have revealed. The verse names a group by what they do with what they were given, and the two things they hide are named together, the proofs and the guidance, so the concealment covers both the evidence and the direction it points to. The proofs are the signs that establish the truth of the messenger, and the guidance is the way the Book sets out, which the sources explain as the commands and prohibitions and the accounts that were in the earlier scriptures. after We made it clear for humanity in the Book. The clause removes every excuse, since the matter was not left doubtful but was set out plainly, and the sources keep it clear that the setting out was for humanity and not for one community, so what is hidden is a public thing. will be condemned by Allah and all those who condemn. The sentence states the outcome plainly, and it names two sources of the curse, the Lord and the whole creation that prays against those who hide, so the person who keeps back what he was given is opposed by everything that has been made. The verse stands after the account of the direction and the house and the walk between the hills, all of which concerned people who had been given the Book before them, and it turns from their argument about a rite to the larger charge, that they had kept back what their own scriptures carried. The warning is therefore attached to a specific occasion and to a standing offence, since the sources carry it of the scholars of the earlier communities and then draw out of it a rule about knowledge that must not be withheld. The verses that follow turn from the concealers to those who turn back to Allah, and the whole passage is built on that division.

**What they hide, and who hides it.**

Those Jews and Christians who hide the clear proofs which Allah revealed showing the truth of the Prophet and what he brought, after Allah had made it clear to the people in their scriptures, Allah removes them from His mercy; and all the angels, the prophets and people call for them to be removed from His mercy. This was revealed about the scholars of the people of the Book and their concealment of the verse of stoning [the adulterers who are married] and the matter of Muhammad, Allah bless him and give him peace. (Those who hide the proofs) the commands, prohibitions and the signs mentioned in the Torah (and the guidance) i.e. the description given there of Muhammad ﷺ and his feature (which We revealed) exposited, (after We had made it clear) to the Children of Israel (in the Scripture) in the Torah: And, in fact, a group of them does conceal the truth while they know." Now the text, in order to conclude the subject, warns those who not only conceal the truth but, going further ahead in obstinacy, persist in their effort.

**What the proofs and the guidance are.**

(Those who hide the proofs) the commands, prohibitions and the signs mentioned in the Torah (and the guidance) i.e. the description given there of Muhammad ﷺ and his feature (which We revealed) exposited, (after We had made it clear) to the Children of Israel (in the Scripture) in the Torah: Those Jews and Christians who hide the clear proofs which Allah revealed showing the truth of the Prophet and what he brought, after Allah had made it clear to the people in their scriptures, Allah removes them from His mercy; and all the angels, the prophets and people call for them to be removed from His mercy. Those who conceal the clear proofs and the guidance that We have revealed after We have shown them clearly in the scripture-they shall be cursed by God and by those who curse This verse alludes to those to whom the Real has unveiled knowledge of the good manners ādāb of traveling but who have become stingy in revealing [this knowledge] to aspirants [who seek] advice and guidance. The following was revealed concerning the Jews Those who conceal from people the clear proofs and the guidance that We have revealed such as the ‘stoning’ verse and the description of Muhammad after We have shown them clearly in the Scripture the Torah — they shall be cursed by God that is He will move them far away from His mercy and by the cursers the angels believers or by every single thing when they supplicate that they be cursed. "Those whom We have given the Book recognize him (The Holy Prophet) as they recognize their own sons.

**What the accursed are described by.**

(such are accursed of Allah) Allah will torment them in the grave (and are accursed of those who have the power to curse) all created beings, save human beings and jinn, will curse them upon hearing their screams from the grave. The following was revealed concerning the Jews Those who conceal from people the clear proofs and the guidance that We have revealed such as the ‘stoning’ verse and the description of Muhammad after We have shown them clearly in the Scripture the Torah — they shall be cursed by God that is He will move them far away from His mercy and by the cursers the angels believers or by every single thing when they supplicate that they be cursed. Those who conceal the clear proofs and the guidance that We have revealed after We have shown them clearly in the scripture-they shall be cursed by God and by those who curse This verse alludes to those to whom the Real has unveiled knowledge of the good manners ādāb of traveling but who have become stingy in revealing [this knowledge] to aspirants [who seek] advice and guidance. Verse 159 above stated that concealing from people clear signs and guidance revealed by Allah Almighty is a terrible crime which earns the curse of Allah Almighty Himself, as well as that of His entire creation.

**What is carried about those who conceal.**

This was revealed about the scholars of the people of the Book and their concealment of the verse of stoning [the adulterers who are married] and the matter of Muhammad, Allah bless him and give him peace. Verse 159 above stated that concealing from people clear signs and guidance revealed by Allah Almighty is a terrible crime which earns the curse of Allah Almighty Himself, as well as that of His entire creation. The ultimate fate of this senseless persistence being all too obvious, Allah Almighty still extends the promise of His mercy and forgiveness to those who repent and reflect on what they did, retrace their steps and correct their negative attitude towards divine truth and, in order to demonstrate their positive stand, come forward and state the truth clearly and publicly. The natural consequence of such a reformed attitude would be that they will enter the fold of Islam believing in Allah and His prophet, which is the touchstone for any disbeliever's honest change of heart. One fears for them that the blessing will be removed from their knowledge when they fall short in it just as they held back in imparting [that knowledge] to the deserving.

**What the jurists drew from it.**

According to the fuqaha' (Muslim jurists), this warning applies to a person who is the only one available in a given situation. It is for this reason that Muslim jurists, while discussing such questions in writing, conclude with a standard warning tag of which means that the question under discussion is sensitive, therefore, a scholar should limit it to his comprehension and refrain from broadcasting it in public. This will not be considered as 'concealment of knowledge' since what is not allowed is the concealment of clear guidance given in the Qur'an and Sunnah which it is rather necessary to disclose and disseminate widely. The expression of clear signs and guidance" in this verse releases a strong suggestion to this effect. It is forbidden to conceal knowledge which must be disclosed and disseminated widely.

**What knowledge must not be withheld, and from whom.**

"Anyone who is asked about something (of religion) which he knows would, in the event that he conceals it, be brought forth by Allah on the Doomsday harnessed with a rein of fire. " (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah and Amr ibn al-'As and reported by Ibn Majah - Qurtubi) As reported in Sahih al-Bukhari, Sayyidna Ali has said: 'Disclose to the common people only that much of knowledge as they have the capacity to understand. Do you want them to deny Allah and His Messenger ?' For, anything beyond their comprehension would breed doubts in their minds and the possibility is there that they may refuse to accept it. "Do not withhold wisdom from those who deserve it, for if you do so, you will be unjust to them; and do not place it before those who do not deserve it, for if you do so, you will be unjust to it." These narrations tell us that in the view of the blessed Companions, the Hadith of the Holy Prophet enjoys some privileges mentioned in relation to the Qur'an.

160.text:
As for those who repent, mend their ways, and let the truth be known. The verse picks up the threat that came before it and opens a door in it, and it names three things that have to be done together, the turning back, the putting right, and the making known. The repentance is the return from the act, and the sources explain the amending as the correction of what was done, so the two are not the same and the verse asks for both. The third belongs to this passage in particular, since the act the previous verse described was a concealment, and what ends it is that what was hidden is brought out openly. they are the ones to whom I will turn in forgiveness. The sentence is put in the first person, so the acceptance comes from the Lord himself and not from anybody else, and the turning named here is the answer to the turning of the servant. for I am the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful. The verse ends with the two names that carry the promise, and the sources take the order as the reaching of the mercy to the one who comes back, so the door is left open while the warning stands. The verse is therefore the exception attached to the warning, and the reader is shown that the way out of the curse is a turning that a person makes and then makes known.

**What repentance and amending mean here.**

Except those that repent turning back from such deeds and make amends in their actions and show clearly what they were concealing — them I shall turn relenting accepting their repentance; I am the Relenting the Merciful to believers. The exception is those who repent to Allah, asking for forgiveness, and regretting having hidden these clear signs, correcting what they do outwardly and inwardly, and making clear the truth and guidance which they had hidden. Except those that repent and make amends and show clearly-them I shall turn [relenting]; I am the Relenting the Merciful. [Except those who] compensate for their past negligence by graciously turning back taking on the task of giving advice to the aspirants. (Except such of them as repent) from Judaism (and amend) worship Allah alone without ascribing to Him any partners (and make manifest) the traits and description of Muhammad. This Ayah refers to those who regret what they have been doing and correct their behavior and, thus, explain to the people what they have been hiding.

**What it is to show the truth clearly.**

Except those that repent and make amends and show clearly-them I shall turn [relenting]; I am the Relenting the Merciful. [Except those who] compensate for their past negligence by graciously turning back taking on the task of giving advice to the aspirants. Surely the clearest proof of the clarity of your actions and the truest tes timony of that by which you call people to God is that your behavior does not contradict what you have alluded to in your speech. (Except those who repent and do righteous deeds, and openly declare (the truth which they concealed).) The exception is those who repent to Allah, asking for forgiveness, and regretting having hidden these clear signs, correcting what they do outwardly and inwardly, and making clear the truth and guidance which they had hidden. (Except such of them as repent) from Judaism (and amend) worship Allah alone without ascribing to Him any partners (and make manifest) the traits and description of Muhammad.

**What the Most Merciful and the Accepter of Repentance carry.**

And I am the One Who accepts repentance, the Most Merciful Verily, those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers, it is they on whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, combined They will abide therein (under the curse in Hell), their punishment will neither be lightened nor will they be reprieved. (These it is towards whom I relent) overlook their past transgressions. (I am the Relenting) towards those who repent, (the Merciful) towards him who dies in a state of repentance. He turns to those who turn to Him, asking for forgiveness and regretting what they have done, and He forgives and is compassionate with them.

**What the verse carries about those who hide knowledge.**

It is forbidden to conceal knowledge which must be disclosed and disseminated widely. "Anyone who is asked about something (of religion) which he knows would, in the event that he conceals it, be brought forth by Allah on the Doomsday harnessed with a rein of fire. (Whoever was asked about knowledge that one has, but he hid it, then a bridle made of fire will be tied around his mouth on the Day of Resurrection.) It is also recorded by Al-Bukhari that Abu Hurayrah said, "If it was not for an Ayah in Allah's Book, I would not have narrated a Hadith for anyone: " (Narrated by Abu Hurayrah and Amr ibn al-'As and reported by Ibn Majah - Qurtubi) This will not be considered as 'concealment of knowledge' since what is not allowed is the concealment of clear guidance given in the Qur'an and Sunnah which it is rather necessary to disclose and disseminate widely.

**What the eternal curse carries for them.**

(it is they on whom is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, combined. They will abide therein (under the curse in Hell).) Therefore, they will suffer the eternal curse until the Day of Resurrection and after that in the fire of Jahannam, where,. Hence, the torment will not be decreased for them,. The torment will not be changed or tempered for even an hour. The Ayah (2:159 above) states that those who hide the knowledge will be cursed, (in this life and) on the Day of Resurrection, by Allah, the angels, all humanity, and those who curse (including the animals) each in its own distinct way. These Ayat sternly warn against those who hide the clear signs that the Messengers were sent with which guide to the correct path and beneficial guidance for the hearts, after Allah has made such aspects clear for His servants through the Books that He revealed to His Messengers.

**What the angels and everything else do for the scholar.**

Certainly, just as everything asks for forgiveness for the scholar, even the fish in the sea and the bird in the air, then those who hide knowledge are cursed by Allah and by the cursers. Moreover, a Hadith states that everything, including the fish in the sea, asks for forgiveness for the scholars. (and cursed by the cursers) means that the angels and the believers will curse them. Mujahid said, "When the earth is struck by drought, the animals say, 'This is because of the sinners among the Children of Adam. Commentators Mujahid and Ikrimah have said that this absence of specification suggests that they are cursed by everything and every living being, so much so, that all animals and insects join in since their misdeeds hurt all created life forms.

161.text:
Surely those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers are condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity. The verse states the two conditions together, the disbelief and the dying in it, and the sources stop on the second because it fixes the outcome. A person whose life ends while he is turned away has nothing left to correct, so the sentence is about the end of a life and not about a moment of doubt. The disbelievers named here are those who were spoken of in the verses before, and the sources carry the report that they are the ones who were given the Book and concealed what it carried. The curse is named three times over and it is spread across the creation, so the one who is cursed is opposed by his Lord, by the unseen beings who serve Him, and by the whole of mankind. The angels are named before humanity, and the sources notice the order, since the world of the unseen comes before the world of the visible. The verse follows on the door that the verse before it opened for those who turn, and it states what becomes of those who do not. The curse it describes is explained in the sources as a removal from the mercy of Allah, which is why the words are given such weight in the rulings about cursing.

**What dying as a disbeliever carries.**

From the words of the text :'and died while they were disbelievers', commentators al-Jassas, al-Qurtubi and some others have formulated the view that it is not permissible to curse an infidel about whom it is not certain that he is to die in a state of infidelity. (Lo! Those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers) in Allah and His Messenger; (on them is the curse of Allah) the torment of Allah (and of the angels) the curse of the angels (and of men combined) the curses directed by believers towards each other will end up as curses on these unbelievers. Those who disbelieve and die in disbelief, not having repented, they are condemned by Allah by being removed from His mercy; and the angels and people all call for them to be removed and excluded from Allah’s mercy. Allah afterwards states that those who disbelieve in Him and remain in this state until they die, then: But those who disbelieve and die disbelieving wa-hum kuffār ‘they being disbelievers’ is a circumstantial qualifier — upon them shall be the curse of God and the angels and of people altogether that is they deserve such a curse in this life and in the next; ‘people’ here is said to be either people in general or believers.

**What the curse means.**

The word 'La nah ' (curse) means: to remove away from the mercy of Allah Almighty'. As far as the infidels as a whole are concerned, including the tyrants and the unjust, it is technically correct, if cursed without any particularization. There is no disagreement that it is lawful to curse the disbelievers. 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and the Imams after him used to curse the disbelievers in their Qunut (a type of supplication) during the prayer and otherwise. From this we also find out that the act of cursing is so grave that it has been disallowed even if the target be an infidel about whom it is not certain that he is going to die as one. It should be clearly understood that the act of cursing becomes effective not only by using the word, 'curse' but all synonyms used are subject to the same ruling.

**Who may be cursed, and who may not.**

There is no disagreement that it is lawful to curse the disbelievers. 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and the Imams after him used to curse the disbelievers in their Qunut (a type of supplication) during the prayer and otherwise. As for cursing a specific disbeliever, some scholars stated that it is not allowed to curse him, because we do not know how Allah will make his end. Others said that it is allowed to curse individual disbelievers. For proof, they mention the story about the man who was brought to be punished repeatedly for drinking (alcohol), a man said, "May Allah curse him! Cursed some infidels by name is explained by the fact that their death in a state of infidelity was divinely revealed to him.

**What the fire will be like for them.**

But those who disbelieve and die disbelieving-upon them shall be the curse of God and the angels and of people altogether. But those who disbelieve and die disbelieving wa-hum kuffār ‘they being disbelievers’ is a circumstantial qualifier — upon them shall be the curse of God and the angels and of people altogether that is they deserve such a curse in this life and in the next; ‘people’ here is said to be either people in general or believers. Abiding therein: the chastisement shall not be lightened for them no respite shall be given them. Abiding: that is they remain forever in their contemptible position insignificant and [find no] lessening of it or relief without kindness or favors. Therefore, they will suffer the eternal curse until the Day of Resurrection and after that in the fire of Jahannam, where,.

**What the report about the concealed knowledge carries.**

Verily, those who conceal the clear proofs, evidences and the guidance, which We have sent down, after We have made it clear for the People in the Book, they are the ones cursed by Allah and cursed by the cursers Except those who repent and do righteous deeds, and openly declare (the truth which they concealed). (Whoever was asked about knowledge that one has, but he hid it, then a bridle made of fire will be tied around his mouth on the Day of Resurrection.) It is also recorded by Al-Bukhari that Abu Hurayrah said, "If it was not for an Ayah in Allah's Book, I would not have narrated a Hadith for anyone: A Hadith in the Musnad, narrated through several chains of narrators, that strengthens the overall judgment of the Hadith, states that Abu Hurayrah narrated that Allah's Messenger said: (Verily, those who conceal the clear proofs, evidences and the guidance, which We have sent down,)"
