There is no disagreement that it is lawful to curse the disbelievers. 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and the Imams after him used to curse the disbelievers in their Qunut (a type of supplication) during the prayer and otherwise. As for cursing a specific disbeliever, some scholars stated that it is not allowed to curse him, because we do not know how Allah will make his end. Others said that it is allowed to curse individual disbelievers. For proof, they mention the story about the man who was brought to be punished repeatedly for drinking (alcohol), a man said, "May Allah curse him! (Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger).

**What the knowledge of the Book carries.**

(Whoever was asked about knowledge that one has, but he hid it, then a bridle made of fire will be tied around his mouth on the Day of Resurrection.) The Ayah (2:159 above) states that those who hide the knowledge will be cursed, (in this life and) on the Day of Resurrection, by Allah, the angels, all humanity, and those who curse (including the animals) each in its own distinct way. These Ayat sternly warn against those who hide the clear signs that the Messengers were sent with which guide to the correct path and beneficial guidance for the hearts, after Allah has made such aspects clear for His servants through the Books that He revealed to His Messengers. Abu Al-'Aliyah said that these Ayat, "were revealed about the People of the Scripture who hid the description of Muhammad . It is also recorded by Al-Bukhari that Abu Hurayrah said, "If it was not for an Ayah in Allah's Book, I would not have narrated a Hadith for anyone:

163.text:
Your God is only One God. The verse is an answer to a question, and the sources carry the account that those who associated others with Allah asked the Prophet to describe his Lord, so what follows is given as a description rather than as an argument. The claim is put in the simplest form, one God and no other, and God is named first so that the reader is told who is being spoken of before he is told anything about Him. There is no god worthy of worship except Him. The sentence repeats the same content in the form of a denial followed by an exception, and the sources take that form as the strongest way of putting it, since every rival is removed first and then the One who stands is named. the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful. The verse closes with two names, and the sources explain them as mercy that is general and mercy that is particular, so the reader is left with the character of the One he has been told to worship and not only with a statement about His number. The verse stands at the head of the passage that spreads out the signs in the heavens and the earth, and the proof follows the claim, so the two belong together. The description is given first and the evidence for it is laid out after it, and the persons addressed are told both what to believe and where to look.

**What the idolaters of Arabia asked the Prophet.**

When they asked him Muhammad to describe his Lord the following was revealed Your God the One deserving of your worship is One God without any equal in either essence or attribute; there is no god except Him He is the Compassionate the Merciful. When the mushrikin (the associators) of Arabia heard the verse 'And your god is one God', all against their own belief, they were puzzled thinking how could there be just one single object of worship for the whole wide world. If this was a serious claim, there has to be some proof in support. That proof has been tersely encased in the present two verses. Allah then declares His Oneness because the unbelievers denied this divine Oneness, saying:

**What the proof in the verses is.**

Then Allah mentions some of the proof that He is alone as the deity, that He is the One who created the heavens and the earth and all of the various creatures between them, all of which testify to His Oneness. If this was a serious claim, there has to be some proof in support. That proof has been tersely encased in the present two verses. (Alif-Lam-Mim. Allah! La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), Al-Haiyul-Qaiyum (the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists).)(3:1, 2)" (And your Ilah is One Ilah (God Allah), La ilaha illa Huwa (there is none who has the right to be worshipped but He), the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.) and:

**What it means that He is One in His being.**

He is One in the state of His being, that is, there exists in the universe of His creation no entity like Him. He is without any duplicate or replica and without any equal or parallel. He is One in claiming the right of being worshipped, that is, in view of the nature of His Being, the comprehensiveness of His most perfect attributes and the great charisma of His creation and its nurture, all human obedience, all ibadah all worship has to be for Him alone. He is One in being free of any conceivable composition, that is, He is free of segments and fragments, units and organs, substances and elements, atoms and particles. There is just no way He can be analyzed or divided or resolved. He is One in being the anterior and the posterior, that is, He existed when nothing did and He will remain existing when nothing will.

**What the Most Compassionate and the Most Merciful carry.**

He is the Most Gracious Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful Ar-Rahim. We explained the meanings of these two Names in the beginning of Surat Al-Fatihah. There is no other true god, and He is the Merciful and His mercy is vast. He is Compassionate with His creation, surrounding them with many blessings. (Your God is one God) without son or partner; (there is no God save Him, the Beneficent) the Tender, (the Merciful) the Compassionate.

**What the servants owe the One who made them.**

In return, we should become God’s devoted servants, living for Him, dying for Him, and setting all our hopes on winning His eternal favour. " The wonder is not that He ascribed the servants to Himself, joined them to Himself, and said, "Surely My servants" [15:42]. The wonder is that He ascribed Himself to the servants and joined His name to their name, saying, "Your God. Our very existence on earth, and all the benefits we derive from the world around us, are manifestations of His unbounded grace and mercy. He is the only worthy focus of man’s attention. Rather, in generosity and loving kindness He Himself is unique and one.

164.text:
Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth. The verse opens a list, and it begins with the widest thing a person can see, so the reader is taken from the heavens above him to the earth under his feet before any particular thing is named. the alternation of the day and the night. The second sign is the passing of time itself, and the sources take it as the coming of the night and its going, each following the other without fail. the ships that sail the sea for the benefit of humanity. The third is the sea and what men build to cross it, and the benefit of humanity is named here to show that the arrangement of the world is made to serve the people who live in it. the rain sent down by Allah from the skies. The fourth sign is the water that comes down from above, and the sender is named so that the rain is not left as a force of its own. reviving the earth after its death. The fifth is what the water does, and the earth is described as dead and then given life, so the reader is shown a raising that he can see every year. the scattering of all kinds of creatures throughout. The sixth sign is the spread of living things across the earth, and the sources note that every one of them is provided for, so the scattering is not a description of chance. the shifting of the winds. The seventh is the movement of the air, which the sources read as mercy at times and torment at others, harnessed to what men need. and the clouds drifting between the heavens and the earth. The eighth sign is the cloud that hangs between the two and runs wherever it is sent, and it is named last among the things themselves because it carries the rain that has just been spoken of. in all of this are surely signs for people of understanding. The list is closed by naming who benefits from it, and the sources explain the understanding as the mind that reads the world as a book, so the signs are there for the people who use what they have been given. The verses before this one stated that Allah is one, and this verse supplies the evidence for the claim, which is why the list is put here and why it ends on the people who understand rather than on the things themselves.

**What the list of signs is for.**

Now in Verse 164, there is a series of signs and proofs in support of the premise that Allah Almighty is really One. Stated simply, these can be grasped by the learned and the ignorant alike. The presence of all these signs in the universe are reflections of the Creator in His creation. But these signs, spread all over the universe, serve as proofs of God’s existence and His role as sustainer of the entire universe, only to one who sincerely reflects on these signs. The following are clear signs of the Oneness of Allah, glory be to Him, for those who understand the evidence and proof: the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the wonders in them; the succession of night and day; the passing of life and death; happiness and sorrow; wealth and poverty; ships that sail through the waters of the sea, carrying food, clothing, trade and other things that people need and which benefit them; water that Allah sends down, bringing the earth to life with the agriculture and pasture that grows in it, and the living creatures He spreads out in it; the changing of the winds from one direction to another; and the clouds, controlled between the sky and the earth.

**What the signs in the heavens and the earth show.**

Verily, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which is of use to mankind, and the water (rain) which Allah sends down from the sky and makes the earth alive therewith after its death, and the moving (living) creatures of all kinds that He has scattered therein, and in the veering of winds and clouds which are held between the sky and the earth, are indeed Ayat (proofs, evidences, signs, etc.) for people of understanding. Therefore, the sky, with its height, intricate design, vastness, the heavenly objects in orbit, and this earth, with its density, its lowlands, mountains, seas, deserts, valleys, and other structures, and beneficial things that it has. (Verily, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, there are indeed signs for men of understanding. Those who remember Allah (always, and in prayers) standing, sitting, and lying down on their sides, and think deeply about the creation of the heavens and the earth, (saying): "Our Lord! You have not created this without purpose, glory to You! (Exalted are You above all that they associate with You as partners). Give us salvation from the torment of the Fire.")(3:190-191) (...and the water (rain) which Allah sends down from the sky and makes the earth alive therewith after its death), which is similar to Allah's statement: (And a sign for them is the dead land. We give it life, and We bring forth from it grains, so that they eat thereof.)(36:33), until: (And no moving (living) creature is there on earth but its provision is due from Allah. And He knows its dwelling place and its deposit (in the uterus or grave). All is in a Clear Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz the Book of Decrees with Allah).)(11:6) Their origination and their perpetuity is the work of His perfect power alone and that there is absolutely no being other than Him who can take that credit. The existence of a limitless world in the form of the earth and the heavens is a proof that there must be a Creator behind it. Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of the night and the day, the ships that run on the sea with what benefits people, the water that God sends down from heaven giving life to the earth after its death, the scattering of every beast therein, the shifting of the winds, the clouds subjected between heaven and earth-there are signs for a people who have intellect.

**What the alternation of the night and day carries.**

This (the night) comes and then goes followed by the other (the day) which does not delay for even an instant, just as Allah said: (It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. They all float, each in an orbit.)(36:40) Sometimes, the day grows shorter and the night longer, and sometimes vice versa, one takes from the length of the other. (Allah merges the night into the day, and He merges the day into the night)(57:6) meaning, He extends the length of one from the other and vice versa. Who can ignore the constant alternation of the night and the day?

**What the ships and the sea show.**

Similarly, the movement of boats on the surface of waters, is a formidable indicator of Allah's power which gave water, a substance so liquid and fluid, the property of lifting on its back ships which carry tons and tons of weight all the way from the East to the West. (...and the ships which sail through the sea with that which is of use to mankind,) Shaping the sea in this manner, so that it is able to carry ships from one shore to another, so people benefit from what the other region has, and export what they have to them and vice versa. If the substance of water was not given a state in which the molecules move freely among themselves while remaining in one mass, a functional fluidity in other words, all this maritime activity would not be there. Even if this fluidity of sea-surface was there, help from winds was still needed in order to cover all those thousands of nautical miles across the seas of the world. The use of the expression :'with what benefits men' points out to the countless benefits that accrue to human beings when they mutually trade their goods through sea freighters.

**What the winds and the clouds carry.**

Then, there is the movement of winds which Allah harnesses into the service of man, and in His wisdom, keeps changing their direction. "If He wills, He can still the winds, then, ships shall remain standing on the back of the seas. Sometimes, the wind brings mercy and sometimes torment. Sometimes it brings the good news of the clouds that follow it, sometimes it leads the clouds, herding them, scattering them or directing them. The clouds run between the sky and the earth to wherever Allah wills of lands and areas. (and the clouds obedient) subservient (between heaven and earth) He says: in all these (are signs) indications of the Lord's divine Oneness (for people who have sense) who believe that they are from Allah.

**What the people of understanding do with the signs.**

(...are indeed Ayat for people of understanding,) meaning, all these things are clear signs that testify to Allah's Oneness. The universe displays God’s very existence and His oneness on a vast scale; it is an amalgam of every aspect of perfection, so that no one with any vision or even a grain of intelligence can fail to discover Him in it. But these signs, spread all over the universe, serve as proofs of God’s existence and His role as sustainer of the entire universe, only to one who sincerely reflects on these signs. For, to be able to arrive at the truth, one has to be sincere in one’s search for it, and one has to rise above worldly considerations before drawing one’s conclusions. This can be achieved only by total absorption, not in externals, but in the search for the inner reality that lies beneath the outward surface of things. In this verse the Lord of the Universe shows the generality of people the road to Himself, so that they will gaze upon the wonders of the dominion of heaven and earth and on the artisanries of land and sea and then recognize the Artisan and attest to His oneness. The generality of the faithful look at the artisanry and from the artisanry reach the Artisan.

165.text:
Still there are some who take others as Allah's equal. The verse turns from the signs that have just been listed to the people who pass them by, and it names their error as a taking of equals, which the sources explain as the setting up of rivals who are worshipped besides Allah. they love them as they should love Allah. The love is named as the measure of the offence, so what is described is not a private preference but an attachment that belongs to Allah alone being given to something else. The sources dwell on this love, since it is what moves a person to obey, and they point out that the same feeling is what the believers give to their Lord. but the true believers love Allah even more. The sentence draws the contrast the verse turns on, and the sources take the comparison as one of strength and endurance rather than of mere quantity, since the love of the faithful is shown in what they do when they are tried. If only the wrongdoers could see the horrible punishment awaiting them. The verse then turns to what the wrongdoers cannot see, and the condition is left open, so the reader is invited to supply the end of the sentence for himself. they would certainly realize that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is indeed severe in punishment. The last clause states what the sight would teach them, that the power is not shared and that the punishment is real, and the sources carry the account of what those who were followed and those who followed will say when the matter is decided. The verse therefore closes the argument that began with the signs, since the same creation that shows the oneness of Allah is shown here to be the reason no other love can be given the place that belongs to Him.

**What the love of the polytheists was given to.**

In these Ayat, Allah mentions the condition of the polytheists in this life and their destination in the Hereafter. They appointed equals and rivals with Allah, worshipping them along with Allah and loving them, just as they love Allah. However, Allah is the only deity worthy of worship, Who has neither rival nor opponent nor partner. In the verses that appeared earlier, there was a strong and positive view of Allah's Oneness. Now the present verse points out to the error made by those who associate others in the divinity of Allah and think that they are caretakers of their needs. Allah mentions after this the unbelievers' love for their objects of worship in this world, and how they disown each other in the Hereafter, saying: Even with these clear signs, there are people who take others besides Allah as their gods, considering them equal to Him, and loving them as they love Allah. When a being (or an object) is taken as a deity, it is assumed to be someone or something worthy of being worshipped.

**What the believers' love of Allah carries.**

Because these believers love Allah, know His greatness, revere Him, believe in His Oneness, then they do not associate anything or anyone with Him in the worship. Rather, they worship Him Alone, depend on Him and they seek help from Him for each and every need. In direct contrast to this profile of the polytheists, there are the true believers who love Allah alone, and very staunchly too, for a poly-theist may turn away from his self-made god in the event of an impending loss, but a true believer reposes his total confidence in Allah, in gain and loss alike, retaining His love and pleasure as his lasting possession, never leaving his Creator whatever the odds against him be. Those who have real faith love Allah more than those others love their gods: they do not worship anyone besides Him; and they love Him in hardship and in ease, while those others only love their gods when things are going well – when things go badly, they call on Allah alone. The Lord of the Worlds says, "The love of the faithful for Me is not like the unbelievers' love for idols, such that every once in a while they incline toward another. Rather, the faithful never turn away from Me and never incline toward anyone else.

**How the love of the faithful differs.**

If this were the only verse in the whole Qur'an about the faithful and God's friends, their eminence and honor would be complete, for the Lord of the Worlds is saying, "They love Me intensely and more completely than the unbelievers love their objects of worship. " And those who have faith are more intense in love for God. The Lord of the Worlds says, "The love of the faithful for Me is not like the unbelievers' love for idols, such that every once in a while they incline toward another. But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else). (But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else) Their attachment to them reaches the proportions of love that is due for Allah alone.

**What the wrongdoers would see if they could.**

(If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah.) if these people knew what they will face and the terrible punishment they are to suffer because of their disbelief and Shirk (polytheism), then they would shun the deviation that they live by. If the wrongdoers could see with their own eyes the punishment that waits in the Afterlife for those who worship others with Allah and commit sins, then they would know that all power belongs to Allah alone and that He is firm in punishing those who stubbornly rebel. If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them), and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them And those who followed will say: " Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them. If they saw this, then they would not worship anyone with Allah.

**What those who followed and those who were followed will do.**

(When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them).) the angels, whom they used to claim that they worshipped, declare their innocence of them in the Hereafter, saying: (And those who followed will say: "If only we had one more chance to return (to the worldly life), we would disown (declare ourselves as innocent from) them as they have disowned (declared themselves as innocent from) us.") (then all their relations will be cut off from them.) "meaning the friendship. (Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them.) meaning, their works will vanish and disappear. ("Glorified be You! You are our Wali (Lord) instead of them. Nay, but they used to worship the Jinn; most of them were believers in them.")(34:41)

**What is carried about the punishment on that day.**

(...and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them.) meaning, when they see Allah's torment, their power and means of salvation are all cut off, and they will have no way of making amends, nor will they find a way of escape from the Fire. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about: If the wrongdoers could see with their own eyes the punishment that waits in the Afterlife for those who worship others with Allah and commit sins, then they would know that all power belongs to Allah alone and that He is firm in punishing those who stubbornly rebel. If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them), and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them And those who followed will say: The general meaning of the verse then is ‘If they were aware in this world of the severity of God’s chastisement and of the fact that power is God’s alone the moment they come to see it with their own eyes on the Day of Resurrection they would not take to themselves compeers’. Allah mentions their false beliefs in their idols, and that those they followed will declare their innocence of them.

166.text:
Consider the Day when those who misled others will disown their followers. The verse takes the reader forward to a scene, and the first thing it shows is the breaking of the tie that held leader and follower together in this world. The disowning is put first, so the loss named is not only the punishment but the abandonment by the very ones who were followed. when they face the torment. The clause places the disowning at the moment the punishment is seen, and the sources take the timing as the point, since the tie is broken exactly when help would be worth having. and the bonds that united them will be cut off. The last clause states the result in the plainest terms, and the sources explain that everything which joined them here, kinship and agreement and shared interest, is severed there. The verse follows the one before it, which described the love that was given to others besides Allah, and it shows where that love ends. The sources carry what the followers and the followed will say to each other, and they notice that the follower asks to return not for the sake of the truth but for the sake of being free of the ones he followed, so the regret of that hour is not repentance. The passage is built so that the reader sees the end of the attachment while he is still in a position to choose it, and the verse before this one named the love that was given to others besides Allah, while this verse names what that love comes to when the power of the beloved is gone. The two verses are read together by the sources as one scene, the leaders disowning and the bonds being cut, and the reader is meant to weigh the attachment he has now against the severing he is shown here. The verse is placed where it is so that the reader meets the end of the attachment before he is told what he may eat and whom he may follow.

**What the disowning on that Day will be.**

(When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them).) the angels, whom they used to claim that they worshipped, declare their innocence of them in the Hereafter, saying: The Jinn will also disown the disbelievers who worshipped them, and they will reject that worship. When idh here substitutes for the previous idh those who were followed that is the leaders disown their followers that is to say when they have denied misleading them the latter and they have seen the chastisement and the cords the bonds of affection and kinship that were between them on earth are cut away before them from them taqatta‘at ‘cut away’ is a supplement to tabarra’a ‘disown’. When the so-called 'people' of their leaders will see this turnabout of theirs, they will fret and fume but will be unable to do anything about it except wishing that there be a return for them to the mortal world where they could, at least, square up with their greasy leaders - 'May be this time they come back to us seeking our allegiance which would be a perfect time to say no to them and to distance ourselves from them and to do to them what they did to us.'. Towards the end of the preceding verse it was said that the punishment of the Hereafter is severe. How severe it will be is now the subject of the present verse.

**What is severed when the torment is seen.**

The severity of the punishment against which the polytheists have been warned will unfold itself when their leaders whom they followed will disown them as their votaries; and they both, the leaders and the led, will witness the punishment, and whatever bonds of leading and following may have existed between them would be snapped apart, very much like it happens in our mortal world when people share in the illegal but wriggle out when apprehended, so much so, that they would even go to the limit of refusing to recognize their accomplices! (...and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them.) meaning, when they see Allah's torment, their power and means of salvation are all cut off, and they will have no way of making amends, nor will they find a way of escape from the Fire. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about: (then all their relations will be cut off from them.) "meaning the friendship. When idh here substitutes for the previous idh those who were followed that is the leaders disown their followers that is to say when they have denied misleading them the latter and they have seen the chastisement and the cords the bonds of affection and kinship that were between them on earth are cut away before them from them taqatta‘at ‘cut away’ is a supplement to tabarra’a ‘disown’. They are stuck with 'their deeds which they see as remorse', and they all, the leaders and their followers, 'are not to come out from the Fire', since the punishment for shirk, the grave sin of associating partners with Allah, is to remain in the Fire for ever.

**What the followers will say there.**

(And those who followed will say: "If only we had one more chance to return (to the worldly life), we would disown (declare ourselves as innocent from) them as they have disowned (declared themselves as innocent from) us.") This Ayah means: 'If we only had a chance to go back to the life so that we could disown them (their idols, leaders, etc.) shun their worship, ignore them and worship Allah Alone instead.' But they utter a lie in this regard, because if they were given the chance to go back, they would only return to what they were prohibited from doing, just as Allah said. (When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them).) the angels, whom they used to claim that they worshipped, declare their innocence of them in the Hereafter, saying: (And who is more astray than one who calls on (invokes) besides Allah, such as will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection, and who are (even) unaware of their calls (invocations) to them? And when mankind are gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), they (false deities) will become their enemies and will deny their worshipping.)(46:5-6) Allah said: ("Glorified be You! You are our Wali (Lord) instead of them. Nay, but they used to worship the Jinn; most of them were believers in them.")(34:41)

**What the punishment will be like on that day.**

Towards the end of the preceding verse it was said that the punishment of the Hereafter is severe. How severe it will be is now the subject of the present verse. The severity of the punishment against which the polytheists have been warned will unfold itself when their leaders whom they followed will disown them as their votaries; and they both, the leaders and the led, will witness the punishment, and whatever bonds of leading and following may have existed between them would be snapped apart, very much like it happens in our mortal world when people share in the illegal but wriggle out when apprehended, so much so, that they would even go to the limit of refusing to recognize their accomplices! When the so-called 'people' of their leaders will see this turnabout of theirs, they will fret and fume but will be unable to do anything about it except wishing that there be a return for them to the mortal world where they could, at least, square up with their greasy leaders - 'May be this time they come back to us seeking our allegiance which would be a perfect time to say no to them and to distance ourselves from them and to do to them what they did to us.'. (And who is more astray than one who calls on (invokes) besides Allah, such as will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection, and who are (even) unaware of their calls (invocations) to them? And when mankind are gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), they (false deities) will become their enemies and will deny their worshipping.)(46:5-6) Allah said: (If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah.) if these people knew what they will face and the terrible punishment they are to suffer because of their disbelief and Shirk (polytheism), then they would shun the deviation that they live by. (As for those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one thinks it to be water.)(24:39)

**What the polytheists and their leaders will see.**

When the so-called 'people' of their leaders will see this turnabout of theirs, they will fret and fume but will be unable to do anything about it except wishing that there be a return for them to the mortal world where they could, at least, square up with their greasy leaders - 'May be this time they come back to us seeking our allegiance which would be a perfect time to say no to them and to distance ourselves from them and to do to them what they did to us.'. (When those who were followed) the leaders (disown those who followed (them) the lowly among people, (and they behold) both the leaders and the lowly (the doom) in the Hereafter, (and all their aims) the pledges and congeniality that were between them in this world (collapse with them). Then the leaders who were followed in disbelief will reject the weak people who followed them because of seeing the terrors and hardships of the Day of Judgement; so, all ties and means of escape will be cut off from them. When those who were followed declare themselves quit of those who followed them. The polytheists set certain animals free in the name of their deities. In these Ayat, Allah mentions the condition of the polytheists in this life and their destination in the Hereafter.

167.text:
The misled followers will cry. The verse gives the words of the people who followed rather than of the ones who led, and the sources explain that these are the ones with the least power and standing, so the scene is shown from the side that had the least power in this world. If only we could have a second chance. The wish is named first, and the sources notice that the request is only to return and not to be forgiven, since what the speaker wants at that moment is the chance to act differently. we would disown them as they disowned us. The last part of the speech turns back on the leaders, and the followers ask for nothing except to do to them what has already been done to the followers, so the verse closes the circle of the disowning described in the verse before it. And so Allah will make them remorseful of their misdeeds. The sentence states what their own words have done to them, and the sources read the remorse as being shown their deeds, so that they see what they did and see it as it is. And they will never be able to leave the Fire. The verse ends with the door shut, and the sources keep the two halves of the scene together, the regret in words and the permanence of the punishment. The passage therefore completes the picture it began with the love that was given to others besides Allah, and the reader is shown what that love produces in the end.

**What the followers will ask for on that Day.**

And those who followed say ‘O if only we might return again to the world and disown them the ones who had been followed as they have disowned us!’ on this day the particle law ‘if only’ is an optative and its response is natabarra’a ‘we disown’. (And those who followed will say: "If only we had one more chance to return (to the worldly life), we would disown (declare ourselves as innocent from) them as they have disowned (declared themselves as innocent from) us.") This Ayah means: 'If we only had a chance to go back to the life so that we could disown them (their idols, leaders, etc.) shun their worship, ignore them and worship Allah Alone instead.' But they utter a lie in this regard, because if they were given the chance to go back, they would only return to what they were prohibited from doing, just as Allah said. (And those who were but followers) i.e. the lowly (will say: If a return) to this world (were possible for us, we would disown them) disown the leaders in this world (even as they have disowned us) in the Hereafter. The weak and those who followed will say, ‘If only we could go back to the earth, we would reject our leaders as they reject us’.

**What the remorse will be made of.**

" Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them. (Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them.) meaning, their works will vanish and disappear. They are stuck with 'their deeds which they see as remorse', and they all, the leaders and their followers, 'are not to come out from the Fire', since the punishment for shirk, the grave sin of associating partners with Allah, is to remain in the Fire for ever. How severe it will be is now the subject of the present verse. (And We shall turn to whatever deeds they (disbelievers, polytheists, sinners) did, and We shall make such deeds as scattered floating particles of dust.)(25:23)

**What the torment will be for those who followed.**

(...and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them.) meaning, when they see Allah's torment, their power and means of salvation are all cut off, and they will have no way of making amends, nor will they find a way of escape from the Fire. 'Ata' reported that Ibn 'Abbas said about: The severity of the punishment against which the polytheists have been warned will unfold itself when their leaders whom they followed will disown them as their votaries; and they both, the leaders and the led, will witness the punishment, and whatever bonds of leading and following may have existed between them would be snapped apart, very much like it happens in our mortal world when people share in the illegal but wriggle out when apprehended, so much so, that they would even go to the limit of refusing to recognize their accomplices! Allah shows them the severe punishment in the Afterlife and the consequence of following their leaders in falsehood: regrets and sorrow, and they will never leave the fire of Hell. If only, those who do wrong could see, when they will see the torment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them), and they see the torment, then all their relations will be cut off from them And those who followed will say: Never shall they exit from the Fire once they have entered it.

**What Allah will show them of their deeds.**

" Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them. (Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them.) meaning, their works will vanish and disappear. They are stuck with 'their deeds which they see as remorse', and they all, the leaders and their followers, 'are not to come out from the Fire', since the punishment for shirk, the grave sin of associating partners with Allah, is to remain in the Fire for ever. So God shall show them their works anguish for them! Allah shows them the severe punishment in the Afterlife and the consequence of following their leaders in falsehood: regrets and sorrow, and they will never leave the fire of Hell.

**What those who were followed will say there.**

(When those who were followed disown (declare themselves innocent of) those who followed (them).) the angels, whom they used to claim that they worshipped, declare their innocence of them in the Hereafter, saying: ("Glorified be You! You are our Wali (Lord) instead of them. Nay, but they used to worship the Jinn; most of them were believers in them.")(34:41) (We declare our innocence (from them) before You. It was not us they worshipped.)(28:63), and: When the so-called 'people' of their leaders will see this turnabout of theirs, they will fret and fume but will be unable to do anything about it except wishing that there be a return for them to the mortal world where they could, at least, square up with their greasy leaders - 'May be this time they come back to us seeking our allegiance which would be a perfect time to say no to them and to distance ourselves from them and to do to them what they did to us.'. (And Shaytan (Satan) will say when the matter has been decided: "Verily, Allah promised you a promise of truth. And I too promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So blame me not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. I deny your former act in associating me (Satan) as a partner with Allah (by obeying me in the life of the world). Verily, there is a painful torment for the Zalimin (polytheists and wrongdoers).)(14:22)

168.text:
O humanity! Eat from what is lawful and good on the earth and do not follow Satan's footsteps. The verse is addressed to all people and not to the believers alone, and it opens with a command to eat, which the sources read as a correction of two opposite errors, the forbidding of what Allah has made lawful and the taking of what He has forbidden. The two words carry two conditions, that the food be lawful and that it be good, and the sources explain the lawful as what the law has made lawful and the good as what is clean and wholesome, so the verse asks about the source of a thing and about its quality at once. The command is then paired with a prohibition, and the footsteps named are the tracks a person follows without meeting the one who made them, which the sources explain as the acts and the customs that lead a person away from what is lawful. He is truly your sworn enemy. The verse states the relation between the human being and the one whose tracks are being followed, so the reader is told that the path is laid by an enemy and not by a friend. The passage it belongs to is the call to all people which follows the signs and the account of those who set up rivals, and the sources carry the account of the people who made certain things unlawful on their own authority, which is why the correction is put as a command to eat rather than as a lecture. The reader is left with a rule about what he takes into his body and a warning about the one who teaches him to narrow or to widen it.

**What was made lawful, and what good means.**

The following was revealed when some said that it was unlawful to take a camel that has been let loose sawā’ib O people eat of what is in the earth lawful halālan is a circumstantial qualifier and wholesome tayyiban is an adjective for emphasis that is to say what is delicious; and follow not the steps the ways of Satan meaning what he embellishes of temptations; he is a manifest foe to you whose enmity is clear;. The objective of the verse is to stress that animals which Allah has made lawful should not be made unlawful by dedicating them to idols. The present Verse is not negating the unlawfulness of such an animal as wrongly conceived by some people. (Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome) that is not prohibited by Allah (in the earth) of what is cultivated in lands and of cattle, (and follow not the footsteps of the devil) the embellishments and whisperings of the devil concerning the unlawfulness of the cultivation of land and of raising cattle. The real meaning of the root word (halla) in (halalan tayyiban: " The word (tayyib) means 'good' as inclusive of the clean and the pure and covers the twin aspects of being lawful, permissible or halal and being naturally desirable.

**What the footsteps of Satan are.**

The word (khutuwat) is the plural form of (khutwah) which is the distance between the two feet when striding. Here the khutuwat of Shaytan means Satanic deeds. Every act of disobedience to Allah is among the footsteps of Satan. "Any vow or oath that one makes while angry, is among the footsteps of Shaytan and its expiation is that of the vow. (Surely, Shaytan is an enemy to you, so take (treat) him as an enemy. He only invites his Hizb (followers) that they may become the dwellers of the blazing Fire.)(35:6), and: The verse means: 'Your enemy, Satan, commands you to commit evil acts and what is worse than that, such as adultery and so forth.

**What the people had made unlawful on their own.**

The following was revealed when some said that it was unlawful to take a camel that has been let loose sawā’ib O people eat of what is in the earth lawful halālan is a circumstantial qualifier and wholesome tayyiban is an adjective for emphasis that is to say what is delicious; and follow not the steps the ways of Satan meaning what he embellishes of temptations; he is a manifest foe to you whose enmity is clear;. Polytheistic practices, such as releasing animals in the name of idols or dedicating them, whether big or small, to a saint or to anyone other than Allah has been declared unlawful in Verse 173 which follows. Why go about making things unlawful on your own which is a grave sin, and when it is dedicated to someone other than Allah it becomes impure and what is impure is unlawful. If anyone dedicates an animal to anyone other than Allah out of ignorance or carelessness and wishes to make amends, he should resolve to retreat from his misdeed and repent on what he did, in which case, the meat of that animal will become lawful for him. That is why the Islamic law holds unlawful all those things which, in any degree, lead to deviation, i.e. diverting man’s natural desire for God in some other direction. The objective of the verse is to stress that animals which Allah has made lawful should not be made unlawful by dedicating them to idols.

**What the enemy does to the children of Adam.**

Verily, he is to you an open enemy He (Satan) commands you only what is evil and Fahsha' (sinful), and that you should say about Allah what you know not. (Surely, Shaytan is an enemy to you, so take (treat) him as an enemy. He only invites his Hizb (followers) that they may become the dwellers of the blazing Fire.)(35:6), and: (Lo! He is an open enemy for you) whose enmity towards you is quite manifest. (Will you then take him (Iblis) and his offspring as protectors and helpers rather than Me while they are enemies to you? What an evil is the exchange for the Zalimin (polytheists, and wrongdoers, etc).)(18:50) Every act of disobedience to Allah is among the footsteps of Satan.

**What Satan commands and what he tells people.**

(He (Satan) commands you only what is evil and Fahsha (sinful), and that you should say about Allah what you know not.) The verse means: 'Your enemy, Satan, commands you to commit evil acts and what is worse than that, such as adultery and so forth. He commands you to commit what is even worse, that is, saying about Allah without knowledge.' So this includes every innovator and disbeliever. (Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome) that is not prohibited by Allah (in the earth) of what is cultivated in lands and of cattle, (and follow not the footsteps of the devil) the embellishments and whisperings of the devil concerning the unlawfulness of the cultivation of land and of raising cattle.

169.text:
He only incites you to commit evil and indecency. The sentence carries forward the warning given in the verse before it, and it names what the enemy actually does, so the reader is told where the tracks he was told not to follow lead. The two words are not the same, and the sources take the first as what harms a person and the second as what is shameful, so the incitement is toward what troubles and toward what disgraces at once. and to claim against Allah what you do not know. The second thing he incites is speech, and the sources notice that the heavier of the two is put last, since to speak about Allah without knowledge is the door through which the forbidding and the making lawful of the earlier verse were opened. The sources carry the account of the kind of suggestion that comes and goes and the kind that is held onto, and they place the safety of the heart in the remembrance of the enemy and in the refusal to speak of what has not been learned. The verse is the reason the command to eat what is lawful was given with a warning, since the one who incites is the same one who teaches men to narrow or to widen what Allah has made lawful, and the reader is left with the two things he must watch, what he does and what he speaks.

**What evil and indecency carry.**

The word ‘su' in means something which bothers somebody good and reasonable. Some commentators have said that su' here signifies sin as such, and fahsha' signifies major sins. he only commands you to evil sin and indecency what is abhorred by the Law and that you should speak against God what you do not know such as forbidding what He has not forbidden and otherwise. the devil (enjoineth upon you only the evil) evil works (and the foul) transgressions, (and that ye should tell) lies (concerning Allah that which ye know not). Satan only commands harmful, evil actions and disobedience that will bring hardship, as well as for you to say things about faith in Allah and His sacred laws that have not been given to you by Allah or His Prophet. (He (Satan) commands you only what is evil and Fahsha (sinful), and that you should say about Allah what you know not.)

**What the suggestion of evil does in the heart.**

The expression ‌ (innama ya'murukum: he only orders you') means instigating a suggestion in the heart. The son of Adam is influenced by a suggestion from the Satan and a suggestion from the angel. The Satanic suggestion has the effect of bringing forth the expedient gains in evil deeds and thereby opening the avenues of negating the truth, while the angelic suggestion promises reward and success for good deeds and leaves the happy effect of a heart in peace at its attestation of the truth." The meaning can be seen more clearly in a hadith from the blessed Companion Abdullah ibn Masud who said that the Holy Prophet has said: Every act of disobedience to Allah is among the footsteps of Satan.

**What claiming against Allah without knowledge is.**

The verse means: 'Your enemy, Satan, commands you to commit evil acts and what is worse than that, such as adultery and so forth. He commands you to commit what is even worse, that is, saying about Allah without knowledge.' So this includes every innovator and disbeliever. Because of his audacity toward God he induces you to speak falsely about God. the devil (enjoineth upon you only the evil) evil works (and the foul) transgressions, (and that ye should tell) lies (concerning Allah that which ye know not). Satan only commands harmful, evil actions and disobedience that will bring hardship, as well as for you to say things about faith in Allah and His sacred laws that have not been given to you by Allah or His Prophet.

**What the command of the enemy comes to.**

The verse means: 'Your enemy, Satan, commands you to commit evil acts and what is worse than that, such as adultery and so forth. He commands you to commit what is even worse, that is, saying about Allah without knowledge.' So this includes every innovator and disbeliever. (Surely, Shaytan is an enemy to you, so take (treat) him as an enemy. He only invites his Hizb (followers) that they may become the dwellers of the blazing Fire.)(35:6), and:

Verily, he is to you an open enemy He (Satan) commands you only what is evil and Fahsha' (sinful), and that you should say about Allah what you know not. He only invites his Hizb (followers) that they may become the dwellers of the blazing Fire.)(35:6), and: he only commands you to evil sin and indecency what is abhorred by the Law and that you should speak against God what you do not know such as forbidding what He has not forbidden and otherwise.

170.text:
When it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they reply, 'No! We only follow what we found our forefathers practicing,' and the refusal is put in the mouth of the people whose way the verses before this one have been describing. The sources take the answer as a claim of inheritance rather than of argument, since nothing is offered in support of the way except that it was found already in place. The question that follows is put as a rebuke, and it asks whether the imitation would still be kept by children whose parents handed on nothing that could be called a reason. Would they still do so, even if their forefathers had absolutely no understanding or guidance, the verse asks, and the force of the question lies in the joining of the two words, since a way can be walked without knowing where it goes and without being shown the road. The sources dwell on this point and bring out that the verse does not censure the following of what is true, whether it comes from a teacher or from the community, but censures the following of what is false on the ground that it is old. They also carry the account of the occasion on which the verse came down and the parable that the next verse makes of those who hear a voice and do not grasp what it asks of them, so the two verses are read together, the refusal and the likeness. The reader is left with the measure this verse sets, that a way is to be weighed by the guidance it carries and not by the number of generations that walked it.

**What the disbelievers were asked to follow.**

And when it is said to them the disbelievers ‘Follow what God has revealed’ pertaining to affirmation of God’s Oneness and the good things that He has made lawful they say ‘No; but we follow what we found our fathers doing’ in the way of idol-worship deeming unlawful the camel let loose and practising the slitting of the camel’s ear sc. bahīra. (And when it is said unto them) to the Arab idolaters: (Follow that which Allah hath revealed) follow the lawfulness exposited by Allah concerning what is cultivated and the cattle raised, (they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers) regarding their unlawfulness. If these disbelievers are told to follow the guidance and light which Allah revealed, they say, resisting stubbornly, that they will follow the beliefs and customs that their fathers followed. When these mushrik people were asked to follow the injunctions revealed by Allah through His Messenger, they refused to do so and insisted that they would rather follow the customary practice they had inherited from their fathers because, as they assumed, their models were divinely appointed to follow the way they adopted.

**What the verse carries about the fathers they followed.**

We shall follow what we found our fathers following," meaning, worshipping the idols and the false deities. ((Would they do that!) even though their fathers), meaning, those whom they follow and whose practices they imitate, and: (...did not understand anything nor were they guided?) meaning, they had no sound understanding or guidance. (What! Even though their fathers were wholly unintelligent) with regard to Religion (and had no guidance) to the practice of any prophet, so how could you follow them? It is also said that this means: if their fathers did not understand about things in this world and did not follow the practice of any prophet, then how could you follow them? Do they follow their fathers even though they understood nothing of guidance or the light, and were not guided to the truth that Allah accepts? Whatḍ Even if their fathers do not understand anything and they were not guidedḍ There is no raising their eyes beyond that which is like them in form class kind and ancestry for they are set on their way. Had they known that their ancestors had no intelligence to restrain them nor guidance to unite them they would have withdrawn from them [understanding them to be] hostile and resisted them [understanding them to be] oppositional [to God's com mand].

**What the lack of understanding means.**

In their lack of understanding, the verse says that the disbelievers resemble the scenario of a person shouting his call to an animal who hears nothing meaningful or significant except a bland cry. The disbelievers, in that state, do hear but not what is intended to correct them, so they are called 'deaf; and they are tight-lipped when it comes to accepting the truth, therefore, they are 'dumb'; and since they do not see their benefit or loss, they are 'blind'. Consequently, with their vital senses so dulled, they seem to understand nothing. (...did not understand anything nor were they guided?) meaning, they had no sound understanding or guidance. Do they follow their fathers even though they understood nothing of guidance or the light, and were not guided to the truth that Allah accepts?

**What following what is true has to do with this verse.**

No doubt, this verse does censure the blind following of forefathers, but at the same time, it provides a rule and its attending conditions proving that following has its permissible aspect which has been indicated in (even though their forefathers used to understand nothing) and (nor had they been on the right path). It is from here that we find out that following the forefathers mentioned in the text of the Qur'an was censured because they lacked reason and guidance. 'Guidance' or the right path signifies injunctions revealed by Allah Almighty, openly and clearly, while aql or reason stands for imperative guidance deduced by the great armed vision of Ijtihad from the recognized sources of Islamic Shari'ah. Now we can see that following the model of those identified in the text cannot be permitted because they do not have a revealed set of laws from Allah, nor do they have the ability to deduce injunctions from the Word of Allah. This is good enough to prove that following forefathers in what is false is forbidden while it is permissible, rather desirable, in what is true. But, this has nothing to do with following what is true which is, in fact, a basic religious principle, and a great means of protecting the religion of Muslims in as much as one who does not have the ability to do Ijtihad must rely on 'following' in matters of religion. As far as following the false is concerned, this is correct.

**What the disbelievers were asked and told.**

Allah states that if the disbelievers and polytheists are called to follow what Allah has revealed to His Messenger and abandon the practices of misguidance and ignorance that they indulge in, they will say, "Rather. Ibn Ishaq reported that Ibn 'Abbas said that this was revealed about a group of Jews whom Allah's Messenger called to Islam, but they refused, saying, "Rather, we shall follow what we found our forefathers following. " So Allah revealed this Ayah (2:170) above." When these mushrik people were asked to follow the injunctions revealed by Allah through His Messenger, they refused to do so and insisted that they would rather follow the customary practice they had inherited from their fathers because, as they assumed, their models were divinely appointed to follow the way they adopted. Allah Almighty refutes this position of theirs by asking how could they go on following the ways of their fathers, under all conditions, to the exclusion of all other ways, even if their fathers did not understand much about the true faith, nor were they blessed with guidance given by their Lord? No doubt, this verse does censure the blind following of forefathers, but at the same time, it provides a rule and its attending conditions proving that following has its permissible aspect which has been indicated in (even though their forefathers used to understand nothing) and (nor had they been on the right path).

171.text:
The example of the disbelievers not responding to the Messenger's warning is like a flock not comprehending the calls and cries of the shepherd. The likeness is drawn between people who are called and animals that hear a sound, so the point is not that no call reaches them but that nothing of its meaning does, and the sources dwell on the shepherd, who calls the flock to what is good for it while it cannot weigh the voice against any other noise. They are wilfully deaf, dumb and blind so they have no understanding. The three words shut the three ways by which knowledge arrives, and the sources read them as a description of people whose faculties are whole and unused, since the verse does not say that they cannot hear but that they make no answer. The sources also carry the account of what such people hear and what they lose by not weighing it, and they notice that the parable follows the refusal in the verse before it, so the likeness is given as the plain picture of a person who keeps the sounds of the world and lets go of their meaning. Over the generations the inherited way hardens, and the sources trace how a practice first defended on the ground of custom becomes a thing a person cannot examine at all, which is why the verse ends on understanding rather than on the call itself. The verse is placed here to show that the message reached them and that nothing in them took it in, and the reader is left with the warning that hearing is not the same as understanding and that understanding is not the same as following.

**What the likeness of the shepherd and the flock carries.**

The likeness the attribute of those who disbelieve and the one who calls them to guidance is as the likeness of one who shouts to that which hears nothing save a call and a cry only a sound not understanding its meaning when they listen to an admonition they are like cattle that hear the cry of their shepherd but do not understand what he is saying; they are deaf dumb blind — they do not comprehend any admonition. (The likeness of those who disbelieve) vis-�-vis Muhammad ﷺ (is as the likeness of one who calleth unto that which heareth nothing) just like camels and sheep with their shepherd: his speech is unintelligible to them when he says to them, for example, eat or drink (except a shout and a cry. Deaf) concerning the Truth, (dumb) regarding the Truth, (blind) to guidance; i.e. they pretend to be deaf, dumb and blind when it comes to the Truth and guidance, (therefore they have no sense) they do not understand Allah's command and the call of the Prophet ﷺ just as camels and cattle do not comprehend the words of their shepherd. And the example of those who disbelieve is as that of him who shouts to those (flock of sheep) that hear nothing but calls and cries. (And the example of those who disbelieve...) meaning, in their injustice, misguidance and ignorance, they are just like wandering animals, not understanding what they are told; if the shepherd heralds them or calls them to what benefits them, they would not understand what is actually being said to them, for they only hear unintelligible sounds. The likeness of those who disbelieve is as the likeness of one who shouts to that which hears nothing save a call and a cry; deaf dumb blind-they do not comprehend.

**What the deaf, dumb and blind means.**

They are deaf to hearing the truth so that it will benefit them, dumb as they are unable to speak about the truth, and blind to seeing it, and because of this they do not understand the guidance which you call them to. (They are deaf, dumb, and blind.) means, they are deaf, as they do not hear the truth; mute, as they do not utter it; and blind, as they do not see or recognize its path and way. The disbelievers, in that state, do hear but not what is intended to correct them, so they are called 'deaf; and they are tight-lipped when it comes to accepting the truth, therefore, they are 'dumb'; and since they do not see their benefit or loss, they are 'blind'. (So they do not understand.) means, they do not comprehend or understand anything. Without the ears of comprehension and acceptance their bodily hearing did not benefit them.

**What the shout and the cry are to the flock.**

The likeness the attribute of those who disbelieve and the one who calls them to guidance is as the likeness of one who shouts to that which hears nothing save a call and a cry only a sound not understanding its meaning when they listen to an admonition they are like cattle that hear the cry of their shepherd but do not understand what he is saying; they are deaf dumb blind — they do not comprehend any admonition. (The likeness of those who disbelieve) vis-�-vis Muhammad ﷺ (is as the likeness of one who calleth unto that which heareth nothing) just like camels and sheep with their shepherd: his speech is unintelligible to them when he says to them, for example, eat or drink (except a shout and a cry. Deaf) concerning the Truth, (dumb) regarding the Truth, (blind) to guidance; i.e. they pretend to be deaf, dumb and blind when it comes to the Truth and guidance, (therefore they have no sense) they do not understand Allah's command and the call of the Prophet ﷺ just as camels and cattle do not comprehend the words of their shepherd. And the example of those who disbelieve is as that of him who shouts to those (flock of sheep) that hear nothing but calls and cries. They descended to the status of animals incapable of actualization taḥṣīl. Allah then gave a similitude regarding the unbelievers vis-�-vis Muhammad ﷺ saying:

**What understanding the call of the shepherd carries.**

(So they do not understand.) means, they do not comprehend or understand anything. Consequently, with their vital senses so dulled, they seem to understand nothing. People reach a level where they are totally unable to hear or understand any argument put forward to them. They act as if they have neither eyes nor ears to see and hear, nor brains to give thought to any argument presented to them. They are deaf to hearing the truth so that it will benefit them, dumb as they are unable to speak about the truth, and blind to seeing it, and because of this they do not understand the guidance which you call them to. The likeness the attribute of those who disbelieve and the one who calls them to guidance is as the likeness of one who shouts to that which hears nothing save a call and a cry only a sound not understanding its meaning when they listen to an admonition they are like cattle that hear the cry of their shepherd but do not understand what he is saying; they are deaf dumb blind — they do not comprehend any admonition.

**What those who follow the forefathers come to.**

In the next generation all these superstitious beliefs become firmly rooted in the human psyche and are upheld with great zeal and fervour as the sacred way of the forefathers. It is from here that we find out that following the forefathers mentioned in the text of the Qur'an was censured because they lacked reason and guidance. 'Guidance' or the right path signifies injunctions revealed by Allah Almighty, openly and clearly, while aql or reason stands for imperative guidance deduced by the great armed vision of Ijtihad from the recognized sources of Islamic Shari'ah. No doubt, this verse does censure the blind following of forefathers, but at the same time, it provides a rule and its attending conditions proving that following has its permissible aspect which has been indicated in (even though their forefathers used to understand nothing) and (nor had they been on the right path). This is good enough to prove that following forefathers in what is false is forbidden while it is permissible, rather desirable, in what is true. At this stage, people become resistant to any rational analysis of these superstitious beliefs. The situation deteriorates further with succeeding generations.

172.text:
O believers! Eat from the good things We have provided for you. The address turns from all people to the believers, and the command is given with the provision named as coming from Allah, so the food is not set down as a right that has been earned but as a gift that has been placed in their hands. The sources explain the good things as what is lawful and clean at once, and they bring out that the earlier command to all people is now repeated for the believers with a stronger claim on them, since the one who has answered the call is expected to look at where his food comes from and at what it does to him. And give thanks to Allah if you truly worship Him alone. The second command joins the table to the worship, and the sources read the joining as the point of the verse, since thanks is not only words but the eating of what has been given and the leaving of what has been kept back. They carry the account of what the good things are and of how a person shows gratitude at his own meal, and they notice that the verse stands before the one that names the few forbidden things, so permission and restraint are taught in that order, the wide table first and the small exclusion after it. The reader is left with a rule that turns the plainest act of the day into worship, and with the reminder that the one who eats what he has been given and names the giver has thanked him without leaving the table.

**What the good things are.**

The permitted ḥalāl is that for which there is no [bad] consequence. The good thing Ṭayyib is that thing whose blessing is not attributed to any created thing. (O ye who believe! Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you) of the lawful things We have given you, (and render thanks to Allah) for it (if it is (indeed) He whom ye worship) it is also said that this means: if you really intend to worship Allah by declaring these to be unlawful, then do not declare them unlawful, for to worship Allah entails that you declare them to be lawful. Eat of the lawful things that We have provided you with, and be grateful to Allah, if it is indeed He Whom you worship He has forbidden you only the Maitah (dead animals), and blood, and the flesh of swine, and that which is slaughtered as a sacrifice for other than Allah. Allah commands His believing servants to eat from the pure things that He has created for them and to thank Him for it, if they are truly His servants. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Messenger, consume the good things that Allah has provided and allowed for you; and be thankful to Allah, outwardly and inwardly, for the overwhelming blessings He has given you. 0 Messengers, eat of the good things and do the righteous.

**What giving thanks at the table carries.**

The true meaning of thankfulness to Him is that you do not take a breath in anything other than the pleasure of the Real so long as the energy given to you by that [permitted and good] food remains. Part of being thankful to Him is acting with complete devotion to Him and not going against Him, if you truly worship Him alone, and do not worship anything besides Him. Human beings should feel thankful and obedient to God while eating food and drinking water. They should express themselves thus, ‘In accordance with God’s commandment, we are eating and drinking what God has provided us with. ’ These emotions evoke in a man the feeling of true devotion to his Maker. As a corollary, they are reminded of Allah's blessings and are taught to be grateful to Him.

**What eating what is lawful does for a person.**

In contrast, eating halal generates inner light, creates a distaste for evil deeds, leads towards high morals, and creates a state in which the heart welcomes ibadah and finds the very thought of sin sickening and of course, prayers are answered. This shows that eating and using what is halal plays a vital role in doing what is good and virtuous. The reason is that the act of eating haram promotes evil instincts, kills the taste of ibadah and makes the prayers ineffective. Therefore, Allah Almighty has told all his prophets to eat from what is good and do what is righteous: Eating from pure sources is a cause for the acceptance of supplications and acts of worship, just as eating from impure sources prevents the acceptance of supplications and acts of worship, as mentioned in a Hadith recorded by Imam Ahmad, that Abu Hurayrah said that Allah's Messenger said:

**What a person owes while eating what he has been given.**

Verse 172 forbids eating that which is Karam and along with it, allows eating that which is halal in all gratefulness to Allah. Human beings should feel thankful and obedient to God while eating food and drinking water. But this psychological make-up changes in the case of self-styled beliefs. In that case man’s attention is diverted to the supposed properties of the things he consumes. Therefore, the same divine blessing which is meant to produce feelings of thanksgiving, evoke instead feelings of veneration for material objects. Part of being thankful to Him is acting with complete devotion to Him and not going against Him, if you truly worship Him alone, and do not worship anything besides Him. The true meaning of thankfulness to Him is that you do not take a breath in anything other than the pleasure of the Real so long as the energy given to you by that [permitted and good] food remains. Earlier, the aim was to correct the error made by the mushrikin when they made unlawful what was good and permissible.
