They read the words as a level ground for the whole of the pilgrimage, since the same standing and the same departure are given to the noble and the poor, and they bring out that the place that was once a badge of rank became a place where a man is known only by his fear of Allah. The sources also notice that the pride of the tribe was joined to a claim of nearness to the House, so the verse cut the claim at the root by naming the place from which the whole crowd departs. And seek Allah's forgiveness. The close turns the pilgrim from the rite to his own shortfall, and the sources carry the account of the invocation of forgiveness that the Prophet taught, in which the servant admits that no one forgives sins but Allah, and they bring out that the asking comes after the labour of the rites so that the worshipper does not carry his own record with him out of the sacred place. The sources also carry the word of the last sermon, that no man has a claim over another except by the fear of Allah, and they bring out that the standing on the plain is a rehearsal of the gathering in which the ranks of the world are set aside. They notice as well that the verse places the asking of forgiveness after the departure, so that the pilgrim leaves the rites with his hands empty and his need open before his Lord, and they read the mercy named at the end as the answer that waits for the one who asks. The reader is left with a road shared by all the pilgrims, a request for pardon at the end of the journey, and the mercy of the One who forgives.

**What the Quraysh did at Arafat.**

The Quraysh of Arabia being the custodians of the Ka'bah enjoyed a unique position of influence and distinction in the country. During the days of Jahiliyyah, while every-one went to Arafat, the Quraysh would, in order to demonstrate their unusual importance, stop at Muzdalifah and stay there. They said that, being the custodian of the Ka'bah and the care-takers of the Har-am it was not proper for them to go out of the limits of the, Haram . Since Muzdalifah is located within the sacred limits of the Haram and Arafat is out of it, they would seize upon the excuse, stay in Muzdalifah and it was from there that they came back. The truth was that they loved to show off their pride and arrogance and made it a point to keep common people at a distance. Al-Bukhari reported that 'A'ishah said, "Quraysh and their allies, who used to be called Al-Hums, used to stay in Al-Muzdalifah while the rest of the Arabs would stand at 'Arafat. Imam Ahmad reported that Jubayr bin Mut'im said, "My camel was lost and I went out in search of it on the day of 'Arafah, and I saw the Prophet standing in 'Arafat. I said to myself, 'By Allah he is from the Hums. The Arabs used to hasten onward from Arafat while the Quraysh and those who followed their religion used to hasten onward from Jam in the Sacred Precinct. This is because the Quraysh used to be called the Hums but the devil led them astray by whispering to them: If you exalt other than your Sacred Precinct, other people will belittle your Sacred Precinct . And so they did not hasten onward from the Sacred Precinct but rather stand at al-Muzdalifah. This was revealed about a group of people called the �Hamsiyyun� who did not want to press on from the Inviolable Place of Worship to 'Arafat during their pilgrimage. Then leave Arafat just as the Prophet Abraham used to do, and do not leave out stopping at Arafat as the people of ignorance used to do.

**What the standing at Arafat with the rest of the people is.**

Then thumma denotes the sequence intended press on O Quraysh from where the people press on that is from ‘Arafa by standing there together with them for they used to stand at Muzdalifa disdaining to stand with other people; and seek God’s forgiveness for your sins; God is Forgiving Merciful to the believers. The third verse : ‌ ‌ ‌,(Then, flow down from where the people flowed, and seek forgiveness from Allah. Certainly, Allah is Most-Forgiving, Very-Merciful) was revealed in a particular background. Their erroneous conduct thus apprehended, Allah Almighty commanded them to go where everyone goes, that is, into the plain of Arafat, and then, return from there with everyone else (it will be noted that in the accompanying translation of the text, the Qur'anic word afidu has been rendered into English liter-ally with the word, 'flow' which succinctly suggests mingling with the multitude, something shunned by the Quraysh of Jahiliyyah). Then depart from the place whence all the people depart and ask Allah for His forgiveness. This Ayah contains Allah's order to those who stand at 'Arafat to also move on to Al-Muzdalifah, so that they remember Allah at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram. Allah commands the Muslim to stand with the rest of the pilgrims at 'Arafat, unlike Quraysh who (before Islam) used to remain in the sanctuary, near Al-Muzdalifah, saying that they are the people of Allah's Town and the servants of His House. When Islam came, Allah commanded His Prophet to stand at 'Arafat and then proceed from there. (...from the place whence all the people depart.) Al-Bukhari reported that Ibn 'Abbas said that 'depart' mentioned in the Ayah refers to proceeding from Al-Muzdalifah to Mina to stone the pillars. (Then hasten onward from the place whence the multitude hasteneth onward) He says: return from whence the people of Yemen have returned, (and ask forgiveness of Allah) for your sins. Allah warned them against this, commanding them to go to 'Arafat and then return from there. Allah, exalted is He, then revealed (Then hasten onward from the place whence the multitude hasteneth onward) . Upon the advent of Islam, Allah, glorious and majestic is He, revealed: (Then hasten onward from the place whence the multitude hasteneth onward), i.e. from Arafah.

**What the pride and the superiority among the pilgrims are.**

To begin with, behaving special and staying disconnected from others is a standing act of arrogance which must almost always be avoided, particularly during the days of Hajj where the garment of Ihram and the homogeneity of place and purpose teach the lesson that all human beings are equal, the distinction of rich and poor, learned and ignorant, big and small does not exist here, therefore, such display of assumed distinction, and that too in a state of Ihram further increases the degree of crime. This statement of the Holy Qur'an teaches us an important principle of social living which demands that the people of a higher status should not cut off their relations with those of a lower status; they should rather behave like members of a large family in their different forms of subsistence, stay and movement. This creates mutual brotherhood, concern and love, removes the walls between the rich and the poor, the employer and the employee. It was during his last sermon of Hajj that the Holy Prophet openly declared for all times to come that no Arab is superior to non-Arab and no white person is superior to a black person. Superiority depends on Taqwa and Ita ah (the fear of Allah and the obedience to His command). Therefore, those who wanted to establish a distinct status for themselves by staying at Muzdalifah, contrary to the rest, were told that this act of theirs was a sin and they must seek forgiveness for it so that Allah Almighty may forgive them and bless them with His mercy. The allusion [in this part of the verse] is that you should not see yourself as different from others because of some manner of dressing patched clothing or some quality that distinguishes you outwardly. Rather you should [consider yourself only as] one among [all] humanity. When the thought comes to you that you have done something or that anything [happens] through you for you or with you seek God's forgiveness and renew your faith for [this kind of thought] is a hidden idolatry shirk that infects your heart. There should be no feeling of superiority over fellow pilgrims, that is, one should ‘press on from where the pilgrims stream forth. ’ Making too much of one’s forefathers, praising their great deeds, is also against the spirit of pilgrimage: pilgrimage is for the glory of God, not for praise of the self.

**What the asking of forgiveness after the rites is.**

Allah frequently orders remembrance of Him after acts of worship are finished. Muslim reported that Allah's Messenger used to ask Allah for His forgiveness thrice after the prayer is finished. It is reported in the Two Sahihs that the Prophet encouraged Tasbih (saying Subhan Allah, i.e., Glorified is Allah), Tahmid (saying Al-Hamdu Lillah, i.e., praise be to Allah) and Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar, i.e., Allah is the Most Great) thirty-three times each (after prayer). (The master of supplication for forgiveness, is for the servant to say: 'O Allah! You are my Lord, there is no deity worthy of worship except You. You have created me and I am Your servant. I am on Your covenant, as much as I can be, and awaiting Your promise. I seek refuge with You from the evil that I have committed. I admit Your favor on me and admit my faults. So forgive me, for none except You forgives the sins.' Whoever said these words at night and died that same night will enter Paradise. Whoever said it during the day and died will enter Paradise.) Teach me an invocation so that I may invoke (Allah) with it in my prayer. (Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran, wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Anta faghfirli maghfiratan min 'indika, war-hamni innaka Antal-Ghafur-ur-Rahim (O Allah! I have done great injustice to myself and none except You forgives sins, so please forgive me and be merciful to me as You are the Forgiver, the Merciful).) Seek forgiveness from Allah for any defects in the performance of the Hajj, for Allah is Forgiving towards those of His servants who repent and He is Merciful towards them. (Lo! Allah is Forgiving) of those who repent, (Merciful) towards those who die in a state of repentance. Then press on from where the people press on and seek God's forgive ness; God is Forgiving Merciful. Then thumma denotes the sequence intended press on O Quraysh from where the people press on that is from ‘Arafa by standing there together with them for they used to stand at Muzdalifa disdaining to stand with other people; and seek God’s forgiveness for your sins; God is Forgiving Merciful to the believers.

200.text:
The verse follows the pilgrim out of the rites and tells him what to do with the memory of them. "When you have fulfilled your sacred rites" sets the moment at the end of the acts and not inside them, so the praise that follows is the closing of the pilgrimage rather than a break in it. "praise Allah as you used to praise your forefathers before Islam" then names the habit the verse is correcting, since the custom at the season was the telling of the names and deeds of fathers and grandfathers, and the verse keeps the shape of that custom while turning it in full toward Allah. "or even more passionately" raises the measure above what the fathers were given, so their memory is not matched but left behind. The turn comes next, "There are some who say, Our Lord! Grant us Your bounties in this world," which is the asking of a person whose request stops at what can be seen, and it is read here as the state of the ones who stood on the same plain with nothing in their hearts but this life. "but they will have no share in the Hereafter" answers that asking with its end, and the verse closes on the loss and not on the finding, so the hearer is left with the two prayers set against each other, the one that asks for this world alone and the one that asks for both, which the verse after this gives. The verse sits at the end of the account of the pilgrimage and turns the tongue of the pilgrim from the memory of his people to the memory of the One he came to, so the closing of the rites is a closing in the direction of Allah and not in the direction of the crowd he stood in.

**The remembrance when the rites are complete.**

And when you have performed and completed your holy rites that is the devotions pertaining to your pilgrimage having cast stones at the Jamrat al-‘Aqaba performed the circumambulation and stopped at Minā remember God by extolling Him and repeating the takbīr saying Allāhu akbar ‘God is Great’ as you remember your fathers as you used to remember them and boast about them at the end of your pilgrimage or yet more intensely than your remembrance of them ashadda is in the accusative because it is a circumstantial qualifier referring to dhikr ‘remembrance’ which itself is in the accusative as the object of udhkurū ‘remember’ because had it come after it it would have functioned as an adjectival phrase. (And when ye have completed your devotions) upon finishing the rites of your pilgrimage, (then remember Allah) say: Now, if Allah Almighty has, in His infinite grace, removed all impediments and one has accomplished his Hajj obligation by successfully performing all required rites, then, the occasion calls for gratitude which further demands that one should keep busy in remembering Allah, avoid wasteful gatherings, engagements or conversations.

**The praise of the forefathers.**

No doubt, contemporary Muslims do not follow the custom of Jahiliyyah any more by holding poetic recitals to eulogize their family trees, but there are thousands of Muslims from all over the world who still spend out these precious days of Hajj in wasteful gatherings, entertainments, amusements, shoppings and similar other pursuits of personal satisfaction. ’ Making too much of one’s forefathers, praising their great deeds, is also against the spirit of pilgrimage: pilgrimage is for the glory of God, not for praise of the self. During the season of pilgrimage, in the pre-Islamic era, people remembered their fathers, events and lineages and, then, boasted about them to each other. Therefore, they were told that, as soon as they have completed their Ihram rites and come to stay at Mina they should dedicate their stay to the remembrance of Allah and leave out the practice of indulging in the reminiscences of their forefathers, specially the boastful claims about their achievements. One of these was that the Arabs of the Jahiliyyah would, once they had finished their rites at Arafat and Muzdalifah and performed their tawaf and sacrifice and stay in Mina hold gatherings to recite poetry and to eulogize the achievements of their forefathers.

**Even more than the fathers.**

We should mention that when Allah used "or" in the Ayah, He meant to encourage the people to remember Him more than they remember their forefathers, not that the word entails a doubt (as to which is larger or bigger). As for the boastful claims about the honour of their fathers, something the people of Jdhiliyyah used to make, this verse eliminates that too by saying that real honour comes through the dhikr of Allah. It is said Your ancestors may have glorious deeds and virtues but Our worthiness from the attributes of sublimity jalāl is far beyond anything due to your ancestors from the best of their states. Sa'id bin Jubayr said that Ibn 'Abbas said, "During the time of Jahiliyyah, people used to stand during the (Hajj) season, and one of them would say, 'My father used to feed (the poor), help others (end their disputes, with his money), pay the Diyah (i.e., blood money),' and so forth.

**The asking for this world alone.**

(�Our Lord! Give unto us in the world,) camels, cows, sheep, male and female slaves and wealth� (and he hath no portion in the Hereafter) of Paradise by performing the pilgrimage. Such people will only ask Allah for the blessing of this world and its beauty in the form of health, wealth and children, and will not receive anything of what Allah has prepared for His faithful servants in the Afterlife. Normally, they would be engaged in acts of devotion to Allah, yet when it came to making a prayer, they would focus all their attention to praying for worldly needs, such as, comfort, wealth, honour and their likes, showing no concern for the life to come. (Our Lord! Give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and save us from the torment of the Fire!")

**No share in the Hereafter.**

For such people the Hereafter holds nothing because their conduct shows that they have gone through the obligation of Hajj merely in a formal manner, or have done it to earn prestige in their society. As for the good of the Hereafter, the best of this includes acquiring Paradise, which also means acquiring safety from the greatest horror at the gathering place. (All praise is due to Allah! You cannot bear it -or stand it-. You should have said: (Our Lord! Give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and save us from the torment of the Fire!) Compared with the time spent by the people of Jahiliyyah in forefather tale-telling which brought them no benefit here, or there, the thing to do here is the dhikr of Allah which is all radiance and benefit for this world, and for the Hereafter. It was to correct this sort of approach in supplication that it was said that there are people who would use the great occasion of Hajj to pray for the insignificant gains of the present life and forget the Hereafter.

**The prayer for the good of both.**

The good of this life concerns every material request of well-being, spacious dwelling, pleasing mates, sufficient provision, beneficial knowledge, good profession or deeds, comfortable means of transportation and good praise, all of which the scholars of Tafsir have mentioned regarding this subject. This is why the Sunnah encourages reciting this Du'a' (i.e., in the Ayah about gaining a good deed in this life and the Hereafter). As long as one remains in this frame of mind, it does not matter if the order of a rite is changed by mistake in performing the rites of pilgrimage, or if one attends to some private business while in the holy land. Al-Qasim bin 'Abdur-Rahman said, "Whoever is gifted with a grateful heart, a remembering tongue and a patient body, will have been endowed with a good deed in this life, a good deed in the Hereafter and saved from the torment of the Fire." As for acquiring safety from the Fire, it includes being directed to what leads to this good end in this world, such as avoiding the prohibitions, sins of all kinds and doubtful matters.

201.text:
The second of the two prayers stands right after the first, and the whole verse is one asking, so it is taken phrase by phrase. "Yet there are others who say, Our Lord" opens on the turn from the group just described, and the address is in the same words the other group used, so the difference between them is not in how they speak to Allah but in what they ask. "Grant us the good of this world and the Hereafter" is the asking itself, and it takes in both homes at once, the good of the life here and the good of the life after, without naming either in detail, so the prayer leaves to the One asked the choice of what is good. "and protect us from the torment of the Fire" then gives a third part, which is not a request for a thing but for safety from a thing, and it stands last because the asking for good is not complete while the danger stands open. The verse before asked for this world alone and closed on having no share in what comes after, and this verse is the answer to it, the same mouth and a different prayer. It is the asking given to the hearers to repeat, and the verse after this gives what follows it, a share for what they earned. The two asks are joined by a single and, and the third part is joined to them in the same breath, so the verse gives the shape of a prayer that leaves nothing out and takes nothing for itself, and it is the prayer the passage puts in the place of the other one.

**Yet there are others who ask.**

And there are others who say ‘Our Lord give to us in this world good a grace and good Paradise in the Hereafter and guard us against the chastisement of the Fire’ by not making us enter it. Yet there is another group of people who have faith in Allah and the Afterlife who ask their Lord for blessing in this world and the ability to do good, just as they ask Him for entry into Paradise and safety from the punishment of the fire of Hell. (And of them (also) is he who saith: �Our Lord! Give unto us in the world that which is good) of knowledge, worship, preservation from sins, martyrdom and booty (and in the Hereafter that which is good) Paradise and its bliss, (and guard us from the doom of Fire) drive away from us the torment of the grave and the torment of hell�. Sa'id bin Jubayr said that Ibn 'Abbas said, "During the time of Jahiliyyah, people used to stand during the (Hajj) season, and one of them would say, 'My father used to feed (the poor), help others (end their disputes, with his money), pay the Diyah (i.e., blood money),' and so forth.

**The good of this world.**

The good of this life concerns every material request of well-being, spacious dwelling, pleasing mates, sufficient provision, beneficial knowledge, good profession or deeds, comfortable means of transportation and good praise, all of which the scholars of Tafsir have mentioned regarding this subject. For instance, hasanah or 'good in this world' shall include personal and family health, increase and benedictory sufficiency (barakah) in lawful livelihood, the fulfillment of all needs, virtuous deeds, desirable morals, beneficial knowledge, honour and prestige, strength of faith, guidance into the straight path and perfect sincerity in ibadat . " It is said that the beautiful thing of this world wanted by the faithful is knowledge and worship, and the beautiful thing of that world is paradise and vision. Then, there are respected people who maintain relations with pious elders of their time, as well as show their regard for deceased saints and walis but the prevailing aim of such relationships is the vague hope that their and ta'widh (prayers and spiritual charms) will work for them, worldly hardships will stay away, and their belongings shall be blessed.

**The good of the Hereafter.**

As for the good of the Hereafter, the best of this includes acquiring Paradise, which also means acquiring safety from the greatest horror at the gathering place. Similarly, hasanah or 'good in the Hereafter' shall cover everything from the Paradise, with its countless and endless blessings to the pleasure of Allah Almighty and the privilege of seeing Him. In the concluding part of this verse, the end of the other class of people who pray for the good of the dunya (mortal world) and akhirah ‌ (Hereafter) both has been stated by saying that they will be rewarded in both the worlds for their correct and righteous conduct and for their prayers. This indicates that they do not care to have what is really good even in this mortal world, on the contrary, they are so drunk with their craze for material things that nothing short of a constant fulfillment of their desires would satisfy them.

**Safety from the torment of the Fire.**

As for acquiring safety from the Fire, it includes being directed to what leads to this good end in this world, such as avoiding the prohibitions, sins of all kinds and doubtful matters. Apart from enjoying peace in the world, and peace in the Hereafter, the verse, refers in the end to the safety from 'the punishment of Fire' as well. This former statement depicts the manner of the idolaters while the latter the way of the believers and is intended to encourage people to petition for good in both abodes for which one is promised a reward as He says. (All praise is due to Allah! You cannot bear it -or stand it-. You should have said: (Our Lord! Give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and save us from the torment of the Fire!) Al-Qasim bin 'Abdur-Rahman said, "Whoever is gifted with a grateful heart, a remembering tongue and a patient body, will have been endowed with a good deed in this life, a good deed in the Hereafter and saved from the torment of the Fire."

**The prayer of both worlds.**

In short, this du a is a compendium of all prayers in as much as it encompasses the entire range of man's worldly and other-worldly objectives. This prayer is more like asking God to give him what is best for man in the eyes of God in this world and what is best for man in the eyes of God in the Hereafter. Therefore, the best prayer for man is to say to his Lord, ‘O my God, give me in this world whatever You see is good for this world, and give me in the next life whatever You see is good for that world and save me from eternal doom.’ So, what is required is that one should not focus all his attention on his material needs as if they were the very purpose of life, but he should, along with it, show far more concern for what would happen to him in the Hereafter, and pray for it.

202.text:
The answer to the prayer of both homes comes in one sentence, and after it a description of the One who answers. "It is they who will receive a heavenly reward for the good they have done" points back to the ones who asked for the good of this world and the Hereafter, and it ties what they receive to what they earned, so the reward is given as the fruit of an act and not as a thing unconnected to it. The wording makes the group plain by pointing at it rather than naming it again, and it takes the earning and not the asking as the ground of the share. "Surely Allah is swift in reckoning" then turns from the reward to the reckoning that settles it, and the word swift is what the verse leaves with the hearer, since a reckoning that is swift is a reckoning that cannot be put off and cannot be forgotten. The verse before gave the prayer, this verse gives what the prayer earns, and the two together close the account of the two groups the passage opened.

**A share for what they earned.**

Those — they shall have a portion a reward from as a result of what they have earned the deeds they have performed such as Pilgrimage and supplication; and God is swift at reckoning reckoning with the whole of creation in half a day of this world as one hadīth states. Those that pray for the good of this world and the Afterlife will receive their share of the great reward for their good actions in the world. For them there will be alloted a share for what they have earned. (But of mankind there are some who say: "Our Lord! Give us (Your bounties) in this world!" and for such there will be no portion in the Hereafter.) meaning, they have no share in the Hereafter. (For these) who are thus (there is in store a goodly portion) a great portion in Paradise (out of that which they have earned) from their pilgrimage. Those-they shall have a portion from what they have earned; If [what they have earned] was good then a good [portion].

**Allah is swift in reckoning.**

(Allah is swift in reckoning) Allah says: when He takes people to task, His reckoning is swift; it is also said that this means: swift in His protection. Following that, it has been said: ‌ (And Allah is swift at reckoning) because His all-pervading knowledge and most perfect power is sufficient to assess the life-long deeds of each and every person who ever breathed in His creation; for this He needs none of those computing mechanisms and means on which only man depends. If it was something else then something else. and God is swift at reckoning [The reckoning occurs] for ordinary people at [the Day of Judgment] and for the elect at every breath. (All praise is due to Allah! You cannot bear it -or stand it-. You should have said: (Our Lord! Give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and save us from the torment of the Fire!)

**The two groups of those who ask.**

It is said that He mentioned two groups: those who say Our Lord give to us in this world and those who say Give to us in this world and the next. The third group which is not mentioned are those who are content with His decree those who submit to His command those who forgo every supplication and request. In the concluding part of this verse, the end of the other class of people who pray for the good of the dunya (mortal world) and akhirah ‌ (Hereafter) both has been stated by saying that they will be rewarded in both the worlds for their correct and righteous conduct and for their prayers. This verse extends a serious warning to those Muslims as well who prefer to pray for their material ends only even at the unique time of Hajj and at places so sacred, devoting most of their concerns towards that goal. This verse also corrects those ignorant dervishes (so called mystics) who think that real ibadah lies in praying for the Hereafter alone and claim that they do not, on that count, care much about the mortal world.

**The gathering and the reckoning.**

‘You shall be gathered before Him’ is the greatest lesson of pilgrimage, given in the plains of Arafat where millions of pilgrims gather annually. This gathering symbolizes the final gathering of all human beings on Doomsday. His punishment is severe towards those who show off in their devotional works. As for the good of the Hereafter, the best of this includes acquiring Paradise, which also means acquiring safety from the greatest horror at the gathering place.

203.text:
The verse closes the account of the pilgrimage with a remembrance and then with a permission. "And remember Allah during these appointed days" names a fixed number of days and puts the remembrance in them, so the ending of the rites is not an end to the remembering but the point where the remembering is asked for on its own. "Whoever departs swiftly on the second day is not sinful" then lifts a burden rather than laying one, and the wording is a leaving of the place where the days are spent, taken here as a matter of choice and not of neglect. "neither are those who stay behind till the third" puts the two on the same footing, so the one who goes early is not blamed and the one who waits is not raised above him. "seeking additional reward" gives the reason the staying is open at all, and it is the ground on which the second choice is taken by those who take it. "so long as they are mindful of their Lord" sets the condition that covers both, so the choice is real only for the one whose fear stays with him. "And be mindful of Allah" repeats that condition after the permission has been given, and the repetition is what the verse is doing at this point, since a permission given at the end of a journey is a place where the heart lets go. "and know that to Him you will all be gathered" closes the passage on the return that has no choice in it, against the two departures that do. The verse is the last of the rites, and it does two things at once, it fixes the days of the remembrance and it settles the question of the two departures, so the pilgrim goes home with a fixed remembrance and a free choice, and with the gathering in front of both.

**The appointed days of remembrance.**

(And remember Allah during the Appointed Days.) means reciting the Takbir – Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, during the days of Tashriq after the compulsory prayers. And remember God by making takbīr saying Allāhu akbar ‘God is Great’ while you cast your stones at the Jamarāt during certain days numbered the three days of tashrīq. In the last of the eight verses relating to injunctions about Hajj, that is, ‌ (And recite the name of Allah in the given number of days), the Hajj pilgrims have been asked to engage themselves in the remembrance of Allah so that their Hajj meets a perfect ending and their post-Hajj life becomes correct and fruitful. The remembrance of the fearful is from dread of being cut off, the remembrance of the hopeful is from wishing to find what they seek, and the remembrance of the lovers is from the tenderness of burning.

**Remember Allah during them.**

Remember Allah by saying, ‘Allāhu Akbar’ (Allah is greatest!), and, ‘Lā ilāhah illā Allāh’ (There is no god except Allah), on the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhū Al-Ḥijjah. (Remember Allah) by saying: �Allah is great�, �there is no god except Allah� and �glory be to Allah�, (through the appointed days) during five days: the day of 'Arafah, the day of immolation and the three days after it. The remembrance of the Beginningless reached the recognizers and they fled from effort to their lot. If we look at the manner in which the choice of returning from Mina has been given to the Hujjaj - no sin if they return on the second day and no sin if they return on the third day - we shall realize that all this is for the convenience of one who fears Allah and obeys His commands, for he really deserves the Hajj, as said elsewhere in the Holy Qur'an 27which means that Allah Almighty accepts (acts of prayer and worship) only from those who are God-fearing and obedient.

**Whoever hastens in two days.**

But whosoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin on him and whosoever stays on, there is no sin on him, if his aim is to do good and obey Allah (fear Him), and know that you will surely be gathered unto Him. If any man hastens on his departure from Minā in two days that is on the second day of tashrīq after he has cast his stones that hastening is no sin for him; and if he delays such that he stays until the third night and cast his stones it is not a sin for him that is they have the choice of either for the sin has been precluded in both cases; if he fears God during his pilgrimage — for such a person is truly a pilgrim — and fear God and know that to Him you shall be gathered in the Hereafter that He may requite you for your deeds. If anyone is in a hurry, he may leave Minā after pelting stones on the 12th of Dhū Al-Ḥijjah – and there will be no sin as Allah has granted that permission. (Then whoso hasteneth (in departure) to return to his family (by two days) after the day of immolation, (it is no sin for him) by this hastening, (and whoso delayeth) it to the third day, (it is no sin for him) by this delay; it is said that this means: there is no reproach on him because of this delay and he shall leave with his sins forgiven; (that is for him who wardeth off (evil) He says: hastening departure is for him who avoids hunting until the third day.

**Those who stay behind.**

Both were corrected in this verse by saying: ‌ : 'Then whoever is early (in leaving) after two days there is no sin on him and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him ...' thereby proving that both parties calling each other sinners are involved in excess and error. All of this applies to those that are mindful of Allah during their Hajj and carry it out in accordance with Allah’s instruction. And remember God in certain numbered days, but if someone hastens on after two days.... (The days of Mina (Tashriq) are three. Those who hasten in two days then there is no sin in it, and those who delay (i.e., remain in Mina for a third day) then there is no sin in it.) If those who are lucky to perform their Hajj are a little more mindful of this factor, they might stay by their solemn pledge later on. Immediately following is a clarification of the duration of stay at Mina and the deadline for throwing pebbles at the three Pillars.

**The fear of Allah in the days.**

It means that one should keep fearing Allah during the special days of the Hajj guarding oneself from any shortcoming in the prescribed acts of Hajj, as he should keep fearing Allah after the Hajj guarding himself against any pride of performance, and keep abstaining from sins because, on the day human deeds shall be weighed on the Balance, his sins will eat away his good deeds, that is, they will nullify the effect and weight of the good deeds. This is why those performing Hajj have been instructed to maintain the quality of Taqwa, (that vital sense of responsibility before Allah). (Be careful of your duty to Allah) He says: fear Allah in taking what is hunted until the third day, (and know that unto Him ye will be gathered) after you die. Therefore, the final word said was about the need to fear Allah and the necessity to obey Him, not only before the Hajj and during the Hajj, but also after the Hajj when one must become much more particular in fearing Allah and alert in abstaining from sins by conscious effort, lest all that one has done in the form of the ibadah of Hajj goes waste.

**The gathering to Him.**

‘You shall be gathered before Him’ is the greatest lesson of pilgrimage, given in the plains of Arafat where millions of pilgrims gather annually. This gathering symbolizes the final gathering of all human beings on Doomsday. When mentioning the first procession (refer to 2:199) and the second procession of the people upon the end of the Hajj season, when they start to return to their areas, after they had gathered during the rituals and at the standing places, Allah said,. Closing this eight-verse unit, it was said: ‌ (And fear Allah and be sure that you are going to be gathered before Him), where He shall make you account for all your open and hidden deeds and give you the reward and punishment for these.

204.text:
The verse turns from the pilgrim to a kind of person, and it describes him in one piece and then in its two halves. "There are some hypocrites who impress you with their views regarding worldly affairs and openly call upon Allah to witness what is in their hearts" is the whole description, and the first half of it is the outer part of the man, the speech that is pleasing and the talk that sounds like sense in the business of this life, and the wording puts the pleasing of the hearer first, so the verse begins where the danger begins, in the ear of the one listening. The second half is the oath, that the inside matches the outside, and the verse joins the two so that the claim about the heart stands on the same tongue that made the pleasing speech. "yet they are your worst adversaries" is the turn, and it comes at the end rather than at the start, so the hearer takes in the pleasant speech before he is told what is behind it, and the word worst sets this group below the open enemy in the order of danger. The verse stands where the passage turns from the rites of the House to the state of hearts, and it is the first of a pair, since the verse after this gives what the same man does when he has gone away from the hearing of it. The verse is a warning to the hearer rather than a description for its own sake, since the danger it names is a danger in the hearing, and the hearer is the one who has to know what stands behind a pleasing voice and an oath about the heart.

**Speech about the life of this world.**

And among people there is he whose speech in the life of this world pleases you but it would not please you in the Hereafter because it contradicts what he actually used to believe; and who calls on God to witness what is in his heart as being in accordance with what he says; yet he is most stubborn in dispute with you and your followers on account of his enmity towards you this was al-Akhnas b. (And of mankind there is he whose conversation on the life of this world pleaseth thee (Muhammad) his speech, words and outward appearance pleases you, (and he calleth Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart) he swears by Allah that he loves and follows you; (yet he is the most rigid of opponents) yet he argues about falsehood and is a staunch opponent. And among people there is he whose speech in the life of this world pleases you; and who calls on God to witness what is in his heart; yet he is most stubborn in dispute.

**Calling Allah to witness the heart.**

He calls Allah to witness that he has faith and goodness in his heart whilst he is in fact lying: he bears great hostility and hatred for the Muslims. It has been reported by Hakim, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim with sound authorities, that this verse was revealed in connection with a particular event relating to the blessed Companion Suhayb al-Rumi . I have come to embrace Islam, and Allah knows I am truthful , this is what Allah states when He says (and he calleth Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart). (Verily, Allah has purchased of the believers their lives and their properties for (the price) that theirs shall be the Paradise. They fight in Allah's cause, so they kill (others) and are killed. It is a promise in truth which is binding on Him in the Tawrah and the Injil and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? Then rejoice in the bargain which you have concluded. That is the supreme success.)(9:111)

**The worst of enemies.**

Allah said, 'They dare challenge Me, but they are deceived by Me. They just go by what is calculated to make a favourable impression on the listener. There is no meaning beyond [their outward selves] and nothing of weight in what they say. (And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you will notice a denial on the faces of the disbelievers! They are nearly ready to attack with violence those who recite Our verses to them. Say: "Shall I tell you of something worse than that? The Fire (of Hell) which Allah has promised to those who disbelieved, and worst indeed is that destination!)(22:72) So enough for him is Hell, and worst indeed is that place to rest And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. (So enough for him is Hell, and worst indeed is that place to rest) meaning, the Fire is enough punishment for the hypocrite.

**The hypocrite and his speech.**

This Ayah indicates that such people pretend to be Muslims, but defy Allah by the disbelief and hypocrisy that their hearts conceal. He would come to the Holy Prophet and try to impress him with his sworn allegiance to Islam, but no sooner did he walk out of his company than he would get busy with his anti-Muslim mischief-making. However, some commentators cite similar events relating to other noble Companions as the background of the verse's revelation (Mazhari). Ibn Jarir related that Al-Qurazi said that Nawf Al-Bikali, who used to read (previous Divine) Books said, "I find the description of some members of this Ummah in the previously revealed Books of Allah: they (hypocrites) are people who use the religion to gain material benefit. This Ayah indicates that when the hypocrite, who deviates in his speech and deeds, is advised and commanded to fear Allah, refrain from his evil deeds and adhere to the truth, he refuses and becomes angry and outraged, as he is used to doing evil.

**What he does when he turns away.**

On one occasion he passed by some crops and livestock that belonged to the Muslims and later that night he set fire to them the crops and slaughtered them the livestock. Upon leaving the Messenger of Allah, he passed by a cultivated field and some asses which belonged to some Muslims. Allah, exalted is He, revealed about him (And when he turneth away (from thee) his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle) [2:205] . He relates that the Real has given some people skill in speaking outwardly yet [He] has turned away from their hearts which are bound by the ropes of deprivation and covered by their own ignorance. (And when he turns away (from you O Muhammad), he struggles in the land to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle, and Allah likes not mischief.)

**The tongue sweeter than honey.**

Their tongues are sweeter than honey, but their hearts are more bitter than Sabir (a bitter plant, aloe). That is why they can never acknowledge truth if it comes from a preacher whom they consider inferior to them. There are others who sell their lives, not for themselves, but for God; it is to find favour with Him that they strive. It was also said that the Ayah means that when such people announce their Islam, they swear by Allah that what is in their hearts is the same of what their tongues are pronouncing. This Ayah indicates that such persons are deviant in the tongue, evil in the deeds, their words are fabricated, their belief is wicked and their works are immoral.

205.text:
The verse follows the man of the verse before it out of the room and shows what he does away from the hearing. "And when they leave you" is the first phrase and the whole turn of the passage, since the pleasing speech was for the ear of the hearer and what comes now is what happens where that ear is not. "they strive throughout the land to spread mischief in it and destroy crops and cattle" gives the work in two parts, the mischief spread and the two things destroyed, and the naming of crops and cattle puts the harm in the fields and the herds, that is, in the food of the people and their wealth, so the mischief is not a word only but a ruin that others carry. "Allah does not like mischief" closes the verse with the ground of the whole account, and it is a description of Allah and not a command to the hearer, so the verse ends by placing the man against something larger than the people he harms. The passage now has the two kinds side by side, the one whose speech is sweet and whose work is ruin, and the one whose life is given up, which the verse after this brings in.

**When he turns away.**

And when he turns his back leaving you behind he hastens he walks about the earth to do corruption there and to destroy the tillage and the stock these last two actions are included in such ‘corruption’; and God loves not corruption that is to say it does not please Him. (And when he turneth away (from thee) when he is angry (his effort in the land is to make mischief therein) by committing transgressions (and to destroy the crops) and stacks of grain by burning them (and the cattle) by killing them; (and Allah loveth not mischief) or those who commit it.

**The mischief in the land and the ruin of the crops.**

The hypocrite has no motive in this life but to cause mischief and to destroy the crops and the offspring, including what the animals produce and what the people depend on for their livelihood. When this Hypocrite leaves you, he works hard to cause corruption by committing sins, and he destroys crops and kills animals. Outward corruption is whatever brings about the ruin of religious affairs and the proper ordering of worldly matters. He would come to the Holy Prophet and try to impress him with his sworn allegiance to Islam, but no sooner did he walk out of his company than he would get busy with his anti-Muslim mischief-making. When they retire to their whis perings and ruinous aims they hasten to corruption make decisions based on worldly [aims] and employ people to help them in furthering their affairs-people from whose hearts God has removed inner sight. (And when he turns away (from you O Muhammad), he struggles in the land to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle, and Allah likes not mischief.) Mujahid said, "If the hypocrite strives for mischief in the land, Allah prevents the rain from falling and thus the crops and the offspring perish.

**Allah does not like mischief.**

Allah does not love corruption in the land and He does not love those that cause corruption. Hence, a hypocrite lies, alters the truth when he quarrels and does not care for the truth. After that the ropes [tying them to] the world become stronger and the bonds of their desires become more closely woven with the prohibited things they have gathered and the debris they have acquired. And of mankind there is he whose speech may please you (O Muhammad), in this worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart, yet he is the most quarrelsome of the opponents And when he turns away (from you O Muhammad), his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle, and Allah likes not mischief And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah", he is led by arrogance to (more) crime.

**Who it was revealed about.**

This was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah. He came to the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, in Medina, and pretended to be a Muslim. Any effort to make such a person fear Allah takes him to the other extreme when he pleases his pride through sin. Ibn Jarir related that Al-Qurazi said that Nawf Al-Bikali, who used to read (previous Divine) Books said, "I find the description of some members of this Ummah in the previously revealed Books of Allah: they (hypocrites) are people who use the religion to gain material benefit. He abandoned his money and preferred to migrate, and Allah revealed this Ayah about him. 'Umar bin Khattab and several other Companions met Suhayb close to the outskirts of Al-Madīnah at Al-Harrah (flat lands with black stones).

206.text:
The verse takes the same man again and gives what happens when he is answered. "When it is said to them, Fear Allah" is the address of a third party, not the verse speaking to him but someone putting the fear of Allah to him, and the wording is short because the whole case turns on the answer. "pride carries them off to sin" gives that answer without quoting it, and the wording puts the pride in the seat of the acting, so the sin is described as the place the pride takes him to rather than as a choice he weighs. "Hell will be their proper place" then names the end of that carrying, and it is given as what is enough for him and what belongs to him, a place he has earned. "What an evil place to rest" closes on the place itself, and the word rest is the point, since the ending of a journey is a settling and this settling is the opposite of one. The verse stands between the description of the mischief and the description of the man who gives his life away, so the two are set against each other with the answer to advice in the middle.

**Fear Allah.**

And when it is said to him ‘Fear God’ in your actions he is seized by vainglory pride and rage in his sin the one he was commanded to avoid committing. (And when it is said unto him: Be careful of your duty to Allah) regarding what you are doing, (pride taketh him to sin) he takes offence because of his pride. When this person who causes corruption is advised to be mindful of Allah by respecting His limits and avoiding His prohibitions, his pride and arrogance prevents him from repenting, and he continues to sin. And of mankind there is he whose speech may please you (O Muhammad), in this worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart, yet he is the most quarrelsome of the opponents And when he turns away (from you O Muhammad), his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle, and Allah likes not mischief And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah", he is led by arrogance to (more) crime.

**The pride of the hypocrite.**

Any effort to make such a person fear Allah takes him to the other extreme when he pleases his pride through sin. When you enjoin someone [like this] to decency he says How can you say this to someone like me when I am such and suchḍ Then he turns it around and attacks you saying You have more need to be enjoined with decency and forbidden indecency because your condi tion is such and such... If God had granted success to help him or mercy had reached him he would have been granted the favor shown to those who have been guided to seeing their errors and observing their bad traits. I swear by Myself that I will send a Fitnah (trial, calamity) on them that will make the wise man bewildered.' I contemplated about these statements and found them in the Qur'an describing the hypocrites: (The signs of a hypocrite are three: Whenever he speaks, he tells a lie. Whenever he promises, he always breaks it (his promise). If you have a dispute with him, he is most quarrelsome.)

**Hell will be enough for him.**

So Hell shall be enough it suffices for him — how evil a cradling a resting place it is! (Hell will settle his account) his destination will be hell, (an evil resting place). The only appropriate reward for him is entry into Hell. So Hell shall be enough for him-how evil a cradling! (And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you will notice a denial on the faces of the disbelievers! They are nearly ready to attack with violence those who recite Our verses to them. Say: "Shall I tell you of something worse than that? The Fire (of Hell) which Allah has promised to those who disbelieved, and worst indeed is that destination!)(22:72)

**An evil place to rest.**

What a terrible place to reside in for its inhabitants! God most high said So hell shall be enough for him meaning [hell is] the state of his estrangement the darknesses of the lower self and the constriction of choice such that he does not hasten in anything except his [lower] desire. The world will end, to give way to a new and finer system in which they will be brought low, and the great will be cut down to size, and those who had been considered lowly will occupy high places in the heavenly world. This Ayah indicates that when the hypocrite, who deviates in his speech and deeds, is advised and commanded to fear Allah, refrain from his evil deeds and adhere to the truth, he refuses and becomes angry and outraged, as he is used to doing evil.

**Who it was revealed about.**

As-Suddi said that these Ayat were revealed about Al-Akhnas bin Shariq Ath-Thaqafi who came to Allah's Messenger and announced his Islam although his heart concealed otherwise. This verse was revealed about al-Akhnas Ibn Shurayq who was both eloquent and good looking and the Prophet ﷺ used to like his speech. But he was a hypocrite and it is alleged that he burned someone's crops and killed a donkey belonging to others. Ibn Jarir related that Al-Qurazi said that Nawf Al-Bikali, who used to read (previous Divine) Books said, "I find the description of some members of this Ummah in the previously revealed Books of Allah: they (hypocrites) are people who use the religion to gain material benefit.

207.text:
The verse turns from the man whose speech is pleasing to the man whose life is given, and the turn is in one phrase. "And there are those who would dedicate their lives to Allah's pleasure" describes a giving in which the thing given is the self and the reason for the giving is the pleasure of Allah, so the verse puts the two halves of an act together, what is handed over and what is sought by the handing over. The wording is a buying and a selling in the language of the passage, and it is read here as a man setting his own life down for a thing that is not his life, which is why the verse before it, where the man sets his life down for the world, is its opposite. "And Allah is Ever Gracious to His servants" closes with a description of Allah rather than with a reward named for the one who gave, and the kindness in the phrase is taken as the ground on which such a giving is possible at all, since the servant who sells himself does it under a care that was there before the act. The two verses together close the account of the two kinds of people the passage set out.

**The man who sells himself.**

But there are other men who sell themselves expend themselves in obedience to God desiring God’s pleasure this was Suhayb b. (And of mankind is he who would sell himself) with his wealth, (seeking the pleasure of Allah) in pursuit of Allah's pleasure. There is another type of person who is a believer, who will sell and give up his soul to follow his Lord and to strive in His path seeking His pleasure. But there are other men who sell themselves desiring God's pleasure; and God is gentle with His servants. So enough for him is Hell, and worst indeed is that place to rest And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. (And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is full of kindness to servants.)

**The pleasure of Allah.**

(And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah.) Those who have been touched by the special favors of mercy and raised up by the fate already preordained [for them] prefer the good pleasure of the Real over themselves and submit entirely to their protector mawlā. The last verse portrays the true, the sincere Muslim who would stake his very life to achieve the good pleasure of Allah Almighty. (Verily, Allah has purchased of the believers their lives and their properties for (the price) that theirs shall be the Paradise. They fight in Allah's cause, so they kill (others) and are killed. It is a promise in truth which is binding on Him in the Tawrah and the Injil and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? Then rejoice in the bargain which you have concluded. That is the supreme success.)(9:111)

**Suhayb, the man who sold himself.**

This was revealed about Suhayb Ibn Sinan and his companions. He ransomed himself from the Meccans with his money; (and Allah hath compassion on bondmen) those who were killed in Makkah. When Suhayb set off to emigrate to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, a group of idolaters from the Quraysh followed him. [When they caught up with him,] he came off his mount, emptied his quiver and held his bow. Sinān al-Rūmī who emigrated to Medina when the idolaters began to persecute him leaving them all his property; and God is Gentle with His servants for He guides them to what pleases Him. O Abu Yahya! and Allah revealed the verse (of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah) .

**Allah is gentle with His servants.**

Allah’s mercy for His servants is vast and He is Kind to them. God is gentle with His servants and because of His gentleness they attain these states-they do not deserve His gentleness because of these states. This was revealed about the parents of 'Ammar Ibn Yasir (Yasir and Sumayyah) and others who were killed by the Meccan idolaters. And of mankind there is he whose speech may please you (O Muhammad), in this worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart, yet he is the most quarrelsome of the opponents And when he turns away (from you O Muhammad), his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle, and Allah likes not mischief And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah", he is led by arrogance to (more) crime.

**The two ways of taking Islam.**

In the previous verses, it was said that there are two kinds of those who make prayers. In the present verse, the same two kinds have been identified as those who are hypocritical and those who are sincere. There are two ways of adopting Islam as one’s religion. Those who put their own interests first and Islam second, and those who unconditionally enter into Islam are people of very different mettle. One who adopts the latter course does not let Islam undermine the habits he is accustomed to, the creeds he cherishes, the profits he craves, the honour he thrives on or the leadership he seeks to preserve and consolidate.

208.text:
The verse addresses the believers by name and gives them two things in one breath, a way in and a way to keep off. "O believers! Enter into Islam wholeheartedly and do not follow Satan's footsteps" is the command whole, and it is taken here in its two halves. The first is the entering, and the word carries the whole of the thing entered, so the command is not to take a part of it and stop but to go in with the whole self, which is what the phrase about the heart in the command comes to. The second is the footsteps, and the wording is footsteps rather than the man himself, so what is refused is the following of a path step by step and not a single open act. "Surely he is your sworn enemy" gives the reason the following is refused, and the word plain in the description is what the hearer is left with, since the enmity is not hidden and needs no uncovering. The verse stands after the account of the man who speaks well and works ruin and the man who gives his life away, and it is addressed to those who are neither, so the command to enter fully answers the two half ways just described.

**Enter Islam wholeheartedly.**

Salām and his companions who after converting to Islam still observed the Sabbath with reverence and were averse to the consumption of camels O you who believe come all of you into submission read al-salm or al-silm that is Islam; kāffatan is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-silm meaning into all of its precepts; and follow not the steps the ways of Satan that is his temptations to you by way of creating divisions; he is a manifest foe to you one whose enmity is obvious. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Messenger, enter Islam completely and do not leave out any part of it like how the People of the Scripture believed in some parts of the book and disbelieved other parts. O you who believe come all of you into submission; and follow not the steps of Satan; he is a manifest foe to you. [God] has charged the believer with making peace with everyone except his lower self for it makes no move except to oppose [the believer's] leader sayyid.

**The footsteps of Satan.**

(...and follow not the footsteps of Shaytan) meaning, perform the acts of worship and avoid what Satan commands you to do. Therefore, the prohibition 'do not follow the footsteps of Satan', an enemy who would cheat you into taking to something which obviously looks very much like your Faith, but happens to be totally contrary to it in reality. Do not follow the ways of Satan, because he has made it clear that he is your enemy. The steps of Satan are what are whispered to you about your inability to hold to the precepts of moral behavior and [your inability] to abandon unwise inclinations that are best ignored.

**The plain enemy of the believers.**

(Lo! He is an open enemy for you) whose enmity is quite manifest. This is the reason a seeker falls short and an aspirant loses interest. It is in this background of the verse's revelation, that believers have been asked to 'enter Islam completely', not making allowances for a faith other than Islam - a divisive approach which makes one an easy target of Satan. Verily, he is to you a plain enemy Then if you slide back after the clear signs (Prophet Muhammad , and this Qur'an and Islam) have come to you, then know that Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.

**The believers who still kept parts of the old ways.**

The following verse was revealed regarding ‘Abd Allāh b. This verse was revealed about 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his followers. This is because when they believed in the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, they observed the laws that he brought forth while still observing the laws of Moses. Since Saturday was the sacred day of rest (the Sabbath) in Judaism, and camel-meat was unlawful, they thought, once they were in Islam, to bring about some sort of a synthesis between the two faiths, through which they could continue to honour Sabbath as it was necessary under the law of Moses while Islam did not require dishonouring it; and similarly, they could simply avoid eating camel-meat in practice while believing that it was lawful, for it was unlawful in the law of Moses but Islam does not make it obligatory to eat it.

**What they kept from the Sabbath.**

They observed the Sabbath and shunned the meat and milk of camels after they embraced Islam. Some Muslims reproached them for this but they defended themselves by saying that they could observe both. This is because they believed in Allah, some of them still followed some parts of the Tawrah and the previous revelations. Secondly, it is possible to take the word, silm as the hal or indicated state of the Faith in Islam, in which case, the translation would be referring to the perfect and complete state of Islam in which the believers must enter. (O ye who believe! Come, all of you, into submission) come all of you to the prescriptions of the Religion of Muhammad ﷺ; (and follow not the footsteps of the devil) follow not the embellishments of the devil regarding the unlawfulness of the Sabbath, the meat of camels and other things.

209.text:
The verse speaks to the same believers and gives what follows a slip. "If you falter after receiving the clear proofs" sets the case, and the two parts of it matter, the slipping and the fact that it comes after proofs that are plain, so the verse is not about a person who has never been given the ground but about one who has it and moves off it anyway. "then know that Allah is indeed Almighty, All-Wise" is the answer, and it is a knowledge asked for rather than a punishment named, so the verse turns the one who slipped toward the two descriptions, the power that cannot be escaped and the wisdom that is in what is laid down. The verse closes the passage that began with the command to enter fully, and it is the warning that belongs to that command, since a person told to go in with the whole self is a person who can come back out. It stands before the verses that carry the argument on to the next matter, and it leaves the hearer with the two names rather than with a threat.

**The slip after the clear proofs.**

But if you slip and incline away from implementing all of its precepts after the clear proofs the lucid arguments have come to you to the effect that this is the truth know then that God is Mighty and nothing can prevent Him from taking His vengeance against you; Wise in His actions. (And if ye slide back after the clear proofs have come unto you) after the exposition which is in your Scripture, (then know that Allah is Mighty) in His vengeance towards anyone who does not follow His Messenger, (Wise) in abrogating the laws of bygone nations.

**Allah is Almighty and Wise.**

Those who still slip, they must remember that Allah is Mighty, having the power to punish, and Wise too, lest one should misread any delay in punishment which comes when His Wisdom so dictates. Allah commands His servants who believe in Him and have faith in His Messenger to implement all of Islam's legislation and law, to adhere to all of its commandments, as much as they can, and to refrain from all of its prohibitions. 'Al-'Awfi said that Ibn 'Abbas said, and also Mujahid, Tawus, Ad-Dahhak, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said that Allah's statement: A single slip after the disclosure of clear proofs is uglier by far than the many slips committed before this disclosure. The correct position is that such coming of Allah Almighty belongs to the Mutashabihat statements of hidden meaning, about which there is a standard policy practiced by the majority of the blessed Companions, the Tabi in their successors, and the revered elders of the Muslim ummah, that is, one must believe in its truth and avoid worrying about as to how this would happen because it is beyond human reason to find out the reality and the nature, the whats and the hows of the 'Being' and the Attributes of Allah Almighty, and this too is included therein.

**The cost of a slip after guidance.**

Those who are known to be treacherous cannot be trusted. As sincerity (ikhlas) can sometimes touch the limits of excess inadvertently, that is, one does intend to come up with more obedience, but that obedience, when observed carefully, turns out to be exceeding the limits set by the Shari'ah and Sunnah. Using an eloquent image, the text goes on to question the ultimate acceptance of truth at a time when it shall no longer remain worth accepting and al'_ matters of reward and punishment shall revert to Allah with no power existing other than Him, why then would anyone become quixotic enough to stand against a Power so obvious, the result of which could be nothing but destruction. When that happens, a sudden surge of belief will not benefit anyone, for that will be a time when fates are sealed, not forged. Verily, he is to you a plain enemy Then if you slide back after the clear signs (Prophet Muhammad , and this Qur'an and Islam) have come to you, then know that Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise. This would mean that their entire person, hands and feet, eyes and ears, feeling and thinking, after having embraced the Faith should all be within the parameters of Islam and the obedience to Allah.

**The believers and the clear proofs.**

This was revealed about 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his companions because they disliked the Sabbath and the meat of camels amongst other things. This is because they believed in Allah, some of them still followed some parts of the Tawrah and the previous revelations. Allah Almighty corrects this thought in the present verse which aims to establish that Islam is an obligation in its totality. Since Saturday was the sacred day of rest (the Sabbath) in Judaism, and camel-meat was unlawful, they thought, once they were in Islam, to bring about some sort of a synthesis between the two faiths, through which they could continue to honour Sabbath as it was necessary under the law of Moses while Islam did not require dishonouring it; and similarly, they could simply avoid eating camel-meat in practice while believing that it was lawful, for it was unlawful in the law of Moses but Islam does not make it obligatory to eat it.

210.text:
The verse asks a question about waiting, and the question is the explanation. "Are they waiting for Allah Himself to come to them in the shade of clouds" puts the case of the people addressed in the form of a waiting, and the wording names the thing waited for in the plainest way, a coming of Allah to them with the clouds as a shade over the coming, so the verse takes up what such people ask for and gives it back to them as a thing that would end the matter rather than begin a faith. "along with the angels" completes the picture, since the coming is not described as hidden or as a sign read from far off but as an arrival with the angels around it, and that is the shape of a thing that leaves nothing to decide. "If He did" is the shortest phrase in the verse and the hinge of it, because it turns the waiting into a supposition and asks what would follow. "then the matter would be settled at once" gives the answer, and the settling is described as complete, so the verse tells the hearer that the coming he asks for is the coming that closes the case, and after it there is no room left for a choice. "And to Allah all matters will be returned for judgment" then puts the same end in another form, without the clouds and without the angels, and it is the phrase the verse leaves standing, since the return of all matters is what happens whether or not the coming asked for happens. The verse stands at the end of the passage that told the believers to enter fully and warned them of the slip, and it turns from the believers to the ones who stand outside asking for a sign, and it answers them with the end of the matter rather than with the sign.

**Waiting for Allah to come in the clouds.**

Do they then wait for anything other than that Allah should come to them over the shadows of the clouds and the angels? Islam completely wait for await that God shall come to them that is His Command; this is similar to where God says or that God’s command should come to pass Q. 1633 meaning His chastisement in the shadows zulal plural of zulla of clouds and the angels? (Wait they) the people of Makkah (for nothing else than that Allah should come unto them) on the Day of Judgement, but this coming is without any modality (bila-kayfa) (in the shadows of the clouds with the angels? Then the case would be already judged) the people of Paradise would already be in Paradise and the people of hell in hell. As sincerity (ikhlas) can sometimes touch the limits of excess inadvertently, that is, one does intend to come up with more obedience, but that obedience, when observed carefully, turns out to be exceeding the limits set by the Shari'ah and Sunnah.

**The matter would be settled.**

The matter is determined the matter of their destruction has been completed and to God all matters are returned in the Hereafter where He will requite each according to his deeds read passive turja‘u al-umūr ‘matters are returned’ or active tarji‘u al-umūr ‘matters return’. The matter is determined and to God all matters are returned that is the veil of the unseen is removed exposing the clarity of the [divine] preordination. Since Islam is the name of that particular way of life which has been given through the Qur'an and Sunnah, there-fore, it does not matter, which facet of life it concerns, it may be beliefs and acts of worship or social dealings or business transactions or government and politics or trade and industry or any other field; what matters is one's entry into Islam as a complete system, an organic whole, unified, indivisible. Using an eloquent image, the text goes on to question the ultimate acceptance of truth at a time when it shall no longer remain worth accepting and al'_ matters of reward and punishment shall revert to Allah with no power existing other than Him, why then would anyone become quixotic enough to stand against a Power so obvious, the result of which could be nothing but destruction.

**All matters return to Allah.**

(All cases go back to Allah) the consequences of all things go back to Allah in the Hereafter. To Allah alone shall all affairs relating to creation return. (Do they then wait for anything other than that Allah should come to them over the shadows of the clouds and the angels?) means, the angels will descend on the shadows of clouds, while Allah comes as He wills. The correct position is that such coming of Allah Almighty belongs to the Mutashabihat statements of hidden meaning, about which there is a standard policy practiced by the majority of the blessed Companions, the Tabi in their successors, and the revered elders of the Muslim ummah, that is, one must believe in its truth and avoid worrying about as to how this would happen because it is beyond human reason to find out the reality and the nature, the whats and the hows of the 'Being' and the Attributes of Allah Almighty, and this too is included therein.

**The waiting and the doubt of the one who will not believe.**

What else is the doubter waiting for, but that God Himself should appear, along with all the angels? But those who cannot bring themselves to accept clear arguments will not be won over by miracles of this nature. The people thought that the Hour would be long in coming but the details tell them of the severity of the matter. [What are described] are acts af ʿāl [of God] only in the sense of the terrible events ahwāl [of that Hour]. God divulges them so as to remove their doubt concerning the gran deur of His affair and the implementation of His power in what He wills.

**The coming of the Lord and the angels.**

(Nay! When the earth is ground to powder. And your Lord comes with the angels in rows. And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance (then) avail him?)(89:21-23) and: The world will end, to give way to a new and finer system in which they will be brought low, and the great will be cut down to size, and those who had been considered lowly will occupy high places in the heavenly world. When that happens, a sudden surge of belief will not benefit anyone, for that will be a time when fates are sealed, not forged. These people who follow the path of Satan, instead of the path of truth, are waiting only for Allah to come to them, as befits His majesty, on the Day of Resurrection in the shadows of clouds to judge them and for the angels to come and surround them from all sides. As regards the possibility of 'Allah Almighty and the angels coming upon them in canopies of clouds,' this will be on Doomsday.

211.text:
The verse puts a question to a people and then draws the lesson out of it. "Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We have given them" is the question, and it is put in the second person, so the hearer is sent to a people who are still there to be asked, and the asking is not for information but for the answer those people give themselves, which is the number of the signs and what came of them. The phrase how many clear signs is the heart of it, since the signs are described as clear, and the verse is not about a people who had no ground but about a people who had it in front of them. "And whoever trades Allah's favour" turns from them to anyone who does what they did, and the word for the act is a trading, a setting of one thing down for another, which is why the phrases that follow give both sides of the trade. "after receiving it" fixes the order, so the case is not of a person who never had the favour but of one who had it in his hand. "for disbelief should know that Allah is indeed severe in punishment" gives the thing taken in exchange and then the knowledge asked of him, and the verse ends on a description of the punishment rather than on the punishment itself, so what the hearer is left with is the severity and not a number. The verse stands after the question about waiting, and it answers that question by pointing at a people who were given what they asked for in signs and lost it, so the passage moves from the sign asked for to the sign received and thrown away, and the verse after this gives the state of the ones who throw it away in this world.

**The Children of Israel and the clear signs.**

Ask the Children of Israel how many clear Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) We gave them. Ask O Muhammad the Children of Israel by way of rebuke how many a clear proof manifest ones such as the parting of the sea and the sending down of manna and quails which they exchanged for unbelief did We give them kam ‘how many’ is the interrogative particle linking the second object of the verb sal ‘ask’ and is also the second object of the verb ātaynā ‘We gave’ and its specifier; whoever changes God’s grace that is what God has blessed him with in the way of signs for these constitute the causes of guidance after it has come to him out of unbelief God is severe in retribution against him. (Ask the children of Israel) tell the children of Jacob (how many a clear revelation We gave them!) how may times We addressed them with commands and prohibitions, and honoured them with Religion in the time of Moses, but they exchanged all that with disbelief. O Prophet, ask the Jews about how many clear signs proving the truthfulness of the messengers were given to them by Allah. So, it should not be strange that many chiefs among the Israelites and the ignorant among polytheists would make fun of poor Muslims.

**Trading the favour of Allah.**

(He who altereth the grace of Allah) whoever exchanges the Religion and Scripture of Allah with disbelief (after it hath come unto him) after what Muhammad has come with ((for him), lo! Allah is severe in punishment) for whoever disbelieves in Him. Whoever changes God's grace after it has come to him God is severe in retribution in taking this grace away. If anyone changes the favour of Allah into disbelief and denial after being aware of it and after it has become obvious, then Allah is strong in punishing the disbelievers and the deniers. The first verse here cites the case of the elders of Bani Isra'il who were punished for their hostility to truth despite clear signs given to them. It has been reported that Sayyidna Ali said: 'Anyone who takes a Muslim man or woman low in status because of his or her hunger, Allah Almighty will put him to disgrace before a gathering of all, from the first to the last. (Have you not seen those who have changed the blessings of Allah into disbelief, and caused their people to dwell in the house of destruction?
