Hell, in which they will burn, and what an evil place to settle in!)(14:28-29) (Every day two angels come down from heavens and one of them says, 'O Allah! Compensate every person who spends in Your cause,' and the other (angel) says, 'O Allah! Destroy every miser.') Also in the Sahih: The last sentence carries a warning for those who pride on their brute economic strength because it is Allah who 'gives, to whom He wills, without measure'. And anyone who falsely accuses a Muslim man or woman of a weakness, Allah Almighty would put him on a high mound until he falsifies himself.' (a1-Qurtubi) The believers spend seeking Allah's Face, and this is why they have gained the ultimate happiness and the best share on the Day of the Return. (...and whatsoever you spend of anything (in Allah's cause), He will replace it.)(34:39) In addition, it is reported in the Sahih (that the Prophet said):

**Severe in punishment.**

Rather than follow the blessed guidance given to them, they chose to stray away from it and, as a result, underwent punishments, for instance, they received the Torah which deserved being accepted but they denied it, consequent to which, they were threatened with Mount Sinai coming down upon them. Again, they heard the Word of Allah which they should have loved and respected but they tinkered with doubts in it and consequently, were struck dead by lightening. Then Allah states that He has made the life of this world beautiful for the disbelievers who are satisfied with it, who collect wealth, but refrain from spending it on what they have been commanded, which could earn them Allah's pleasure. Lastly, the chain of prophets that appeared among them from time to time should have been a matter of great satisfaction for them, yet they started killing them for which they were punished, having been deprived of power.

**The Children of Israel and the asking of them.**

The benefit of questioning [the children of Israel] was to make them acknowledge the issue of proof. Questioning them was not for the pur poses of resolving any doubt on the part of the Messenger concerning what had been plainly established by proof. If it is arguments that he seeks to make him truly believe in the message of Islam, then arguments have been provided in full measure. They witnessed his hand (when it became lit with light), his parting the sea, his striking the rock (and water flowed from the rock), the clouds that shaded them during the intense heat, the manna and the quails, and so forth.

**The signs they were given.**

Further again, they should have been grateful when Mann and Salwa was sent for them but they disobeyed and spoilage set in. But those who cannot bring themselves to accept clear arguments will not be won over by miracles of this nature. When that happens, a sudden surge of belief will not benefit anyone, for that will be a time when fates are sealed, not forged. Despite this they disbelieved and turned away from them. In the wake of such misdeeds, some of which find mention in the earlier part of Sarah al-Baqarah, the divine law is that one who changes the blessings or clear signs of Allah, especially after it has come to him when he should have followed its guidance rather than turn back and go astray, then, the ultimate must come to pass, that is, Allah Almighty punishes such a deviant severely. Allah mentioned that the Children of Israel, were witnesses to many clear signs that attest to the truth of Moses regarding what he was sent with for them. These signs attested to the existence of the Creator and the truth of Moses by whose hand these signs appeared.

212.text:
The verse gives the state of the two groups in this world and then their place on the Day. "The life of this world has been made appealing to the disbelievers" is the first statement, and the wording puts the making of the appeal in the passive, so the life of this world is described as a thing made pleasing to them rather than as a thing they found pleasing by themselves, and the verse is naming a state they are in. "and they mock the believers" is the second, and it follows from the first, since the mocking is what a person does when the world in his eyes is worth more than what the believers have. "Those who are mindful of Allah will rank above them on the Day of Judgment" then turns the order over, and the turn is in the word above, so the verse sets the rank of the Day against the rank of this world and tells the hearer which of the two is the real one. "And Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit" closes on the provision, and the phrase without limit is what answers the mocking, since the provision of this world is not given as a mark of rank and cannot be read as one. The verse stands after the account of the people who traded the favour for disbelief, and it explains the trade by naming what was taken in exchange, the appealing life of this world, and it goes on to the verse after this, which tells the believers what the testing of them is like and how near the help is. The two ranks in the verse are the two ranks of the passage, and the hearer is told which of them lasts.

**The life of this world made appealing.**

Decked out fair to the disbelievers of Makkah is the life of this world in disguise and they have fallen in love with it; and they deride the believers on account of their poverty the likes of Bilāl al-Habashī ‘Ammār b. (Beautified is the life of the world) what is in this world of comfortable living (for those who disbelieve) Abu Jahl and his entourage; (they make a jest of believers) Salman [al-Farisi], Bilal [Ibn Rabah], Suhayb [al-Rumi] and their fellow believers because of their abject poverty. For those who disbelieve in Allah, the worldly life and its temporary pleasures and enjoyments have been made to seem glamorous. And whoever changes Allah's favor after it has come to him, [e.g., renounces the religion of Allah (Islam) and accepts Kufr (disbelief)] then surely, Allah is severe in punishment Beautified is the life of this world for those who disbelieve, and they mock at those who believe. The other way is to take up Islam, only to the extent that it does not clash with one’s everyday life; and only so long as it serves, or at least does not harm one’s own interests.

**The mocking of the believers.**

Yāsir and Suhayb al-Rūmī mocking them and treating them condescendingly with their wealth; but those who fear idolatry namely those mentioned shall be above them on the Day of Resurrection; and God sustains whomever He will without reckoning with ample sustenance in the Hereafter or in this world when He gives to those that were mocked possession of the property and lives of those that mocked them. Then Allah states that He has made the life of this world beautiful for the disbelievers who are satisfied with it, who collect wealth, but refrain from spending it on what they have been commanded, which could earn them Allah's pleasure. They may look down upon the true believers, but this state of affairs is quite short-lived. It is in this context that the Holy Qur'an says: 'Adorned is the present life for those who disbelieve' because of which 'they laugh at those who believe', although, these Muslims who have said no to kufr and shirk shall be in a state better than that of the disbelievers on the day of Qiyamah (Doomsday), for the disbelievers will be in Jahannam (Hell) and the believers, in Jannah (Paradise).

**Above them on the Day of Judgment.**

(But those who ward off) disbelief and ascribing partners to Allah: i.e. Those who are mindful of Allah by fulfilling His commands and avoiding His prohibitions will be above such people in the Afterlife when Allah will make them live in the gardens of Paradise. When people bear witness [on the Day of Resurrection] and when the error of ignorance is dispelled from their hearts they will know those who are in a state of loss and those who have gone far astray. They witnessed his hand (when it became lit with light), his parting the sea, his striking the rock (and water flowed from the rock), the clouds that shaded them during the intense heat, the manna and the quails, and so forth. Lastly, the chain of prophets that appeared among them from time to time should have been a matter of great satisfaction for them, yet they started killing them for which they were punished, having been deprived of power.

**Provision without limit.**

Allah gives without any limit or account to whichever of His creation He wishes. The believers spend seeking Allah's Face, and this is why they have gained the ultimate happiness and the best share on the Day of the Return. The whole point of man’s being tested in this world is that he should believe in God, without having seen Him and solely by virtue of His arguments. In fact, people would go to the limit of abandoning their faith when it happens to be against their worldly interests and would even have the audacity to laugh at those who love and practice it. The last sentence carries a warning for those who pride on their brute economic strength because it is Allah who 'gives, to whom He wills, without measure'. One is to do so without any consideration for one’s own interests and reservations; to do what Islam enjoins on one and refrain from what it forbids. If it is arguments that he seeks to make him truly believe in the message of Islam, then arguments have been provided in full measure.

**The believers mocked and the ones above them.**

Salman and his fellow believers (will be above them) in this world by having a strong argument against them and also by having status and standing (on the Day of Resurrection. Allah giveth) abundant wealth (without stint) without faltering or affectation; it is also said that He gives to whoever He wills in Paradise without stint (to whom He will). Rather than follow the blessed guidance given to them, they chose to stray away from it and, as a result, underwent punishments, for instance, they received the Torah which deserved being accepted but they denied it, consequent to which, they were threatened with Mount Sinai coming down upon them. The world will end, to give way to a new and finer system in which they will be brought low, and the great will be cut down to size, and those who had been considered lowly will occupy high places in the heavenly world. (The son of Adam says, 'My money, my money!' Yet, what is your money except that which you eat and use up, wear and tear, and spend in charity and thus keep (in your record). Other than that, it will go away and will be left for the people (the inheritors).)

213.text:
The verse takes the whole history of the revelation in a few clauses, and each clause is a step in it. "Humanity had once been one community of believers before they lost faith" is the first state, a single community, and the phrase about the loss of faith tells the hearer that the single community did not last and that the ending of it was a loss rather than a growth. "Then Allah raised prophets as deliverers of good news and as warners" is the second step, and the two offices are named together, so the sending is described as both a promise and a warning and not as one of them. "and revealed to them the Scriptures in truth to judge among people regarding their disputes" gives what the prophets were sent with, and the purpose of the sending is stated as judgment in the disputes, so the Books are described as the ground on which a dispute between people is settled. "And no one disputed the Scriptures except the very people who received them after clear proofs had come to them" is the turn of the verse, and the wording is careful, since the dispute is not put on those who never received the Book but on those who had it in their hands, and the clear proofs are named again so that the dispute is not a matter of missing ground. "out of jealousy, Then Allah, by His grace, has guided the believers to the truth regarding those disputes" gives the reason for the dispute and then the answer to it, and the answer is a guidance given by grace and not a conclusion arrived at by the disputants. "And Allah guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path" closes the verse on the guidance itself, and the hearer is left with the two ends of the story, a community that was one and a guidance that comes to whom it comes.

**One community of believers.**

(Mankind were) in the times of Noah and Abraham (one community) of disbelievers; as it is said that this means: there were in the time of Abraham followers of the true Religion (Muslims), (and Allah sent Prophets) from the children of Noah and Abraham (as bearers of good tidings) of Paradise for whoever believes in Allah (and as warners) from hell for whoever does not believe in Allah, (and revealed therewith the Scripture) He sent down Gabriel to them with the Scripture, (with the Truth) expositing what is true and what is false (that it might judge) so that each prophet would judge by his Scripture (between mankind concerning that wherein they differed) in Religion; it is also said that this means: so that the Scripture is used as a final authority; and it is also said that this means: so that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ rules them by the Scripture. All of them were in agreement and guided following the way of their father Adam, until the Satan misguided them. The verse means that during the early period of human life, people adhered to one true faith, later on differences crept in, which led to disputations following which came the need to send prophets and Books. Then, temperamental multiplicity gave way to the promotion of self-interest which caused disputes to surface, so much so that a time came when beliefs too were disputed which in turn reached a point when the very root, the fine line of distinction between the true and the false, got all mixed up.

**The prophets as bearers of good news and warners.**

For this reason, God sent messengers bringing good news of the mercy of God for those who had faith in Him and followed Him and warning the disbelievers of the severe punishment of God. The verse tells us that Allah Almighty sent His prophets and Books into this mortal world for no other purpose but that people, who had left the single ummah following the true faith and branched out into different sects, should again be assembled into the same one community. Allah protected the believers by means of the prophets from that which they differed over in matters of Religion, and directed them from falsehood to the Truth. Very simply, just as the disbelievers took to the ways of their elders in the form of denial, hostility and prophet-bashing, all true Muslims on the straight path should take to the consistent practice of their elders, the great prophets by staying patient against injuries inflicted on them, nevertheless, keep calling them to the true Faith with wisdom, sound advice and good grace.

**The Scriptures revealed in truth.**

Together with the messengers, God also sent books containing the undoubtable truth so that they could judge between people with respect to their disagreements. (And only those unto whom (the Scripture) was given differed concerning it) concerning the Religion and Muhammad ﷺ (after clear proofs had come unto them) clear proofs from their own Scripture, (through hatred one of another) out of resentful envy from their part and this is why they disbelieved in it. The words of the text say: :that is, 'Allah Almighty sent prophets who were to carry glad-tidings of eternal peace and bliss to those who follow the true Faith and to give warning of the punishment of Hell to those who turn away from it. What is true, as stated earlier, is that all prophets and divine Books aimed at assembling people around one true faith to which they initially adhered. (O Allah! Show us the truth as truth, and bestow adherence to it on us. Show us the evil as evil, and make us stay away from it, and do not confuse us regarding the reality of evil so that we will not be led astray by it, and make us leaders for the believers.)

**The dispute after the clear proofs.**

It causes them to deny truth itself—the very thing that they in their complacency claimed to monopolize. Their claim to have a monopoly over truth makes them proud and prejudiced. (We are the last (nation), but the first (foremost) on the Day of Resurrection. We are the first people to enter Paradise, although they (Jews and Christians) have been given the Book before us and we after them. Allah has guided us to the truth wherever they disputed over it. This is the day (Friday) that they disputed about, Allah guided us to it. So, the people follow us, as tomorrow is for the Jews and the day after is for the Christians.) They were then split into believers and disbelievers. In terms of allusion and according to the tasting of the chevaliers of the Tariqah, this verse has another intimation and another meaning. (O Allah, the Lord of (angels) Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and earth and Knower of the seen and the unseen. You judge between Your servants regarding what they have disputed in, so guide me to what have been the subject of dispute of the truth by Your leave. Indeed, You guide whom You will to the straight path.)

**The jealousy of those who received the Scriptures.**

Why, they contend should we accept what is taught to us by another? "The creatures are at ease in the ruins of their own makeup wink just once to throw the creatures into turmoil!" [DS 696] Then a courier came from the infinite world to their tininess. Those who are blessed with some insight into the wisdom behind the style of the Holy Qur'an would not find it difficult to answer the question, for the Holy Qur'an, while relating past events, does not report the whole story- anywhere, instead, it eliminates parts in between, which could be understood contextually. Some others have said that the period dates back to the time of the deluge in the days of Sayyidna Nuh in which all living were swept away except those who had boarded the ark with Sayyidna Nu-h .

**Allah guides whom He wills.**

(And Allah guides whom He wills) means from among His creation. (And Allah by His will guided those who believe) by means of the prophets (unto the Truth of that concerning which they differed) in Religion. " When this messenger turned its face from that infinity to their tininess, they all became aware, captive to desire, subjugated by will, wounded by wisdom, their ears fixed on their own fortune and lot: Then, to make sure that the teachings of the Holy Qur'an remain intact in their original form and live right through the Day of Doom (Dooms’ Day), Allah Almighty promised to create and sustain a set of people from the community of Muhammad a group which will always adhere to the true Faith, keep circulating the correct teachings of the Qur'an and Sunnah among Muslims all over the world without ever flinching against any opposition or hostility.

214.text:
The verse answers a thought the believers might have, and it answers it with what happened to those before them. "Do you think you will be admitted into Paradise without being tested like those before you?" is the question, and the shape of it is what does the work, since the entering of Paradise and the testing are put in one sentence and the question asks whether the first can come without the second. The comparison with those before them is inside the question, so the verse does not have to argue the point, it only has to point at the people who already went through it. "They were afflicted with suffering and adversity and were so violently shaken that even the Messenger and the believers with him cried out" gives the account of them, and it gives it in two degrees, the suffering and the adversity first and then the shaking, and the shaking is described as reaching the Messenger himself and the believers with him, which is the furthest point the verse can name. "When will Allah's help come?" Indeed, Allah's help is always near" is the cry and the answer to it in the same breath, and the answer is not a date but a nearness, so the verse ends where the cry ends, with the help described as near rather than as delayed. The verse stands after the account of the mocking in this world and before the questions about what to spend and about fighting, and it prepares the hearer for both, since a person told that the help is near is a person being told that the road to it is a hard one, and that the ones who walked it before him walked it in the same shaking.

**Entering Paradise and the testing of those before.**

Do you believers think that you will enter Paradise whilst you have not faced a trial like the people of the past? There is only one way to earn Paradise, and that is by total self-abnegation. He fancied that this work could be finished merely by wishing and that he could reach the treasure without suffering. It was made the resting place for precious pearls and night brightening gems, and then sharks and huge fish were made the veil of those pearls and gems. Passion for the beauty of that night-brightening pearl cleanses his intellect of the ocean's terrors, so he does not give those meanings access to himself. They go to the ocean's shore and see its difficulties, and dread appears in them because of the danger of those sharks. (Then We destroyed men stronger (in power) than these and the example of the ancients has passed away (before them)(43:8) and:

**Suffering and adversity.**

(Affliction) fear, calamities, hardships (and adversity) sickness, pain and hunger (befell them) visited them, (they were shaken as with an earthquake) in hardship, (till the Messenger (of Allah) until their Messenger (and those who believed along with him) those who believed in him (said: When cometh Allah's help) over the enemy? They were afflicted with severe sickness and poverty and were shaken by frightening events to the extent that they wanted the help of Allah to come as quick as possible; and the messenger and the believers with him began saying, ‘When is the help of Allah coming? That they reached a point of suffering when they cried out as to when will the help of Allah come, was not because of any doubt since that would be against the dignity of their station. (When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes grew wild and the hearts reached to the throats, and you were harboring doubts about Allah. There, the believers were tried and shaken with a mighty shaking. And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease (of doubts) said: "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion!")(33:10-12) Further from this point, the present verse recounts the enormous amount of suffering faced by past prophets and believers at the hands of hostile disbelievers.

**The Messenger and the believers cried out.**

The following was revealed after the Muslims suffered a trying experience Or did you suppose that you should enter Paradise without there having come upon you the like of what came upon those believers who passed away before you? of trials so that you may endure as they did; a new sentence begins here explaining the previous one They were afflicted by misery extreme poverty and hardship illness and were so convulsed by all types of tribulations that the Messenger and those who believed with him said read yaqūla or yaqūlu not expecting to see any help on account of the extreme hardship afflicting them ‘When will God’s help come?’ the help which we were promised; and God responded to them Ah but surely God’s help is nigh in coming. Apparently, this verse seems to indicate that nobody shall enter Paradise unless he goes through hardships and sufferings, although, Qur'anic statements and sayings of the Holy Prophet prove that many sinners will enter Paradise simply because of the grace, mercy and forgiveness of Allah Almighty, and that they shall undergo no hardship either. This is because hardship and suffering have different levels. " He said, "Such is the case with Prophets, they are tested, but the final victory is theirs." (The saw would be placed on the middle of the head of one of those who were before you (believers) and he would be sawn until his feet, and he would be combed with iron combs between his skin and bones, yet that would not make him change his religion.) The previous verse has said how hostile the disbelievers have been to prophets and believers and, in a way, has comforted Muslims hurt by the mockery of disbelievers that there is nothing new about this antagonism. The lowest degree is to resist against one's own desiring self and the Satan, or to strengthen the bases of one's beliefs by countering the forces working against the true Faith.

**When will the help of Allah come.**

Religion's pain is indeed marvelous, for when you suffer it, you will be like a candle-better once your head's cut off. [DS 485] The high Firdaws is a sweet garden and meadow, but the road there is difficult, a rosebed full of thorns. The moth reaches union with the candle when it burns, and the candle finds life when it loses its head. It is because they see truth as destructive to the dream world they have built up; they view it as damaging to their own interests and honour, as threatening to the comfortable, secure lives to which they have become accustomed. " The tongue of his state will say, "Each month two thousand of the passionate like me are killed, and not one lets out a sigh." If the opposite happens, the sharks will take his life as booty and his name will be written in the register of "I don't care. They pleaded (to Allah) for victory against their enemies and invoked Him for aid and deliverance from their hardships and trials. Who else other than the prophets and the pious of the community would be more deserving of what Allah likes?

**The help of Allah is near.**

’ The help of Allah is close to those that have faith and trust in Him. (Now surely Allah's help) over your enemy by means of your safety (is near). But in order to be faithful to God, we are required to make sacrifices of this nature. (By Allah! This matter (religion) will spread (or expand) by Allah until the traveler leaves San'a' to Hadramawt (both in Yemen, but at a great distance from each other) fearing only Allah and then the wolf for the sake of his sheep. You are just a hasty people.) (Alif-Lam-Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say: "We believe," and will not be tested? And We indeed tested those who were before them. And Allah will certainly make known (the truth of) those who are true, and will certainly make known (the falsehood of) those who are liars.)(29:1-3) In fact, the call was made in the background of Allah's promised help for which the time and place was left undetermined. Making such a prayer is not against one's trust in Allah (tawakkul) or against the station of prophet hood.

215.text:
The verse is a question and an answer, and the answer is a list. "They ask you ˹O Prophet in˺ what ˹way˺ they should donate. Say," is the question put to the Prophet and the command to answer it, and the question is not about whether to give but about the way of the giving, so the verse deals with the direction of the gift and not with its size. "Whatever donations you give are for parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and ˹needy˺ travellers" is the answer, and it is given as a list of people rather than as an amount, and the order of the list is what the hearer is left with, since it begins with the nearest of kin and moves outward to the traveller who has no tie of blood at all. The list is the whole of the ruling in the verse, and it names no share for any of the five, so the giving is described by its direction and not by its division. "and ˹needy˺ travellers" is the last of the five and the widest of them, since the traveller is named for his need on the road and not for his place in the family. "Whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah." closes the answer with the knowledge of Allah, and the close is what makes the list work, since a giving whose direction is fixed and whose amount is left open needs the knowledge of the One it is given to as its ground. The verse stands between the verse about the help that is near and the verse about fighting, and it turns the believer from the hardship he has been promised to the wealth in his hand.

**What they should spend.**

"Whatever you spend of good must be for parents and kindred and orphans and Al-Masakin (the poor) and the wayfarer, and whatever you do of good deeds, truly, Allah knows it well. Your Companions, O Prophet, ask you what they should spend from their wealth and where they should allocate it. These two verses are not concerned with the obligatory zakah because the threshold of holdings for the obligatory Zakah is fixed, and the obligatory ratio of spending under it has also been fully determined through the Holy Prophet . (Ibn al-Mundhir - Mazhari) that is, 'what do we spend from our wealth, and where?' According to a narration reported by Ibn Jarir this question was not that of Ibn Jamuh alone, rather, it was from Muslims in general. The Qur'anic answer to the first question shows that the second part of the question, that is, where should they spend, has been given more importance and answered frontally and clearly. The statement about spending the surplus' (al-'afw), that which is extra to needs, has been interpreted as an obligatory injunction by the blessed Companion Abu Dharr al-Ghifari and others . But Islam urges him to spend for the cause of God, which is quite a different form of expenditure, involving spending on others rather than just on oneself.

**For parents and relatives and the poor.**

Then, the other part of the question, that is, what should they spend, was answered as a corollary through the words, ‌ 'And whatever good you do, Allah is all-aware of that'. (Say: "Whatever you spend of good must be for parents and kindred and orphans and Al-Masakin and the wayfarer,") meaning, spend it on these categories or areas. Any permissible and pure wealth you spend should be given to parents, close relatives in need, needy orphans, the poor who have no wealth and the traveller who is cut-off from his family and home. Another rule of conduct which emerges from this verse is that even the gift given or food served to parents and other near of kin, if the intention is to obey Allah Almighty in doing so, will be included under spending in the way of Allah and will deserve reward with Him. This also removes the doubt about the inclusion of parents as recepients of spending under verse 215, although, giving Zakah to parents is not permissible under the teaching of the Holy Prophet . Now, from this point onwards, there appear some details concerning this obedience which relate to one's wealth, life and other matters of marriage and divorce.

**Whatever good you do is known to Allah.**

(And whatsoever good ye do) whatever wealth you spend on these, (lo! Allah is Aware of it) Allah knows it as He knows your intention and He will reward you for it. Allah knows of any good you do as believers, no matter how small. Nothing is hidden from Him and He will reward you for it. Whatever you have given and will give, I who am the Lord know it and am aware of it. Imperatives such as - 'leave disbelief and hypocrisy and enter Islam completely', 'listen to none when it comes to obeying the command of Allah', 'spend your wealth and give your life to seek the pleasure of Allah' and 'show fortitude against all sorts of hardships and sufferings' - have been emphatically mentioned in previous verses. When the Holy Qur'an commanded Muslims to spend in the way of Allah, some Companions came to the Holy Prophet and requested an elaboration of the injunction. Similarly, one who does not pay back his debt yet goes on squandering money in voluntary charities is not liked in the sight of Allah. If this were to be said in other words, one could say that the Fatwa (religious ruling) was given by Allah Almighty Himself.

**The question and its answer.**

In the present verse , the istifta' or questions asked by the noble Companions has been reported in the words, 'They ask you as to what they should spend'. However, the first part of the question, that is, what should they spend, was answered as a corollary, and considered sufficient. The Ayah means, 'They ask you (O Muhammad) how they should spend,' as Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid have stated. Someone asks, "What should we do with our property? The blessed Companion and commentator of the Holy Qur'an, Abdullah ibn Abbas has said: 'I have not seen a set of people better than the Companions of the Holy Prophet who, (despite their great attachment to matters of Faith and their deep love for and close relationship with the Holy Prophet) asked very few questions.' The questions asked relate to a total of thirteen problems only, which have been answered in the Holy Qur'an because these noble souls never asked a question unless absolutely necessary (Qurtubi). The same question has been repeated in verse 219 in the same words : but the answer to this one question has been given differently in the present verse and later on, in verse 219.

**Who asked the question.**

This was the question posed by ‘Amr b. al-Jamūh. He was a wealthy elderly man and went to ask the Prophet s what and for whom he should expend; Say to them ‘Whatever you expend of good min khayrin ‘of good’ is an explication of mā ‘whatever’ covering small and large amounts and denotes one half of the question represented by the expender; God responds with regard to the one receiving the expenditure this pertaining to the other half of the question in the following it is for parents and kinsmen orphans the needy and the traveller that is they are the most deserving of it; and whatever good you may do by way of expending or otherwise God has knowledge of it’ and will requite it accordingly. Those fortunate Companions did not ask how to spend because they had not found their way to poverty, but in hopes that this caress would reach them from the Exalted Presence: Another tendency is to expend all one’s energy on attaining a high worldly position—something which meets the eye—while everlasting reward, which we as yet cannot see, should be one’s most important goal. In short, the considered explanation of the heads of expenditure was given in the first verse , perhaps, in view of the real concern of the questioner about where to spend. However, the majority of Companions, their successors (the Tabi in) and the great imams of the Faith interpret the Qur'anic verses in question to mean that whatever has to be spent in the way of Allah should be surplus to needs.

216.text:
The verse lays an obligation and then answers the feeling that meets it. "Fighting has been made obligatory upon you ˹believers˺" is the obligation, and the wording puts the making of it in the passive, so the obligation is described as laid on them and not as taken up by them, and the address is to the believers, which is who the obligation binds. "though you dislike it" is the second phrase and the honest one, since the verse names the dislike in the same breath as the command and does not wait for the hearer to admit it. "Perhaps you dislike something which is good for you and like something which is bad for you" then takes the dislike and sets it against the knowledge of what is good, and the two halves of the phrase answer each other, so the verse is not telling the believer to stop feeling the dislike but telling him that the feeling is not a measure. "Allah knows and you do not know" closes the verse on the difference between the two knowledges, and it is the ground of the whole verse, since the command stands and the dislike is left standing with it because the knowledge behind the command is not the knowledge of the one who receives it. The verse stands after the questions about spending and before the question about the sacred months, and it is the point where the passage turns from the wealth of the believer to his life, and the verse after this takes up the first question that came out of it. The dislike named in the verse is not blamed in it, and the knowledge that answers it is not the hearer's.

**Fighting made obligatory.**

Prescribed for you obligatory for you is fighting disbelievers though it be hateful to you by nature because of the hardship involved. (Warfare is ordained for you) in times of a general call to arms with the Prophet ﷺ (though it is hateful unto you) hard on you; (but it may happen that ye hate a thing) fighting in the way of Allah (which is good for you) in that you obtain martyrdom and spoils, (and it may happen that ye love a thing) abstaining from fighting in the way of Allah (which is bad for you) in that you will not obtain martyrdom or spoils. In this Ayah, Allah made it obligatory for the Muslims to fight in Jihad against the evil of the enemy who transgress against Islam. Verse 216 establishes the obligatory nature of Jihad even though it may be burdensome for some temperaments. Fighting in Allah’s path has been chosen for believers even though it is something that is naturally disliked, because it means risking one’s life and wealth. Some other verses of the Qur'an and the sayings of the Holy Prophet however, have clarified that this obligation is not absolute, that is, every Muslim is not charged to perform it as Fard Ayn (absolute and mandatory obligation on every Muslim) instead, it is Fard ala al-Kifayah whereby, should a group of Muslims come forward to discharge this obligation, other Muslims would be considered absolved from it.

**Though you dislike it.**

(...though you dislike it) means, 'Fighting is difficult and heavy on your hearts.' Indeed, fighting is as the Ayah describes it, as it includes being killed, wounded, striving against the enemies and enduring the hardship of travel. Prescribed for you is fighting though it be hateful to you. The injunction declaring Jihad as obligatory appears in the first of the three verses under comment in the words: It is the opposite for the comforts of the hearts which are immediate muʿajjala since they follow the property of drawing near taqrīb. In order to save face in the eyes of men, they defy truth, though they would do better to seek honour with God; and God honours only those who uphold the truth. (...and it may be that you dislike a thing which is good for you) meaning, fighting is followed by victory, dominance over the enemy, taking over their lands, money and offspring. It is better to accept the good news of the Real's guarantee of ease than the anxious thoughts of the lower selves that warn of impending difficulty and harm.

**You dislike what is good for you.**

Yet it may happen that you hate a thing which is good for you; and it may happen that you love a thing which is bad for you because the soul inclines towards those desires which result in its destruction and its rejection of the religious obligations that would bring about its happiness. Perhaps then even if you are averse to it you will find much good in fighting as a result of victory booty martyrdom or reward; while if you were to reject fighting even if you would like to do so you will find much evil because then you may be subjugated impoverished and denied the reward; God knows what is good for you and you know this not so strive in what He commands you. Hence, one might covet something, yet in reality it is not good or beneficial for him, such as refraining from joining the Jihad, for it might lead to the enemy taking over the land and the government. Yet it may happen that you hate a thing which is good for you; and it may happen that you love a thing which is bad for you; God knows and you know not. An example of this is striving in Allah’s path, which means – in addition to the great reward – the defeat of the enemy and promotion of Allah’s word. Here, the promise of good has been extended to those also who may not be able to take part in Jihad because of some compulsive excuse or because of engagement in some other religious service.

**Allah knows and you do not know.**

(Allah knows, but you do not know.) meaning, He has better knowledge than you of how things will turn out to be in the end, and of what benefits you in this earthly life and the Hereafter. (And Allah knoweth) that fighting in His way is better for you, (ye know not) that abstention from fighting in His way is bad for you. Allah knows full well what is good and what is not, whereas you do not. Towards the end of this verse, it is as a mode of persuasion that Jihad has been identified as something which may, temperamentally, appear 'hard' but one must remember that human intelligence and effort fails so many times when it comes to the outcome. This scenario of human reasoning and planning failing time and again is a matter of repeated experience, therefore, it was said that fighting in the way of Allah may obviously appear to be a loss of life and property, yet the time will come when realities will be unveiled and we shall find out that this loss was no loss, instead, it was the ultimate in gain, and a source of eternal peace. Therefore, one should not decide on things being good or bad as prompted by personal desires, rather, one must say yes to the command of Allah and follow it consistently as the most expedient course of action. In this case, the truth is that it is Allah Almighty who knows the reality of everything while man does not possess the full range of that knowledge.

**When the verse was revealed.**

This was revealed about Sa'd Ibn Abi Waqqas, al-Miqdad Ibn al-Aswad and their associates. It was then revealed regarding 'Abdullah Ibn Jahsh and his companions who killed 'Amr Ibn al-Hadrami and their asking about warfare during the sacred month-in reference here to Rajab: i.e. the last afternoon of Jumada II, before seeing the moon of Rajab-for the unbelievers had censored them from doing so. People like to lead free and unrestricted lives, but it is better for them to adhere to God’s laws.

217.text:
The verse is the longest answer in the passage and it moves in steps from a question about a month to a statement about the Fire. "They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about fighting in the sacred months. Say," is the question and the command to answer it, and the question is about a fixed time, so the verse begins with a case and not with a principle. "Fighting during these months is a great sin" is the first answer, and it gives the month its weight, since the fighting in it is named a great sin and not a small one. "But hindering ˹others˺ from the Path of Allah, rejecting Him" then sets a second thing against it, and the turn is in the but, so the verse is weighing two sins and not excusing one. "and expelling the worshippers from the Sacred Mosque is ˹a˺ greater ˹sin˺ in the sight of Allah" completes the second thing and gives the comparison, and the greater is in the sight of Allah, which is the measure the verse uses. "For persecution is far worse than killing" states the ground of the comparison in one phrase, and the persecution is set against the killing, so the verse is putting the driving of a person out of his faith above the taking of his life. "And they will not stop fighting you until they turn you away from your faith—if they can" turns from the weighing to the intention of the other side, and the if is the limit of that intention. "And whoever among you renounces their own faith and dies a disbeliever" puts the case back on the believers, and the two conditions are joined, the renouncing and the dying in it. "their deeds will become void in this life and in the Hereafter" gives what follows, and the void is in both homes. "It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever." closes the verse, and the forever is the last word the hearer is given.

**Fighting in the sacred month and the raid at Nakhlah.**

Thus the Prophet s sent forth the first of his raiding parties under the command of ‘Abd Allāh b. This expedition proceeded until they reached Nakhlah where they found 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami leading a trade caravan for the Quraysh. (They question thee (O Muhammad) with regard to warfare in the sacred month) about waging war in the month of Rajab. The people ask you, O Prophet, about the law regarding fighting in the sacred months of Dhū Al-Qa‘dah, Dhū Al-Ḥijjah, Muḥarram and Rajab. Now, Rajab is counted among the sacred months, and Arab feeling ran high with regard to the age-old tradition of respect for these months. Some have said that the abrogator of this injunction is the very conduct of the Holy Prophet since he himself besieged the city of Ta'if during the 'sacred months' and it was during the 'sacred months' that he sent the noble Companion Amir al-Ash'ari on the military expedition of Awtas .

**Hindering from the Path of Allah and expelling from the Mosque.**

(Say: Warfare therein) in the month of Rajab (is a great (transgression) deserving a great punishment, (but to turn from the way of Allah) but preventing people from the Religion of Allah and His obedience, (and to disbelieve in Him and in the Inviolable Place of Worship) and turning people away from the Inviolable Place of Worship, (and to expel its people from it, is a greater sin) deserving a greater punishment (with Allah) than the killing of 'Amr Ibn al-Hadrami; (for persecution) associating partners with Allah (is worse than slaughter) the slaughter of 'Amr Ibn al-Hadrami. Say Fighting in it is a grave thing; but to bar from God's way and disbelief in Him and the sacred mosque and to expel its people from it-that is graver in God's sight; and sedition is graver than slaying. This Ayah means, 'If you had killed during the Sacred Month, they (disbelievers of Quraysh) have hindered you from the path of Allah and disbelieved in it.

**Persecution is worse than killing.**

(...and Al-Fitnah is worse than killing.) means, trying to force the Muslims to revert from their religion and re-embrace Kufr after they had believed, is worse with Allah than killing.' Allah said: The effect of heedlessness on hearts is more serious than the harm caused to the lower selves by error for surely the lower self is kept from good fortune ḥaẓẓ but the heart is kept from the Real ḥaqq. When the call to truth was raised among the Quraysh, not only did they deny it themselves, but they sought to prevent others from following it. (They ask you concerning fighting in the Sacred Months. Say, "Fighting therein is a great (transgression) but a greater (transgression) with Allah is to prevent mankind from following the way of Allah, to disbelieve in Him, to prevent access to Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah), and to drive out its inhabitants, and Al-Fitnah is worse than killing.) It was then that was revealed (They question thee (O Muhammad) with regard to warfare in the sacred month) up to His saying (for persecution is worse than killing), i.

**They will not stop fighting you.**

They the disbelievers will not cease to fight against you O believers until so that they turn you from your religion to unbelief if they are able; and whoever of you turns from his religion and dies disbelieving — their good works have failed that is they are invalid in this world and the Hereafter. (And they), the people of Makkah, (will not cease from fighting against you till they have made you renegades from your religion) the religion of Islam, (if they can) if they are able to do so. The gist of the discussion is that initiating a fight during these months is forbidden forever, but in the event that disbelievers mount an attack on Muslims, then Muslims are permitted to fight back in their defence. But, it can certainly be conceded that the absolute forbiddance of fighting in the 'sacred months' which seems to reflect from the verse referred to holds an exception whereby it would become permissible for Muslims to defend themselves, or counter attack the aggressor if disbelievers themselves start the fighting during these months.

**Whoever renounces his faith and dies a disbeliever.**

The specification of death as a condition is because if that person were to return to Islam again his original deeds would not be invalidated and he will be rewarded for them and he would not have to repeat them deeds such as performing the Pilgrimage al-Shāfi‘ī is of this opinion. (And whoso becometh a renegade) whoever renounces Islam (and dieth in his disbelief: such are they whose works have fallen) their works are thwarted and their good deeds rejected (both in the world and the Hereafter) and they will not be rewarded in the Hereafter. They said to him: 'Do you allow fighting in the sacred month?' As a response, Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse (They question thee (O Muhammad) with regard to warfare in the sacred month) . Some examples of 'deeds going waste in this world' are that the wife of an apostate goes out of the bond of marriage; if a relative of an apostate dies as Muslim, he gets no share in the inheritance; all obligations such as prayers and fasting fulfilled in one's state of Islam are reduced to nothing; for such a person funeral prayers are not offered and he or she is not buried in the graveyard meant for Muslims. 'Deeds going waste in the Hereafter' means that one gets no reward for acts of worship and enters the Hell to stay there forever.

**The deeds that become void.**

Several others among the respected Successors (Tabi'in) regard this injunction as provenly un-abrogated, but in accordance with the ruling of the majority of Muslim jurists as stated by al-Jassas, this injunction is one of the abrogated ones as maintained by a consensus of jurists and fighting is no more forbidden in any month. Ruh al-Ma ani, under comments on this verse, and al-Baydawi, under the explanation of the first section of Surah al-Bara'ah have reported a consensus of the community on the abrogation of the forbiddance of fighting during the 'sacred months' (Bayan al-Qur'an). However, al-Tafsir al-Mazhari answers all these arguments by saying that the sanctity of the 'sacred months' is clearly present in the verse known as Ayah al-sayf or the Verse of the Sword, that is : They said, ' Amr bin Hadrami was killed by Waqid bin 'Abdullah: 'Amr, means the war has started, Hadrami means the war has come, as for Waqid (bin 'Abdullah): the war has raged (using some of the literal meanings of these names to support their fortune-telling!). Towards the end of the verse , it has been said that the act of turning into an apostate after having become a Muslim shall be dealt with under the injunction: ‌ that is, they shall be those whose deeds have gone waste in this world and in the Hereafter. Should an apostate become a Muslim once again, at least this much is certain that he could hope to salvage himself away from Hell in the Hereafter, while during the remaining tenure of his life in the mortal world, the injunctions of Islam will be operative for him.

218.text:
The verse names three things and then one hope. "Surely those who have believed, emigrated" is the first and the beginning of the second, and the joining of the two in one phrase is what the verse is doing, since the belief and the leaving of the home are set down as one state and not as two separate merits. "and struggled in the Way of Allah" is the third, and it comes last of the three, so the verse moves from what a person carries, to what he leaves, to what he does with his life after the leaving. "they can hope for Allah's mercy" is the answer to the three, and the word hope is what the hearer is left with, since the verse does not give the mercy as a thing already in their hands but as a thing they may hope for, and the hope is described as theirs. "And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful" closes with the two descriptions, and they are the ground of the hope, because the three things named before are the things a person does and the two names are what Allah is. The verse stands at the end of the account of the raiding party and the month in which it fought, and it answers that account, since the people it describes are the people who did what the verse before it describes, and the mercy it gives is the answer to the sin it named. The three things in the verse are the three things that passage was about, and the hope at the end of it is the verse's own word for what the believer is left with.

**Those who believed and emigrated.**

When those of the raiding party of ‘Abd Allāh b. (Lo! Those who believe) in Allah and His Messenger, (and those who emigrate) from Makkah to Medina (and strive in the way of Allah) by killing the unbeliever 'Amr Ibn al-Hadrami, (these have hope in Allah's mercy) they shall obtain Allah's Garden. Those who have faith in Allah and His Messenger, who leave their homes as emigrants towards Allah and His Messenger, and fight to promote Allah’s word are the ones who are eager for Allah’s mercy and forgiveness. (That is, such persecution gave the believers the opportunity to show the strength of their faith, and in spite of the adverse atmosphere, their continuing trust in God. This made them stand out from those who, weak in faith, proved unable to withstand the pressure, and lost their trust in God.) He also gave him some written instructions and ordered him not to read them until he marched for two days. 'Abdullah should then read the instructions and march to implement them, but should not force any of those who were with him to accompany him.

**Struggle in the Way of Allah.**

One side is to emigrate from one's home, homeland, and means and to go forth seeking knowledge. On the one hand, some were exposed as servants only of themselves; for who else but one who has no fear of God—pursuing only his own selfish ends—would persecute God’s servants? Towards the end of the verse , it has been said that the act of turning into an apostate after having become a Muslim shall be dealt with under the injunction: ‌ that is, they shall be those whose deeds have gone waste in this world and in the Hereafter. (They ask you concerning fighting in the Sacred Months. Say, "Fighting therein is a great (transgression) but a greater (transgression) with Allah is to prevent mankind from following the way of Allah, to disbelieve in Him, to prevent access to Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah), and to drive out its inhabitants, and Al-Fitnah is worse than killing.) They will abide therein forever Verily, those who have believed, and those who have emigrated (for Allah's religion) and have striven hard in the way of Allah, all these hope for Allah's mercy.

**Hope for the mercy of Allah.**

The master Abū ʿAlī Daqqāq said, "The caressing of the seekers of knowledge reaches a place such that tomorrow, when they rise up from the dust, they will be mounted on the feathers of an gels, according to the Prophets words, 'Surely the angels will put down their wings for the seeker of knowledge, approving what he is doing.'" Then Abū ʿAlī said, "Since the seekers of knowledge will be mounted on the feathers of angels, how can anyone imagine what the seekers of the Known will be mounted on? " Did we but know that the visit is true, we would make our face an earth so that You might approve. * Beautiful idols walk on forbidden ground. On the other hand, out of this persecution came emigration and peaceful missionary struggle—acts of true faith on the part of those who remained devoted to God through all torment and oppression; there were others, of course, who, unable to withstand the pressure, forsook their faith. They have taken the word: here in the sense of 'anytime' meaning thereby that the disbelievers should be killed in whatever month or time they are found. Should an apostate become a Muslim once again, at least this much is certain that he could hope to salvage himself away from Hell in the Hereafter, while during the remaining tenure of his life in the mortal world, the injunctions of Islam will be operative for him. " He then said to his companions, "Allah's Messenger has commanded me to march forth to Nakhlah to watch the movements of the caravan of Quraysh and to inform him about their news.

**Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.**

(And Allah is Forgiving) of what they have done, (Merciful) towards them, since He did not punish them. Allah forgives the sins of His servants and is merciful towards them. The Hadith statement: : 'You have embraced Islam with all the good deeds which you have performed earlier' means just this. Abdul-Malik bin Hisham, who compiled the Sirah (life story of the Prophet), related that Ziyad bin 'Abdullah Bakka'i said that Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar Al-Madani wrote in his book on the Sirah, "Allah's Messenger sent 'Abdullah bin Jahsh bin Riyab Al-Asadi in Rajab, after he (the Prophet) came back from the first battle of Badr. He remained with Allah's Messenger until he was martyred during the incident at Bir Ma'unah (when the Prophet sent seventy Companions to Najd to teach them Islam, but Banu Sulaim killed them all except two). When 'Abdullah read the instructions, he recited Istirja' [saying, 'Truly! to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return'; and refer to (2:156)] and said, "I hear and obey Allah and His Messenger.

**The raiding party of Abdullah ibn Jahsh.**

Jahsh thought that although they had been released from the sin of having slain in the sacred month they would not receive any reward the following was revealed Verily the believers and those who emigrate and depart from their homeland and struggle in God’s way in order to elevate His religion — those have hope of God’s compassion His reward; and God is Forgiving of believers Merciful to them. The following was also revealed about 'Abdullah Ibn Jahsh and his companions: When they saw the Companions they were frightened, but when they saw 'Ukkashah bin Mihsan their fears subsided, since his head was shaved. When the faithful are persecuted in this way, and forced to leave their homes, they sometimes even have to take to arms in self-defence. Ruh al-Ma ani, under comments on this verse, and al-Baydawi, under the explanation of the first section of Surah al-Bara'ah have reported a consensus of the community on the abrogation of the forbiddance of fighting during the 'sacred months' (Bayan al-Qur'an). Then, a caravan belonging to the Quraysh passed by carrying raisins, food stuff and some trade items for the Quraysh. 'Amr bin Hadrami, whose name was 'Abdullah bin 'Abbad, was in the caravan, as well as 'Uthman bin 'Abdullah bin Al-Mughirah and his brother Nawfal bin 'Abdullah from the tribe of Makhzum, and Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, a freed slave of Hisham bin Al-Mughirah.

219.text:
The verse carries two questions and two answers, and a close that covers both. "They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about intoxicants and gambling. Say," is the first question, and it is about two things at once, a drink and a game of chance, so the answer has to cover both. "There is great evil in both" is the first half of the answer, and the word great is what the verse puts first, since the evil is not named as a small matter. "as well as some benefit for people" is the second half, and it is given in full, so the verse does not deny that there is a benefit in the two things but names it and puts it in its place. "but the evil outweighs the benefit" is the weighing, and it is the ruling of the verse in one phrase, since the two sides are named and then compared. "They ˹also˺ ask you ˹O Prophet˺ what they should donate. Say," is the second question, and it is the same question an earlier verse answered, asked again, so the passage returns to the wealth of the believer after the ruling on the drink and the game. "Whatever you can spare." is the whole of the second answer, and it is the shortest answer in the passage, since it names no amount and no list but leaves the measure in the hand of the giver. "This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you ˹believers˺, so perhaps you may reflect" closes the verse on the making clear, and the reflection asked for is the answer to it, so the verse ends with the hearer's part rather than with the ruling. The two answers in the verse are the two the passage needed, one on what a person takes into himself and one on what he gives out of his hand.

**Intoxicants and gambling.**

They ask you about wine and divinatory arrows gambling and what the ruling is regarding them. They also ask you about gambling (which refers to wealth taken in a competition between two people in which both contribute to the winning total). Al-Hakam said that Miqsam said that Ibn 'Abbas said that this Ayah means, whatever you can spare above the needs of your family. This was revealed about 'Umar Ibn al-Khattab who prayed: �O Allah! But, here we are in this modern age, called 'the age of progress' by those handicapped by superficial vision and lack of insight into its aftermath, where we see wine of all sorts given new names and labels, where ever-new kinds of interest and ever-innovative corporate methods to promote it have been invented, commandeered and given the safe name of 'banking'; so it is with gambling where thousands of dubious forms have found currency. (O you who believe! Intoxicants (all kinds of alcoholic drinks), and gambling, and Al-Ansab, and Al-Azlam are an abomination of Shaytan's handiwork. So avoid (strictly all) that (abomination) in order that you may be successful. Shaytan wants only to excite enmity and hatred between you with intoxicants (alcoholic drinks) and gambling, and hinder you from the remembrance of Allah and from As-Salah (the prayer). So, will you not then abstain?)(5:90-91) Isn't it that man, who should be an agent of public good, a model of sympathy and sacrifice, stoops to the level of a beast while gambling, and starts seeing his life in the death of his brother, and finding delight in his distress, and searching for gain in his loss, and goes about harnessing all his abilities to promote his selfishness?

**Great evil and some benefit.**

"In them is a great sin, and (some) benefits for men, but the sin of them is greater than their benefit. Say to them ‘In both that is in the partaking of both is great sin a variant reading for kabīr ‘great’ has kathīr ‘much’ because of the fighting cursing and swearing that ensue from it; and profit for men by way of delight and enjoyment in wine and acquiring money effortlessly from gambling; but the sin in them that is the degenerate behaviour in which they result is greater graver than the usefulness’. (in both is great sin) this is after they were declared unlawful, (and (some) utility for men) by means of their trading, i.e. before they were unlawful; (but the sin of them) after their being declared unlawful (is greater than their usefulness) before they were made unlawful; and then both were prohibited. However, the harm and sin resulting from them is greater than the benefit; so, a logical person should avoid such actions. None of the crimes such as theft, robbery, adultery, kidnapping and fraud are devoid of some benefit, for had they been totally benefitless no sane person would ever go near them, even though the most perfect people in all such crimes are those known for their tact and intelligence. This verse also provides the rule that the elimination of evil takes precedence over the acquisition of benefit, that is, should something give a certain benefit along with causing some harm, it becomes necessary to abandon the benefit in order to stay safe against the harm.

**The evil outweighs the benefit.**

If they are calculated to be more harmful than beneficial, they are to be avoided. But, viewed from a purely moral angle, drinking and gambling lead to such spiritual danger as far outweighs any benefits they may confer. However, since wine was not forbidden clearly and explicitly during hours other than those of Salah, there were some who continued drinking during other hours until when there occurred yet another incident. There is no more than a whiff of this wine's reality in this world, and nothing but a show of that drunkenness, for this world is a prison, and what can a prison put up with? Here, the question is about wine and gambling which has been answered by Allah Almighty by pointing out that the use and practice of these two things breeds major sins while people may also get some benefits from them, but the sin they release is far too grave than the benefit they give, implying that both these are worth abandoning. In this verse, the acknowledgement of some benefits of wine and gambling has been combined with the instruction to desist from them which helps us deduce the rule that the presence of material benefits in something or act is not contrary to its being declared haram under the Islamic law. Looked at from another angle, the harm brought by this large-scale gambling is much worse than that released by the older form of gambling, for its evil effects are far-reaching and spell out the ruin of a whole nation.

**What they should spend and what they can spare.**

And they will ask you what that is to say how much they should expend. (O son of Adam! If you spend whatever you can spare, it would be better for you; but if you keep it, it would be worse for you. You shall not be blamed for whatever is barely sufficient.) This was revealed about 'Amr Ibn al-Jamuh who asked the Prophet ﷺ: �What should we spend from our wealth�. (Start with yourself and grant it some charity. If anything remains, then spend it on your family. If anything remains, then spend it on your relatives. If anything remains, then spend it like this and like that (i.e., on various charitable purposes).) It means that one should not, by such spending, get into personal trouble in the material life of this world, or by wasting away somebody's due right, get into the pain of answerability in the life to come. Allah has thus allowed spending from the orphan's estate by its executor, in reasonable proportions, on the condition that he has the intention to compensate the orphan later on, when he can afford it.

**So perhaps you may reflect.**

(Thus Allah maketh plain to you revelations) the commands and prohibitions and the insignificance of this world, (that ye may reflect) that it is evanescent. With such clear explanations, Allah describes the sacred law to you so that you may reflect. The answers to the above questions reveal certain fundamental principles: firstly, if something does more harm than good, it should be eschewed: secondly, any wealth in excess of one’s actual needs should be spent for the cause of God: thirdly, in one’s dealings with others, one should avoid any action which could lead to evil, and engage only in such activity as will bring some positive benefit to society. That is why, soon after the revelation of this verse, some noble Companions took this good counsel of the Holy Qur'an so seriously that they stopped drinking then and there. Perhaps, this is why the Holy Qur'an has elected to mention wine and gambling side by side in an identical manner since Qimar or gambling has an intoxicating pull of its own which makes one ignore the concern of what is good or bad for him. So just as He explained to you what has been mentioned God makes clear His signs to you that you might reflect.

220.text:
The verse opens on the tail of the verse before it and then turns to a question. "upon this world and the Hereafter" is the ending of the answer about what to spare, and it stands here as the measure the two homes give to a gift, so the verse before this is closed with the thought that the giving is weighed in both. "And they ask you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning orphans. Say," is a new question, and it is about a class of people rather than about a thing, so the answer that follows is about how they are to be treated and not about an amount. "Improving their condition is best" is the first answer, and the word best is what the verse puts first, since the improving of the orphan's state is set above the keeping apart from him. "And if you partner with them" gives the case the question was about, the sharing of the wealth and of the household, and "they are bonded with you ˹in faith˺" answers it with the tie that already stands between the guardian and the orphan, so the sharing is not described as a danger but as a thing that has a ground in the faith. "And Allah knows who intends harm and who intends good" puts the case where no rule can reach it, in the intention, and the two intentions are named together so the verse is not only a warning. "Had Allah willed, He could have made it difficult for you" then names the ease in the ruling as a thing willed, and it is the phrase that answers the fear the question came out of. "Surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise." closes the verse with the two descriptions, and the wisdom in the second is what the whole answer rests on, since the ruling is given as a mercy and not as a burden. The verse is the answer to a fear, and it gives that fear its place rather than blaming it.

**Concerning the orphans.**

They will ask you about orphans and the distress their affair caused them for if they became intimate with them they may slip into error but if they put aside the money due to them and prepare their meals for them separately this would distress them. Your Companions ask you, O Prophet, about the guardianship of orphans and how they should deal with them: whether they can mix their wealth with that of the orphans for expenses, food and accommodation? Allah told His Prophet: they ask you about sharing food, drink and shelter with orphans, O Muhammad: (Verily, those who unjustly eat up the property of orphans, they eat up only fire into their bellies, and they will be burnt in the blazing Fire!)(4:10) were revealed, those who took care of some orphans, separated their food and drink from the orphans' food and drink. (And they ask you concerning orphans. Say: "The best thing is to work honestly in their property, and if you mix your affairs with theirs, then they are your brothers.) Ibn Jarir reported that 'A'ishah said, "I dislike that an orphan's money be under my care, unless I mix my food with his food and my drink with his drink."

**Improving the affairs of the orphans.**

Say ‘To set their affairs aright in terms of their funds by looking after it and your mingling with them is better’ than you not doing this; and if you intermix with them your funds and theirs they are your brothers in religion and it is only natural for one to intermix his affair with his brother so you do too; God knows well him who works corruption in their property when he intermixes with them from him who sets it aright and God will requite both; and had He willed He would have harassed you and made it difficult for you by prohibiting you from intermixing with them. Therefore, the situation was brought to the notice of the Holy Prophet following which came the guidance given in this verse. Allah has established these rules so that you may think about what benefits you in this world and the Afterlife. It is, therefore, more useful to lay down some, fundamental guidelines: to wish others well and to keep in mind not just our own interests, but also the interests of those with whom we have to deal, thinking of them as brothers. Allah has thus allowed spending from the orphan's estate by its executor, in reasonable proportions, on the condition that he has the intention to compensate the orphan later on, when he can afford it. (Indeed Allah is Mighty) and takes revenge against whoever spoils the wealth of orphans, (Wise) ruling that the wealth of orphans should be improved.

**Partnership with them and the mixing of wealth.**

However, there is no harm if you mix their wealth with yours for living expenses, as they are your brothers in faith and it is normal for brothers to help and look after the affairs of one another. Hence, they joined their food and drink with the food and drink of the orphans. It was not permissible for them to use food which belonged to the orphans, nor did they have the right to give what belonged to the orphans in charity. Then Allah revealed (And if ye mingle your affairs with theirs, then (they are) your brothers) upon which they mixed their own wealth with the wealth of orphans . Patience in bearing with them by giving counsel and abandoning one's weariness in guiding them is better than being permissive to the point that it could be said that one did not uphold one's obligation toward them. If you are kind to them by arranging their affairs without taking anything in return and without touching their wealth, it is better in the sight of Allah and carries greater reward.

**Allah knows who intends harm and who intends good.**

And Allah knows (the one) who means mischief (e.g., to swallow their property) from (the one) who means good (e.g., to save their property). (And Allah knows (the one) who means mischief (e.g., to swallow their property) from (the one) who means good (e.g., to save their property).) meaning, He knows those whose intent is to cause mischief or righteousness. Allah knows the guardian who, by mixing the wealth of orphans with his, means harm and the one who means well. This is for the elect who take from the surplus of their wealth according to their capacities. (O you who believe! Intoxicants (all kinds of alcoholic drinks), and gambling, and Al-Ansab, and Al-Azlam are an abomination of Shaytan's handiwork. So avoid (strictly all) that (abomination) in order that you may be successful. Shaytan wants only to excite enmity and hatred between you with intoxicants (alcoholic drinks) and gambling, and hinder you from the remembrance of Allah and from As-Salah (the prayer). So, will you not then abstain?)(5:90-91) Then, when the prayer was called for, a person used to herald on behalf of Allah's Messenger , "No drunk person should attend the prayer." 'Umar was summoned again and the Ayah was recited to him.

**Had Allah willed He could have made it difficult.**

(Had Allah willed He could have overburdened you) He could have forbidden such sharing. Consequently, the recipients of this warning were so scared that they, out of preventive measure, started preparing and storing meals given to orphans separately. Since there was general lack of carefulness about the rights of orphans in pagan Arabia, as elsewhere, warning was given that consuming what belongs to the orphans is like filling bellies with embers of Hell. Surely God is Mighty victorious in His affair Wise in His actions. (Thus Allah makes clear to you His Ayat in order that you may give thought. In this worldly life and in the Hereafter.) meaning, just as He stated and explained these commandments for you, He also explains the rest of His Ayat regarding the commandments and His promises and warnings, so that you might give thought in this life and the Hereafter. 'Ali bin Abu Talhah said that Ibn 'Abbas commented, "Meaning about the imminent demise and the brevity of this life, and the imminent commencement of the Hereafter and its continuity." (And if Allah had wished, He could have put you into difficulties. Truly, Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise) meaning, if Allah wills, He will make this matter difficult for you.

**Who it was revealed about.**

This was revealed about 'Abdullah Ibn Rawahah who asked the Prophet ﷺ about whether it was lawful to share food, drink and shelter with orphans. When the verse (Lo! Those who devour the wealth of orphans wrongfully, they do but swallow fire into their bellies) [4:10] people rushed to separate their own wealth from the wealth of orphans they were in charge of. When Allah, exalted is He, revealed the verse (And approach not the wealth of the orphan save with that which is better), whoever had an orphan's wealth with him proceeded to isolate his food and drink from the orphan's food and drink, and whatever remained of the orphan's food was kept aside until the orphan would use it or it gets bad; and this was a source of anguish for people. They went and mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, and as a response, Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed (And they question thee concerning orphans. Say: To improve their lot is best), by mixing their food and drink with their food and drink .

221.text:
The verse gives two commands and then the reason for both. "Do not marry polytheistic women until they believe" is the first, and the until in it is what makes the command a waiting rather than a refusal, since the door is closed on the state and not on the person. "for a believing slave-woman is better than a free polytheist" gives the measure, and the measure is set against the two things the world weighs, freedom and rank, so the verse takes a slave and a free woman and puts the belief above the freedom. "even though she may look pleasant to you" is the clause that meets the objection before it is made, and it names the look of the woman as the thing that pulls against the command. "And do not marry your women to polytheistic men until they believe" is the second command, and it is the same command turned round, with the women of the believers named as the ones given in it. "for a believing slave-man is better than a free polytheist" repeats the measure on the other side, and the repeating is what makes the ruling plain, since the same balance is struck in both directions. "even though he may look pleasant to you" closes the second command with the same clause. "They invite ˹you˺ to the Fire while Allah invites ˹you˺ to Paradise and forgiveness by His grace" then gives the ground of both commands, and the two invitations are set against each other, so the marriage is described by where it leads. "He makes His revelations clear to the people so perhaps they will be mindful" closes the verse on the making clear and on the mindfulness asked for in answer to it. The two commands in the verse are one ruling stated twice, and the reason for both of them is the invitation at the end of it.

**Do not marry the polytheist women.**

O Muslims Do not marry idolatresses disbelievers until they believe; a believing slavegirl is better than an idolatress who may be a free woman; this was revealed as a rebuttal of the idea that it was shameful to marry a slavegirl and that it was better to marry an idolatress free woman; though you may admire her because of her beauty and wealth this provision excludes the womenfolk of the People of the Scripture as indicated by the verse Q. 55 lawful to you are the chaste women among those who were given the Scripture. Do not get married, O believers, to those women who give partners to Allah until they have faith in Him alone and enter the path of Islam. Allah prohibited such marriage, saying: do not marry idolatresses women (till they believe) in Allah; (for lo! A believing bondwoman) marrying a believing slave woman (is better than an idolatress) who is a free woman (though she pleases you) though you may like her comeliness and beauty; (and give not your daughters in marriage to idolaters till they believe) in Allah, (for lo! A believing slave) Allah says: giving your daughters in marriage to a believing slave (is better than an idolater) is better than your daughter marrying an idolater who is free (though he pleases you) though his body and strength may please you.

**A believing slave-woman is better.**

A believing slave is better than an idolater though you may admire him for his wealth and good looks.
