The fifth point worth considering is that the meaning of the permission to Muslim men to marry Jewish and Christian women under formal Nikah (marriage contract) is simply to state that such Nikah if made, will become valid and the children born out of this wedlock will be ligitimate. The Holy Prophet has said that a Muslim should seek to marry a woman who fully observes Islamic faith and conduct -- so that she becomes for him a source of strength in their joint pursuit of their faith, and their progeny may have the opportunity to grow up under their care as practising Muslims. Out of these, if we consider the belief in Akhirah even the Jews and Christians from amongst the people of the Book agree with Muslims in accordance with their original faith, wherein, very similarly, it is kufr (infidelity) even in their original faith to attribute partners with God.

**The marriage of the believing women.**

A Muslim who marries someone of another faith may have to compromise on his beliefs, in which case it will be his faith that suffers; and if he refuses to do so, it will be his marriage which will flounder. The effect of such marriages in contemporary times when non-Muslim people of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, have a record of political deception, political marriages, entry into Muslim families with persuasion techniques and spying objectives is too obvious and has been admitted by Christian writers themselves as reported in some details by Major General Akbar in his book, Hadith-e-Difa,. But if the word Mushrik is taken to mean specially those non-Muslims who are not from amongst the Ahl al-Kitab (People of the Book i.e. the Jews and the Christians), this verse needs no exception, because it covers only those non-Muslims who do not believe in any prophet and scripture. It is not correct to marry women from among the group of people who, on the basis of their name and identity, are considered from among the people of the Book but are not proved to be so after a scrutiny of beliefs.

**They invite to the Fire.**

Those the people of idolatry call to the Fire because they invite one to perform deeds that merit this and for this reason one should not marry with them; and God calls through the voice of His prophets to Paradise and pardon that is to the deeds that merit these two by His leave by His will so that His call may be heeded by marrying with His friends; and He makes clear His signs to the people so that they might remember that they might be admonished. (These invite unto the Fire) they invite to disbelief and to works that lead to hell, (and Allah inviteth unto the Garden) by means of His divine Oneness, (and unto forgiveness) through repentance (by His grace) by His leave, (and He expoundeth thus His revelations) His commands and prohibitions regarding marriage (to mankind that they may remember) so that they may take admonition and refrain from unlawful marriage. Those (Mushrikin) invite you to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His leave, and makes His Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) clear to mankind that they may remember. (Those (Al-Mushrikun) invite you to the Fire) meaning, associating and mingling with the disbelievers makes one love this life and prefer it over the Hereafter, leading to the severest repercussions.

**Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness.**

(...but Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His leave) meaning, by His Law, commandments and prohibitions. Allah, on the other hand, invites to good actions which will lead to entry into Paradise and forgiveness of sins by His permission and grace. Those call to the fire; and God calls to paradise and pardon by His leave; and He makes clear His signs to the people so that they might remember. To illustrate the purpose of the matrimonial bond, the relationship between man and woman may be likened to that of a farmer and his field. Therefore, it was said that these people call everyone to come to Hell while Allah Almighty calls man to Paradise and to His forgiveness and, for this purpose, states His injunctions openly and clearly so that people follow the wise counsel. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, sent a man from Ghaniyy called Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, an ally of Banu Hashim, to Makkah to try to free some Muslims who were held prisoners there. But then he became worried as a result of what he had done which made him rush to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, to inform him of what had happened.

**Who it was revealed about.**

This verse was revealed about Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi who sought the permission of the Prophet, Allah, bless him and give him peace, to marry 'Anaq, who was a poor, fairly beautiful woman from Quraysh. This verse was revealed about 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah who owned a black slave. This was revealed about Marthad Ibn Abi Marthad Al-Ghanawi who wanted to marry an idolatress woman by the name of 'Inaq. If the word, Mushrik in this verse is taken to mean non-Muslims as a whole it would be necessary to exempt non-Muslim women of the Ahl al-Kitab (the people of the Book) from the purview of this injunction, because it is expressly stated in another verse that: How can people who do not believe in God, in the prophethood of Jesus Christ and in the Bible as revealed scripture be Christians? Allah, exalted is He, therefore revealed about them (for lo! a believing bondwoman is better than an idolatress though she please you) .

222.text:
The verse is a question and an answer about a state, and the answer moves in four steps. "They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about menstruation. Say," is the question and the command to answer it, and the question is about a thing that happens to the women of the believers, so the ruling that follows is a ruling for the household and not for a public matter. "Beware of its harm!" is the first step and the ground of the rest, since the verse begins by naming the harm in the state rather than the prohibition, and the hearer is told what the state is before he is told what to do in it. "So keep away" is the second step, and it follows from the harm, so the keeping away is given as the answer to a danger and not as a mark set against the woman. "and do not have intercourse with your wives during their monthly cycles until they are purified" is the third step and the specific one, since the keeping away is now named as one act and the end of it is fixed at the purifying. "When they purify themselves, then you may approach them in the manner specified by Allah" is the fourth step, and it gives both the return and the way of it, so the verse does not leave the husband to guess at what stands open after the purifying. "Surely Allah loves those who always turn to Him in repentance and those who purify themselves." closes the verse with the two things Allah loves, and the second of them is the word the whole ruling has been about, so the verse ends on the purifying as a thing loved and not as a thing shunned. The four steps in the answer are the four things a ruling of this kind needs, the harm, the keeping away, the end of it, and the return.

**The question about menstruation.**

They will ask you about the monthly period that is menstruation and the spot in which it occurs and how should one treat women during it. (They question thee (O Muhammad) concerning menstruation) this was revealed about Abu'l-Dahdah who asked the Prophet ﷺ about it. Your Companions ask you about menses (which is the blood of menstruation that naturally comes out of the womb at certain times of the month). In this context it has been said in the verse 222 that "Allah loves those who are most repenting." By using this expression the Holy Qur'an has given a subtle indication to the prohibition of carnal intercourse, even with one's wife, because it can never be a productive act, and there is no question of 'cultivation' therein. Imam Ahmad recorded that Anas said that the Jews used to avoid their menstruating women, they would not eat, or even mingle with them in the house. (They ask you concerning menstruation. Say: "That is an Adha, therefore, keep away from women during menses and go not in unto them till they are purified.)

**The monthly period and the harm in it.**

Say ‘It is an ailment filth or the place whence it issues is so; so part with women refrain from sexual intercourse with them in the monthly period in this time or in the part affected; and do not approach them for sexual intercourse until they are pure yathurna or yattahharna the original tā’ of yatatahharna has been assimilated with the tā’ that is until they have cleansed themselves after its cessation; when they have cleansed themselves then come to them in sexual intercourse as God has commanded you’ by avoiding it the female organ during menstruation and not resorting to any other part. The basic purpose of these verses is to declare the prohibition of having sexual intercourse with a woman in a state of menstruation. The Jews used to banish women in their menstruation out of the house and refrain from eating, drinking and having sex with them. It is also reported in the Two Sahihs that Maymunah bint Al-Harith Al-Hilaliyah said, "Whenever the Prophet wanted to fondle any of his wives during the periods (menses), he used to ask her to wear an Izar (a sheet covering the lower-half of the body). The scholars agree that the woman is obliged to take a bath, or to perform Tayammum with sand, if she is unable to use water, before she is allowed to have sexual intercourse with her husband, after the monthly period ends.

**Keep away until they are purified.**

(And when they have purified themselves) and have had a major ritual ablution (ghusl), (then go in unto them) you may have sex with them (as Allah hath enjoined upon you) as you were dispensed to do before, i.e. penetration ought to be in the pudendum. Truly, Allah loves those who turn unto Him in repentance and loves those who purify themselves Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth, when or how you will, and send (good deeds, or ask Allah to bestow upon you pious offspring) for your own selves beforehand. (And when they have purified themselves, then go in unto them as Allah has ordained for you.) indicates that men should have sexual intercourse with their wives after they take a bath. Umm Salamah said, 'Wait until Allah's Messenger comes.' When Allah's Messenger came, the Ansari woman was shy to ask him about this matter, so she left.

**Approach them as Allah has specified.**

This is to indicate that the sexual intercourse has not been allowed for satisfying the sexual lust only, but also to make it a valid source for having children. The Jews used to say: 'Whoever penetrates his wife from a back position, the child born to them as a result of this intercourse would be born cross-eyed'. We should take care to ensure that our deeds measure up well on God’s scale of justice, for if they fail to do so, there is no way we can avoid His punishment. It is also the view of Sa'id bin Musayyib, Abu Salamah, 'Ikrimah, Tawus, 'Ata , Sa'id bin Jubayr, 'Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, Mujahid bin Jabr, Al-Hasan and other scholars of the Salaf (the Companions and the following two generations after them). (Truly Allah loveth those who turn unto Him) those who repent of transgression (and loveth those who have a care for cleanness) those who have a care for turning away from transgression and filth. In addition, Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah reported that 'Abdullah bin Sa'd Al-Ansari asked Allah's Messenger , "What am I allowed of my wife while she is having her menses? In addition, Imam Ahmad reported that 'Ali bin Talaq said, "Allah's Messenger forbade anal sex with women, for Allah does not shy away from truth.

**Allah loves those who repent and purify themselves.**

Truly God loves that is He rewards and honours those who repent of sins and He loves those who cleanse themselves from impurities. Allah loves those that frequently repent from their sins and are extra mindful of cleanliness. It is said that [it refers to] those who repent from error and those who cleanse themselves from imagining that their salvation is through repentance. It is said that [it refers to] those who repent from doing forbidden things and those who cleanse themselves from familiar things and considerations [of anything but God]. (If anyone of you on having sexual relations with his wife said: 'In the Name of Allah. O Allah! Protect us from Satan and also protect what you bestow upon us (i.e., the coming offspring) from Satan,' and if it is destined that they should have a child then, Satan will never be able to harm him.) One of these women would not obey her husband and said, 'You will not do that until I go to Allah's Messenger (and ask him about this matter). ' She went to Umm Salamah and told her the story. (and loves those who purify themselves.) meaning, those who purify themselves from the impurity and the filth that include having sexual intercourse with the wife during the menses and anal sex.

**The practice of the Jews and what was revealed.**

When the Jews were told about the Prophet's statement, they said, "What is the matter with this man? The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, was asked about this, and as a response Allah, exalted is He, revealed (They question thee (O Muhammad) concerning menstruation. Say: It is an illness, so let women alone at such times and go not in unto them till they are cleansed) . Ibn Abu Hatim said that Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated that Jabir bin 'Abdullah told him that the Jews claimed to the Muslims that if one has sex with their wife from behind (in the vagina) their offspring will become cross-eyed. (Your wives are a tilth for you) was revealed about some people from the Ansar who came to the Prophet and asked him (about having sex with the wife from behind). They all, along with the majority of the scholars, harshly rebuked the practice of anal sex and many of them called this practice a Kufr.

223.text:
The verse carries on from the ruling before it and gives the shape of the lawful. "Your wives are like farmland for you" is the comparison the verse is built on, and the wording puts the likeness in one word, so the verse is describing what the wife is in this act and not what she is in herself. "so approach them ˹consensually˺ as you please" is the permission, and it comes out of the comparison, and the as you please in it is the widest phrase in the verse, so the hearer is told that the manner stands open. "And send forth something good for yourselves" turns the verse from the act to what a person puts in front of himself, and the sending forth is described as good and as for the self, so the verse joins the act to the account that is kept of it. "Be mindful of Allah" is the command that covers the permission, and it stands in the middle of the verse so that the openness before it is not read on its own. "and know that you will meet Him" gives the ground of the mindfulness, since the meeting is the point at which what was sent forward is found. "And give good news to the believers" closes the verse with an address to the Prophet and a word for the believers, and the good news is the last thing the hearer is given after the mindfulness and the meeting, so the verse ends where the passage has been going, on the believers and what is promised to them. The verse joins the permission and the mindfulness in one breath, and it puts the good news at the end so that the hearer is not left with the command alone.

**Your wives are like farmland.**

Your women are a tillage for you that is the place where you sow the seeds of your children; so come to your tillage that is the specified place the front part as in whichever way you wish whether standing up sitting down lying down from the front or the back this was revealed in response to the Jews saying that if a person had vaginal intercourse with his wife from behind the child would be born cross-eyed; and offer for your souls righteous deeds such as saying ‘In the Name of God’ bismillāh when you commence intercourse; and fear God in what He commands and prohibits; and know that you shall meet Him at the Resurrection where He will requite you according to your deeds; and give good tidings of Paradise to the believers who feared Him. (Your women are a tilth for you (to cultivate) He says: the vulvas of your wives are plantations for your offspring (so go to your tilth) your plantations (as ye will) as you please, from behind or front as long as the penetration is in the pudendum, (and send (good deeds) before you for your souls) righteous children, (and fear Allah) regarding penetrating your wives in their anus or having sex with them during menstruation, (and know that ye will (one day) meet Him) that you will see Him after you die and He will reward you according to your deeds. Your wives are a place for you to sow your seed: they produce children for you just as the land produces crops. Your women are your tillage, so come to your tillage as you like. Do you know the story behind this Ayah?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'We, the people of Quraysh, used to have sexual intercourse with our wives from the back (in the vagina).

**Approach them as you please.**

He said, "Your women are your tillage, so come to your tillage as you like. In this context, it has been said, "Come to your soil from where you will". It indicates that in so far as the ultimate place (of penetration) is a 'soil' (which stands for the female vagina which is productive like a soil), one can elect whatever way he likes to reach this ultimate place. (Your wives are a tilth for you) was revealed about some people from the Ansar who came to the Prophet and asked him (about having sex with the wife from behind). It is also the view of Sa'id bin Musayyib, Abu Salamah, 'Ikrimah, Tawus, 'Ata , Sa'id bin Jubayr, 'Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, Mujahid bin Jabr, Al-Hasan and other scholars of the Salaf (the Companions and the following two generations after them). (And when they have purified themselves, then go in unto them as Allah has ordained for you.) indicates that men should have sexual intercourse with their wives after they take a bath. Imam Ahmad recorded that Anas said that the Jews used to avoid their menstruating women, they would not eat, or even mingle with them in the house. He calls them men when He says, "In it are men who love to make themselves pure, and God loves those who make themselves pure" [9:108]. So approach the plantation, which is the vagina, from whichever direction and in whichever manner you wish as long as intercourse takes place in the vagina.

**Send forth something good for yourselves.**

(...and send for your own selves beforehand.) means, mention Allah's Name, by saying, 'Bismillah', before having sexual intercourse. Send forth something good for yourselves, such as having sexual intercourse with the intention of gaining closeness to Allah and with the hope of pious offspring. In this context it has been said in the verse 222 that "Allah loves those who are most repenting." In another place He said, "That you may rest in them, and He placed between you love and mercy" [30:21]. Abu Dawud reported that 'Ikrimah related to one of the Prophet's wives that she said that whenever the Prophet wanted to fondle (one of his wives) during her menses, he would cover her sexual organ with something. (...and send for your own selves beforehand.) meaning, by performing the acts of worship while refraining from whatever Allah has prohibited for you. I went to Hafsah bint 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abu Bakr and said, "I wish to ask you about something, but I am shy.

**Know that you will meet Him.**

Know that you are to meet Him on the Day of Resurrection and will have to stand before Him to receive the reward for your actions. Truly, Allah loves those who turn unto Him in repentance and loves those who purify themselves Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth, when or how you will, and send (good deeds, or ask Allah to bestow upon you pious offspring) for your own selves beforehand. This is to indicate that the sexual intercourse has not been allowed for satisfying the sexual lust only, but also to make it a valid source for having children. (If anyone of you on having sexual relations with his wife said: 'In the Name of Allah. O Allah! Protect us from Satan and also protect what you bestow upon us (i.e., the coming offspring) from Satan,' and if it is destined that they should have a child then, Satan will never be able to harm him.) Ibn Abu Hatim said that Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated that Jabir bin 'Abdullah told him that the Jews claimed to the Muslims that if one has sex with their wife from behind (in the vagina) their offspring will become cross-eyed. (...so go to your tilth, when or how you will,) meaning, wherever you wish from the front or from behind, as long as sex takes place in one valve (the female sexual organ), as the authentic Hadiths have indicated. Until it cuts itself off from creation and makes its own secret core pure of other than the Real, it will not come under these words: If you put a corpse into the ocean a thousand times, it will never become pure, for the impurity belongs to its own entity.

**Good news to the believers.**

(Give glad tidings to believers (O Muhammad) Allah says: give glad tidings, O Muhammad, to the believers, who ward off penetrating their wives in their anus and further abstain from having sex with them when they are menstruating, that Paradise will be theirs. O Prophet, give the believers good news of everlasting blessings that will surely please them when they meet their Lord: seeing His Blessed Face. Know also that in this house of the decree, vile things are of two sorts. Doing good works means acting with the Hereafter in mind. (...and give good tidings to the believers (O Muhammad).) meaning, those who obey what Allah has commanded and refrain from what He has prohibited.

224.text:
The verse takes up the oath and refuses one use of it. "Do not use Allah's Name in your oaths as an excuse for not doing good, not guarding against evil, or not making peace between people" is the whole of the command, and it is given in one piece because the three things it names are three faces of one act. The first is the good not done, and the verse puts it first, so the case it answers is a person who has taken an oath that stands between him and a good act. The second is the evil not guarded against, and the third is the peace not made between people, so the verse covers the good left, the harm left, and the quarrel left standing. The phrase as an excuse is the heart of the command, since what is refused is not the oath but the use of the Name as a reason. "And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" closes the verse with the two descriptions, and they answer the two sides of the case, the word spoken in the oath and the intention behind it, so the hearer is told that the excuse offered in the Name is heard by the One whose Name it is. The verse stands at the head of the verses about oaths, and the verse after this gives what Allah does with the oath that was not intended, so the passage moves from the oath used as an excuse to the oath that slipped out.

**The oath as an excuse.**

Do not make God by swearing in His Name a hindrance a cause of impediment in your oaths that is setting up such impediments by swearing in His Name frequently so as not to be pious and God-fearing; in such instances oaths are hateful and result in perjury which requires a redemption effected by doing the opposite of the oath such as performing righteous deeds and so forth which constitute an act of obedience; and to put things right between people this means do not be prevented from doing righteous deeds as mentioned just because you swore against them; nay do them and make redemption; this understanding of the verse is justified by the reason for its revelation namely their refraining from such deeds; surely God is All-Hearing of what you say Knower of your circumstances. Do not make God a hindrance in your oaths to be pious and God-fearing; and to put things right between people; surely God is All-Hearing Knower. The Verse warns those who swear in the name of Allah that they will not do some vituous deeds or that they will not effect a compromise between two groups. Swayed by anger and obstinacy, sometimes an individual swears an oath that he will not do anything which would benefit a certain person.

**The good left undone and the peace unmade.**

They swore oaths that they would refrain from such and such a good deed, so that when they were called upon to join in some good act, they would decline, saying that they had already taken an oath to the contrary. To refrain from good acts is in itself bad enough, but swearing to this in the name of God is much worse. (By Allah! It is more sinful to Allah that one of you implements his vow regarding (severing the relations with) his relatives than (breaking his promise and) paying the Kaffarah that Allah has required in such cases.) Yet if you have taken an oath not to do any good actions, then do good actions and make a compensation for the oath.

**The peace between people and the good undone.**

He says: return to that which is better for you and make amend for your oaths; it is also said that this means: avoid making oaths by Allah about not showing kindness to anyone and your not making peace between people. The Verse reminds them that by this behaviour they are using the name of Allah as a barrier against the good deeds, which is a severe violation of the sanctity of the name of Allah, and they must avoid it in any case,. But if perverse acts are done in the name of God, there is a manifold increase in the evil perpetuated. It is said Do not make the mention of God into a net to catch the debris of this world.

**Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.**

(For Allah is Hearer) of your oath to stop showing kindness to people, (Knower) of your intentions and the amends that will absolve you from your oaths. Allah hears your statements and knows your actions and will reward you for them. And Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower (i.e., do not swear much and if you have sworn against doing something good then give an expiation for the oath and do good)Allah will not call you to account for that which is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for that which your hearts have earned. Keep the mention of your Lord free of the banality of any worldly concerns. (And let not those among you who are blessed with graces and wealth swear not to give (any sort of help) to their kinsmen, Al-Masakin (the poor), and those who left their homes for Allah's cause. Let them pardon and forgive. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?)(24:22) (By Allah! Allah willing, I will not vow to do a thing and then see a better act, but I would do what is better and break my vow.) Muslim reported that Abu Hurayrah said that Allah's Messenger said: This Ayah means, 'Allah does not punish or hold you accountable for the Laghw (unintentional) vows that you make.' The Laghw vows are unintentional and are just like the habitual statements that the tongue repeats, without really intending them.

**The swearing and the breaking of the oath.**

This was revealed about Abd Allah ibn Rawahah to warn him against boycotting the husband of his sister, Bashir ibn al-Nu'man. Abd Allah ibn Rawahah had sworn that he will never visit him, speak to him or reconcile between him and his sister. I swore by Allah that I will not do any of these and it is forbidden for me not to honour my oath . But Allah warned him against doing so, saying: do not make Allah a reason by means of which you make oaths, (to your being righteous) that you should not honour your oath (and observing your duty unto Him) and ward off severing ties of kinship (and making peace) and not make peace (among mankind). This was revealed about 'Abdullah Ibn Rawahah who swore not to show kindness to his sister and her husband and not to speak with them or make up between them. Allah commands, 'You should not implement your vows in Allah's Name to refrain from pious acts and severing the relations with the relatives, if you swear to abandon such causes.' Allah said in another Ayah: (Whoever makes a vow and then finds what is better than his vow (should break his vow,) pay the Kaffarah and perform the better deed.) Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and several others said that this Ayah means swearing about a matter while knowing that he is lying.

225.text:
The verse divides the oaths into two and gives the ruling on each. "Allah will not hold you accountable for unintentional oaths" is the first half, and the holding to account is what is lifted, so the verse is not saying that the unintentional oath is nothing but that it brings no account. The word unintentional fixes the case, and it is the oath that came out of the mouth without the heart going with it. "but for what you intended in your hearts" is the second half, and the turn is in the but, so the account is put on the intention and the place of the intention is named as the heart. The verse therefore joins the two halves in one measure, since what is not counted and what is counted are both fixed by the same thing, what the heart meant. "And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing" closes with the two descriptions, and they are the ground of the first half, since the forgiving is what covers the slip and the forbearing is what does not hurry the account. The verse stands right after the command about the oath used as an excuse, and it answers the fear that command might leave, since a person told not to use the Name in his oaths is a person who needs to know what becomes of the oaths that came out of him without his meaning them. The ruling is short and it turns on one word, and the verse after this takes up the oath that binds a man in his own house.

**The unintentional oath.**

God will not take you to task for a slip that results in your oaths which is what the tongue utters spontaneously and unintentionally such as ‘By God’ ‘Indeed by God’ in such instances there is no sin and no redemption required; but He will take you to task for what your hearts have earned what their intention is when you commit perjury in your oaths; and God is Forgiving of slips in your oaths Forbearing since He delays the punishment of the one deserving it. (Allah will not take you to task for that which is unintentional in your oaths) by imposing amends for unintentional oaths such as saying: �No, by Allah� or �Yes indeed, by Allah� upon buying and selling and upon other instances of idle talk. Allah will not take you to account for those oaths that you swear unintentionally, such as if someone carelessly says, ‘No, by Allah!’ or ‘Yes, by Allah! For ex-ample, guided by his information and supposition, one ends up declaring on oath that a certain person has arrived while that person had not arrived in reality. (Whoever swore and (unintentionally) mentioned Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza (two idols) in his vow, should then say, 'There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah'.)

**What the hearts intended.**

(But He will take you to task for that which your hearts have garnered) what is hidden in your hearts. However, He will take you to account for intentional oaths. This Ayah means, 'Allah does not punish or hold you accountable for the Laghw (unintentional) vows that you make.' The Laghw vows are unintentional and are just like the habitual statements that the tongue repeats, without really intending them. In the first case it means a false oath sworn without volition over something in the past, or it could have been sworn with volition while the oath-taker considers it to be true in his supposition. Therefore, the Prophet ordered them to intentionally recite the slogan of Ikhlas, just as they mentioned these words by mistake, so that it (the word of Ikhlas) may eradicate the word (of Shirk). For instance, if someone intentionally declares on oath to the effect that he or she would or would not perform a certain act, then, acting contrarily requires kaffarah. As compared to this, the oath which has been declared reprehensible is the one that has been uttered intentionally knowing it to be false.

**The slip of the tongue in the oath.**

Given this meaning, the word, laghw is inclusive of ghamus, which being an act of sin, however, does not require kaffarah . Similarly, if someone swears on oath for some-thing in future unintentionally, while he has been actually wanting to say something else, but the words of oath come out of his lips mistakenly, this type of oath also falls in this category. Swayed by anger and obstinacy, sometimes an individual swears an oath that he will not do anything which would benefit a certain person. In ancient times, a variety of such oaths was very common among the Arabs. And Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower (i.e., do not swear much and if you have sworn against doing something good then give an expiation for the oath and do good)Allah will not call you to account for that which is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for that which your hearts have earned. They swore oaths that they would refrain from such and such a good deed, so that when they were called upon to join in some good act, they would decline, saying that they had already taken an oath to the contrary. The Messenger said this statement to some new Muslims whose tongues were, before Islam, used to vowing by their idol Al-Lat.

**Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing.**

(And Allah is Forgiving) of your unintentional oaths, (Clement) in that He does not hasten punishment upon you; it is also said: idle talk is an oath for committing transgression. Allah forgives and tolerates the sins of His servants and is not hasty in sending punishment. If one refrains from it and makes amends, then Allah does not take one to task for it; but if one does not refrain from so doing, then Allah will take one to task for it. This is known as ghamus (perjury), and is an act of sin, but according to the Hanafiyyah, it does not require kaffarah or expiation. (And let not those among you who are blessed with graces and wealth swear not to give (any sort of help) to their kinsmen, Al-Masakin (the poor), and those who left their homes for Allah's cause. Let them pardon and forgive. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?)(24:22) (By Allah! Allah willing, I will not vow to do a thing and then see a better act, but I would do what is better and break my vow.) Muslim reported that Abu Hurayrah said that Allah's Messenger said: (By Allah! It is more sinful to Allah that one of you implements his vow regarding (severing the relations with) his relatives than (breaking his promise and) paying the Kaffarah that Allah has required in such cases.) Allah commands, 'You should not implement your vows in Allah's Name to refrain from pious acts and severing the relations with the relatives, if you swear to abandon such causes.'
