The appointment is given first and the objection second and the answer third, and the order is the shape of the verse, since the answer is not a defence of the man but a statement about who appoints, and the verse lets the objection be heard in full before it is answered.

**Allah has appointed Saul.**

The restoration of the Ark of the Covenant was an extraordinary testimony to the appointment of Talut (Saul) by God’s own will. (Talut is the Qur'anic name of the king known in the Bible as Saul) When the Bani Isra'il saw this sign, they believed in the kingdom of Talut, who then mounted an attack on Jalut while the weather was very hot. The name of the prophet mentioned here is Samuel (Arabic: Hebrew: Shemuel). When the infidel Amalekites were made to rule over them, they began thinking about correcting the situation. These people from the Bani Isra'il had abandoned the injunctions given by Allah Almighty. When Allah Almighty willed the return of the chest, it so happened that the infidels were struck by some epidemic or calamity at places where they carried this chest. Then, the angels took control of the bullocks and made it reach Talut's doorsteps. The Bani Isra'il used to have the legacy of a wooden chest (also identified as the Ark of the Covenant). Moses and other prophets of Bani Isra'il would keep this chest in the frontline of the battlefield. Goliath) overcame Bani Isra'il, he took this chest away with him. Its barakah (blessing, benediction) used to give them victory. Nonplussed, they loaded it on two bullocks and drove them off.

**How can he be our king.**

" They said, "How can he be a king over us when we are fitter than him for the kingdom, and he has not been given enough wealth. Their leaders objected to this appointment and said, ‘How can he rule over us when we have a greater right to rule than he does, since he is not from the children of kings and he has not been given vast wealth which he can use in his rule! They said How can he be king over us when we have better right than he to kingship seeing he has not been given amplitude of wealthḍ He said God has chosen him over you and has increased him broadly in knowledge and body jism. (When they said to a prophet of theirs: "Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of Allah)."

**Deserving of kingship and without riches.**

(when we are fitter than him for the kingdom, and he has not been given enough wealth?) They said that Talut was also poor and did not have the wealth that justifies him being king. But, Talut was not a descendant of the house of kings among them, which was exclusively in the offspring of Yahudha (Judah). They deemed it unlikely that Saul could be a king because he was poor and without property. [God] explained to them that merit is by the choice of the Real and that if [Saul] lacked wealth God has increased him in knowledge and has favored him over you by his knowledge and body jism. It is said that He meant that [Saul] was praiseworthy in the qualities of the self nafs not large in [his] physical frame binya for as it is said in the adage So and so is a name without a body fulān ism bi-lā jism that is a man without substance. Some people stated that Talut used to bring water to the people, while others stated that his profession was dyeing skins. The Jews, thus, disputed with their Prophet while they were supposed to obey him and to say good words to him.

**Knowledge and stature.**

He the prophet said to them ‘God has chosen him over you for kingship and has increased him broadly amply in knowledge and body at that time he was the most knowledgeable and the most handsome of all the Children of Israel and the most perfect of character. Samuel (said: Lo! Allah hath chosen him) to be king and sovereign (above you, and hath increased him abundantly in wisdom) the knowledge of warfare (and stature) size and physical strength. ’ Their prophet said to them, ‘Allah has selected him over you and has given him great knowledge and physical strength. The king should have sufficient knowledge, be fair looking and should have a strong soul and body.' He then said: Therefore, only that person will be held to be a true believer who is broadminded in his thinking and who takes decisions on the basis of realities rather than prejudices and other petty considerations. Stirring up controversies on all issues was indicative of their degeneration.

**Allah grants kingship to whoever He wills.**

God gives the kingship to whom He will in the way He does and there can be no objection; and God is Embracing in His bounty Knowing of those who deserve it. (Allah bestoweth His sovereignty on whom he will) in this life even if he is not of royal descent. (And Allah grants His kingdom to whom He wills.) meaning, Allah Alone is the Supreme Authority Who does what He wills and no one can ask Him about His actions, while they will be asked (about their actions by Him). (And Allah is All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Knower.) meaning, His favor is encompassing and He grants His mercy to whom He wills. Allah grants authority to whomever He wishes in accordance with His wisdom and mercy. God gives the kingship to whom He will; and God is Embracing Knowing. He knows which of His creation is most deserving’. And Allah is All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Knower.

**The knowledge and the choosing.**

(Verily, Allah has chosen him above you) meaning, 'Allah chose Talut from amongst you while having better knowledge about him.' Their Prophet stated, "I did not choose Talut to be your king on my own. (...and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature.) meaning, 'Talut is more knowledgeable and honorable than you, and stronger and more patient during combat, and has more knowledge of warfare. (Allah is All-Embracing) in His gift, (All-Knowing) about whom He gives to, because they said to their prophet that it was he who chose Saul rather than his being appointed by Allah. This is because Allah has perfect knowledge, wisdom and kindness with His creation. He also knows those who deserve to be kings and those who do not deserve it. They forgot [God's] right of free choice ikhtiyār and viewed the situation instead with the eye of the external world. Rather, Allah has commanded that upon your request. God’s decrees are based on knowledge and broadmindedness.

248.text:
The verse gives the sign that settles the objection. "Their prophet further told them" is the frame, and the further in it is what joins this verse to the one before, so the speech is a continuation of the same answer. "The sign of Saul's kingship is that the Ark will come to you" is the sign, and the sign is a thing coming rather than a word spoken, so the verse puts the proof of the kingship in an object that can be seen. "containing reassurance from your Lord and relics of the family of Moses and the family of Aaron" describes what is in the Ark, and the two things in it are a reassurance from Allah and the relics of two families, so the sign carries both a comfort and a memory. "which will be carried by the angels" gives how it comes, and the carrying by the angels is what makes the coming a sign rather than a return. "Surely in this is a sign for you" names the thing as a sign again, and the naming is for them, the ones who objected. "if you ˹truly˺ believe." is the condition at the end, and it puts the seeing of the sign on the faith of the one who sees it, so the verse closes by turning the sign back onto the believers and away from the object. The verse stands between the appointment of the king and the marching out of the army, and it is the thing that ends the argument the verse before it opened. The sign is given to the people who asked for the appointment to be justified, and it is given as a thing that will come to them rather than as an argument about the man, so the verse settles the question by putting an object in front of the council and leaving the object to speak. The two families named in it are the two whose relics are in the chest, and the naming is what ties the sign to the history of the people who are being asked to obey.

**The sign of the kingship.**

And their prophet said to them after they had demanded a sign of his kingship ‘The sign of his kingship is that there will come to you the Ark a chest containing the images of the prophets which God sent down to Adam and which was handed down to them sc. the Israelites until the Amalekites seized it from them in battle. Their prophet said to them that the mark of his being truly chosen as their king was that Allah would return to them the Ark. Their Prophet then proclaimed, "The sign of the blessings of Talut's kingship over you is that Allah will give you back the Tabut (wooden box) that has been taken from you. They then acknowledged his kingship and hastened to enlist in the holy struggle and he chose seventy thousand of their young men. (When they said to a prophet of theirs: "Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of Allah)."

**The chest of the Israelites.**

The Israelites had a sacred chest, or box, known as the Ark of the Covenant (at-tabut), which they had had in their possession from the time they left Egypt. The Bani Isra'il used to have the legacy of a wooden chest (also identified as the Ark of the Covenant). This was a chest revered by the Israelites which was taken away from them. When Allah Almighty willed the return of the chest, it so happened that the infidels were struck by some epidemic or calamity at places where they carried this chest. Goliath) overcame Bani Isra'il, he took this chest away with him. The beasts took it of their own accord to Bayt ash-Shamsh, a city of Judah. When the infidel Amalekites were made to rule over them, they began thinking about correcting the situation.

**The tranquillity in the chest.**

The tranquility of one group was in the ark, and the ark was under the determination of the Children of Israel, sometimes here and sometimes there, sometimes like this and sometimes like that. In it there was tranquillity and relics left behind by the family of Moses and Aaron, such as the staff and a few tablets. He it is who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the faithful [48:4]. The tranquility of the other group is in their hearts, in the grasp of the Real's attributes. " Whenever someone finds a drink from the cup of recognition on the carpet of the religion's good fortune, the cupbearer of that drink is the sultan of tranquility. (wherein is Sakinah from your Lord) meaning, peace (or grace) and reassurance. 'Abdur-Razzaq stated that Qatadah said: The exalted lodging place of the sultan of tranquility is the capital city of the heart:

**The relics of the family of Moses and Aaron.**

(...and a remnant of that which Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron) left behind,) It contained the Ten Commandments engraved on stone, as well as relics of Moses and Aaron. It guided them on their journey, and led them on from victory to victory. Moses and other prophets of Bani Isra'il would keep this chest in the frontline of the battlefield. Ath-Thawri said, "Some said that it contained a pot of manna and the remnants of the Tablets, while some others said that it contained (Moses') staff and two shoes (and refer to 20:12)." (...and a remnant of that which Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron) left behind,) Meaning, Moses' staff and the remnants of the Tablets. This is the same Tafsir of Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and 'Ikrimah, who added, "And also the Torah." 'Abdur-Razzaq said that he asked Ath-Thawri about the meaning of,. (And their Prophet) Samuel (said unto them: Lo! The token) the sign (of his kingdom) that it is from Allah (is that there shall come unto you the Ark) that was taken from you (wherein is peace of reassurance) mercy and tranquillity; it is also said that this means: it includes the wind (the triumph) of his victory, of golden colour in the form of a human face (from your Lord, and a remnant of that which the house of Moses) a remnant of Moses, i.e. his Scripture; as it is said: his tablets and staff (and the house of Aaron left behind) what Aaron had left behind, namely his cloak and turban, (the angels bearing it) the angels leading it.

**The angels between the earth and the sky.**

The angels bore it between the earth and the sky while they gazed at it until finally they placed it before Saul. Ibn Jurayj stated that Ibn 'Abbas said, "The angels came down while carrying the Tabut between the sky and the earth, until they placed it before Talut while the people were watching. Then, the angels took control of the bullocks and made it reach Talut's doorsteps. " As-Suddi said, "The Tabut was brought to Talut's house, so the people believed in the prophethood of Sham'un (Simeon) and obeyed Talut." They used to commence fighting invoking it before their enemy and marching behind it as well as experience peacefulness in its presence as God says therein is a Spirit of Peace reassurance for your hearts from your Lord and a remnant of what the folk of Moses and the folk of Aaron left behind which were Moses’s pair of sandals and his staff Aaron’s turban a measure qafīz of the manna that used to come down on them and the pieces of the broken tablets the angels bearing it tahmiluhu l-malā’ikatu the circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb ya’tiyakum ‘there will come to’.

**A sign for you if you believe.**

(Lo! Herein) in giving you back the Ark (shall be a token) a sign (for you) that he has been made king by Allah (if (in truth) ye are believers). In that there is a clear sign if you are true believers. But in the town where this Ark was placed, plague and pestilence broke out and the Philistines were terrified. (Talut is the Qur'anic name of the king known in the Bible as Saul) When the Bani Isra'il saw this sign, they believed in the kingdom of Talut, who then mounted an attack on Jalut while the weather was very hot. (Verily, in this is a sign for you) testifying to my truth in what I was sent with, my prophethood, and my command to you to obey Talut,. Verily, in this is a sign for you if you are indeed believers. Shiblī said, "The curtains were taken down and the veils lifted in the realities of the secret core, and many unseen things were unveiled to my secret core.

249.text:
The verse carries the story to its battle and gives the test that divides the army. "When Saul marched forth with his army, he cautioned:" is the setting, and the caution is given before the meeting with the enemy, so the verse puts the test on the road and not in the fight. "Allah will test you with a river" names the test, and the test is named as Allah's while the river is only its place, so the verse describes a trial and not a hardship. "So whoever drinks ˹his fill˺ from it is not with me" gives the first half of the rule, and the drinking of the fill is what separates the man from the army, so the act is a small one and the consequence a large one. "and whoever does not taste it—except a sip from the hollow of his hands—is definitely with me." gives the second half, and the exception in it is the sip from the hollow of the hands, so the rule is not a prohibition of drinking but a limit on it. "They all drank ˹their fill˺ except for a few!" is what happened, and the few are the same few the verse before it left standing. "When he and the ˹remaining˺ faithful with him crossed the river, they said," carries the story over the water and gives the second speech. "Now we are no match for Goliath and his warriors." is the speech of the ones who counted the enemy. "But those ˹believers˺ who were certain they would meet Allah reasoned," is the turn, and the certainty in it is about the meeting with Allah and not about the battle. "How many times has a small force vanquished a mighty army by the Will of Allah!" is their answer, and the will in it is where the victory is put. "And Allah is ˹always˺ with the steadfast." closes the verse, and the steadfastness is the quality the whole test was about.

**The test of the river.**

(Verily, Allah will try you) meaning, He will test you with a river, which flowed between Jordan and Palestine, i.e. , the Shari'ah river, according to Ibn 'Abbas and others. (Whosoever therefore drinketh thereof) from the river (he is not of me) he is not going to be with me in the fight against my enemy and will not go further, (and whoever tasteth it not he is of me) against my enemy, but then he made an exception, (save him who taketh (thereof) in the hollow of his hand) and this was enough for them, their beasts and transportation. The allusion in this verse is that God tests human beings in their association with others with this world and with the lower self. Ibn Jarir reported that Al-Bara' bin 'Azib said, "We used to say that the Companions of Muhammad who accompanied him on the battle of Badr were more than three hundred and ten, just as many as the soldiers who crossed the river with Talut. He gave the order that, while crossing the river, no one was to drink more than a handful of water from it.

**Whoever drinks his fill is not with me.**

If anyone drinks from it, he will not be on my path and must not join me in fighting. The person who does not drink from it will be on my path and will join me in the fight. Bayt al-Maqdis the heat was intense and so they asked him for water; he said ‘God will try test you in order to distinguish the obedient among you from the disobedient with a river between Jordan and Palestine whoever drinks of it of its water is not of me is not of my followers and whoever tastes it not he is of me except for him who scoops up with his hand’ ghurfa or gharfa ‘a scoop’ satisfying himself therewith and not taking more he is also of my followers. There are some whose association with these things is limited to that which is required for [them to earn a] basic livelihood and what is necessary for their salvation and security. Ibn Jurayj stated that Ibn 'Abbas commented, "Whoever took some of it (the river's water) in the hollow of his hand, quenched his thirst; as for those who drank freely from it, their thirst was not quenched." So whoever drinks thereof, he is not of me; and whoever tastes it not, he is of me, except him who takes (thereof) in the hollow of his hand.

**They all drank except for a few.**

But they drank of it when they reached it and saw that it was abundant except a few of them who restricted themselves to a scoop it is reported that one scoop was enough for each man and his horse and they numbered over three hundred; and when he crossed it with those who believed the ones who confined themselves to the one scoop they the ones that drank profusely said ‘We have no power today against Goliath and his troops’ that is no power to fight them and they were cowardly and did not cross it. (But they drank thereof) when they reached the river however they drank as much as they wanted to, (all save a few of them) 313 men who did not drink except as they had been directed. When they reached the river, all the warriors drank from its water, except a few of them who held back despite being extremely thirsty. (and whoever tastes it not, he is of me, except him who takes (thereof) in the hollow of his hand.) meaning, there is no harm in this case.

**The power against Goliath and his hosts.**

(We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts. But those who knew) and were convinced (that they would meet Allah) in person after they died (exclaimed: How many a little company) of believers (hath overcome a mighty host) of unbelievers (by Allah's leave!) by the help of Allah. However, God was with them and they emerged victorious under the leadership of Saul. There are others who go beyond the limit of what is required and extend their association with things of the world self and creation for the sake of carnal desire and their own preference. Therefore, a delegation met him and said to him, ‘Now that you have aged, you should appoint a king from amongst us, in order that we may wage war against our enemies under the command of our leader.

**A small force and a mighty army.**

Those who thought with certainty that they would meet God at the Resurrection and these were the ones that crossed it said ‘How often kam ‘how’ functions as a predicate meaning kathīr ‘many’ a little company group of men has overcome a numerous one by God’s leave by His will; and God is with the patient’ providing them with help and assistance. The perfect who fully succeeded in their trial but did feel concerned about how low they were in numbers. (And when Saul set out) went forth (with the army) through a wasteland and became very thirsty, they asked him to provide them with water, i.e. After a period of time the Israelites wished to take some action against the Philistines, so that they might recover their lands from them. ("How often has a small group overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave?" And Allah is with As-Sabirin (the patient).)

**Allah is with the steadfast.**

His army was of eighty thousand then, according to As-Suddi, but Allah knows best. The wisdom behind this test, as perceived by this humble commentator, appears to be as follows. Not difficult to imagine is the excitement created on such occasions but there are not many who would stay firm in their hour of trial. When they were given the Ark back, they accepted him as their king and went out with him to fight. Those that were convinced that they would meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection said to them, ‘So many believing groups small in number have defeated a disbelieving group large in number with Allah’s permission and assistance. So, their knowledgeable scholars strengthened their resolve by stating that Allah's promise is true and that triumph comes from Allah Alone, not from the large numbers or the adequacy of the supplies. So, being patient, when water is made available without asking in a state of intense thirst, is a proof of steadfastness, and dashing for water is a proof of its absence. Allah states that Talut, the king of the Children of Israel, marched forth with his soldiers and the Israelites who obeyed him.

250.text:
The verse closes the story of Talut by putting one prayer in the mouths of the men who came out to fight. "When they advanced to face Goliath and his warriors, they prayed, Our Lord" is the whole scene in a single clause, and the order of it is the point, since they move first and then speak, and what they ask for is not the death of Goliath but what they themselves have to become before the day is decided. "Shower us with perseverance" is the first request, and the wording is of something poured out on them, a patience given rather than summoned, an endurance held as an honour in the middle of the struggle. "make our steps firm" is the second, and it is about the footing of men in a battle line, the feet of those who are expected to stand when every part of them wants to turn and run, so the request is for the hearts to be steadied before the ground is held. "and give us victory over the disbelieving people" is the third, and it names the outcome that numbers cannot reach, and the wording leaves the decision with the one who is asked. The three requests therefore run from inside a person to the ground under their feet and then to the result of the whole affair, and the verse stops there without an answer. The next verse takes the answer, the routing, the killing of Goliath, and the rule about how one set of people is checked by another, which is why the prayer stands here as a request for firmness on the day rather than a claim about the outcome of it.

**Patience and firmness are asked for first.**

So when they went forth against Goliath and his troops facing them in military columns they said ‘Our Lord pour out upon us patience and make firm our feet by strengthening our hearts for this struggle and grant us victory over the disbelieving folk!’ Our Lord, grant us patience in our hearts, make our feet firm so that we do not flee or lose courage before our enemies, and give us Your assistance and support against the disbelieving people. First they sought firmness and patience for the sake of the sufferings they had previously endured and then they said and grant us victory over the disbelieving folk! The most important of their concerns was patience and standing up to the enemy and only after that [were they concerned for] help for themselves.

**What a victory in such an encounter needs.**

What is essential to gain a victory in any such encounter is that the participants must have the capacity to persevere, whatever the odds, and must obey their leader. (And when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts they) those who believed (said: Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance) honour us by bestowing patience on us, (make our foothold sure) in war, (and give us victory against the disbelieving folk) Goliath and his people. When the faithful party, who were few under the command of Talut, faced their enemy, who were many under the command of Jalut,. Not difficult to imagine is the excitement created on such occasions but there are not many who would stay firm in their hour of trial. The perfect who fully succeeded in their trial but did feel concerned about how low they were in numbers. So, being patient, when water is made available without asking in a state of intense thirst, is a proof of steadfastness, and dashing for water is a proof of its absence.

**How one set of people is checked by another.**

And if Allah did not check one set of people by means of another, the earth would indeed be full of mischief. This Ayah indicates that if it were not for the fact that Allah checks one set of people with another, such as when Talut and the bravery of Dawud helped the Children of Israel (against Goliath), then people would have perished. (For had it not been that Allah checks one set of people by means of another, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and Masjids, wherein the Name of Allah is mentioned much, would surely, have been pulled down.)(22:40)

**The help they sought and the enemy they named.**

So when they went forth against Goliath and his troops [the hosts of Saul] exonerated themselves of all power and strength and turned to God seek ing His succor asking for His aid and trusting in His help. Moreover [the hosts of Saul] indicated that they were seeking help against [the enemy] not out of revenge for what had been taken from them but because they [the enemy] were disbelievers enemies of God. They stepped forward to assert His right and to succeed for His sake and then to find their worldly portion from [His] help. That was why they were all the more terrified at the sight of the apparently strong army of their enemies.

**What was done to Goliath afterwards.**

Israelite accounts claimed that (Prophet) David killed Goliath with a slingshot that he had, which he launched at Goliath causing his death. So they routed them by Allah's leave and Dawud (David) killed Jalut (Goliath), and Allah gave him (Dawud) the kingdom [ after the death of Talut and Samuel] and Al-Hikmah (prophethood), and taught him of that which He willed.

**The recital, and what it conforms to.**

But Allah is full of bounty to the 'Alamin (mankind, Jinn and all that exists)These are the verses of Allah, We recite them to you (O Muhammad) in truth, and surely, you are one of the Messengers (of Allah) This Ayah states, 'These Ayat (verses) of Allah that We have narrated for you in truth conform to the exact manner that these stories have occurred and to the truth that still remain in the (Divine) Books that the scholars of the Children of Israel have and know. Now the events and sayings mentioned in this story tell us that there were three kinds of people among them: In the words of the Bible, ‘Then all this assembly shall know that the Lord does not save with sword and spear, for the battle is the Lord’s and He will give you into our hands’ (1 Samuel, 17:47).

251.text:
The previous verse was a prayer asked before the battle, and this one is the answer to it, given in five short clauses and then widened into a rule. "So they defeated them by Allah’s Will" is the first clause, and the wording places the routing inside a will that is not theirs, so the victory they asked for is described as something that came to them rather than something they produced. "and David killed Goliath" gives the man and the killing in four words, and the brevity belongs to the verse, since the fight with the champion of the enemy is not told as a feat of strength. "And Allah blessed David with kingship and wisdom and taught him what He willed" then gives what came out of the day, a kingship, a wisdom, and a teaching whose content is left open because the giving is the point. "Had Allah not repelled a group of people by the might of another" changes the size of the question, and it states a rule about how the world is held, which is also an answer to the prayer, since repelling covers what is done to an army and what is done to the feet that stand. "corruption would have dominated the earth" is the consequence being turned away, and the word for it is the same one used for what is done to a people and to the places where God is remembered. "but Allah is Gracious to all" closes the verse with a description of what God is to all creation rather than with the fighting, and the verse after this turns from the battle to the recital.

**The day they were routed, and the men who were put on trial.**

And they routed they broke them by the leave of God by His will and David who was among the ranks of Saul’s army slew Goliath; and God gave him David the kingship over the Children of Israel and Wisdom prophethood after the death of Samuel and Saul and the combination of kingship and prophethood had never come to anyone before him; and He taught him such as He willed of the manufacture of mail-coats and the speech of birds. And they routed them by the leave of God so that nothing not even a trace remained of them. (So they routed them by Allah's leave) meaning, they defeated and overwhelmed them by Allah's aid and support. When the faithful party, who were few under the command of Talut, faced their enemy, who were many under the command of Jalut,. Not difficult to imagine is the excitement created on such occasions but there are not many who would stay firm in their hour of trial. The perfect who fully succeeded in their trial but did feel concerned about how low they were in numbers. Pour forth on us patience, and set firm our feet and make us victorious over the disbelieving people. (they invoked: "Our Lord! Pour forth on us patience...") meaning, send down patience on us from You. (and set firm our feet) meaning, against the enemy and save us from running away and from feebleness,.

**The kingship and the wisdom given to David.**

(So they routed them by Allah's leave) by Allah's help (and David) the Prophet (slew Goliath) the unbeliever; (and Allah gave him the kingdom) Allah gave David sovereignty over the Children of Israel (and wisdom) understanding and prophethood, (and taught him of that which He willeth) i.e. how to make armour. So they routed them by Allah's leave and Dawud (David) killed Jalut (Goliath), and Allah gave him (Dawud) the kingdom [ after the death of Talut and Samuel] and Al-Hikmah (prophethood), and taught him of that which He willed. (and taught him of that which He willed.) meaning, what He willed of the knowledge that He bestowed on (Prophet) Dawud. The prophet of God, David, killed their leader Goliath and God gave him kingship and prophethood and taught him many sciences as He willed, including those that are beneficial for this world and those for the hearafter. Talut promised that whoever killed Jalut, would marry his daughter and would share his kingship and authority. Later, the kingship was transferred to Prophet Dawud in addition to being granted Prophethood by Allah. (...and Allah gave him (Dawud) the kingdom) that Talut had and,. (and Al-Hikmah) that comes with the prophethood, meaning, after Shamwil. [Allah then said:].

**How people are repelled from one another.**

Had God not repelled people some ba‘dahum ‘some’ substitutes for saying ba‘dan min al-nās ‘some people’ by means of others the earth would have surely been corrupted with idolaters defeating and slaying Muslims and mosques being destroyed; but God is bounteous to all worlds by repelling some by means of others. (And if Allah had not repelled some men by others) as He repelled through David the evil of Goliath from the Children of Israel (the earth would have been corrupted). If it were not the system of God to drive back the evil of some people by means of others, there would be corruption on earth as the evil ones would gain authority. Allah repelled from the believers, by means of the prophets, the evil of their enemies, and He repelled from those who refrained from participating in the fight for Allah's sake, by means of those who fought in His sake, the evil of their enemies. If it were not thus, the earth would have been corrupted.

**When one set of people is not checked.**

(And if Allah did not check one set of people by means of another, the earth would indeed be full of mischief.) This Ayah indicates that if it were not for the fact that Allah checks one set of people with another, such as when Talut and the bravery of Dawud helped the Children of Israel (against Goliath), then people would have perished. (For had it not been that Allah checks one set of people by means of another, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and Masjids, wherein the Name of Allah is mentioned much, would surely, have been pulled down.)(22:40) Now the events and sayings mentioned in this story tell us that there were three kinds of people among them:

**How the victory was brought about, and what a slingshot was.**

But at the time of the fighting He brought the victory about through the hands of David. Because of Goliath's bulk and size David's victory over him was unimaginable but as the one who spoke for them said: He had no weapon with him but a slingshot; the victory was his because the help of God was with him. Israelite accounts claimed that (Prophet) David killed Goliath with a slingshot that he had, which he launched at Goliath causing his death. As the story goes [David] was of middling stature not large in body a compact person. He met me with his sword drawn and said to me One of us is gone.

**Kindness to all the worlds, and the victory of the strong.**

But Allah is full of bounty to the 'Alamin (mankind, Jinn and all that exists)These are the verses of Allah, We recite them to you (O Muhammad) in truth, and surely, you are one of the Messengers (of Allah) (But Allah is full of bounty to the 'Alamin (mankind, Jinn and all that exists) meaning, by His mercy and favor He fixes some of them by some others. Surely, Allah has the wisdom, the supreme authority and the clear proof against His creation in all of His actions and statements. Had God not repelled people some by means of others the earth would have surely been corrupted; but God is bounteous to all worlds. If mankind were to make common cause and agree with one another alto gether the weak would be destroyed by the victory of the strong. (But Allah is a Lord of Kindness to all the worlds) by this repelling. However, God is Bountiful to all of His creation.

252.text:
The account of Talut and David has just closed, and this verse turns from what was recited to the one reciting it. "These are Allah’s revelations which We recite to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth" takes the verses of the battle and names them, so the account of the past is offered not as history but as something sent down and then read out, and the words in truth say what the reading is for, since the events have been told as they happened and as they still stand. "And you are truly one of the messengers" is the second half, and the order of the two halves is the argument, because the claim about the messenger is drawn from the claim about the revelation, and the emphasis in the clause stands where it does because the denial fell on that claim and not on the story. The verse therefore ends the section that began with Talut and lays the ground for the verse after it, which ranks the messengers above one another, and the wording one of the messengers is what that next verse takes up.

**The verses recited in truth.**

These verses are the verses of God We recite to you O Muhammad as narration in truth and assuredly you are one of the Messengers of God the emphasis is made here with the particle inna of innaka ‘surely you are’ with the remainder of the statement being a rebuttal of the disbelievers’ saying ‘You are no Messenger’. (These are the revelations of Allah) i.e. the Qur'an which relates the events of past nations (which We recite unto thee (Muhammad) which We send Gabriel with to you (with Truth) to exposit the Truth and falsehood, (and lo! thou art of the number of messengers) to all human beings and jinn;. It is being said here that these verses in which this event has been mentioned 'are the verses of Allah that We recite to you with all veracity' and this proves that you are certainly among the Messengers.'. Those are the clear verses of Allah which are recited to you, O Prophet, and they contain true stories and just laws.

**The prophethood asserted, and the kingdom given to David.**

Since the affirmation of the prophethood of the noble Messenger of Allah is also a major objective of the Holy Qur'an, it has been so asserted as and when the occasion warrants. That he is correctly reporting the event (in verses 246-251), while he neither learnt it from someone nor heard it anywhere nor saw it, is a miracle which is a sound proof of his prophethood. So they routed them by Allah's leave and Dawud (David) killed Jalut (Goliath), and Allah gave him (Dawud) the kingdom [ after the death of Talut and Samuel] and Al-Hikmah (prophethood), and taught him of that which He willed. But Allah is full of bounty to the 'Alamin (mankind, Jinn and all that exists)These are the verses of Allah, We recite them to you (O Muhammad) in truth, and surely, you are one of the Messengers (of Allah)

**What the scholars know, and what was not devised.**

This Ayah states, 'These Ayat (verses) of Allah that We have narrated for you in truth conform to the exact manner that these stories have occurred and to the truth that still remain in the (Divine) Books that the scholars of the Children of Israel have and know. You did not have knowledge [O Muḥammad] regarding these long ago beings from the past nor was this something you devised. Rather you came to know of them through information given by God .

**How one set of people is checked, and the mercy behind it.**

This Ayah indicates that if it were not for the fact that Allah checks one set of people with another, such as when Talut and the bravery of Dawud helped the Children of Israel (against Goliath), then people would have perished. (For had it not been that Allah checks one set of people by means of another, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and Masjids, wherein the Name of Allah is mentioned much, would surely, have been pulled down.)(22:40) (And if Allah did not check one set of people by means of another, the earth would indeed be full of mischief.) (But Allah is full of bounty to the 'Alamin (mankind, Jinn and all that exists) meaning, by His mercy and favor He fixes some of them by some others.

253.text:
The verse ranks the messengers, and it does so in two halves, since the gifts are listed first and the fighting among their communities then answers them. "We have chosen some of those messengers above others" opens with a choosing, and the wording leaves the reason inside the act, so the difference is given and not earned. "Allah spoke directly to some" is the first gift, and the directness of it is the point, since a speaking with nothing between the two is what the phrase carries. "and raised some high in rank. To Jesus" names the second gift and moves at once to a third, so the rank is a height within one message, and the name arrives before anything is told about him. "son of Mary" stands with the name, because the proof is given to a man whose mother is known. "We gave clear proofs and supported him with the holy spirit" then gives two more, a proof that makes the case and a support that keeps the one it is given to standing. "If Allah had willed" changes the subject from the gifted to the people after them, and "succeeding generations would not have fought among themselves after receiving the clear proofs" states what another will would have produced, proofs arriving and no fighting after them. "But they differed" is the fact against that supposition, and "some believed while others disbelieved" divides them. "Yet if Allah had willed" repeats the clause and "they would not have fought one another" repeats the consequence without the proofs, so the repetition is where the emphasis sits. "But Allah does what He wills" ends on the will itself, which is where both halves meet.

**Whom God spoke to, and whom He raised in rank.**

Those tilka is the subject messengers al-rusul is either an adjective or the predicate some We have preferred above others by assigning a particular trait to one not found in the other; some there are to whom God spoke such as Moses and some He raised in rank namely Muhammad on account of his call being to all peoples his being the Seal of the Prophets on account of the superiority of his community to all others the sundry miracles and the many special qualities. (Of those messengers) whom We have named for you, (some of whom We have caused to excel others) by bestowing honour upon them, (and of whom there are some unto whom Allah spake) this is Moses, (while some of them He exalted (above others) in degrees) this is Abraham whom Allah took as a friend, and Enoch whom Allah raised to an elevated place; (and We gave Jesus son of Mary clear proofs) commands, prohibitions and the working of marvels (and We supported him) strengthened and assisted him (with the holy Spirit) with Gabriel, the pure. Some of them Allah spoke to, such as Moses, and others He granted a high rank, such as Muhammad ﷺ – who was sent to the entire humankind as the last of the prophets and whose nation was preferred over all other communities. (Those Messengers! We preferred some of them to others; to some of them Allah spoke (directly) meaning, Musa and Muhammad , and also Adam according to a Hadith recorded in Sahih Ibn Hibban from Abu Dharr.

**Higher status, the hadith about superiority, and the comfort the verse gives.**

Since the words ‌ (Those are the Messengers some of whom We have given excellence over others) in this verse clearly indicate that some prophets are given higher status than others, we have a difficulty on our hands when we compare this with a hadith, where the Holy Prophet has said: This is because a prophet's having higher status means that he has a high station in the sight of Allah. Obviously, this knowledge cannot be acquired through conjectures and surmises but should such a proof come from the Qur'an and Sunnah, establishing the precedence of some prophets over some others, then it will be necessary to believe in it. (Don't give me superiority above the Prophets, for the people will become unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to be resurrected to see Musa holding on to the pillar of Allah's Throne. I will not know whether the unconsciousness Musa suffered on the Day of the Trumpet sufficed for him, or if he got up before me. So, do not give me superiority above the Prophets.) In another narration, the Prophet said, (Do not give superiority to some Prophets above others.) In Verse 253, beginning with ‌ ('those are the Messenger’), the purpose is to give solace and comfort to the noble Prophet since the deniers refused to recognize his prophethood, inspite of the fact that it was conclusively proved, as has been stated in the verse 252: ‌ (And certainly you are among the Messengers.) as well.

**The clear proofs and the support given to Jesus.**

Allah gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear miracles confirming his prophethood, such as bringing the dead to life and curing the leper and the blind; and supported him with the angel Gabriel to give him strength in fulfilling Allah’s instruction. (And We gave 'Isa, the son of Maryam, clear signs) refers to the proofs and unequivocal evidences that testify to the truth that 'Isa delivered to the Children of Israel, thus testifying that he was Allah's servant and His Messenger to them.

**Why the generations fought after the proofs came.**

And had God willed that all people be guided those who came after them after the messengers that is their communities would not have fought against one another after the clear proofs had come to them because of their disagreement and their leading one another astray; but they fell into variance as He willed and some of them believed and adhered firmly to his faith and some disbelieved as the Christians did after Jesus al-Masīh and had God willed they would not have fought against one another repeated here for emphasis but God does whatever He desires giving success to whomever He will and disappointment to whomever He will. And had God willed those who came after them would not have fought against one another after the clear proofs had come to them; but they fell into variance and some of them believed and some disbelieved and had God willed they would not have fought against one another but God does whatever He desires. (And if Allah had so willed it, those who followed after them) after Moses and Jesus (would not have fought one with another) differed with one another (after clear proofs had come unto them) the exposition in their Scriptures of the description and traits of Muhammad. If Allah had willed, succeeding generations would not have fought against each other, after clear Verses of Allah had come to them, but they differed some of them believed and others disbelieved. (And if Allah had so willed it, they would not have fought one with another) they would not have differed with one another in the matter of the religion; (but Allah doeth what He will) with His servants.

**Some believed and some disbelieved, and what differing in religion means.**

(If Allah had willed, succeeding generations would not have fought against each other, after clear Verses of Allah had come to them, but they differed some of them believed and others disbelieved. If Allah had willed, they would not have fought against one another.) meaning all this happened by Allah's decree, and this is why He said next,. (But they differed) in the matter of Religion, (some of them believing) in every Scripture and Messenger (and some disbelieving) in the Scriptures and messengers.

**Declining communities and earlier saints.**

They have been treated with total irreverence, as creatures of no account whatsoever, for the simple reason that their contemporaries believed themselves to be successors of earlier saints and thus were in no need of further religious counselling, particularly by someone who appeared to be inferior to their own predecessors. When communities begin to go into a decline, they become preoccupied with wordly interests, yet they do not wish to forfeit their ‘right’ to salvation, and as a form of psychological defence, attach themselves mentally to hallowed religious personalities. Those who have come to reform and revitalize the Muslim community since the passing of the Final Prophet have fared no better. They felt that none could surpass the prophet they believed in.

255.text:
The verse is built as a list of descriptions, and the guidance is in following each one in order. "Allah! There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining" opens with the name and then with a denial and an exception, so what is negated comes before what is affirmed, and the two names that follow carry the rest of the verse between them, a living that has no beginning and a sustaining that keeps what is sustained in being. "Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him" is the first clause of negation after the names, and the wording is of what does not seize or overtake Him, so the least of what weakens a creature is refused of God, and the point of the pair is that the smaller term and the larger one are both excluded. "To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" is the claim of ownership stated twice, once for each of the two creations, and the letter at the beginning of the clause carries the sense of ownership, so what is owned is described as a possession that includes creatures and servants. "Who could possibly intercede with Him without His permission" is put as a question, and it settles the case of those who expect to speak on behalf of someone else, since the asking and the permission are two different things. "He fully knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them" then covers the whole of what can be past or future for them, and "but no one can grasp any of His knowledge" sets the limit on the other side, so the knowledge is complete in one direction and only given in the other, and "except what He wills to reveal" is the opening in that closed door. "His Seat encompasses the heavens and the earth" is the image of extent, and "and the preservation of both does not tire Him" closes the description with the ease of what would be a burden, so the verse ends where the first two names began, and "For He is the Most High, the Greatest" gives the reason for the whole list.

**The Ever-Living, the Self-Standing and the whole universe.**

God there is no god that is there is none worthy of being worshipped in all existence except Him the Living the Everlasting the Eternal Sustainer the One constantly engaged in the management of His creation. God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Standing. This verse describes the Oneness of Allah's being and attributes in a unique manner – He s living, He hears and sees, He speaks, He is self-existent, He is eternal and everlasing, He is the innovator and creator of the entire universe, He is above changes and effects, He is the Master of the whole universe, He is so exalted in His majesty tht no one can speak before Him without His permission; He is the wielder of such absolute power that the tremendous function of creating the universe, sustaining it and making it work steadily, does not cause him to tire or relax. They mean: 'one who himself stands firmly and keeps others sustained and supported, all simultaneously.' Qayyum is an attribute of Allah Almighty with which no created being can be associated, for what depends on others for its own existence and survival can hardly be expected to support something else. When the word, Qayyum, appearing in the previous sentence; told man that Allah is holding in perfect working unison the whole universe, which includes in itself, all skies and earths and all there is in them -- one could stray on to the idea, naturally so, in view of man's instinctive inquisitiveness, that the sacred 'Being' doing such a stupendous task must, at some time, feel tired, and need due moments of rest and sleep.

**Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.**

Drowsiness or sleep does not come upon Him due to the perfection of His life and existence. The third sentence is 'Neither doze overtakes Him nor sleep.' The word (: sinatun) denotes drowsiness which is the preliminary effect of coming sleep, while the word, : nawm refers to full sleep. Slumber does not seize Him neither sleep; to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants; who is there that is to say none is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave? in this for him.

**What belongs to Him, and who may intercede.**

To Him belong whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. (Who is he that intercedeth with Him) from amongst the dwellers of the heavens and the earth on the Day of Judgement (save by His leave?) except by His command? This too has now been made clear that no mortal could even dare breath in the most exalted Presence of Allah Almighty; but there are servants of Allah Almighty who have received the favour of His approval and acceptance and who would be specially allowed to speak and intercede. They are never serious in matters of religion, and as a result believe that intercession by certain religious seers or the performance of certain rituals, or the observance of certain forms is enough to earn salvation in the Hereafter.

**The knowledge that is before them and behind them.**

He knows what lies before them that is creation and what is after them of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter; and they encompass nothing of His knowledge that is they know nothing of what He knows save such as He wills to inform of it by way of His messengers. (He knoweth that which is in front of them) in front of the angels regarding the matter of the Hereafter and who is to intercede (and that which is behind them) of the life of this world, (while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save that He will). Allah says: the angels know nothing of the Hereafter or of the life of this world save that which Allah has taught them. The sixth sentence is: : 'He.knows what is before them and what is behind them.' It means that Allah Almighty is aware of all the states and events surrounding them. 'Before' and 'after' may also mean that Allah Almighty is aware of all states and events before their birth and after their birth. The seventh sentence is :'And they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills.' It means that man and the rest of the created beings cannot cover even a part of Allah's infinite knowledge except a certain part which Allah Almighty Himself allows to be given out of His knowledge. He knows what has happened in the past and what will happen in the future. The creation has no share in His knowledge unless He wills to grant them some of it.

**The Seat that encompasses the heavens and the earth.**

His throne subsumes the heavens and the earth it is said that His knowledge encompasses them both; it is also said that the kursī ‘throne’ itself subsumes them on account of its vastness as in the hadīth ‘The seven heavens compared to the kursī are like seven silver coins lying in a metal shield of armour’; the preserving of them the heavens and the earth wearies Him not does not burden Him; He is the Sublime above His creation by virtue of His subjugation of them the Tremendous the Great. The eighth sentence is: ‌ ‌ :'His Kursi extends to the Heavens and to the Earth.' It means that His Kursi (translated as chair or base of power) is so magnified that its spatial infinity houses, within itself, the seven heavens and the earth. However, there are authentic narrations in ahadith which simply tell us that Arsh (translated as 'throne', being a seat of authority) and Kursi (chair) are heavenly bodies many times larger than the heavens and the earth. His Throne covers the vastness of the heavens and the earth.

**What the tremendous verse carries, and how such texts are treated.**

This is Ayat Al-Kursi and tremendous virtues have been associated with it, for the authentic Hadith describes it as 'the greatest Ayah in the Book of Allah.' Imam Ahmad recorded that 'Ubayy bin Ka'b said that the Prophet asked him about the greatest Ayah in the Book of Allah, and 'Ubayy answered, "Allah and His Messenger know better. These and similar Ayat and authentic Hadiths about Allah's Attributes must be treated the way the Salaf (righteous ancestors) treated them by accepting their apparent meanings without equating them [with the attributes of the creation] or altering their apparent meanings. His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth, and He is the High, the Tremendous. (Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists)[2:255] in Āl-'Imrān, it is in,. (Alif-Lam-Mim. Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists)[3:1-2] while in Ta-Ha, it is in,. (Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists)[2:255] and,. The ninth sentence is: :'And it does not weary Him to look after them.' It means that supporting the two magnificent creations of the heavens and the earth is not the least burdensome for Allah Almighty since doing so, with the perfect power of the Absolute Master, is easy.

256.text:
The verse comes straight after the two verses about the battle with Goliath and about how God repels some people by others, and it states a rule about how belief is not entered by force. "Let there be no compulsion in religion" is the demand, and the wording is general, so it is not a permission to ignore the religion but a denial that anyone can be driven into it, and the strength of the clause is that it comes as a prohibition on an act rather than as a description of a fact. "for the truth stands out clearly from falsehood" gives the reason, and the sense of it is that the case has already been made plain, so coercion would add nothing to what is already visible, the way a road that is lit needs no one pushed along it. "So whoever renounces false gods and believes in Allah has certainly grasped the firmest, unfailing hand-hold" is one run of wording, and the two halves of faith come first in it, a turning away and a turning to, with the reward named as a grip on a support that is firm and does not give way, so the person is not described as strong in himself but as the one who has done these two things, and the two adjectives carry the whole argument of the image, the firmest in what it is and unfailing in how long it lasts. "And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" closes the verse with the two attributes that answer the situation, since a hearing God takes note of what a person gives voice to under compulsion and a knowing God takes note of what the heart did not. The verse before it was about a fight, and this verse limits what a fight can do to a belief, which is the connection the commentators draw between the two.

**No compulsion in religion, and what the words reach.**

(There is no compulsion in religion), meaning, "Do not force anyone to become Muslim, for Islam is plain and clear, and its proofs and evidence are plain and clear. (There is no compulsion in religion) no one from among the people of the Book and the Magians should be coerced to believe in the divine Oneness of Allah after the Arabs' embrace of Islam. No one is forced to enter the religion of Islam, as it is clearly the true religion and there is no need to force anyone to believe in it.

**Rectitude made clear from error, and why the heart is not coerced.**

Rectitude has become clear from error that is say through clear proofs it has become manifest that faith is rectitude and disbelief is error this was revealed concerning the Ansār of Medina who tried to compel their sons to enter into Islam; so whoever disbelieves in the false deity namely Satan or idols tāghūt ‘false deity’ is used in a singular and plural sense and believes in God has laid hold of the most firm handle the tight knot unbreaking that cannot be severed; God is Hearing of what is said Knowing of what is done. Really and truly, coercion and compulsion to make one accept a faith are not possible at all because faith is not related to outward physical response; it relates to the heart. Coercion and compulsion affect nothing but the outsides of physique and this is all that is affected by jihad and qital (fighting in the way of Allah). Anyone who realizes the truth of it inwardly and holds to it outwardly will win in the two abodes and will be happy in both worlds.

**What the Helpers would not give up, and the children they raised.**

The Helpers said: 'We will not leave our children!' Upon which Allah, exalted is He, revealed (There is no compulsion in religion. The right direction is henceforth distinct from error) . This verse was revealed about a man of the Helpers who had a black boy called Subayh whom he used to coerce to become Muslim . When Banu An-Nadir (the Jewish tribe) were evacuated [from Al-Madīnah], some of the children of the Ansar were being raised among them, and the Ansar said, 'We will not abandon our children.' Allah revealed,. Ibn Jarir recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said [that before Islam], "When (an Ansar) woman would not bear children who would live, she would vow that if she gives birth to a child who remains alive, she would raise him as a Jew. The women of the Helpers whose boys always died in infancy used to vow to bring up their boys as Jews if they were to live.

**What jihad and qital are not for, and what jizyah protects.**

They say this verse tells us that there is no compulsion in faith, although the teaching of jihad and qital (fighting) in Islam appears contrary to this principle. Looking at this a little carefully, we can find out that the objection is not valid, since the teaching of jihad and qital in Islam is not to coerce people into accepting Faith. Had it been so, why would there be Islamic injunctions of jizyah to provide an umbrella of security for kuffar (disbelievers) which protects their life, property and honour? Islam has firmly banned the killing of women, children, the aged and the crippled etc., even in the heat of jihad on the battlefield, since they are incapable of creating disorder. Similarly, it has stopped the killing of those who become law-abiding citizens by promising to pay jizyah (compensatory dues paid by free non-Muslims under Muslim rule against guarantee of the security of their life, property and honour). It is for this reason that Allah Almighty has ordained that the fasad created by these people should be removed by and qital .

**The handhold that does not break.**

Whoever rejects all those things that are worshipped besides Allah and frees himself from them, and has faith in Allah alone, has held on to the strongest rope for salvation on the Day of Resurrection and which will never break. As there is no danger of such a rope breaking apart and causing a fall, so there is no danger of destruction or loss in Islam -- should somebody just abandon the rope, that would be an entirely different matter. It was for this reason that such a person was likened to one who holds on firmly to the 'ring', the looped support of a strong rope, and thus manages to avoid falling down. (then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break) means, "He will have hold of the true religion with the strongest grasp. " Allah equated this adherence to the firm handhold that never breaks because it is built solid and because its handle is firmly connected. (And he who rejecteth false deities) the command of the devil and the worship of idols (and believeth in Allah) and in what has come forth from Him (hath grasped a firm handhold) has taken in trust �there is no God save Allah� (which will never break) will never cease, vanish or perish; it is also said that this means: for him who believes in it, the bliss of Paradise will never cease and he will never be taken out of Paradise, nor will he perish by staying in the Fire.

**Taghut, and the pole and the handle in the dream.**

(Whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah, then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break. And Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower) is in reference to, "Whoever shuns the rivals of Allah, the idols, and those that Shaytan calls to be worshipped besides Allah, whoever believes in Allah's Oneness, worships Him alone and testifies that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, then. Man's honor resides with his religion and his status is based upon his character, even if he was Persian or Nabatian." 'Umar's statement that Taghut is Shaytan is very sound, for this meaning includes every type of evil that the ignorant people of Jahiliyyah (pre Islamic era of ignorace) fell into, such as worshipping idols, referring to them for judgement, and invoking them for victory. I saw that I was in a green garden,' and he described the garden's plants and spaciousness, 'and there was an iron pole in the middle of the garden affixed in the earth and its tip reached the sky. I said, 'I cannot.' Then a helper came and raised my robe from behind and said to me, 'Ascend.' I ascended until I grasped the handle and he said to me, 'Hold on to the handle.' I awoke from that dream with the handle in my hand. (As for the garden, it represents Islam; as for the pole, it represents the pillar of Islam; and the handle represents the most trustworthy handhold. You shall remain Muslim until you die.)

258.text:
The verse tells of a debate, and it arranges the debate so that the reader watches one argument fail and a second one end it. "Are you O Prophet not aware of the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because Allah had granted him kingship" opens with the man unnamed and with his reason for speaking given in the same clause, since the kingship that was granted to him is what made him think he could dispute about the one who granted it. "Remember when Abraham said" then moves to the words themselves, and the request is to attend to what was claimed. "My Lord is the One Who has power to give life and cause death, He argued" puts the claim of the Lord first as a matter of power over life and death, and the answer "I too have the power to give life and cause death" is the same words turned into a boast, which is where the exchange splits, because Abraham was describing what his Lord does and the king was describing what he himself can arrange to happen. "Abraham challenged him" introduces the second demand, and it is put as a challenge rather than as a description. "Allah causes the sun to rise from the east" states what everyone sees daily, and "So make it rise from the west" asks for the one thing that would settle the case, so the movement is from a claim about the unseen to a demand on the sky. "And so the disbeliever was dumbstruck" is the end of the argument, stated in four words without any reply being given, and "And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people" closes the verse with the reason a man of that kind was left where his argument broke, so the verse that began with a granted kingship ends with guidance withheld.

**Who Nimrod was, and what the kingship gave him.**

The verse refers to Namrud the emperor of Babylon, who denied the very existence of God and had a debate with Sayyidna Ibrahim on this issue. The king who disputed with Ibrahim was King Nimrod, son of Canaan, son of Kush, son of Sam, son of Noah, as Mujahid stated. It was also said that he was Nimrod, son of Falikh, son of 'Abir, son of Shalikh, son of Arfakhshand, son of Sam, son of Noah. Have you not seen him who disputed with Abraham concerning his Lord because of the fact that God had given him the kingship? that is his arrogance towards this very grace of God this was Nimrod Nimrūd. It is in this context that the Holy Qur'an says: 'the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship." (Bethink thee) have you not been informed (of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord) about the Religion of his Lord, (because Allah had given him the kingdom) he is Nimrod Ibn Canaan; (how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death) gives life upon the resurrection and causes death by ending the life of this world, (he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said) give me proof of what you say. As-Suddi stated that the debate between Ibrahim and Nimrod occurred after Ibrahim was thrown in the fire, for Ibrahim did not meet the king before that day.

**The claim to give life and cause death, and the answer.**

When idh is a substitution for hājja ‘disputed’ Abraham in response to the other’s question ‘Who is this Lord of yours to whom you are calling us?’ said ‘My Lord is He who gives life and makes to die’ the One that creates life and death in bodies; he Nimrod said ‘I give life by sparing and make to die’ by killing. Abraham explained to him the attributes of his Lord by saying, ‘My Lord is the One Who gives life to the creation and causes them to die’. " The foolish king did not understand the real nature of 'giving life' and 'bringing death.' Therefore, he argued that he, too, can kill anyone through his order and bring thereby death to him and can also let off a person sentenced to death and give thereby life to him. Qatadah, Muhammad bin Ishaq and As-Suddi said that he meant, "Two men who deserved execution were to be brought before me, and I would command that one of them be killed, and he would be killed. " However, it appears that since Nimrod did not deny the existence of a Creator, his statement did not mean what Qatadah said it meant. So Nimrod brought two prisoners, killed one and spared the other and then said: this is my proof.

**Why the argument was changed and a second one brought forward.**

The Real relates that Abraham moved from one sound proof with the accursed enemy to another which was clearer not because there was anything wrong with the [first] proof but because of the shortcomings in the understanding of the disbeliever. When Sayyidna Ibrahim felt that his addressee is unable to understand the real nature of 'giving life' and 'bringing death,' he switched over to another argument and said, "Allah brings the sun out from the East, now, you bring it out from the West. The meaning that we provided is better than the meaning that some philosophers offered, claiming that Ibrahim used the second argument because it was clearer than the first one. So, instead of persisting with this point, he changed the subject and chose another example, one with which Nimrod would not be able to argue.

**The sun from the east, and what the demand proves.**

Abraham then put forward another stronger argument by saying to him, ‘The Lord I worship is the One Who brings the sun from the direction of the east; so, you should bring it from the direction of west! The reason is that as soon as he heard the argument, he came to the conclusion that (he himself or anybody else cannot bring out the sun from the East or the West and) it is surely a divine function which proves the existence of God. And once it is proved that it is God who brings the sun out from the East, it necessarily follows from it that He has the power to bring it out from the West also. This only proves the existence of the Creator, Who does what He wills, for these things could not have occurred on their own without a Creator who created them, and He is the Lord that I call to for worship, Alone without a partner." When Abraham realised that this man was a fool Abraham resorting to a more sophisticated argument said ‘God brings the sun from the east; so bring you it from the west.

**Confused, perplexed, and unable to reply to the demand.**

’ Then the disbeliever was confused perplexed and amazed; and God guides not the folk who do evil disbelieving to the art of argument. " Since the king was aware of his weakness, inadequacy and that he was not able to reply to Ibrahim's request, he was idle, silent and unable to comment. Some people doubt the validity of the last argument of Sayyidna Ibrahim because Namrud could have refuted it by a counter demand from Ibrahim and could have said, "If there is a God, let Him bring the sun out from the West." Abraham, of course, could have answered this claim made by Nimrod, but he did not want the conversation to deteriorate into a heated polemical discussion. (Thus was the disbeliever abashed) the one who disbelieved kept quiet and could not argue.

**A political claim and a message about the sun.**

When Abraham preached the message of the One God in the land of Iraq, his teachings had no direct connection with politics or government in the country. Though Abraham’s message was apolitical, it nevertheless appeared to Nimrod as a threat to his political claims, for according to the message taught by Abraham, even the sun was part of God’s creation. Had his subjects accepted Abraham’s message of the One God, it would have amounted to demolishing the theological base on which the edifice of his political power rested. However, that was not the case in pre-democratic times, when kings sanctioned their rule over their subjects by laying claim to being some kind of divine incarnation. A contemporary of Abraham, he was one of those monarchs who used this method to back up his right of sovereignty over the people. The sun was believed by his people to be the Chief of the gods and was thus revered by them as an object of worship. For instance, should one be endowed with worldly wealth and power, one may consider these to be a personal success, the outcome of one’s own talent. It is evident from the words used in the verse that if an infidel is given political power or a high worldly status, there is no harm (for a Muslim) in referring to him as a holder of that position (Qurtubi). What made Nimrod commit this transgression, utter disbelief and arrant rebellion was his tyranny and the fact that he ruled for a long time.

259.text:
The verse is the second of two accounts of a man who was shown resurrection, and it moves through a whole sequence of questions and answers. "Or are you not aware of the one who passed by a city which was in ruins, He wondered" gives the place and the reaction in one breath, so the man is defined first by what he is looking at, a town emptied and fallen, and then by the question that this produces in him. "How could Allah bring this back to life after its destruction" is the question, and it is about the city rather than about himself, which is why the answer that follows takes the form of his own death. "So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years then brought him back to life, Allah asked" puts the doing and the asking side by side, and the question is not for information. "How long have you remained in this state, He replied" then gives the answer of a man measuring from what he remembers, and "Perhaps a day or part of a day, Allah said, No" is the correction, so the word for the uncertainty and the word for the refusal stand together. "You have remained here for a hundred years" states the length, and then the evidence is pointed out one thing at a time: "Just look at your food and drink" and "they have not spoiled", so the untouched food is the first proof of the time that has passed, and "But now look at the remains of your donkey" is the second, since the donkey did spoil, and the two are shown against one another on purpose. "And so We have made you into a sign for humanity" carries what the whole thing was for, and "And look at the bones of the donkey" with "how We bring them together then clothe them with flesh" turns the eyes from the man to the animal and from death to the assembling of a body. "When this was made clear to him, he declared" is the moment the seeing ends, and "Now I know that Allah is Most Capable of everything" is what the man takes from it, a knowledge he did not have in that form before.

**The city that fell, and the man who passed by it.**

(Have you not looked at him who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord?) means, "Have you seen anyone like the person who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord" Then, Allah connected the Ayah,. Or such as he who passed by a city that was all in ruins to its roofs he said How shall God give life to this now that it is deadḍ So God made him die for a hundred years then he raised him up; He said How long have you tarriedḍ ; he said I have tarried a day or part of a day ; He said Nay you have tarried a hundred years. (Or (bethink thee) the like of him who, passing by a township) He says: do you not know about 'Uzayr Ibn Shurahya who passed by the township of Dayr Hiraql (which had fallen into utter ruin, exclaimed: How shall Allah give this township life after its death) How can Allah bring the people of this township back to life after their death? Or did you see such as he Ezra ‘Uzayr who the kāf of ka’lladhī ‘such as he who’ is extra passed by a city namely the Holy House sc. Mujahid bin Jabr said that the Ayah refers to a man from the Children of Israel, and the village was Bayt al-Maqdis, after Nebuchadnezzar destroyed it and killed its people. (up to its roofs) indicates that the roofs and walls (of the village) fell to the ground. 'Uzayr stood contemplating about what had happened to that city, after a great civilization used to inhabit it. Or do you know the example of the one who passed by a town in which the roofs had fallen, the walls had collapsed and the people had died, making it a deserted ruin?

**The question, and what it was not.**

(Oh! How will Allah ever bring it to life after its death) because of the utter destruction he saw and the implausibility of its returning to what it used to be. This was not a question of denial a matter of ignorance or an indication of doubt in divine power for this report is about Ezra ʿUzayr the prophet and it is not possible for the prophets [ ] to doubt or be ignorant. It is generally thought that in the first incident, the prophet in question was Ezra (Uzayr) (5th century BC), while in the second, as the Quran itself makes clear, it was Abraham, who lived between the years 2160 and 1985 BC. Allah (said: How long hast thou tarried) O 'Uzayr?

**The hundred years, and why the man thought it was one day.**

(He said: I have tarried for a day) and then looked at the sun still in the horizon and said (or part of a day. He) Allah (said: Nay, but thou hast tarried) you were dead (for a hundred years. Just look at thy food) figs and grapes (and drink) juice (which have not rotted! Look at thine ass!) look at the bones of your ass how white they look! The scholars said that since the man died in the early part of the day and Allah resurrected him in the latter part of the day, when he saw that the sun was still apparent, he thought that it was the sun of that very day. The city was rebuilt seventy years after the man ('Uzayr) died, and its inhabitants increased and the Children of Israel moved back to it.

**The food that did not spoil, and the donkey.**

Look at your food the figs and drink the cup of juice it has not spoiled despite the length of time the final hā’ of yatasannah ‘to spoil’ is said to belong to the original root s-n-h; but it is also said to be silent in which case the root would be s-n-y; a variant reading omits the final hā’; and look at your ass how it is and he saw that it had died and all that remained were its withered white bones. He had grapes, figs and juice, and he found them as he left them; neither did the juice spoil nor the figs become bitter nor the grapes rot.

**The bones set up and clothed with flesh.**

And look at the bones of the ass how We shall set them up how We shall raise them back to life nunshiruhā or nanshiruhā derived from the two expressions nashara and anshara; a variant reading has nunshizuhā meaning ‘How We shall move it and make it stand’; and then clothe them with flesh’ and when he looked at it he saw that the bones had been reconstituted and clothed with flesh and that the Spirit had been breathed into it making it bray.
