**A testimony not concealed, a heart that is sinful when it is hidden, and the people asked not to refuse when they are called.**

And do not conceal the testimony if you are summoned to give it; whoever conceals it his heart is sinful the heart is mentioned because it is the locus of the testimony and because if it sins there are other sinful consequences and so the person will be punished as though he were a sinner; and God knows what you do nothing of which can be hidden from Him. After that, the Holy Qur'an directs the people that they should not refuse to be witnesses when it is required from them, since evidence is the way to revive truth and the method to resolved disputes.

**Standing out firmly for justice as witnesses to Allah, and the scribe whose wages are asked for.**

(O you who believe! Stand out firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah, even though it be against yourselves, or your parents, or your kin, be he rich or poor, Allah is a better Protector to both (than you). So follow not the lusts (of your hearts), lest you avoid justice; and if you distort your witness or refuse to give it, verily, Allah is Ever Well-Acquainted with what you do)[4:135] and in this Ayah [2:283] He said,. For this reason, the Muslim jurists have said that the scribe who demands his wages while writing, or the witness who claims his legitimate two-way conveyance allowance, are entitled to get it as a matter of their right. After that, the attention of the scribe has been drawn to the fact that Allah Almighty has given him the ability to write, for which he can show his gratefulness by not refusing to write.

**A shield mortgaged for food, and a purchase on credit that a man must make good.**

The Two Sahihs recorded that Anas said that the Messenger of Allah died while his shield was mortgaged with a Jew in return for thirty Wasq (approximately 180 kg) of barley, which the Prophet bought on credit as provisions for his household. For instance, if a person has made a purchase on credit, then he is the one who should dictate the entries of the document because this will be a written agreement on his behalf. If the case involves the police and a crime, the chief of the police station would call the witness everyday and any time, and on occasions, would have him sit there for hours. Therefore, every decent person engaged in earning his livelihood has been forced to take the appearance in court as punishment for no crime of his, and therefore, he has been left with no choice but to avoid it as far as he can.

**The particulars of a transaction taught to a people, the written word, and a guardian for a man who cannot dictate.**

He teaches them the particulars of their transactions with one another and teaches them to adopt caution and bear witness [as explained in this verse] so that no injury will occur between them. The written word has taken the place of human speech but think of the days of fourteen hundred years ago when almost the entire business of the world was conducted verbally. Since such a person does not have the ability to dictate a document, it was said that, in a situation like this, his wali or guardian should dictate the written agreement. The guardian of the mute, or the speaker of the language unknown to the scribe could also do this, and should he make somebody his representative, it would still be possible. This is why the Muslim jurists, may Allah's mercy be upon them, have said that simple writing of an agreement is not a conclusive proof in the sight of Islamic Shari'ah.

284.text:
The verse leaves the paperwork of a debt and takes the whole picture. "To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" is stated as a fact of ownership before anything is asked of a person, and the wording covers both places without exception, so the record a man keeps of a debt is set inside a possession that he does not have. "Whether you reveal what is in your hearts or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it" then moves the accounting from a courtroom to a chest, and the sources weigh the clause carefully, since a bringing to account of what was never spoken looks like a burden no one could carry, and they read it against what was forgiven rather than counted. "He forgives whoever He wills, and punishes whoever He wills" gives the outcome of that account, and the two halves are put in the order of mercy first, while the will in both clauses refuses any man the idea that he has settled where he stands. "And Allah is Most Capable of everything" ends the verse on a capacity that has no limit attached to it, which is the same quality the section has been building toward through a threat of war, a respite for a debtor and a record that cannot be lost. A reader who has been told to write down what he owes is here told that what he intended was never hidden, and the verse after this answers by describing how a believer replies when he hears it. What the verse does not do is explain why a will of that kind chooses one person and not another, and the sources are careful here, since a clause about forgiving and punishing by a will can be read as an end to argument, while they read it as a reason for hope rather than as a division already made. The two clauses are also in an order, a forgiveness named before a punishment, which is where the section about a debt had put its own emphasis, on what is written off rather than on what is owed.

**Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and the ownership that covers it.**

(Unto Allah (belongeth) whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings and marvels; He commands His servants with whatever He wills; (and whether ye make known what is in your minds) in your hearts; this refers to the discourse of the soul after the arousal of one's misgivings but before one divulges it (or hide it, Allah will bring you to account for it) Allah will requite you for it. (To Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is able to do all things)

**What is hidden in a breast, what is made known in a mind, and the account a people are brought to.**

Whether you disclose manifest what is in your hearts or hide it of evil and resolve for it God shall take you to account for it informing you of it on the Day of Resurrection. When the verse ( and whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide, Allah will bring you to account for it) was revealed, objection crept into the hearts of the prophetic Companions as it never did before. Here, warning has been given that it is haram (unlawful) to conceal evidence. 'If you concealed the truth of a matter knowingly, your Lord who is all-Knowing and all-Aware, will make you account for it' - this interpretation of the verse has been reported from Sayyidna Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Sha'bi and Mujahid (Qurtubi).

**The forgiving and the chastising, the anxiety a people carried to the Prophet, and the doubt another answer takes away.**

Then He will forgive whom He will to forgive and chastise whom He will to chastise both verbs are apocopated fa-yaghfir ‘he will forgive’ wa-yu‘adhdhib ‘he will chastise’ if taken as the responses to the conditional in tubdū ‘if you proclaim’; but they may also be read with a final nominative inflection yaghfiru yu‘adhdhibu in which case it would constitute a new clause and follow on from an implicit fa-huwa ‘then He’. However, other ulama' have answered this doubt by saying that the hadith, in which forgiveness of things hidden in the heart has been mentioned, refers to the involuntary thoughts that enter the human heart without volition; in fact, they would still keep coming even if one tried to stop them. When they carried their anxiety to the Holy Prophet he instructed them all to firmly resolve to obey and act in accordance with the Divine imperatives, and say that is, we heard, and we obeyed.

**The one who intends an evil deed not recorded as such, and the angels charged with writing down deeds.**

(Allah said (to His angels), "If My servant intends to commit an evil deed, do not record it as such for him, and if he commits it, write it for him as one evil deed. If he intends to perform a good deed, but did not perform it, then write it for him as one good deed, and if he performs it, write it for him as ten good deeds.") Therefore, let one do what one must but let him be sure that there is someone there - his Raqib and Hafiz, the One Who is watching and guarding over him, and Who is recording all that is happening to him, externally and internally, and a full accounting of which has to be given on the day of Resurrection. It was for this reason that man was warned through this verse at the end of the Surah, by telling him that, in carrying out obligations or in abstaining from the prohibited, it was quite possible to dodge people around, to find an excuse and to get away with it. It appears in another hadith that Allah Almighty will say on the day of Doom (Qiyamah): 'This is the Day when hidden things will be surveyed and secrets concealed in hearts will be laid out in the open. And (forget not that) My angels charged with writing down your deeds wrote down only those visible on the outside, and I know what angels do not know, nor did they write those in your Book of Deeds.

**The placement of the verse at the end of the surah, and the people of the Two Scriptures before you.**

The placement of this verse at the end of Surah al-Baqarah has great wisdom behind it because Surah al-Baqarah is such an important and consequential Surah of the Holy Qur'an, that a fairly large part of Divine injunctions appears in it. This conforms to the report of Sayyidna Ibn Umar appearing in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim: 'I have heard from the Holy Prophet that the believer will be drawn near his most exalted Lord when Allah Almighty will make him recall his sins one by one and will ask him if he knew that he had committed those sins. When Allah, exalted is He, revealed to His Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, the verse ( and whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide, Allah will bring you to account for it) [2:284], the prophetic Companions found this hard to cope with. (Do you want to repeat what the People of the Two Scriptures before you said, that is, 'We hear and we disobey?' Rather, say, 'We hear and we obey, and we seek Your forgiveness, O our Lord, and the Return is to You.) (Allah burdens not a person beyond his scope. He gets reward for that (good) which he has earned, and he is punished for that (evil) which he has earned. "Our Lord! Punish us not if we forget or fall into error".)

285.text:
The verse states a belief rather than commanding one. "The Messenger firmly believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord" puts the prophet in the same class as the people he is addressing, and the wording of a firm belief is about assent settled in a heart, while the sources attend to the phrase from his Lord as the reason the assent is firm, since what is believed is not a claim but something sent. "and so do the believers" brings the community into the same sentence, so the verse does not describe a private conviction of a messenger standing alone. "They all believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers, They proclaim" is the first list of its kind in the sūrah, four objects of a single assent, and the wording puts the books and the messengers beside God and the angels, which is why the sources discuss the pairing, a faith that is not complete with one of them missing. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers" is given as something they say, and the negation is general, so the belief includes the prophets a people used to take and leave. "And they say, We hear and obey" is the answer the previous verses asked for, since the people of the earlier scriptures were told to say it and gave a different answer, and "We seek Your forgiveness, our Lord" then puts a request inside the confession of a hearing, while "And to You alone is the final return" closes on the end the section has been turning toward since the verse about a day when every soul is paid in full. What is brought to these two verses describes the companions arriving with anxiety about what was laid on them and leaving with the prayer the next verse carries. The verse has no command in it at all, which is the reason the sources spend their effort on what the four objects of a belief cover rather than on what a person must now do, since a report about an assent is asking to be understood before it is asked to be obeyed. A reader who looks for the verb that governs the passage will find it in the previous verse, in the instruction to be mindful, while this verse only describes who believes what and what they say when it is put into words.

**The Messenger believes, and the believers believe with him.**

The Messenger Muhammad believes in affirms the truth of what was revealed to him from his Lord namely the Qur’ān and the believers wa’l-mu’minūna is a supplement to al-rasūlu ‘the Messenger’; each one the tanwīn of kullun stands in place of the second noun in an annexation sc. kullu wāhidin believes in God and His angels and in His Books all of them and each of them and His messengers and they say ‘we make no distinction between any of His messengers’ believing in some and disbelieving in others in the manner of the Jews and the Christians. (The Messenger believeth) the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ believes (in that which hath been revealed unto him from his Lord) i.e. the Qur'an and its content, and then the Prophet ﷺ said on behalf of his Lord (and (so do) the believers. Each one believeth in Allah and His angels and His scriptures and His messengers-We make no distinction between any of His messengers-) they say: we do not disbelieve in any of his messengers (and they say: We hear) the saying of our Lord, (and we obey) the command of our Lord, i.e. we hear and obey our Lord. One of the distinct ones is that they come at the end of Sarah al-Baqarah where most of the injunctions of Shari ah appear briefly, or in detail, such as, those dealing with the articles of faith, modes of worship, mutual dealings, morals and social living etc.

**The four objects of an assent, and the distinction that is not made between the messengers.**

Now that He has mentioned faith, the Uprising, the Garden, the Fire, the prayer, the alms tax, retaliation, fasting, hajj, struggle, marriage, divorce, menstruation, the waiting period, expenditure, foster relationship, forswearal, divorce initiated by the wife, in heritance, charity, vows, buying, selling, usury, debts, and ransom; and He has mentioned the stories of the prophets and the signs of His power, God completes the surah by mentioning that His prophet and the faithful assent to the truthfulness of all of it. After that it was clearly stressed that the 'believers' of this ummah (Muslim community) will do nothing as was done by past communities when they planted seeds of discord among messengers of Allah by accepting some as prophets and by denying that status to others. Nervously excited, the noble Companion presented themselves before the Holy Prophet g and said: ia Rasool Allah, till now we thought that we shall be called to account for only those deeds that we do with our will and choice, and we shall not be called to account for thoughts that cross our minds involuntarily.

**The door opened in heaven, the vision Gabriel bore, and what Allah sent forth to a people.**

Jibil lifted his sight to the sky and said, 'This is a door that was opened just now in heaven, and it was never opened before.' An angel came down through the door to the Prophet and said, 'Receive the good news of two lights that you have been given and which no Prophet before you was given: the Opener of the Book (Al-Fatihah) and the last Ayat in Surat Al-Baqarah. As narrated by Sayyidna Ibn Abbas the Holy Prophet said that Allah Almighty has sent forth these two verses out of the treasures of Paradise and the 'Rahman' had already written them by His own hand two thousand years earlier than the creation of all things and beings. As it appears in the Mustadrak of al-Hakim and in Bayhaqi, the Holy Prophet said that Allah Almighty has concluded Sarah al-Baqarah with these two verses, which have been given to me in His grace from out of the special treasure that lies under the Arsh (Divine Throne).

**The praise that opens the verse, the people who are true and obedient, and the difficulty a man escapes from.**

This is praise and laudation of the Prophet, who explained these rulings and delivered the message, and of the faithful, for we have recognized, accepted, and held firm to all the rulings, boundaries, stories of the prophets, and marks of God's power and tremendousness that were mentioned. Here, the first of the two verses opens with words of praise for the Muslims who are true and obedient, those who said yes with all their heart to all injunctions ordained by Allah, and were all set to carry them out. This way it is extremely difficult to escape punishment.' Although, the Holy Prophet g knew the correct intended meaning of the verse but he, in view of the generality of its words, did not elect to say anything on his own. Muslim recorded that 'Abdullah said, "When the Messenger of Allah went on the Isra journey, he ascended to the Sidrat Al-Muntaha in the sixth heaven, where whatever ascends from the earth ends at, and whatever descends from above it ends at. (Our Lord! Lay not on us a burden like that which You did lay on those before us (Jews and Christians),) means, "Even if we were able to perform them, do not require us to perform the difficult deeds as You required the previous nations before us, such as the burdens that were placed on them.

**The belief that Allah exists and is One, and the knowledge of a Prophet based on seeing and hearing.**

This 'iman consisted of the belief that Allah Almighty does exist and that He is One and that He is endued with all the perfect attributes, and that there are angels, and that all Scriptures and all Messengers sent by Allah are true. The knowledge of the Holy Prophet is based on seeing and hearing while the knowledge of other Muslims takes the form of 'iman bi l'ghayb or 'believing without seeing' as based on the 'ru'yat' or 'seeing' of the Holy Prophet .

286.text:
The last verse of the sūrah opens with a relief and then teaches a prayer. "Allah does not require of any soul more than what it can afford" is stated first, so the petitions that follow are made by people who already know that the asking is not a trap, and the wording of a capacity is handled by the sources as the rule that closes the section about a debt, a burden a man cannot carry is not laid on him. "All good will be for its own benefit, and all evil will be to its own loss" then puts the account back on the person, and the two halves are a pair, so neither the credit nor the cost travels outside the soul that earned it. "The believers pray, Our Lord! Do not punish us if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord! Do not place a burden on us like the one you placed on those before us. Our Lord! Do not burden us with what we cannot bear, Pardon us, forgive us" is the body of the prayer, six requests given in one speech, and the wording of the first covers a slipping and an error together, which is why the sources discuss whether what a man does unawares is taken from him. The middle petition asks about the past, and the burden being asked to be spared is explained as the narrow obligations laid on earlier communities, while the next one repeats the opening rule of the verse as a request, so what was stated to the believers as a fact is spoken back to God as a prayer. "Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us" moves from what is lifted to what is covered, and "You are our only Guardian. So grant us victory over the disbelieving people" ends the sūrah on a patronage and a help against a people who reject, which is where the very first verses of the section left the believers, between a fear that does not arrive and a grief that does not find them. What is brought to these two verses describes them as a gift given on the road of the night journey, and the sources read the whole sūrah as closing on the prayer it opens with. Between the two there is a change of voice worth marking, since the first two clauses are spoken about a person and the last six are spoken by him, so the verse moves from what a soul is charged with to what a soul asks for, and a reader who has just heard that no burden is laid beyond a capacity is taught to ask that it stay so.

**No soul charged beyond its capacity, and the good a soul has earned.**

God charges no soul save to its capacity that is what it is capable of bearing; for it is what it has merited of good and its reward and against it is what it has earned of evil and its burden no person shall be requited for another’s sin or for what he has not earned even if he was tempted to do it. (For it (is only) that which it hath earned) of good, and of leaving the discourse of the soul, forgetfulness, error and coercion, (and against it (only) that which it hath deserved) of evil, the discourse of the soul, forgetfulness, and coercion.

**What a people say when they are asked, the chastisement they ask not to be met with, and the errors concealed from others.**

Say Our Lord take us not to task by way of chastisement if we forget or err by straying from the right path unknowingly — as You used to take to task those before us God has lifted this burden from this community as reported in hadīth. When the believer called upon Allah with this supplication, Allah lifted from them the discourse of the soul, forgetfulness, error, coercion and absolved them from being turned into animals, making the ground swallow them or being tossed by the waves. Allah's forgiveness for what is between Him and them, that He conceals these errors from His other servants, and thus does not expose them before the servants, and that He grants them immunity from further error.

**The burden laid on those before us, and the severe restrictions that were placed on them.**

(Our Lord! Lay not on us a burden like that which You did lay on those before us (Jews and Christians),) means, "Even if we were able to perform them, do not require us to perform the difficult deeds as You required the previous nations before us, such as the burdens that were placed on them. Indicated here are the severe restrictions placed on the Bani Isra'il (Israelites), such as, a piece of cloth could not be made fully pure unless cut or burnt, or that repentance could not be accepted without killing.

**The petition as an acknowledgement of favour, the animals a people were turned into, and the prayer a man is taught to make.**

The petition here then is a way of acknowledging God’s favour; our Lord burden us not with a load an affair which we cannot bear such as You did lay upon those before us namely upon the Children of Israel as for example the killing of oneself in repentance the paying of a quarter of one’s property for alms and the severing of the impure part. (Pardon us) by not turning us into animals as you turned some of the people of Jesus into animals, (absolve us) from making the ground swallow us up as you made the ground swallow up Korah (Qarun); (and have mercy on us) by not being tossed up by the waves as you did to the people of Lot. Our Lord do not burden us beyond what we have the power the strength to bear of obligations and trials; and pardon us effacing our sins and forgive us and have mercy on us with mercy added to Your forgiveness; You are our Patron our Master and the Guardian of our affairs; so grant us assistance against the disbelieving folk by establishing definitive proof for us and victory over them in battle for it is expected of a patron that he assist his clients against their enemies. In this context, several other verses of the Qur'an and many reports from ahadith prove that one who does something good which persuades others to act similarly, then its reward will continue reaching the original doer of the good deed as long as the later followers of the original deed continue with their good deeds. The noble Qur'an, towards the far end, teaches Muslims to make a special du a or prayer in which forgiveness has been sought on commission of some act because of forgetfulness or neglect or mistake.

**The second kind of thought that is involuntary, what is borne in mind about a burden, and the doubt that could have risen.**

The second kind is involuntary, that which just issues forth without choice or volition, for instance, saying something other than what one actually intended to say, or a palsied hand moving unintentionally caused pain to somebody. It was said: :'Allah burdens not anyone beyond his or her capacity.' Therefore, thoughts that enter the heart without one's intention and control and are not translated into action, stand all excused in the sight of Allah Almighty. But it should be borne in mind that the drive of the meaning of this verse is that, one will initially face direct reward or punishment for what is done with intention and volition. After that comes the second verse where the doubt, which could have risen during the comprehension of some sentences in the previous verse, has been removed in a style that is very special.

**You are our supporter and helper, the trust placed in You, and what was given to the Messenger on the night journey.**

(You are our Mawla) meaning, You are our supporter and helper, our trust is in You, You are sought for each and every type of help and our total reliance is on You. In short, Allah Almighty bestowed His best when He promised the acceptance of all these prayers through His Rasul the last among the prophets, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. When Allah, exalted is He, revealed to His Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace, the verse ( and whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide, Allah will bring you to account for it) [2:284], the prophetic Companions found this hard to cope with. Allah revealed after this (The messenger believeth in that which hath been revealed unto him from his Lord) the whole verse, and Allah abrogated it by His revelation (Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope) [2:286] to the end of the verse . The Messenger of Allah was then given three things: the five prayers, the last Ayat in Surat Al-Baqarah and forgiveness for whoever did not associate anything or anyone with Allah from his Ummah." So the Last Hour will commence while Muhammad's Law remains the only valid Law, and all the while a group of his Ummah will always be on the path of truth, apparent and dominant.
